review_text:
Located inside the Ludlow Hotel, the latest hype machine from the Torrisi team has the familiar high prices and excellent food as their other spots.

This time it's French food, and it's pretty good, but nothing was particularly memorable or as mind-blowing as at Carbone.

It's not a stuffy French restaurant, and is more on the casual side with pretty loud music playing. It's not that big, but feels more spacious with creative mirror placement.

On to the important stuff, we got too much food, which was all pretty good:

- Flatbread with Creme Fraiche
Complimentary to start, this was really excellent. It's a small round piece of bread that is very hot and even more buttery. Off to a great start.

- Gnocchi Parisienne ($14)
This was quite good, and like all the rest of the food here, very rich. The gnocchi actually reminded me more of Korean-style rice cakes, which was actually a good thing. The creamy sauce and tomatoes added the richness and flavor that the spongy gnocchi needed.

- Lamb Carpaccio ($16)
This was an impressively-plated large portion of carpaccio topped with goat cheese and figs. It was delicious, but the only problem is that the portion of pita provided for eating the lamb with was way too small. 

- Roquefort Salad ($16)
This was a tasty salad, but not a $16 salad. Mostly composed of roasted beets, but filled with funky blue cheese, candied cashews and other veggies, it was filled with tons of strong flavors. It was definitely way richer and not as healthy as you might expect a salad to be.

- Meunière ($26)
A very simple, clean plate, this was just a great piece of trout. It was definitely prepped with plenty of butter, and was very filling and satisfying for a piece of fish.

- Short Ribs Au Poivre ($33)
I was disappointed to hear they weren't serving the Cote de Beouf for 2, but this was a great consolation. This was a really generous portion of meat, an excellent slab of extremely soft and buttery short rib.

- Cauliflower Roti ($10)
Pretty tasty for cauliflower, this is a good choice for something a little lighter, even though it's still pretty oily too.

- Pommes Frites ($10)
You gotta have frites at a French restaurant, and these were really great, as well as very different from any I've had before. Instead of long, thin fries, they were more in the shape of potato chips, but much thicker and very crispy. These are a must as a side to go with your entrees.

- Tarte Tatin for 2 ($18)
They don't have a dessert menu yet, but do have 4 options available. The one that most caught our attention (aside from the Beignets, which we should've ordered as well) was this Tarte Tatin topped with Rum Raisin Ice Cream. Not particularly large, I don't see why it's listed and priced as "for 2", but it was delicious. The tart was super buttery, and definitely needs that cool, refreshing ice cream to go along with it.

As expected from this group, and from the high prices, service was perfect throughout the meal. Everybody was very friendly and the waitstaff was on point. The food was good, but maybe not good enough to justify the prices, and probably not enough to make me want to come back, especially given how much of a pain it will be soon to get a reservation once the reviews start coming in. I would probably go to Sweet Chick next door instead for some really satisfying food for half the price.

Really disappointing. They ran out of half the menu by 9:30. The food is good, but for the price it should be excellent. 
Started with lamb carpaccio which was nice but lacked that delicate dissolving quality. Tomato gnocchi was very average, felt tired. Ordered the bouillabaisse for main, the seafood itself was great but I expected a classic French, thick, rich seafood broth and it was quite thin. 
Highlight was oyster service, great idea and gorgeous oysters. 
Not worth the $300 for 3 price

Dear New Yorkers,

Have you ever been to a restaurant in NYC where your meal is served 2hrs after bring seated? Cold? Mediocre with respect to taste .... oh did I mention that literally half of the items on the menu are not available because ' we ran out'.. Did you say 'no' , well neither have I until... Dirty French. 

I would say half of the restaurant is not only staffed with aspiring actors, writers , artists,  its filled with aspiring wait staff. Have you ever waited 45 minutes to give your order? 'No' you say, then come to Dirty French.

If you're into new experiences in NYC dining Dirty French is the place to for you.The best part is if you don't find something acceptable, call the manager Jess Taylor! He'll tell you how 'its out of his hands' and give you a business card, well isn't that nice. Just when you thought you saw it all , you meet the first NYC manager with zero customer service. Thanks Dirty French

This experience was very disappointing especially because the owners know the NYC restaurant game (Torrisi, Carbone). First I'll start with the good...my four Belmondo drinks were great (when you wait two hours for food you end up drinking alot) and the bread and whipped fromage they bring out first was excellent (I should have just asked for a plate of that as my meal). 
Now on to the bad....they were late seating us, which probably isn't even worth mentioning except that mostly everything else was bad too. It took awhile for the waitress to come over and discuss the menu with us. Once she did she informed us they were out of their signature dishes, which also meant there was no beef or chicken on the menu so for someone who only eats those two things I didn't have too many options (it was suggested to me that I order sides as my main dish (rice pilaf and green beans). Once we got over the "nothing is available" hurdle we waited. And waited. And waited. Our food took two hours to arrive. I saw people sit down after us, eat their food and leave before our food even came. We really tried not to complain and understand new restaurants have growing pains but this was a week after they opened and this team should know their way around a busy restaurant. The waitress sent over the manager as she had done previously when there was no food available. This time it was Jes Taylor. He asked how our meal was and we shared our grievances and we were told he was sorry and that it was out of his hands. He offered his card incase we were willing to give them another try and offered to make our reservation but said that he could not guarantee a reservation time we wanted. So basically it was the same as calling the reservation line or emailing the general reservation team?!

To sum it up: the food was disappointing, the service was disappointing and the manager, Jes Taylor was disappointing.

Oh and the cherry on top of it all, at 11:45pm we were asked if we wanted dessert....really? Who eats dessert after eating a pork chop at 11:45pm??

I understand that every restaurant has a bad night but it is how you recover that makes the difference. The service was well meaning but confused and scatty. Half the items form the menu where not available and we waited almost an hour for what we were able to order;some apps and a few sides. The meal was expensive and lackluster and the manager just apologized and said "it was out of his hands" I am sorry but it IS in your hands. Your job is to manage and recover the mistakes of your staff. . Too many great restaurants in the area to waste your time on this overpriced confused lot.

Anticipated a marvelous Steak Dinner .... I WAS WRONG. 

Pro:  (very little)
Imperial Planter's Punch for 2 was tasty (Part 1 - why they received one star)
Flat bread was fantastic. (Part 2 - one star)

Oysters were so so, but having the waiter displaying them in a heavy iced serving bowl was a bit much, more like you were forced to order.

CONS: (HUGE)
Pretty boy waiter couldn't even take our order properly.  He stopped serving us after he found out that he forgot to tell us that the cote de boeuf was limited availability, basically ruining our experience at this pretentious restaurant.  Man up bad server.

The manager didn't even have the decency to come to the table to ask how dinner was.  
Basically was served flat bread and oysters even before we could place our meal order and have the menus taken from the table.  

NEED TO ADD LIMITED AVAILABILITY ON MOST THINGS ON THE MENU AND THE WAITWR EXPLAIN IT TO CUSTOMETS PRIOR TO ORDERING!!!

Dirty French needs to work on the service.  
I will not be going back after the HORRIBLE SERVICE.  

LES is not fancy, stop trying to be SOHO or TriBeCa.  You make the neighborhood look bad.

Thanks for the bad dinner.  Your restaurant made us have better dinner somewhere else.  

Never again.

So my real rating is a 4.5 but I'm rounding up instead of down because other people are giving it one star for no good reason. 
I've actually been here twice now and yes, they ran out of items, but understand that they're still figuring stuff out. If you're going to come to a new restaurant their first few weeks you better expect that the servers and the chefs are still figuring things out. The trout, short rib, the bass, the beet salad, the tuna tartare, the cauliflower and the duck were all awesome. The lamb saddle could have been better and the gnocchi wasn't my favorite. Kind of had a spicy sausage taste to it. 
Best of all, the Grand Prixe and the bread starter are amazing... And so are the braised oysters. 
The music is great, the ambiance is happening,  and the decor is retro. This place can be a 4.5 and will be soon once they figure out how much food to prepare without having a lot go to waste.

Wow. I had read the few reviews on here before going to Dirty French last night (9/12) and was actually not looking forward to it based on them. Thank goodness we opted to keep our reservation, because it was one of the better dining experiences that I have had in a LONG time. Our reservation was for 9:45, and we were a little early and were walked over to the Lobby Bar (very cool vibe) and had a pre dinner cocktail. We were probably seated a little bit before ten. 

We had NO issues with service, and if anything our waitress was great and helpful with recommendations. They were out of the short rib, which I had been planning to try and that was kind of a bummer, but nothing else as other reviewers have reported. The warm flatbread with soft cheese that was served to start was seriously delicious - other restaurants would charge for that! My husband and I split the roasted clams almondine and we have honestly been talking about them ever since. Incredibly flavorful and a different twist on clams - highly recommend! I ended up getting the lamb, which was delicious and made me less sad about missing out on the short rib and my husband got the duck l'orange, which was also delicious (and we go to a lot of French restaurants and are big fans of that dish, so we had a high bar). We split a side order of the roasted cauliflower and loved that as well. My only regret is that we did not try the dessert - the beignets sounded delicious but we were in the mood for gelato next door and passed on dessert. 

Perhaps Dirty French needed a week to work the kinks out, but we loved our experience. The wait time for food and between courses was no longer than anything else, the lobby bar (and outside bar area) were a great vibe to wait for your table or after dinner, and the restaurant itself was welcoming and they played awesome music. Again, we had no issues with service - I somehow managed to spill two drinks and they were incredibly accommodating about replacing them. We will absolutely return - I would love to try more of the starters, but the clams were so delicious I am not sure I can bring myself to go back and NOT order those again. Looking forward to trying to short rib and the cote d'boef. Yes, the restaurant wasn't cheap (entrees in the high 30's) but not outrageous either given that it is a Torrisi restaurant. I would definitely recommend it!
Excellent food. The backed clam was outstanding. The lamb main course was brilliant. Great food.

disappointed ,

I'll caveat this review by saying the restaurant just opened so there will inevitably be some kinks...

The apps were good, the service was spotty/borderline annoying, and the entrees were meh. 

Our waiter was pushing the ostentatious silver bowl of oysters hard...coming back every few minutes to ask if we had decided which oysters we wanted.. We didn't want any oysters! Stop asking. It took a few requests to get a drink menu but the cocktails were good.

The sommelier had a fake snooty accent. That provided some amusement.

The complimentary naan-ish bread was buttery and delicious served with a dollop of labne. The kale salad was good as was the tuna piri piri tartare. The boudin needed more flavor and the lamb carpaccio was okay. 

The porgy fish was deep-fried and very basic looking. The pork tenderloin was not very flavorful. The pineapple/banana gratin with rum raisin ice cream is a miss.

Overall, everything was VERY buttery. I would only go back for drinks and apps next time.

My husband and I had a great evening at Dirty French. From the previous reviews it seems the restaurant had a difficult start, but on September 12 it was an amazing experience.

We arrived on time for a 7:15p reservation. The staff was friendly and sat us at our table immediately. Once we were handed menus, a waiter offered us oysters which we opted out of.  They then mentioned a variety of hams that were not listed on the menu and we ordered one of the three selections.

After ordering cocktails the complimentary bread and cheese spread arrived to our surprise. Hot from the oven it was nice to have something to nosh on while perusing the menu. Our server shared her recommendations, answered all of our questions then gave us plenty of time to decide on our selections.

Next the beautifully thinly sliced ham arrived - I think from Kentucky. It was lightly smoked and served with grilled bread and a delicious pickled spread. Okay now we were concerned that we would be getting too much food.  So when our server returned we asked about certain appetizers and entrees in regards to the serving sizes.  She gladly answered our question and again gave us more time to decide AND eat our ham and bread.

Finally, we decided on sharing the Gnocchi Parisienne, which was a perfect sharing size after our starters. The dish while buttery was surprisingly light.

Next the Chicken and Crepes for 2 (which before we ordered were told was a whole chicken) came out and took over our whole table.  It's a fun dish for a couple.  The crepes were thin and delicate but could hold a bit of chicken, one of the three spreads (harissa, apricot jam and hot mustard) and all 3 toppings of cilantro, hot peppers and radishes. The breast of the chicken was served in a large serving bowl covered in a delicious sauce.  The rest of the chicken (thighs, attached to legs with the claws) was rubbed in an exotic spiced lemon rub and cooked until charred. So different and yummy.

We ordered the Haricot Vert and the Pommes Frites to go with our chicken.  There was a ton of food, but I ate all of the string beans because of the amazing sauce on top of them. We took a doggie bag home with the chicken.

This meal was paired wonderfully with a recommendation from the sommelier, who offered an array of choices. She was knowledgeable, not pushy and pleasant.

I was hoping for a cheese course, which I was told would be joining the dessert menu in the future, so my husband and I shared the Beignets with a decadent espresso sauce.  I was happy to have the sauce on the side for dipping because the plain doughnut was delicate and sweet enough with a bit of powdered sugar.

I would love to go back to Dirty French - if I can score a reservation.  The staff was professional, helpful and friendly. The space inviting and comfortable. And the food innovative and delicious.

I am extremely disappointed in this restaurant. I am not one to complain, but the service was horrendous. It took an hour to get a dozen oysters, plus a half hour for a kale salad and tuna tatar and another forty minutes for entrees. Our waiter never once checked in on us. I know this is a new restaurant and they are still working out the kinks, but seriously, service should be a priority if they expect returning customers. 

On top of the shitty service I got food poisoning that night. I later found out that the rest of my party also had upset stomachs. I will not be returning to this restaurant.

This place is slammed already, and only been open for 2 weeks (give or take). I was really impressed at the flawless execution and confident service. Our server, Jenny, took such good care of us. I went here to celebrate a milestone with my boyfriend. The food is truly first rate, with a couple of stand-out exceptional dishes we had the pleasure of trying. Best of all, this is a concept that is unique and has not been tried anywhere else in the NY dining scene yet, incorporating all the flavours and techniques from the whole of the French-speaking world... Indochine, Creole, Europe, Africa, Caribbean, etc. Really exciting food! 

Must try: Duck a l'Orange, Tuna Tartare
Misleading menu. Weird and uncomfortable service. Mediocre to bad food. EXTREMELY overpriced. Will not go back. Threw away $300...

We had dinner with friends on a busy East Village Saturday evening.  It was a wonderful experience.  Our waitress Jenny had a delightful demeanor and was informative and thoroughly familiar with the menu and helped us make great choices.  The service and delivery of food was flawless.  The restaurant was extremely well staffed and the staff was attentive without being over bearing.  The flatbread to start was delicious, the oysters some of the sweetest we've ever had, the tuna tartar and organic salad were delicious and all four main courses (sea bass in papilliote, lamb, duck, pork) were lovely and tasty.  The atmosphere is vibrant and cool and the music volume and selection were excellent.  It's a tough reservation to secure but totally worth it!  Dont' miss Dirty French!
Trout was amazing, only thing my stomach was like where's the rest! Sooooooo I ordered desert... I would definitely recommend this place!

Nice vibe one expects from the chain.
The wait staff were exceptionally friendly, intelligent, helpful and informed.
Great colour coded uniform.
The food was positively filthy French!
It's a great fusion and pastiche of Classic French cooking. Incredibly generous portions, unfussy, balanced and deeply flavored food. 
Highly recommend & suggest booking a room at the Ludlow too.

Everything you want -

Food is well-executed; similar feel to other MFG spots, manages to be over the top ambitious and comfortable/approachable/rustic at the same time.

Both have amazing food, but DF is a noticeable value over Carbone's pricing while offering similar lux protein options.

Great space, open but intimate. Staff was well trained; for a new restaurant, service was crisp and cadence of courses was on point.

Grilled clams made me angry they were so good. table order a few rounds of them.

get on this

Went here Friday at 6:30.  Place was jammed full of beautiful well dressed people.  The space is really cool with some crazy sculptures lining the restaurant.  There is also a huge lobby bar with loungy sofas and chairs.  Cocktails were ok..maybe not quite worth the $16 though.

We started with a dozen amazing oysters.  Not much to say except they were excellent quality plump and juicy

The complimentary hot salted bread came next with the yogurt? spread.  As other reviewers said, this is delicious stuff.

For an appetizer we had the Boudin.  This was our favorite overall dish.  Its a single large sausage with pork/pork liver.  Minerally and absolutely incredible!  GET THIS.

We also had the Chicken for two. Another very tasty dish that was fun to eat and assemble with the white and dark meats using 3 different sauces, crepes, chilis, etc.  Ton of food.

Last was the lamb saddle.  Perfect piece of meat cooked to perfection.  Though too salty.

In fact the one negative thing I can think of is perhaps the food overall is a bit too salty.  Lowering the salt a tad on the meat dishes would help out I think.  (except for the bread--don't mess with it!  :)


Not sure what other reviewers experienced, but service was simply outstanding.  Our waiter came around all the time..bus boys were constantly refilling waters, two sommeliers came by to talk wine, the food came out very quickly, and the manager stopped by twice.  

Note:  They play 1980s music.  LOUD.  It feels like a party inside.  This is not a quiet romantic restaurant, but a bustling happening scene.  I mean this in a good way too.

Seriously awesome. I'm glad we waited a few weeks after it opened. We're definitely going back. Bread to start with whatever dip was delicious. Both raw and cooked oysters rocked. Ham dish was solid. The tuna tartar prep was unique and excellent. We're generally appetizer-focused people, but the entrees were out-of-this world. Special aged duck was ridiculously good, and the grass-few ribeye with the extra ground-up concoction they brought with it could not have tasted better - that steak was at least tied for best I've had this year, perhaps the best. Also had the bass which was good, but at that point we were all oriented around the meats. The sides we had were cauliflower, salad, and bacon which were well-executed. I also have to say even though I was full as heck, the coconut creme brulee with thai basil was phenomenal.

For full review: http://www.scrumphsus.com/blog/2014/9/30/dirtyfrench

After thumbing through pics of lamb carpaccio and foie gras in crispy bric dough scattered throughout my IG feed for the past month, I attempted to snag a table at Dirty French, the latest venture from Team Torrisi focused on French cuisine with Moroccan and Southeast influences. 

Since they opened around Labor Day, tables earlier than 10pm were nonexistent and it took about two weeks until I received a call that a last minute table opened up around 8pm. So much for the Barry's Bootcamp session I had planned to attend that evening.

Running a few minutes late, I walked past Katz's when my eyes were naturally drawn to the bright pink neon signs silently screaming out DIRTY FRENCH.

Sohee and I walked in and saw the cutest frog butler holding a stack of cards in bright pink, their signature color. After a short wait, we were led to a table near the bar where the bartender looked pretty spiffy in his white tux and red bowtie.

As we perused the gorgeous menus printed on textured paper, I was nervous because most of the early reviews lambasted the restaurant for horrible service and dishes being 86'd midway through service but the Jackson 5 blaring from the speakers put me at ease and made me want to groove.

We listened to the specials of the evening but decided to skip the cote de beouf as it was $189 for 44 oz. Instead, we went for the foie gras appetizer, the short ribs, and the porgy fillet as recommended by the knowledgeable waiter who answered all my questions with patience.

The complimentary made to order flatbread with herbs was still warm from the kitchen and served on a polished silver tray. On the side sat a huge dollop of creamy fromage blanc that easily pwns the familiar plate of stale rolls and cold butter served at too many establishments.

Since it only came with one piece of bread, I put in an order for an extra slice of bread but instead received a brand new order complete with cheese. Not complaining.

The foie gras plate was brought out within minutes and although my preferred preparation for foie is seared vs terrine, this particular rendition proved there is always more than one way to nirvana.

The smooth foie filling benefitted from the bric dough's wafer-like texture as well as the streaks of date puree which cut through the richness of the foie along with squeezed lemon that brightened the dish overall. The taste of the date puree instantly transported me back to 5th grade - my chinese friends know what's up when I say that it tasted like the inimitable Haw Flakes.

The comfortable pacing continued when the short ribs and porgy were brought to the table. As Sohee started on the short rib, I cut a nice piece of porgy and brought it to my mouth. Very flavorful and juicy while the crispy skin injected another layer of flavor. It was served butterflied with a variety of herbs such as tarragon and chervil.

The acidity of the dish came from the green tomatoes and talleggio olives in light pickled marinade. Well-balanced and a hearty portion that is great for sharing.

The short ribs au poivre meant that it was coated with one of my favorite things in the world: green and black peppercorns. From the first bite to the last, there were fireworks in my mouth.

The short rib had a great balance between Thai and Vietnamese flavor profiles with the meat being marinated in hoisin and fish sauce along with Kaffir lime juice. Bold, sweet, and tangy, this dish satisfied in terms of flavor even if the short ribs were slightly overcooked.

I enjoyed both dishes that were on opposite ends of the spectrum. One one hand you have the porgy that was light, refined, and dotted with notes of acidity while the short ribs' pungent fish sauce, sweet hoisin, and smoldering peppercorns made you clear your throat. My only disappointment was that for $33, the dish should have come with more than 3 pieces of short ribs.

We had dessert plans somewhere else but next time, I'm trying the cote de beouf, lamb saddle, and the duck dusted with ras el hanout, a spice that I adore but can't find on many menus.

At the end of the delicious meal I was reminded to not rush too quickly to judgment. I'm guilty of this all the time when it comes to not only restaurants (only 3.5 stars on yelp? uh, skip) but movies as well (I don't watch movies with a RT score of less than 65%).

In this case, don't believe the Yelp haters and form your own opinions after dining at Dirty French.

Came in on a Monday night with my girlfriend, made a reservation that morning.  Waited a couple minutes for our table which was up against a mirrored column and pretty awkward - most of the tables aren't like that ;)  Luckily the couple sitting next to us in the corner was on dessert and we were able to move when they got up.  I typically don't like to do things like that after already being seated, but our server was great about it and the corner allowed us to sit next to each other which made it all the easier to share food.

Started with the foie gras terrine which was ok.  It's a bit too tart, especially as I was drinking the Belmondo which was tequila, lemon, ginger etc.  Not a good pairing and probably would have been more enjoyable otherwise. It also comes colder than room temp and would have tasted better warm I think.

We made the awesome choice of ordering the Cote de Boeuf which was $109 that day for I believe 25ish ounces.  Our waiter recommended the steak rare which was perfect.  It came with fried leeks which had a strong vinegar flavor. I recommend eating them at the same time as the steak - the mixture in your mouth is amazing.  The Bearnaise sauce was buttery and delicious, completely out of this world.  Had a side of haricot vert which was topped with scallions and were charred and delicious in texture and taste. The chefs also creatively take the steak caps and create a  sort of ground up sausage which adds a nice extra delicious touch.  This is really the basis for my 5 star review - this was one of the best steaks I've had in a very long time, possibly ever.  The presentation was also awesome.

Service was good, there were a few small mishaps but completely understandable and staff went out of their way to make up for it.  I came in with low expectations and was definitely pleasantly surprised.  I think a lot of the reviews on here are overly negative and most seem to have been written in the first week or two of service which is pretty unfair as all openings have their kinks to work out.

I'm looking forward to being back for the juicy steak and to try some of the other dishes on the menu.  If the food is consistently this good I think this restaurant will prove to live up to the hype.

You have to be insane not to give this place 5 stars.  Their French bistro classics hit with Moroccan and New Orleans spices are incredibly different (not to mention delicious) for NYC and the scene is electric.   I've had the opportunity to dine at Dirty French twice and I was blown away both times. The service is consistently great as is the fare.  The oysters (you gotta try some grilled) and ham starter is a must and their duck a'lOrange was probably the most delicious thing I've ever tasted in my life. Applause for the som who picked very reasonably priced and delicious bottles of wine! 

Must try:
Lamb Carpaccio 
Tuna Tartare
Black Bass 
Duck a l'Orange
Chicken and Crepes (for two) 

Check out #DirtyFrench on Instagram for better pics of the dishes!

I had fantastic meal here with friends. There is a big bar in the back so come early and get a few drinks before your meal. The restaurant is fun and delicious and entertainingly decorated.

I enjoyed the Broadbent ham (a special). The "Amandine" clams were crazy good, and the trout was really flavorful. Great pommes frites too, of course.

Come, try it out, and enjoy!

Amazing atmosphere, perfect for a date. In addition to the amazing bread (of course), the appetizers were the stand out here.  The lamb carpaccio, foie gras and tuna tartar were fabulous.  As were the green bean and pommes fries sides. Skip the oysters, I hated the way they were pushed on you.  Save yourself for more bread.

I guess that you're going to get it right. The question is when.
The place is beautiful even if the music is loud.
For the lovers of the group that own carbine et all, they will put up with anything. I concur with the reviewers that complain about the service. It's beyond that service is not up to par for a restaurant of this category there is an issue with the training and the attitude.
We ended up with a waitress called Sarah that was more interested in her comfort that in  taking care of us. She took her time and even when I called her over she wouldn't come. The best was when I asked for the check and then I motion for her to come get the check and she motioned with her hand relax and be patient.ha ha
the food is very good in the kitchen is still figuring out the pace.  it took forever two of us arrived at eight is finished eating at 10.15. And it was not because we took our time they did
The wine list is fantastic but very pricey.
I would wait until they get their act together but if you don't care about service and pace you  can go now

Ok so here is the brief run down about the new dirty french ... I would def try it once . Food is very good . Not great, but very good .Would I go again ? Probably not . Here is why. Well I'm an upstate New Yorker and when I do come down to the city every few months or so, my fiancé and I crave amazing food and have pretty high expectations . When you come to NYC, especially with one of us being a former New Yorker ... You know what $200-250 for a dinner for two can get you . 

     This place is cute and trendy and fun for sure . Very lower east side but with a classier high end twist. While you wait for your table you will see the typical hipsters with super skinny jeans and cycle jackets on , but next to them you will see the couples dressed to impress with the designer sport jacket and cocktail dress on. 

     Staff is friendly and accommodating . ambiance is nice . Dim and playing great 80s tunes . Made for a great date night setting in the city . Appetizers were probably the highlight . Tuna tartare.... Amazing , nice touch to be served with the crepe and a touch of spice . Def go for the tuna tartar.
Clams almandine . Excellent . The house made bread, probably the highlight of the evening . 
 As for the entrees they were just ok. we were told the short rib marinated 14 days and cooked 12 hours, it was good but nothing I'm dying to comeback for . The trout blackened w pesto and sautéed in brown butter was disappointing . Not bad, but def wouldn't order again.

In a nutshell, service was on point and appreciated . Ambiance was good for a Friday night when you wanna kick back, slam your first few drinks and get a buzz on and forget your stressful work week . For a midweek date night? Probably not.  Dinner with friends here would be fine anytime .
Something to add is for an upscale restaurant in NYC , it leaves a bad taste in your mouth when you go to the ladies room before your dinner , and stop there after your dinner and there is still no toilet paper in the restroom even after telling the hostess .
   Im far from being high maintenance . In the sense that I don't necessarily need a bathroom attendant to give me soap and wrap the door handle in fresh paper before touching it after having an amazing meal in manhattan and spending the usual $200ish on the meal for two... But toilet paper ? Come on ... Def needs some fine tuning . But give it a try. After all, it is a "torrisi" restaurant .

Only rarely am I inspired to write a review on Yelp. Last night's dinner at Dirty French was one such occasion.  I'll keep it simple -- the gratis flatbread with fromage blanc was AMAZING. The Roasted Clams were AMAZING. I have never eaten clams with so much flavor and such a unique, delicious flavor. The nuts complement the clams beautifully.  The Brook Trout with dried sesame and apricots was not just AMAZING, it was actually the best fish I've ever tasted.  I woke up this morning planning my next visit. I hope I can get a reservation.

The flat bread was sensational, best that I have had.  The appetizers were very good, baked clams and lamb carpacio were both winners.  As for main courses, the chicken for two was also very nice.  The duck however was a major disappointment.  I am a huge duck fan and this was just not very good.  The fat wasn't rendered and the skin was inedible.  No sauce at all to accompany the duck.  Haricot vert were ovewhelmend with spices.

Unique and innovative. This clubby warm bistro elevates dining to a new level far above other destination hot spots offering Brussels sprouts with crisp pancetta or pork belly sliders with Asian slaw. The lowly chicken is turned into magic, served for two with razor thin crepes, wine reduction, herbs, Chilis and radishes followed by a thigh and leg in a perfect confit. The grilled oysters with garlic and pesto should be the last thing you eat before the asteroid strikes the Earth. All the culinary wonders are served by a relaxed, engaging top professional staff. 
Best of luck getting a table at this home run spot but definitely worth the effort and not to  be missed by rational adults.

This space is really trying, but this was the most disappointing meal I've had in the last year in New York City. Running the line between trendy, and upscale the decor and staff seem confused, Our waiter tried to push on our group of 4 a 50 ounce côte de boeuf for $214, the chicken for two $72, four side dishes all $10 a piece and oysters MP. 

That's all great and fine if you have extreme appetites and the food is delicious, but the food was offensive. 
The Chèvre salade which used kale as the greens had about three crumbles of decent goat cheese, and was so over salted you could not taste the ingredients whatsoever. Kale is a beautiful flavor when prepared correctly, but it is also particularly hard to cover up and this salad achieved that in an unwanted. 
The two guests accompanying my husband and I had ordered the chicken and I may be mistaken but I believe that this should be a stand out dish at any restaurant who presents themselves as French. The over presentation with the "crêpes" may be pulling away from the focus on the preparation of the actual chicken, and to me  a roast chicken dish should not need sauces and pickled peppers to accompany it when juicy, properly seasoned with crisped skin. 
My poisson (Black Bass) dish was the same story -  so over oiled and sauced that you could not even taste the fish. 
The largest sin being the pommes frites.... offensive to anyone who has indulged in french fries from even McDonalds. 
The best part of the dinner was the bread and fromage blanc brought to the table at the beginning of the meal, that should say something about the rest of the meal. 

Don't even get me started on the website layout, and theme..............

I have been fortunate to travel all over and have experienced some of the best restaurants in the world. This is my new favorite. I have never tasted chicken so beautiful. Not only was the skin crispy but the meat literally melts in your mouth. The sauces and the seasonings are mind blowing. We also had a phenomenal steak and clams lightly cooked to perfection. The atmosphere, service, presentation are the best I have ever seen. This is a restaurant I will want to go back to time and time again. If I could, I would give it six stars.

Really yummy and great atmosphere. We waiting a little bit to sit down, even though we had a reservation, but the service was good and the food was tasty. The sides, green beans and potatoes were great. The bread...yummy!! Would definitely go back.

seriously amazing!!! must go!! 

Absolutely love this place and im a NY resident and a big foodie
The fresh bread they bring you is to die for. Had 3 of them

The lamb tartare with figs is amazing and the seabass baked in parchment paper with preserved butternut squash and the duck yummmmmm

definitey coming back!!

We came on a Saturday night and it was very crowded so I almost opted to go to another restaurant.  I just don't like packed restaurants and especially ones that have just opened.  The food was AMAZING. One of the best meals I have had in NYC and the wine steward recommended a $180 bottle of wine and we said something less expensive.  He recommended a bottle that was $78 and it was great-3 bottles later!
The only thing I think they need to work on is making people feel special.  One of the owners was there and was watching over the place but never made a personal attempt to meet anyone. There is a disconnect.  I recently dined in Austin and the chef came out of the kitchen and visited with the guest.  It was a nice touch.
One of the guest at dinner was a pastry chef at a top NYC restaurant.  She loved the desserts and she is very picky!

Dirty French as I experienced it on Tuesday night is a Cryin' Shame. The concept has so much potential. The execution disappoints on so many levels. Food over-flavored and then some. Service lacks the graciousness for which good French brasseries are famous.  Conception of dishes is unpleasant in its attempt to surprise you. Blackened spiced-up everything sort of deal. Are the main ingredients high quality? No clue. Couldn't taste 'em. 

There are huuuge service flourishes. Paper cut off a cooked fish!!!! Oysters you didn't order proffered at your table!!! ... and yet both entrées and dessert were late. These flourishes are rendered more hilarious since they haven't really gotten the tight layout right yet so you have an extreme closeup of a waiter's rear as he tries to speed up the paper- unveiling of your neighbor's fish. Tables all around us were leaving quantities of food uneaten. "Bouillabaisse Noire" ($39) was great for two bites and then your palate tires of the strong flavors. My dinner partner ordered Steak au Poivre ($37(?)) and was unimpressed by both the cut and the flavoring. 

The flat bread they bring everyone to start is great. To get an idea, just go to your local Indian resto and order out fresh Naan bread. Get some fromage blanc from Whole Foods and heat it up. There you go. I also liked the Haricots Asiatiques, but we had trouble finishing them since they were so greasy and heavily spiced. How do you make me tire of haricots verts?! 

For all this, the wait staff was stressed AND late. Called to try to get a certain reservation pushed back 15 min and  was turned down. 15-45 min after we arrived, there were still empty tables all over the room. The lovely female maitre d' wearing that black Halo dress everyone has and so so much eyeliner looked to be in the throes of some crisis the entire time we were there. Calm down everyone! 

Best thing here is the people watching, not least for the staff who are just trying. so. hard. The dining crowd is both Hipsters and overdressed European tourists. Have a drink and and those potato things at the bar.  

I will check back in with this restaurant because I like the idea. I hope they can work their deal out. For now just smudge your black kohl eyeliner and go to Balthazar or Cafe Luxembourg instead. :)

Food was killer. Whatever that bread was that you start with was unreal, had several salads to share with four people and then had the Bouillabaisse Noire, which I think of very frequently with fervent affection. Service was also great. Did NOT think the price was too high for what you get. Overall highly recommend. And also really enj

Everything I had here was great and the service was really good - we sat at the bar (didn't have a reservation) so I think we evaded all of the service-related issues other people were experiencing in other reviews.  It was probably one of the best bar dining experiences I've had... their "frites" are quite nice/unique, the bread was amazing but would probably kill me if I ate it all, and we got a light meal of tuna tartare and salmon with blackened seasoning (was a little over-seasoned, but not a big deal).

The other thing that was impressive was the service.. the bartender was very attentive, personable, making good suggestions for us.. I liked the napkin/placemat thing that was set up so it seemed more like a real meal than just bar food, the food came out quickly, and I didn't feel like other patrons were lunging over me for drinks.  All in all, a good experience, I'd try coming back for table service (with a reservation).  I'll have to come on pay day, though - the prices are unusually high ($16 cocktails... the above-mentioned meal was around $105--for "bar food"!)

Definitely exceeded my expectations, I just hope they can fix whatever problems other people seem to be complaining about.  If my table experience is as good as this time I'll probably re-rate this 5 stars.

Pros: food was amaze, especially the steak au poivre. After finishing that dish, felt like I never wanted to eat anything else again. EVERYTHING WE ORDERED WAS A HIT, cept maybe the chocolate fondant cake, which was mediocre. 

We ordered steak au poivre - like juicy butter
pomme frites
grilled large oysters - lots of herbs, buttery, briny and delicious
clam almondine
foie gras terrine - not like regular terrine, almost had texture of seared foie gras but wrapped in a delicious thin flaky blanket in log form. YUMMM

cons: waited 30 minutes after my already late 10PM resy, had to keep asking for water refills, slightly inattentive staff. I don't hate waiting but at least check in or something to update us on the time to show some acknowledgement. 

Food was great but overall experience could have been way better.
Service horrible. Food awful. The only thing you should eat is the free bread, which is amazing. Definitely run away if you still having time! Overhyped for sure

I liked this place! Great drinks and we had a good meal. Got the chicken, which was delicious - such a wonderful spread, though agree with all the other reviewers that say the crepes dry out if you don't eat them immediately. And also had the clams almandine which were great, though a few were sandy. For dessert, we got the snowball - a very playful dessert that showed up looking like a pink snowball...but the texture was amazing! Our waitress was very good, though service was a bit aloof. Loved the concept and would come back again.

The moment I stepped into the sexy, intimate space, I loved Dirty French. We were seated at a tiny corner table, but we didn't mind. As newly weds, it was a good excuse to cuddle up to each other. 

We were pressented with the cocktail list and I know that Carbone, and Torrisi know a thing or two about good cocktails so I had to try one. The Zaragoza sounded a bit bizarre to be honest: tequilla, vanilla yogurt, creme de peche, fresh lime and clove. But it was incredible. The yogurt gave it a creaminess that cut right through the tequila and was perfect. So good in fact that I had more than one! 

Then, the most incredible bread arrived to our table. We devoured it and really enjoyed the ricotta dip it came with. As others have said, it's very similar to a naan that you'd find at an Indian restaurant. 

To start we shared the tuna tartare. It had great flavor and came with crepe. I loved smothering tuna onto the crepe. Very fresh! 

The chicken and crepes for two was outstanding. One of the best dishes I've had in recent memory. It was huge and four people could easily share this dish and maybe two apps and one other mains. It came out in a cash iron and was in a rich honey mustard gravy. The legs and thighs came out a few minutes later and had a char and Asian glaze. It also came with perfectly thin crepes. We rolled up the chicken with thai basil, peppers and the crepe and it all was so harmonious! 

We were so full but I really wanted to try dessert. Unfortunately they were out of the apple tart tatin, but we shared the beignets and they were fabulous. Warm, puffy and covered with powdered sugar, just as they should be. Cannot wait to return!

Excellent wine and ambiance but the food didn't totally do it for me.  That said, the mushroom "millefueille" was ingenious and delicious, flatbread also very good... will probably end up giving this another try....

I am a fan of some of the Carbone/Torrisi restaurants, particularly Parm and Torrisi Italian, so I was looking forward to Dirty French.  Unfortunately the food was not up to the standard of either of the other two, not even Carbone.  Both of my dishes -- clams (chewy greasy)  and the lamb were greasy.  My companion's trout was good, but the kale salad tough. The lemon preserve dessert, not very interesting.  Otherwise the service was good, the atmosphere and décor, excellent.  Too bad about the food.

Dirty French is definitely a cool place to be these days.  From the difficult reservations to the dark ambiance and music, it's everything that gets New Yorkers excited.  The food wasn't too bad either--the stars of the show were definitely the flat bread (which just so happens to be the best complimentary bread you'll ever have at a restaurant), the grilled oysters (in the style of escargots), and the chicken.  Some of the appetizers were tasty and had interesting twists (like the spicing on the lamp carpaccio and the pasty wrapped foie gras).  The much hyped steak, the côte de bœuf, while tasty, is priced in the stratosphere--about $250 for a 42 oz steak is a little much.  Though it was executed well, there are others out there that are comparable and a fraction of the cost (e.g. Minetta).  The cocktails are definitely on better end of restaurant cocktails (and make me miss ZZ's Clam Bar).  All in all, this is a great spot if you order correctly and/or utilize an expense account.
Awful not even a french restaurant and very dirty for sure...steak au piovre was very hard,  service sucks waited for 40 mins to get our order.. Area is cool but there are better choices in that hood

halfway through our apps I was already planning and looking forward my next time here! started with the lamb carpaccio and millefeuille and the foie gras terrine.  all three were amazing.  for our mains we split the chicken and crepes and the short rib.   the chicken was served two ways - both were good but the legs were definitely my favorite.   the short rib had a taste similar to Katz's pastrami.  dessert was the tart and beignets.   we had 5 ppl at our table and we all left so full.   oh the bread! so soft and flavorful.   it was like a thick naan kind of flatbread.    so chewy.   can't wait to go back...

Been here for the first time on friday and really enjoyed it! The complimentary flat bread with ricotta is divine!!! The drinks were very good and the service was great.The lamb carpaccio was amazing!  We also had the duck which was nothing special, the tuna tartar tasty but so spicy I couldn't handle... 
Overall was a great experience!

I've been eating out a lot these days and for some reason have been having some subpar + $$$ meals of late. The worst combination.  Luckily a visit to Dirty French broke that streak!

The interior is what I would describe as Moulin Rouge on a sedative. It's got some glitzy furnishings but somehow you get a very laid back vibe. Unexpectedly soothing. Dimly lit (I was there for dinner).

Went with a party of 4 total.  We ordered: 
Apps: Foie Gras, Mille Feuille and Lamb Tartare - personally I am not into foie gras nor lamb but the others LOVED it.  Mille Feuille was actually slivered layers of mushrooms in a curry sauce - so good.
Main:  Steak Poivre (which is actually something more like short ribs), the controversial Chicken for 2 - The steak was a favorite of everyone hands down. MUST TRY.  Chicken for 2 was also very good but I just wanted less sauce but overall it's definitely a strong dish.  The charred chicken pieces were my fave (over the pieces in the saucepan in the sauce).
Sides: french fries that don't look like french fries but delicious crispy smashies and the haricot vert.

General consensus was that the meal overal was just a TAD too salty but the flavors were just so strong that we overlooked it.  

Total bill (for 4 ppl with the above + 2 desserts + drinks) = $80pp

I can see why it's popular of late but i'm glad that they actually serve good food to boot.

Sometimes a place gets totally hyped up, you go, and it disappoints. I work in the restaurant business so I get that sometimes places have off nights. Well the night I went with my dear friend and business partner for dinner at Dirty French we were  impressed. We both had great cocktails (forgot the name of it), but essentially their margarita which had a  rim made up of delicate salt crystals. 

Our server was lovely, and sweet, not pushy in any way. As much as I try to keep eating bread to a minimum it's a little hard when you're presented with fresh fluffy and light flat bread topped with fine herbs and fresh cheese and olive oil. Yep, that pretty much got all eaten up. We debated what to get for dinner, but I think we made some right choices. We got oysters (delicious), the crudite salad which was on point and refreshing. The tuna tartar which was good, but I would insist one gets. The Lamb saddle (yes!) and the fries. Dear lord, the fries. A MUST! 

Place was lively, the music made us smile the whole night and made us nostalgic. We skipped out on dessert, but we were tempted. 

I look forward to returning.

Very enjoyable dinner for four last night. Enjoyable ambiance in the Ludlow Hotel. Staff was friendly. Matra di guided us through the wine list and picked a reasonable one with the moderate mark up. 

Breads were amazing with a side of humus. I had the trout, which was excellent. Perfectly grilled and not much seasoning. Really got the flavor of the fish. Sides of bacon was thick and satisfying.

Deafeningly loud, utterly pretentious and awful. I reviewed this restaurant last week when I went there, and when I saw that the NY Times had given it a positive review, I felt it necessary to edit and expand on my original review to warn the unwary public. 
A credit card was required for the reservation, with a threatened $50 cancellation fee, yet upon arrival at the appointed time, our party of 4 was made to wait for 30 minutes without apology. Perhaps they should have offered a $50 credit to the bill for the inconvenience? We waited at first in the adjacent hotel bar, asking the hostess to alert us when the table was ready, but this level of customer service seemed to be above what they were capable of offering, and we had to migrate over to the maitre d' podium to press our case of being eventually seated. 
So. Damn. Loud. Not just hard surfaces everywhere, but bad 80's music pumped in at concert level. You cannot carry on a conversation. I don't mind a bit of buzz but this is ridiculous. 
The absurdly pretentious "Sommelier" approached with the wine list. Our waitress took our order (repeated several times due to necessity to shout). When it became apparent that we weren't ordering an important bottle and multiple a la carte items, the service level dropped perceptibly and our waitress spent her time at other tables. 
They did deliver the flatbread, delicious as described. We should have stopped there. 
3 of us ordered steak au poivre, one ordered the scallops. The scallops were reportedly OK but not great. The steaks were extremely greasy and tasted odd, not of beef, which made me seriously wonder if it was horse meat. I do not recall ever eating a greasier steak in my life. Disgusting, and at this point we just wanted to leave. A predictable hassle tracking down the missing waitress to obtain the bill. 
I would put this place in the category of a total "scene" restaurant, like Lucky Cheng's. If you need others to notice that you're someplace trendy, come here. If you want good food, go elsewhere.

It amazes me how restaurants like this provide a reservation and then give it away.  My wife and I needed to come to LES for work and booked a room at the hotel and made dinner reservations.  When we checked to confirm we were told they would not accommodate us leaving us in disbelief.  Do not trust this place!

Dirty French has been on my radar for a Fashionplate for a while- Mediterranean french cuisine on the lower east side in the cool Ludlow Hotel, sign me up! We had reservations on the weekend at Dirty French and were surprisingly seated pretty quickly, we had heard before the wait was long.  Dirty French in the Ludlow Hotel and has a cool, fun and eclectic vibe.  I am a lover of all things hot pink and want the black and hot pink curtains for my apartment as well as the hot pink rooster ceramics.  We were seated a great table for four and started of with some cocktails and half a dozen raw oysters and half a dozen broiled oysters.  OMG I am definitely coming back for the broiled oysters, seriously beyond amazing.  The roasted clams were good but nothing could touch those broiled oysters in the herb infused buttery goodness.  We also had the Millefeuille, which was an amazing delicate mushroom dish with a green curry sauce, it  was outstanding. At this point we switched to a great Pinot Nior that made my night. The crudite salad was also great.  For a main I split the duck l'orange and a side of haricots, which were perfection.  The steak was also great we heard from our other dining companions.  We then indulged in the delicious tarte tartin which was an amazing end to a wonderful meal.

I want to be completely fair and start by saying that I was 20 minutes late for our reservation.

However, that does NOT in any way, shape or form justify the service we received during the meal.

This was my holiday dinner with my 2 reps, and I intended to give them a lovely, stress-free evening at a new restaurant with a mounting reputation. Instead, we got the complete opposite.

I have never felt so rushed at a restaurant in my life. I understand that they need to turn the table, however there is no justification for literally telling the people seated that they do indeed have other people coming in after us and we needed to move things along.

This waiter should not be waiting tables, as this is customer service 101. He was also very sure to point out that the reservation was at 6pm- yes, as I said before, I was late. But alas, he felt the need to point that out to me once again. 

I just want to say that this is not the service one expects to receive at a two star restaurant (or any restaurant, for that matter.) I wanted to show appreciation to the people working with me and relax with them for an evening... Instead all we felt was pressure to get out as quickly as possible,

This one really burns... Shouldn't happen, especially not in NYC. Our evening was basically ruined as we were all in a pretty bad mood because of this. And you can imagine how pissed I was to drop over $400 for this service.

I'm not even going to say anything about the food, as I've already spent as much time on this review as they gave me to have my meal.

Luckily I work in the restaurant industry and I will be sure this gets around.

Delicious meal! Went here with my sister and two other friends last night. Very crowded and noisy inside, but I don't mind that. The service was excellent. Very attentive, but not annoying. Noticed every detail and took care of things right away (a little water spilled for example, and was promptly cleaned up within seconds). The sommelier recommended an excellent wine that went so perfectly with all the dishes, i drank every glass that was poured and I'm not even a wine fan, so that's gotta be saying something. In terms of what we ordred, we had the lamb carpaccio, the boudin, the cote de boeuf, the chicken and crepes, the bacon d'hotel, the pommes frites and champignons. Every dish was soo damn good. Even had a glass of hibiki on the rocks to top it off.  All that and two bottles of wine, bill came in at a little over 600$ and worth every bit. Will be back next time i'm on the east coast.

I have been sitting here for at least a few minutes debating whether to go with 4 or 5 stars for Dirty French, after really thinking about it, the only negative that I can come up with is the price, but I knew that going in so how can I judge them negatively on that. The Torrisi Group in NYC has been taking over the restaurant scene with their beautiful over-the-top high end restaurants and Dirty French is no exception. The space is beautiful and similar to how others have described it, it's very Moulin Rouge with some weird mannequin heads on the shelf. 

We had a 6:00 pm reservation on a Friday night, we were sat immediately at a nice round table, there were 3 of us. The reason that I made the reservation at 6 pm was that on the menu there is a rotisserie section where they put their lamb saddle, the duck, the chicken, and the steak. There are only limited quantities of these offered each night, so when they are gone they are gone. If you make a later reservation you run the risk of them being out of multiple things by the time you get there, so keep that in mind. 

We of course started off with the flat bread and the whipped cheese that comes with it and man that flatbread is pretty much the best that I have ever had, it is ridiculously good and we tried not to eat our weight in it to save room. 

We started off with a dozen of the broiled oysters, they were awesome, they were Dirty French's take on a Oysters Rockefeller, at $24 for 6 they were pricey but the oysters were huge and just super awesome. We then did the Tuna Tartare, again this was just awesome, it had the perfect amount of heat and was just super well prepared and balanced. 

For entrees we went with the short ribs which were amazingly cook but yes the portion size is small, it comes with a few pickle spears and this feels like Torrisi's take on Jewish pastrami and pickles to me. We also did the Sea Bass that came with clams in a holy basil pistou sauce. The presentation of this dish is just over-the-top amazing. The fish and vegetables are all steamed in a rice paper dome. The dish is served at the table with the dome intact. The Server then cuts the dome open in front of you and rolls back the rice paper and tops it with the basil sauce at the table. Totally awesome and the fish was perfectly cooked and it was a very nice light dish. The lamb saddle was a huge portion, way more than I thought it would be but I mean all of this in a good way. It comes with potatoes au gratin. The lamb was exquisite, it was beyond perfectly cooked and unbelievably juicy I don't know how they did it but I would like to know. We also did a few sides, the mashed potatoes and the mushrooms, both were $10 a piece. They were quite small portions so we would definitely not order the potatoes again but the mushrooms were literally one of the best things at the table, we were fighting over them. 

At the end we had to decide on dessert, we got some, we went with the Napoleon and the Chocolate Ganache Cake. Both were again amazing, the Napoleon was very light and airy and a very nice end to the dinner for me. The cake looked super rich and heavy but was not nearly so which was a pleasant surprise, the pistachio ice cream is came with was a perfect pairing. 

We also indulged quite a bit with the cocktails which were adequately priced at about $14 per drink. As you can see, we ate and drank a lot and the bill came out to about $150 per person with tip included, which is very expensive but not over the top so just be prepared if you want to go all out you are going to spend some cash.

Torrisi bro's done it again !!!! Blasting it's way through LES is brilliant way to go ! Be bold or be gone !! If people are complaining about this place being pretentious then they must from outta town or they just don't get it. After a year of carbone and zZ clam bar one should know what to expect walking into a torrisi joint, if you don't then you deserve one star for being a dumbA&@S. Same concept here~oldies but goodies, blasting 80's music that forever changed lives ! Nothing wrong with that ! Usually people that need a lot of attention needs peace and quiet...go to Daniel and have a spoon up your &@%#. Now to the food~Explosive Flavors ! Yes ! had the baked clams (carbone's better) MilleFeuille which I loved. lamb carpaccio~delicious, foie gras~mmmmm. Seafood bouillabaisse, Chicken for 2 which is beautifully presented and delicious also, accompanied with crepes, trio of sauces & herbs. Blows Nomad's truffle chicken out of town. And lastly the Mighty 60 day aged cote de boeuf ! Accompanied with Fried leeks, smooth & buttery Béarnaise sauce and what ?!?! Dry aged beef FAT mushroom carpaccio. Put it all together and you have one of the cockiest dish in NYC ! Served in a massive concoction and presented to us made it more over the top... I mean why not, for $160 rib steak~it better be. As we all know zZ clam bar has the best cocktails in NYC so here is nothing less then amazing also. Dirty's cock hold its own but without the fancy presentation like zZ's. Atmosphere is radiated by the gigantic bulbed mirror which I love !!! Shining brightest amongst the hip crowd. Service is a bit lacking but with Dirty's atmosphere I don't think it's end of the world, unlike carbone a bad waiter can ruin your whole night. For dessert we had a excellent lemon tart & sorbet trio (guava, coconut & passion fruit) which are both nice palate cleansers, and the Napoleon which is the best dessert I had this year, move aside lady M. Tartin don't really care for. After a year of underwhelming new restaurants, I can honestly say dirty French is nothing short of extraordinary and I can't wait to be back to try everything on that damn miraculous foodgasmic menu.

Just so everyone knows, when I read the words "Dirty French" in my head, they are automatically sung the same way Justin Timberlake says "Dirty Pop" way back from his *NSYNC days. I have no idea why or how or what the hell. It just is. And now I bet it's that way for you, too. Yeah, you're welcome.

Anyway. Dirty French. (Mm-hmm. Told you.) The trendy, new-ish restaurant in the Ludlow Hotel that is about as tough to pin down as one of Stefon's nightlife recommendations on SNL. Think Tarantino remaking Moulin Rogue, but set in the Dirty Dancing version of the Catskills. Subtle this place is not. So, let's start with the food, before my brain starts hurting all over again.

The complementary flatbread is no joke. In fact, it may be the best I've ever had, thanks to its light, puffed pita-like nature and the outstanding sidecar of creme fraiche. It's amazing something this delicious is actually free. The Lamb Carpaccio is a popular (and understandably not free) starter. The employment of cumin, figs, eggplant, and yogurt suggested more of a Moroccan influence than traditional French, but savory and satisfying all the same.

When it comes to main courses, be forewarned about the Meunière, however. It's covered - and I mean covered! - in sesame seeds. It's also drenched in butter, but that suddenly takes a backseat to said seeds. After my first bite, I really didn't know how this was gonna pan out, but I gotta tell you, I started to really enjoy what Dirty French was doing with trout here. For what I initially mistook for a light fish dish was really something heavier, a rich mix of oily and nutty. And I actually kinda crave it just thinking about it. Credit to the chef for a no-holds barred, bold approach to something that could've been super bland. Knowing full well there's more of the menu to explore, I'd probably still order this one all over again.

I had some trouble with the cocktail list, to be honest. I found a ton of great ingredients that are typically trigger words for me, but the trouble is, they all appeared in different drinks, and I never got around to sampling any one that hit the spot. Maybe you'll have better luck in that department than I did. I was perfectly happy shoveling trout in my mouth, to be honest, so no harm, no foul.

And now we return to the decor. I still can't decide if the hot pink accents (cursive neon name out front, painted roosters on shelves, etc.) are off-putting or appropriate. The place has a bit of an '80s-excess-meets-backstage-cabaret vibe, like I said earlier in more pop-culture-y terms. And it's also sorta casual and sorta expensive at the same time? That, and if it weren't for the food, you'd hardly know this place was a French restaurant. It's a caricature. Of what, I'm not so sure. But it would appear they have the same attitude towards decor as they do their dishes - that is, go big or go home. It just happens to be a hell of a lot more convincing in their food.

Anyway. Take it away, JT...

Dirty French!

Sometimes its worth splurging once in a blue moon on a special meal. Everything we ate at Dirty French was insanely delicious. We shared the scallops, short ribs entrees potato souffle side and mushroom with green curry and tuna tartar appetizer. The short ribs were covered with some sort of delicious rub and the scallop dish was particularly unique. Check out the mushroom dish that was apparently baked with a crispy exterior and the creamiest heart attack inducing Joel Robichon recipe potatoes that you will ever eat. Everything including the Gaverztamener and the chocolate dessert were top notch. The best meal that I've eaten in NYC in a long long time.
I just don't get it. Mushy trout. Insipid bass with rubbery clams. The curry mushroom was great, but did not save the day. Hope you have better luck.

So, Dirty French, you just get 3 stars.  Your food would be 4-star quality, but being constantly accosted by several servers every 5 minutes made the circumstances super annoying.  We arrived early for our rez, we had a drink at the bar, and then sat on time.  You acted like we were 45 minutes late and that there was someone waiting to sit at our specific table.  It wasn't pleasant.  Felt hurried.   Sorry, for a $220 bill for 2 people with a $62 bottle of wine, apps, 2 entrees, and 2 desserts, I don't think you should be rushing people.  It's rude and we weren't even there for 2 hours.  Between our dessert and bill, we had no less than 5 people hovering over us.  Every few minutes, someone would walk by and ask if we were done. NO! It's a sampler and a selection of beignets.  Perhaps they have never been to France where a meal isn't a sprint and a relaxing experience?  This isn't a pre-theater meal, folks.
Had the crudite salad, duck a l'orange, and the glace sampler and beignets.  Food was good but not the best duck that I've ever had.  Just ok.  The short ribs that my dining companion had looked great, but again, it wasn't life-changing.  
The final straw for me really was when we got up... and the older man shoved himself into one of our empty seats before the table was even cleared, as the server had leaned over to tell them they could move to our spot.  Seriously?  Control the situation already and don't make it so uncomfortable.  Mentioned it to the manager, she seemed mildly apathetic about the whole thing, although quite nice.   Not that impressed truthfully, but maybe it was an off night.

I've always wanted to try this place but as previous reviews mention it's hard to make reservations. I was really surprised when I got there and I saw a lot of empty tables.
Anyways, overall I really like the vibe of this restaurant, especially because it's located in the Ludlow hotel, they play loud music from the 80s which our entire party enjoyed very much.

Food wise, I have to agree with previous reviews, the portion sizes are for starving people, thank god we ordered a couple of servings of the complimentary bread - it's really amazing! 5 stars for the bread although I was surprised to find an Indian bread at this venue.

Lamb carpaccio - a must try, very interesting
Mushroom millefeuille - very creative dish, please try it! 
Kale salad - whatever

Our mains is where my criticism starts. The duck a l'orange was way too sweet and its presentation sloppy, so was the steak. I was really disappointed with portion size and presentation, the dishes were very bland.

Dessert wise I had high expectations because I usually love desserts but I didn't particularly enjoy the tarte tatin. It tasted a bit boring and chewy. I like when the tarte tatin still has some "crisp" to the dough.

I ordered a cocktail that they didn't have but they said they would try to make it (yay) only to realize that they aren't even capable of making good drinks. The waiter brought my drink to the table when I was in the bathroom and never checked with me if I liked it. Don't tell me "we don't have it but I can see if we make it" and then serve me something else and don't check in with me.

However, I think I will go back to try more dishes. Overall ambiance is "fun" and it makes it a perfect spot to go before going out on.

I went there the first night it opened during this past Fashion Week. 

Pros: The ambiance is killer. Perfection. The lighting and decor, everything. The cocktails, preferably the planters punch is top notch, right down to the glassware it is served in. The food is also amazing! I mean, Carbone and Torrisi have the best restaurants in the city, so you're safe. I haven't had the the chicken for two, but planning on getting it when I go back soon! I heard it's the best thing on the menu.

Cons: It was opening night, I get it. But it did take long to be seated once we arrived at our slated  reservation time.

The Chicken & Crepes Pour Deux is possibly the best-cooked chicken I've ever had at a restaurant. 2 different preps in one, the leg confit complete with goth clawed  feet. The softest and juiciest chicken breast served in a cast-iron skillet with really delicious crepes on the sides. Perfection -- except for the super rich creamy sauce that is way too mustardy. I didn't feel with the accompaniments served alongside (fresh tarragon, basil, mint, tamarind paste, hot pepper and radish slices, etc) went so harmoniously with the chicken and ended up using them on the duck confit that my husband ordered. Said duck was good but kinda chewy....
The outlandish, almost phantasmagory green trumpet mushroom millefeuille in curry was probably my most favorite taste of the night -- but, again, just a bit too rich.... Lamb carpaccio tasted like it had all ingredients for greatness that just refused to work together, probably demotivated by cumin's leadership.
The Foi-gras Terrine, Broccoli Gratin, and Bacon d'Hotel = good but I found them underwhelming for how much they are trying and charging for their efforts.
Desserts: The sorbet trio is 2/3 wonderful - but the passionfruit third gots to go...   The coconut + something Napoleon was great. 
The service is perfect. And I think I can learn to live with a $50 pp cancelation fee if it means that you don't have to wait for your table and don't have to wait for your entire party to arrive to be seated. I liked that. 

BOTTOM LINE:
Expensive!!!
Inventive to the point of something is a bit off (both dishes and decor)
Delicious, masterful, yet too rich (to the point mild nausea on the way home)
Am I dying to go back any time soon? -- Not really.

While it's next to impossible to snag a decent dinner reservation time here on a weekend, I settled for a 4:30pm slot on New Year's Day for a late "lunch" which turned out to be perfect after being up all night celebrating. 

My best gal and I kept it simple: fresh oyster appetizer, chicken and crêpes, side of pommes frites, Napolean desert. 

Verdict? One of my favorite meals this past year. When the customary  complimentary flatbread and whipped cheese is hands down the best you've had, you know you're in for a treat. The crêpes are fun, and the pommes frites with smokey bacon (?) dip made me gasp with delight.

I'll definitely be back and bringing more friends with me.

The complimentary flatbread is a delicious as everyone has already said (oh god, it was sooooooooooooooo good) as was the mushroom mille-feullie...however, the whole experience was a little overwrought and surprisingly fussy.  And super-expensive.  Like, no shit expensive.  Like I won't bother going back expensive.

Food 4
Service 4
Ambiance 4
O/all 4

Things to note:
1/ ambiance is like moulin rouge
2/ service is attentive but our waiter was a bit awkward
3/ the price point is a bit high, think 15-20 apps and salads, with mains 25-35
4/ portion sizes on the smaller end
5/ food is mainly a hit with a few misses--best beet salad i have ever had, scallops were good, oysters had tasty condiments, pass on the mushroom mille feuille
6/ the complimentary bread and chesse was super tasty

Was the food good, generally it was.  Was it worth it, not quite but worth one try.  More of a biz lunch and dinner place, or like a 3rd date to impress a girl.

We had a vey lovely experience here (brought my family for my dad's birthday) the waitstaff was extremely pleasant and knowledgeable about the menu. They do have wine specialists obviously very knowledgable about the wine selection. We were able to pick a wine that satisfied everyone at the table which was awesome, she also wrote down the wine for us.... So great!

Although the food wasn't quite what we expected. My mother tried the monkfish while although was delicious, was only a piece of fish in a light vegetable curry. The dish needed something more, i.e. vegetable / rice. I tried the lamb which was cooked with care, the fat was rendered down nicely, perfectly cooked medium rare, very salty though.

We finished with the beignets served with a Carmel sauce... Literally to die for... I was definitely the one scraping the last of the Carmel sauce from the dish.

Overall the atmosphere is undeniably delightful. I would definitely return for drinks and dessert. Dinner was overpriced for what it was.

There are many reasons to go to Dirty French.  But, without question, the main reason is the Chicken & Crepes Pour Deux.  We order chicken at the best spots in the city (and sometimes special order it at places like Danielle)--without question, Dirty French has the best chicken in the City.  

The rest of the meal is also great.  The mushroom millefeuille is different and fantastic.  The desserts are great, especially the beignets (although a bit too much rose water) with carmel.  

It is great to have fantastic food in a relaxed atmosphere.  It is no wonder this is one of the hottest spots in the City right now -- and for once, the food lived up to the hype.
Great meal. Super nice staff. Loved the trumpet millfeuille, clams, duck, lamb and lemon tart. Highly recommend.

I only had drinks there but my friend had bunch of food (see pics uploaded). I had a bite of everything and I wouldn't say I love the food. They are decent, and nicely presented. The drinks were great. And the top-notch service just blew my mind. We sat at the bar and there was only 2 bartenders. However, he paid attention to us all the time and when the food comes, he came out of the bar and served us from behind. I think outstanding service like this will definitely make me want to come back, even their food was just ok. Maybe I will try different dishes next time.

I enjoyed the trendy Dirty French restaurant, it is a great ambiance with 80's vegas vibe which is chic and trashy at the same time. The menu goes with the vibe of the restaurant, a fusion of flavors and ingredients. The chicken for two is a must, they serve it on a lovely platter for you and your guest. Now that they are serving Breakfast, I will have to check them out! Overall a fun dining experience with good to great food.

It is actually my favorite restaurant right now in the city. 
I love the location, the service, the decoration, the 80's music and the drinks 
The food is to died for. To start the oysters, the roasted clams, the fresh ham and the boudin 
For main course I have tried almost everything and I don't have any complains. The boulangere (lamb), the duck al orange and the short rib are a must try

And for dessert all are great and incredibly tasty. My favorite is the coconut, guava, passion fruit it is just too hard to describe you just have to try 

Also, if you finish dinner and want to stay for another drink not a problem they have a great bar at the back with a nice indoors garden

Love this place!!! Well done
Overseasoned, over the top food. Clashing flavors galore. Unappetizing. Totally disappointed.

Major Food Group puts out solid restaurants.  Everyone in NYC knows this.  Dirty French lives up to the hype.

First: The bartenders there are insanely talented, and Thomas Waugh's drinks are worth taking a cab to the LES to try.

Second:  The food is delicious, and insanely well presented.

Third:  Management is very present and attentive.  That ship is being run very well.

Go and check it out.

Step inside the budoir like room of Dirty French where the Major Food Group succeeds in dishing dirty delicious French and North African fare. Same corporate dull service as Parm, but the food here is not inspired by nostalgia, but by INNOVATION. 
The much heralded warm flat bread with herby cows milk cheese is worth the hype. I went with the black bass en papilote- while I tasted no clams the flavor of the pistou was erotic & EXOTIC. The cabbage baked in the oven with a green/ herby sauce was also bursting with South of France flavor. The food at Dirty French will transport you to a South of France locale, if you can get a reservation & have the francs.

This is one of the most overhyped restaurants in the city.  Spectacular name.  Great decor.  Mediocre food.  Terrible service. Way overpriced for what it is.  This trendy new spot is all hype and no substance. 

In fairness, we went for brunch so it is possible that they deliver a better dinner experience.  One if the worst brunches I have had in NYC.

We just had Brunch today for a whopping 450.00 for 3 people.  The service was so poor that we had to involve management.
