We  were ignored by the wait staff  to the point that  our meal took an hour to arrive.  Also, ala carte was impossible with NO substitution or even bread to tide us over.  After management was called upon we were offered a new waitress whom proceeded to pour 24 dollar glasses of wine with out warning us that it could be a pricey reach for a cheap tasteless variety of wine.  The worst thing was that when our meals did arrive--They were meak and tasteless.  The presentation was sloppy and the food cold!!!! ALL FOR  450.00.  If you think you need to be here--You don't!!  There are better places.  What stinks is that this was on a top ten list.  WHOM DOES ONE TRUST ANYMORE.  Sorry folks  it was disappointing.

Don't go for brunch...waited 30 minutes for food after they took our order...when it arrived it was cold and soggy.  Who puts maple syrup on your french toast for you?  We were polite...asked them to sub just the bagel because it wasn't toasted like requested.  2nd one came...same result.  By then we were done...but guess what we had to ask our waiter, bus boy and manager for our check..that took another 20 minutes.  Hope dinner is better but we won't try.  P.S only 5 tables were filled...3 servers...so it's definitely the kitchen and floor management.

Nice ambiance, but the food was totally disappointing. First they served me a $20 glass of wine which was, although from the same winemaker as the one advertised on the menu, not the same wine, nor the same vintage. It turned out to be ok but you'd think they would get it right for that price. But it doesn't end there. I ordered a kale salad, which turned out to be a watercress salad. When I pointed it out to the waitress, she claimed in utter disdain "it's a baby kale salad!" - which it wasn't -- the leaves look noticeably different not to mention that they taste noticeably different. Then, I ordered the "Steak au Poivre" which had a subtitle on the menu "Short Rib", which was a little confusing since Steak au Poivre is supposed to be filet mignon, with a Peppercorn sauce. Well, what came was neither filet mignon, nor short rib but some in between dry and overcooked type of meat. Actually, three small pieces of it, and no peppercorn sauce to be seen but rather a dry pepper rub. All three pieces looking a bit lost on a plate with no vegetables whatsoever other than the green recycled unnamed salad pieces for the decoration. Good thing we had ordered a side to go with it.

Went here for lunch with a friend yesterday. They had a lot of space available, so we were able to walk in. Our server was extremely friendly and attentive, and the bartender crafted me an off-menu (albeit sugary) mocktail to start. 

Decor was quirky, dominated by bright pink plastic hens throughout, although the main space has a traditional bistro feel.

The menu is classic French bistro- we had the roast beef au jus and the lamb burger. Both came on crusty perfect bread. The jus was excellent, and the lamb burger came with smashed fries that were perfectly made. Unfortunately it was just too much meat and fat for us to handle, and I ended up leaving half my sandwich untouched. Likewise, the trumpet mushroom millefeuille appetizer was tasty with really fresh "green" curry, but the flavor profile was entirely too one-dimensional for the size of the dish.

The complimentary flatbread starter was savory and the delicious cheese took the flavor up several notches. If they reduced their lunch portions, this would be a great mid-day spot!

Dirty French is now open for lunch! I had Lamb burger and dry aged beef sandwich to share with friend. Both dishes were just OK but flatbread was delish!! I also highly recommend you to try Grilled oysters! This dish was O.M.G. The best grilled oyster I ever had in my life! I'm just warning you it was very very garlicky if you have to go back to work after lunch! The lunchtime atmosphere was lovely *\(^_^)/* I would love to try Lamb Carpaccio from dinner menu next time.

Food was fantastic - I would recommend this place to people and I would go back. Staff was great, experience was great and the only short coming of the place is the stupid decor. Food is too refined to have nic naks randomly placed and dirty looking walls.

Another wonderful hit from the Torrisi team!  

Came on a Tuesday night and thankfully had wonderful service.  We arrived at 6:30pm and lingered until 10pm and at no point in time were we rushed by our server. 

Food was incredible - S could not stop raving about the flatbread. He loved it so much that we even asked for a second serving! 

For apps we shared the serrano ham which was amazing! The mustard sauce and grilled bread were a perfect combination.  We also had the millefuille which was very good but the ham was the real star of the apps

For entrees, I had the duck l'orange which was incredible - I would order it again and again. There were only 2 slices but the serving was generous and after the apps, it was perfectly sized.  S had the bass which was good - but I liked the duck so much more. 

Can't wait to come back and try other dishes!

I hate to classify myself as a foodie but I frequent these kinds of places often.  This fits the stereotype of overhyped restaurants.  Unfortunately, my reservation was "accidentally" cancelled by Major Food Group's reservations.  I had to show proof by having Open Table send me the cancellation made by the restaurant when I looked into the matter.  Major Food Group accomodated me by giving me a later reservation which I didn't think was the way to handle it. So I called the restaurant and spoke to the manager and he easily gave me my original reservation back.   After speaking to head of guest relations at Major Food Group I got excuses instead of really handling the matter like the manager did.  It was as if I was arguing with a child.  I asked her to call me to discuss the matter but instead I got emails saying they did not "intentionally" cancel my reservation.  Of course I know that but why do I have to get a later reservation due to their mistake.  I finally was told they were going to speak to Open Table and look into the matter.  Of course I haven't heard back.

Overall the food is typical of most foodie restaurants...over buttered, over salted and rushed to get you to order more food or to get you out of there.  I'm glad I tried it because I know in the future I can sit at the bar or patio if I'm in the area and not have to go through the bureaucracy of trying to get a reservation.  The service was typical as well.  Too many servers coming up to you to give you your food and too many servers coming up to you to take it away.  

The good news is New York City has tons of restaurants that can give you good ambiance, great food without stressing you out and annoying you about the experience.

This place was not as much of a mad house that we anticipated, especially since its the "It" restaurant now and hard to get resos.

That being said, the food in this hotel restaurant was extraordinary!

Our favorites were the gnocchi and the sole. The short ribs were also very good but a little heavy handed with salt.

Overall, the food was great and worth the moderate 30 minute wait. We would definitely wait again and we will definitely be back!

I was very excited about trying Dirty French.  On arrival, service was very good -- great drink (Dirty Water) from the bartender, who was very excited to talk about how they made their Cumin Rye, and gave me a sample pour.

The service was nice -- sommelier made a good recommendation of the Pinot Noir.  We loved our starters of oysters and the lamb carpaccio (great use of Szechuan Peppercorn).  

Unfortunately, from here....it all went downhill.  (1) The runners brought the wrong main for my friend -- sea bass en papillote instead of trout meuniere.  The waiter then left it on the table so we could "enjoy" it while he went to the kitchen for the proper dish.  We tasted the sea bass...and it was underwhelming.  Way too heavy on the citrus -- really overwhelmed the fish (2) The duck, although very tasty was the wrong temperature.  It came out luke-warm.  Excellent sauce though.  The trout meuniere was quite good.

Finally -- we opted for the "Tarte" for desert.   It was meant to be a lemon tart with merengue and Marcona almonds.  The taste was completely overwhelming and seemed almost artificial.  We barely finished half.

Even upon seeing that we hadn't finished our desert, the waiter did not enquire on wether or not we had liked it.

Overall, OK with some inspired moments.  Not a place I'm likely to return to.

Am a big fan of the group --loved Torrisi, adore Zz (hosted a birthday there), regularly get Parm. I was very excited to try Dirty French and, while not disappointed I am not sure it lives up to the rest. Flatbread and fries were wonderful -duck close behind but did not come at the right temperature. Sea bass was more exciting in presentation than taste and clams tasted way rubbery and did not work with the dish's overall texture. Trout was good but not better than a classic sole meunière at a traditional Frenchie place. Lemon tarte for dessert was a strong recommendation by the (very nice and opinionated) waiter but contained little tarte and way too much lemony artificiality (something too sweet and too tart at once). Wine was good and sommelier was very attentive. Good, but not up to what I have come to expect from the group.

We went for brunch. The service was poor. Our waiter just didn't seem to care.  Food was good overall, but inconsistent. The Tartine was simply thick toast with a tomato jam and prosciutto - which I could have made easily at home
Brunch was ok, the food is quite 'heavy'. The service was poor and uninterested (they blamed it on a busy Valentine's evening).
Chicken was epic, grilled oyster was insanely delicious as well.  Reservation was at 10 PM and wasn't seated until 10:15 PM, but food made up for it.

Having been fortunate to have eaten at Carbone, the Torrisi Bros love letter to all things purely Italian American, I was very curious to try Dirty French, and then I became extremely concerned about that, because I started to hear things like "impossible to get in, full of over trendoidy people, blah blah blah...." and found out it was in the Ludlow Hotel, and I'm ever the more dubious about HOTEL Restaurants.  Unless you've proven yourself, it's never that great.  Well....

Dirty French was absolutely fantastic.  I mean this in the most sincerely complimentary of ways, but it took me back to the 90's when Coffee Shop in Union Square was not just the place to be seen, but the eats were also top notch, and it was fantasy driven, made you feel like whether you were on the way up, or on the way down, it was the place to go, eat Moqueca, drink Cachaca and feel beautiful.  

Dirty French's concept is also unique in that, they decided to incorporate all cuisines that have French influence into a wild gumbo.  There is Morocco, New Orleans, Haiti, and Vietnam.  In the hands of someone else, this could go WILDLY WRONG and seem downright "fashion food."  It was not that in the least.

I came here for my 10 year wedding anniversary, I am married to a delicious man, and they gave us an entire booth for ourselves during the beginnings of prime time, which in their case, is...no joke....6PM onward, this place is PACKED on the weekends, and I was here on a Saturday night, prime time.  The booth was so we could sit next to each other and canoodle.  This, is a mighty fine room, for canoodling, it walks the line between kitsch, and being downright sexy, so you laugh as you take in the decor, which is always a great way to start any experience.

We started with cocktails (Lillekois in our case) which I must congratulate the mixology master in question, and/or bar program manager because it bears the distinction of being a tropical cocktail that I found neither tragically pandering, nor cloyingly sweet.  The same cocktails btw, can be enjoyed in both the Ludlow bar and the "gardens" and they are FANTASTIC.  The first thing they brought out was a gorgeous puff pastry/flatbread with herbed creme fraiche that was like...forgive me, sex on my tongue.  It was that good.  A tuna tartare is such a boring menu item in 2015 it's all but ubiquitous at this point, but add thai bird chiles and a melange of herbs, namely mint, thai basil and cilantro, and it's DAZZLING.  I had Duck L'orange as my main course, and it was MAGNIFICENT, the Ras Al Hanout spices taking the twee out of the French Classic Julia Child once said she'd be happy to have as her last meal on Earth.  She'd have loved this as well.  My husband had a Steak Au Poivre, done with a short rib, that was luscious and well seasoned, unctuous and rich.  Dessert was an outrageous Baked Alaska, that was citrusy and bright, the meringue a lovely marshmallowy foil for it.  A chocolate cake with crunchy feuilletine layer, and gorgeous fudgy dense chocolate was equally amazing.

It's not cheap, but then...you already knew this.  It's also very very very hard to get in, but it's WORTH making this an effort to attempt to land a table.  I really enjoyed this place.  It achieves where a lot of thematic quasi hipster restaurants fail.  The fun is as good as the food, and the food is as good as the fun.

I didn't quite understand the fuss about the bread UNTIL i went and had the bread, and its really probably the best bread I've had.  Its really more a grilled flatbread, but iits amazing, crispy and warm well seasoned.  Seriously the highlight of the meal.  Like others have mentioned, service is pretty awful.  Everyone is friendly but timing of the dishes were painful, expect to wait for almost everything - for drinks, to order, your food, your check... even with the bad service I will be back, the food is kick butt.  The Bahn Mi at lunch is amazing, same with the french dip.
The ribs are amazing! Service was great. The dessert, however, was a huge disappointment. It seems like they forgot the sugar I the chocolate cake and the pistachios in the pistachio ice cream!

What a disappointing experience. This restaurant is very underwhelming and pedestrian, but the attitudes of the staff are off-the-charts snooty. And this isn't a seasoned waitstaff fitting a restaurant with such luxurious aspirations, either. They're all hipster 20-somethings. 

Everything we ate was barely passable and ridiculously overpriced. One standout awful item was the pomme frites. They are essentially big McDonald's hash browns served with a bland sour cream-like dipping sauce. They were upsettingly bad. How can you ruin french fries???  This should be an excellent staple of any French bistro, even one trying too hard to be hip. 

The saving grace was the cocktails, also available at the lobby bar, which I quite enjoyed. The Lilikoi and the Belmonde were both very good, the former being more unique. 

Honestly, I just feel like this restaurant group is expanding WAY too quickly into too many diverse areas, and the quality is suffering as a result. Torrisi was one of my favorite NYC restaurants until it was stupidly closed so that they can get another bite at the publicity apple (seems to be an obsession of these guys...), and Parm continues to be one of the best places for sandwiches - but with each new restaurant, they seem to get worse and worse.

Meh.  Fairly disappointed. Space is ok.  Warm. Cozy.  Small. Boisterous. They were going to try to squeeze 8 of us into a booth that was tight for 6.  Luckily we only ended up being 6.
Staff was good.  Not amazing, but good.  
Appetizers-grilled oysters-VERY good
The flatbread that they brought when we sat down-AMAZING. 
In fact if I just had those two plates all night I would have gone 4 stars. Unfortunately we ordered main courses. 
Steak Au Poive- not good. Way over-crusted with pepper corns.  And I LOVE pepper.  The cut (short rib) was just wrong for me.  The waitress did say that it is not braised, to be fair.  But then, not enough sauce to help cut the pepper crust.  Very disappointed. 
My clients ordered the duck and the lamb.  Duck needed more crisp on the skin, but was flavorful ( I tried it).  The lamb was good according to my other guests. 
Overall - meh.  Lots of new places to try.  Hopefully better results.

Cute decor but brunch was meh. I ordered the Oeufs which is eggs any style with toast and potatoes. I asked for creamy scrambled eggs and the waiter denied my request stating the staff does not have the bandwidth for such request. Ummmm ok, rude.

Eggs came out below standards and toast was sliced baguette that was so hard to bite into. I've had better service and food at the IHOP.

Maybe the service and quality of food is better at dinnertime. But I won't be back to find out.

Great overall experience. Food was exceptional, servers were very gracious, and sommelier was stellar. However the bartender was overly pretentious given her expertise. Easy fix - find a less awkward and condescending bartender.

Drinks were good- service was not so much. No coat check so you carry your coat till you can find a hook or you get seated- which is way past your reservation time. the bread they bring you is good- like a nan with a bit of ricotta on the side.  it's not much- just enough to break off a few bites per person. They recommended the chicken crepes for two- probably because it was the most expensive thing. I do not recommend it.  The dark meat was dry- the white meat was a bit odd in flavor. Cooked to perfection and tender for the breast but the flavor was a preference. They forgot two of the apps we ordered- and the baked Alaska desert was - eh. Probably won't go back unless there's a reason. The drinks were good enough that I would go back for them.
Yay, that was good. Great service and food. I think that was the best Beet Salad in NYC. The Tuna Tartare was phenomenal. Can't wait to go back for more!

Mixed bag on Saturday night, but we left happy. 

Good news:
- lovely space, dark and cozy, fun vibe.
- chicken and crepes amazing -- such a fun dish to share. 
- millefeuille even more amazing (trust me, try them!)
- adorable waitress with a great smile. 
- decent wines by the glass

Bad news
- some attitude at the door
- we waited 30 mins, though we'd reserved a table and arrived on time.
- bartender was the slowest in history. Not kidding. He needed 10 minutes per customer. Surreal level of weeds growing around him.
- touristy clientele
I had an excellent experience here! I loved the food! Loved eh vibe and serve was 5 Stars! I would definitely go back. I also love the music....it's soul music!

Super accommodating, friendly, great food, sexy vibe - but there's more. 
I was supposed to meet a friend there. We're huge fans of Major Food Group -- the owners of DF, Carbone, Parm, etc -- and had high expectation before our lunch reservation.
However, we ran into a friend and his baby whom wanted to come along. I decided I might as well bring my infant, too.
So there we where -- three men, two babies, a stroller and a car seat for a Friday reservation for a party of two.
"No problem guys, come on in!" said the maitre d'. Amazing on a busy day.
All in all a great place -- but probably even greater without babies and strollers. DF/MFG continue to deliver.

Pros: The food was very tasty and the portions were just right. I had the duck. 
The bartenders were very friendly and helpful. 

Cons: It was very difficult to make a reservation after 5:30 and before 10pm (even though we called a couple weeks in advance), so we showed up and took our chances. The hostess said the tables were all reserved, so we ate at the bar. Imagine our dismay, then, at the fact at a 4-top and 2-top table sat empty the whole time we ate. 

My advice to the manager: If someone is late for their reservation, call them, and if they don't answer, give the table away. You could be losing business!

Buttery goodness! I was skeptical about this place due to the mixed reviews on Yelp. I have to say it was one of the best and most memorable dinners and service I've had in a while. The music surprisingly was a lot of fun and lively,which really added to the wonderful ambiance. 

Our waiter was a gem, he was so gracious and friendly, and most importantly down to earth. The food was out of this world, definitely come hungry- the food is heavy, but tasty and delicious. 

The drink selection varies- you can have a very good glass of French wine anywhere from $13-$24. I chose the $13 glass and thought it was great. Others I was with tried the carafe of spiked punch and said it was really tasty and a good amount for 2 people to share. 

The flatbread they offer as a complementary starter was also wonderful. I'm actually surprised they would offer it for free. It was warm and buttery and came with a chive type spreadable cheese which was quite tasty, though I was completely fine with the bread on it's own. I could honestly come back and just eat this all night it was that good. 

Here's what we ordered for our appetizers:
-Mussels appetizer
-Lamb carpaccio 
-Grilled Oysters
-Mielle feuille mushrooms

I recommend them all. I particularly loved the oysters, they were massive! They were grilled, and then drenched in butter, spinach and garlic. You could really only eat one or two, they are very heavy, but taste amazing. The mushroom was also unique, the curry had a mint flavor and the texture of how how the mushrooms wer sliced were almost like eating a work of art. 

I had the bass as my entree and it was quite a production when they brought it to the table. It was wrapped in a bubbled paper which the waiter cut open at the table to reveal the plated fish. It was a really nice and elegant presentation. The fish was very tender and tasty. The portion size was really nice as well. I was very full and satisfied after the apps and the entree. 

A few of the girls got the duck and said it was one of the best they had. One person got the chicken for two. It's not huge so may not be enough for two, but you will definitely not be able to eat all of it for one. She took some home in a doggy bag. Another guest got the short rib and also shared the sentiment that it was one of the best she's ever had. We got the benets for dessert- again, they were fantastic. 

Overall, a wonderful experience, I would return.

A FEAST for the senses! Whatever you order, will be very, VERY delicious. Had the Mille Feuille, because we had seen and heard about it, and it was delicious. The curry sauces and cooking of the mushrooms were amazing. I had black bass and it was light and delicious, as was the potato puree. And the chocolate gateau was incredible--light texture but rich flavor with a little salt and pistachio on top. 
This is a great special occasion restaurant, as well as one for a group. It is not cheap, but it's worth it. Great staff and a nice atmosphere--nothing unique (dark booths and tables, brasserie setting) but comfortable. One tip, if all you can get is the 5:45pm reservation, take it. For one thing, everything will be onto menu, they will not have run out of anything. And you won't feel like the only ones there, the restaurant is always full. By 6:30 every table is full and the music (which is good) is louder and the night is in full swing.

I made a reservation four days in advanced and was told that normally I should make a reservation at least month in advanced to get a table. 

When we got there, they made us wait 30 minutes to be seated. When we finally sat down, it took 30 more minutes for our drinks to come. We ordered very simple drinks; tequila soda and vodka martini. 

The bread was incredible. Unfortunately the amazing food was overshadowed by the terrible service.  

At the end of the night my friend and I were going to split the bill. The waiter accidentally charged the entire bill on my card. It took him five minutes to explain to me what happened. Never going back.

I think it's more of a 3.5 but I'll be nice and round up.

Came here on a Tuesday night at 7 without a reservation and immediately got 2 seats at the bar. Seems they've opened up their heated garden now so that means more space to accommodate everyone. 

Pre-dinner cocktails ($16) were so good that if anything I'd return just for drinks. I had the Ludlow Gimlet and my friend got the Belmondo (like the best, most refined margarita you'll ever have!)

Started with the tuna tartare and the Mille Feuille. Both excellent and the flat bread with goats cheese that came with was too delicious to resist.

For entrees I got the duck a l'orange with a side of the rice pilaf. Initially I thought it was a small portion but it was very rich so actually just the right amount. My friend got the steak and despite the fact that I don't like steak, I had to try a bite. It was worth it! Again, small and very rich though.

We finished with sorbet and the Baked Alaska, which may have been my favorite thing. They set it on fire as they served it, although I think it could have done with a little more heat to get the outside of the meringue a little crispier and more heat would have enhanced the ice cold yumminess inside. 

We decided to go all-out given that we'd wanted to eat here for an age. The $300 bill for 2 (including a $100 bottle of wine, excluding tip) at the end wasn't a shock but it still stung a little! On the subject of service, our bar tender / server was great at the start but got very distracted as the night picked up and his friend arrived.

Glad I finally got to try it and think it's a beautiful looking space. Wouldn't rush back for the food at those prices, but I'd definitely go back for cocktails and dessert.

Disregard anyone who complains about service.  Wait staff is great.  Friendly and helpful, enthusiastic and attentive.  It is a busy spot, you need a res, and be prepared to wait a bit (what do you want them to do - kick people out?).  The food is worth every second of wait time.  Delicious - layered, multi dimensional, rich, approachable, unpretentious, fearless use of fat and salt (where all the flavor lies), multicultural (not just French).  Have been there twice and loved EVERY dish.  How often do you say that about any restaurant?

just had lunch there today, march 31st. just ok. i had the endive salad with shrimp. the shrimp had a dusty metallic order/taste. not good at all. the seasoning on top could not mask it. the endive was absolutely nothing special. good service. very pretty room. would not bother travelling downtown to go there again. also thought carbone was not as good last time i went. maybe they are losing the plot.

Excellent meal with unusual but delicious flavor combinations.  Millefeuille, foie gras and carpaccio to start were great, especially the foie gras.  Chicken with crepes was playful - chicken was juicy, sauce was interesting and "bahn mi" style condiments for the crepe made the entire experience unusually good and different.  Duck a l'orange was the best i have ever had.  Finish with the beignets, not your typical donut.  Only complaint is the wine list is ridiculously overpriced - great bottles but not enough range.  Went with $65 Gigondas and felt the sommelier was judging me.

A cute cosy classy  bistro with a european vibe. Its atmosphere is high end yet still warm (perfect date spot). The naan bread with cheese was my favorite. 
what to get: haricot verts , lamb carpaccio , steak, grilled/baked oysters, pork ribs. 
just ok: mille fuille, chicken with crepes, salmon, frites. 
Nothing was bad but those were the things that stood out along with the glaring fact that this is a place for small groups (4-6). There is a lounge attached thats excellent.

Don't come here thinking this restaurant is the French version of Carbone because it's not. Totally different food prep & concept, completely different service and atmosphere. One would assume with the can't-lose dream team of Mr. Z, Carbone & Torrisi behind this place, it would be amazing. It was not. It was fine, nothing to write home about. Dirty French is fairly new. Maybe that's it. As of right now, I will not recommend this place to anyone. Our server was very good, however, the busboys ruin the service by hovering over you waiting to take your plate after every bite. Such a turn-off. 

On to the food. I made the reservation here with the intention of ordering the chicken for two. I had to scrap that idea after I discovered that a portion of the bird is served with a mustard-based sauce and since my fiancé has a strong aversion to mustard or anything mustard-like, I decided to go with two separate entrees. Some dishes were much better than others. Although I can appreciate the unusual spices & seasonings used in some dishes, the exotic flavors will not translate well with a lot of people. The lamb Carpaccio was great, while the Millefeuille was a dud. The garishly green curry sauce didn't work with the expertly prepared trumpet mushroom. For entrees, I chose the orange duck and my fiancé went with the Brook trout. The duck was a tad too salty. The meuniere was tasty albeit a bit sweet with the apricot glaze and all. If you're looking to go light, then this is this dish to order. Sides consisted of Pommes frites & puree. Both were outstanding.

The cocktails were excellent. Beignets for dessert were ok. Would I return? Probably not in the near future. Drinks only.

Dirty French is ridiculously hyped up. The decor was pretty marginal, the music was fun (80's hits), and the food was very good. But for some reason it just didn't glow in the dark for me. I don't know if it was the service, or just the fact that I was expecting something special and it didn't deliver. I prefer Beauties & Essex and Carbone. I suppose it's worth coming to check it out.

Where do I even begin with this place? Let me just say that the food is actually quite good but the service was so unbelievably awful that I will never be coming here again. It is such a shame too because I am such a fan of the Major Food Group restaurants, especially Santina where there service and food is superb.

So we went for brunch and had reservations for 11:15. It took them 15 minutes to seat us. THERE WAS NO ONE IN THE RESTAURANT. To be quite literal, there were 2 tables being occupied, JUST TWO. The hostess kept staring at the table looking like she was ready to bolt over as soon as they were done, clutching the menus in her hand and apologizing every 2 seconds, AWKWARD. I mean, how long does it take to put napkins and utensils on the table that was right next to the station? Seriously?

Anyway, once we were finally seated, our waitress came over and asked if we wanted tap or bottled water. Her demeanor was pretty awful and pretentious. Whatever, fine. Finally, we were ready to order and our waitress just vanished for a good 15-20 minutes. We kept glancing around trying to find her in the empty restaurant and she was no where to be found. Then another waiter/manager (I am unsure who he was) came over and asked if we needed anything. We replied that we were just looking for our waitress and he replies "Yea, me too". Really? How unprofessional! How about "I'm sorry, let me check on that for you" or whatever, anything else but "yea me too". He asked if he could bring us anything else in the meantime and my friend asked for a cup of coffee. He came by and brought an empty cup. LOL Yes, and empty cup which didn't get filled for another 10 minutes.

Our waitress finally came over after an eternity. We were honestly contemplating going to sweet chick next door, that's how long we were waiting. The food came out SUPER fast, go figure. The food was great too. Really, really delicious. BUT the staff was so awful I will never come here, nor recommend anyone to go here either. There are plenty of amazing places to eat in NYC, what usually makes people come back is the service and/or something that sets the apart from all the other great places to eat. They are so unorganized here. There is one person that fills water, one that fills coffee, one that takes your order, one that takes away your plate (hovering over you, I might add). Like get your sh*t together. There were like 5 people in the restaurant and a million employees running around like chicken without heads and/or pulling disappearing acts. Thanks but no thanks!

The concept of this restaurant is great, and is carried through from the design of the drinks to the food, and the demeanor and approach of the staff that you interact with. It is all based on classical french styles but messed with just enough to make it seem new and fun. Nothing is sacred, some might feel it is trying too hard but they get just the right amount of tongue in cheek in my opinion. 

The atmosphere is good, friendly, bustling and happy, and for a place often described as a "scene" bar it doesn't feel pretentious or showy at all. If I was rating the first 10 minutes of the experience (pre-dinner cocktails at the bar) then the review would have been an awful lot better, but sadly the dining experience was less enjoyable. There were a lot of substitutions to the menu (e.g. hanger steak instead of short rib, pork ribs instead of the country chop), maybe we just got unlucky but it seemed like they were scaling back to slightly cheaper cuts, but the prices were just as high. Even if the original items had been available, the prices here are premium for fairly humble ingredients. Sadly, the fusion techniques largely lost the ability of great french cooking to elevate such humble items into masterpieces. A lot of the food was quite bland and underseasoned, and as you would expect from such a self-assured place, there are no condiments on the table to adjust the seasoning to your taste. The pictures on the menu and in official reviews show beautifully presented food, but less thought seemed to have gone into what we saw during our meal. It wasn't sloppy but hardly inspired either. 

A special mention should be made about the wine service, which cost at least one of those missing stars alone. We told our server that we would like wine and chose a bottle that we were interested in (we have a couple of people in the group that know wine well) but we were unable to order from the server and had to wait for the sommelier as he would best know what was available. We ordered food but still no sommelier or other drinks so we asked again, he arrived after our appetizers. It was a good job that no advice was needed as none was forthcoming, the sommelier merely marked the bottle we asked for with his finger and wandered off. The wine arrived when we were about half way through our main course, not exactly an ideal dining situation! We ordered another straight away guessing that if it would take as long again, we would be done by the time the second arrived; sadly we were correct. 

I wanted to like this place and feel with a little more attention to detail it could be a great option in the area, but maybe it is happy with being the hot new spot where people care more about the name and the vibe than the food and the wine.

I read all the reviews before dining here last night and I have to say I am on the side of the 4+ star reviews.  Yes, the hostess with the clipboard was taking her job way too seriously, and I didn't appreciate her urging us to take our table way before our reservation time.  But I can death stare back any 25 year old with an exaggerated sense of importance in executing her seating duties.  The bartender was engaging and made good beverage recommendations.  Extra points for frosted rock glasses and perfect ice cubes.  Once seated by the aforementioned seating-meister, our server and his shadow for the evening took time to explain the specials, menu items and wine list.  The naan was delicious as noted by other reviewers.  We had several varieties of oysters, all fresh and delicious.  Someone had the mussel special and the broth was intoxicating to this non-mussel eater.  I wanted to swim in it.  The flavors were unbelievable. Our dinners were:  lamb saddle, seared scallops, black bass and steak au poivre.  Sides: charred hericots vert and frites.  Nothing left.  All delicious, and all the while the service was attentive and not overbearing.  Our wine glasses were refiled without too much delay, as was the water.  Our water choice of NYC tap was not judged by our server as far as I could tell.  Dessert:  beignets and baked Alaska.  Nothing left.  We had a very enjoyable evening, delicious food and we all agreed we'd be back for more.  On our way out, we stopped to chat with a manager who was working the floor to inquire about the shadow our server had following him around all night as we were curious as to his job description.  He very nicely explained that the gentleman was training to be a waiter and was just that, a shadow for the evening.  We then discussed our dinner and service, and he genuinely seemed interested in what we had to say, which I guess was not difficult considering we had only good things to say.

This place was phenomenal.....the foie gras was the best I'd ever had and the chicken--I know it's just chicken but this is beyond any kind of chicken I have ever had! In this creamy mustard sauce and it came in two parts in a wrought iron pan......fabulous really but call a month ahead for reservations!

The chicken two ways is amazing. Perfect combination of rich gravy on white meat in savory crepes and then followed by crispy grilled dark meat.  The biggest challenge here is not filling up on the bread at the beginning of the meal. Arriving early and having a drink the lobby bar lounge makes for a great lingering experience.

Why is the food here so delicious?!?!

I really didn't know what to expect, but was initially put off by the long delay in being seated for our reservation (which, I will say, front of house did try to resolve as quickly as possible with frequent updates and several attempts at creative solutions along the way).

But the instant the complimentary flatbread hit the table, all was forgiven.

Readers far and wide, heed my warning: the flatbread will entice and enamour you, with little to deter you from ordering second (or third!) helpings of what may be the most intoxicating opening salvo of bread I've ever had.  But fight the temptation; resist, I say! because there is much more that lies ahead you will want to be able to enjoy.

If you want to start the evening with a mouthful of decadence, order the foie gras terrine.  Lush and captivating, the crepe-like bric wrapped around the terrine added a much enjoyed layer of texture with each and every bite.  The millefeuille of mushrooms was also a savoury treat; not quite as luxurious as the terrine, but as delicious as they come when it comes to vegetables.

The brook trout is wildly understated in the menu, buttery and succulent in a way you wouldn't expect fish to be.  The steak au poivre was aggressively seasoned and a beautiful piece of meat, although compared to the other offerings, actually a bit disappointing not because it fell short in any way, but because everything else was so impressive.  My favourite of the night, however, was the pork: the glaze was a surprisingly well-layered blend of flavours, hitting all the notes I would want out of a savoury bite.  

We probably did not do as good as a job when ordering dessert, as the beignets were comparatively benign compared to dinner itself.  The chocolate cake was also not bad, but also not brilliant.

I would come back again, if not for the flatbread alone.  But there was much more on the menu we wanted to try, and we would certainly round off the evening again with another order of pork.

I wanted to love dirty french and parts of the meal were amazing but other parts were just so so. My husband loved the duck a l'orange, the bread was fantastic but the lamb was very fatty (even for me). Not a bad place for a celebration but perhaps not worth the high prices.

Shady rolled into DF to conquer the Torrissi Groups latest incarnation with an atypical ( for Shady) ill informed and low brow posse. Shady put that all aside and went to work on his vision quest to die while dining in NY's best. Lets just start by saying this was a high point of dining in the past year-and Shady has hit some pretty- pretty nice spots. Lets get to it:
Starters-Lamb carpaccio, tuna tartare,grilled oysters, foie gras  and the chèvre salad. I would say the tuna was possibly the best tartare Shady has met, and the foie gras and oysters and lamb carpaccio were similarly regarded. 4 stars across the board. 
Dinner- the chicken crepes for 2, several orders of the steak au poivre, the pork ribs..all off the charts good. The crowd , despite their general lack of taste and class, all agreed on the genius of the meal. Sides were the pomme frites and some sprouts, and we all polished off the meal with some beignets and some chocolate dessert. 
With copious cocktails, the bill came to 130$ per person. Stacey our server was patient dealing with Shady's problematic cohorts and was terrific. 
All in all, a special meal. Love the hotel . Get there early and enjoy drinks in the atrium. On a nice night this all in is a special evening. Enjoy!

Was invited to Dirty French for my birthday last week. I was a little nervous after looking at the menu because the selections looked a bit ordinary, but when the food came out, the dishes were everything but plain. 

Our waiter started us off when their house flatbread, accompanied by a herb cheese. The bread was warm, soft and chewy, with spices liberally springkled on top. Try not to stuff yourself with it and save room for dessert. You'll want the lemon tart to help cut all the richness of the meal. 

I'd recommend the foie gras tarine, their king oyster mushroom millefueille (which sits on this subtle coconut curry), the perfectly crispy skinned duck, and their bass. The proteins were perfectly cooked, but its the bold flavors of their sauces that will get you going bite after bite. Do not be deceived by the simplicity of their menu. The pairing of some ordinary items like orange and duck are done up with a fun and unexpected twist. All in all, I would definitely come back again. 

Oh.... so why didn't they get 5 stars? Well, the wait staff was a little weird. We were greeted by a waitress, who took our order and disappeared. The waitress was replaced by a waiter, who later told us that some of the items we had ordered were either changed for the day or sold out. It was just a little funny that it wasn't mentioned the second we sat down. And then our waiter came by very very often to check on us. Thanks dude, but when I tell you we're ok.... we're ok!

I have mixed feelings about Dirty French.  The service was excellent.  And the food was solid, but it felt a little try-hard in spots and value didn't seem quite there.  Some dishes were nice, though.  The tartares/carpaccio were great.  The steak for 2 was definitely NOT worth it.  Not even close to worth it.

Our waitress was really nice, though, and it was a really fun night/spot.

The lamb carpaccio may be the best thing I have ever eaten.  The duck was very good too.  Great flat bread.  The mushroom millefeuille was interesting in the execution but middling in taste with a very green and oddly textured sauce.  The swordfish was okay.  The beignets were good.  Our waiter was very attentive and while the food came out quickly, we did not feel rushed.

I have been dying to come here since it opened. The lamb carpaccio is not to be missed, neither is the flatbread. The foie gras was off to me, but my fellow diner absolutely loved it so maybe it just wasnt for me. Not sure what else I would come back here for other than the tartare and lamb again, but they do look to have some great meat options. Great spot to try on my birthday.

Fairly underwhelmed with this spot considering the price point...

The Bread: 5/5
Stunning, fresh, and delicious.  Really... worth all the sins

Food: 4/5

The Terrine was exquisite. Very shareable and rich.  The Millefeuille was perhaps one of the best dishes I have had in memorable history and certainly the most original, unique and satisfying dish of the evening. The rest of our mains: Porc aux Moutardes, Hanger Steak, Brook Trout were satisfyingly simple.  No shout out, but a great entree course for the most part.

For a crispy Duck a l'orange, this is not the place to go.. An ambitious approach to a classic, this dish was probably oversold (see service) and was definitely an interesting texture not in line with the sell..  The asparagus was similarly off the mark for us.  It was sold as a refreshing answer to the Spring day and in all actuality, probably was just something that needed to be moved.  It was not a hit at our table and I would not recommend for any season.

Service: 2/5
We were whisked quickly to our seats and promptly and has a mismatch of service.  The runners, for the most part, were spot on, humerous, knowledgable and smart.  I agree with some other reviews that service can be a little bit awkward// off the cuff.  It seemed like for some of the service items were not ironed out (share plates, silverwear, clearing, etc)

The sommilier was spot on, well presented and even though we were sticking to cocktails, arranged a gin tasting for one of our party that was really above and beyond.  We were impressed.

Our waitress Emily was really the pivot to the experience.  It did seem as if she were put upon by our presence.. After a fairly condesencing discussion about getting additional bread (it is truely crack, and we were offered a second platter by the runners) we were off to the races.... We then recieved the oversold duck and she seemed frustrated when one of our party asked if the skin was supposed to be crispy...  Thats cool that it is not, but come back with a solution, you sold it after all...  

The piece de resistance was the bill delivery when she asked the head of the table if she could split the check...  Really amateur in my opinion.. If we were at Applebees, I would understand it, but when you are spending 70+ a person, it just left a bad taste in our mouths and a good amount of confusion.

All in all, I would not hestitate to recommend the menu and the beverage service.  If I happen to have another chance to dine there, I do hope I am lucky enough to enjoy a different server...

Went here for my best friend's birthday. We had a 9:30 reservation on a Wednesday night. They made us wait an hour and fifteen minutes for our table, claiming they would comp our drinks but never did. Cocktails were also overpriced for what they were. According to the hostess, the people who had our table before us wouldn't leave...but then after about an hour, she said they had just gotten the check. I know they are a hot spot, but I've been to plenty of other trendy, nicer, and more expensive restaurants that didn't treat me so poorly.

When we finally got to the table, the service was quick, but I did notice them taking a long amount of time between people leaving and the staff cleaning them/seating new customers. Food was okay, but they added too much pepper to every single dish. Including my beet and Roquefort salad, which probably would have been tasty without it. The flatbread and dip that they serve was the highlight of the meal.

Prices were standard for this type of trendy place (even though it looks like a dirty dive bar inside), but I'd rather take my money elsewhere. I've been to much nicer restaurants in NYC (Per Se, Eleven Madison Park, Jean Georges, etc.) where I didn't have to wait at all for my reservation. Not worth the money or time we spent. Left a bad taste in my mouth.

The food and cocktails here are very good, especially the duck, the pineapple tatin and the lilikoi cocktail. The room is loud and the crowd annoying. Worst, however, is the service: starting with the maitre d' who simply pointed at my table instead of showing me to it and ending with our waiter Kyle who dropped our check without our asking while we were still eating. The restaurant business is a service industry; if these poseurs don't want to provide service they should find something else to do! It's too bad because we live nearby and would happily come here often if it weren't for the worst service I've ever encountered.

I was so excited to try this place and it wasn't hard to get a reservation on a week day about a week in advance.  We were seated right away when we arrived and I would just say the restaurant itself is lit a little on the dim side.  It's beautifully romantic in a fancy diner kind of way.  Note that the tables that are booths are quite close together.  While I was comfortable in my seat, my chair was constantly getting bumped by waiters that were coming and going.

OK THE FOOD.  SO GOOD.  SO DECADENT.  

This isn't a light meal, not even if you order the fish.  The food is really rich with lovely salts, butters and creams, and not that I'm complaining, but you shouldn't come here if you're on a diet.  Nothing is diet about this place.  

They start you off with really yummy flatbread that comes with a delicious fromage blanc.  I usually try to resist the bread, but this one I just couldn't.  We also ordered a salad (you don't need to know which one because I'm pretty sure they're all good) and the terrine which was way too much decadence for two people to share.  It was probably better for 4 people. 

We both ordered fish dishes which were paired with a great riesling, recommended by the sommelier.  My bass was cooked to perfection and the coconut sauce it was in was amazing.  A tiny bit on the salty side, but good nonetheless.  I don't know about you, but I am in love with salt.  I would marry it if I could.

We finished our meal off with an peanut butter and jelly like paris-brest.  This wasn't my favorite part of the meal, but it was an interesting dessert.

Service was always with a smile and it was attentive.  I'd consider coming back, but the hors d'oeuvres are better shared with a few people, in my opinion.  Yum Yum!

What to say.....
Beautiful, great food and a a very nice staff. 
I am not sure if I will run back, but it's not a place to avoid. 

Two thumbs up!

Came by here after dinner for a couple drinks. When we arrived there were plenty of tables, they told us there were none. We were eventually seated. We got drink menus, but waited about 20 minutes for someone to take our order. The coffee came sooner one my friends ordered. The drinks came after another 15-20 minutes, and the waitress spilled one drink all over the table and into the coffee, so we had to wait for the coffee. It took about 20 minutes to get the bill, I had to ask for it twice. The service here is pretty bad, but the drinks are decent. The food looked good, but we didn't eat here.

I enjoyed the ambiance considerably and the service was very good.  The food was good, although I found a few of the dishes lacked balance at times.  

Tuna Tartare was very good but it was very spicy.  It really had a kick to it.  I don't particularly mind that so no foul here but I think some will find it overpowers a bit.  I found a similar issue with the mustard sauce with the chicken for two.  I liked the creativity with the crepes and the presentation was interesting and unique.  The mustard sauce was a bit overwhelming though and it was tasty enough where it didn't need to overpower the dish the way it did.  The chicken itself was moist and perfectly cooked.

The bread is fantastic.  We even took a second one home and was just as good the day after.  They have great old fashioned stemware for the cocktails they serve.  My only problem with it is it is tiny, so basically they are charging $17 for a 6 oz martini.  

Overall, it was worth the visit.

Probably more like 4.5 stars.  Slight deductions for initially rushed service, an expensive wine list and for the foie gras terrine which was completely overpowered by a preserved or burnt lemon spread.  Otherwise, really great flavors, and an unusual mixture of textures.  Food was fun to eat. Drinks were also a highlight.

Dirty French opened with fairly mixed acclaim late last year, thanks to the backing of the well-known trio of Torrisi, Carbone, and Zalaznick (or Major Food Group). The restaurant is part of the Ludlow Hotel, in a relatively tightly-packed space that sports red banquettes against the perimeter of the white brick and wood walls, which all converges towards an antique carnival mirror - one that eerily calls to mind the piece that fell onto diners at Balthazar. By day, it takes on a more relaxed and casual ambiance but by night, it transforms into a space that resembles a club, with a volume to match.

But let's get started on the food. Our group of six was promptly seated and quickly decided on our appetizers and mains, and were soon presented with their famous starter - a plate of flatbread dotted with herbs and served with fromage blanc. It's a welcome first bite, as the flatbread is both chewy and crisp with just the right amount of seasoning, and the fromage provides a cold, creamy contrast to the dough. I was tempted to ask for more, but the arrival of our starters interrupted my attempt.

My friend and I split the Lamb Carpaccio, a beautifully presented dish that featured paper-thin slices of lamb dotted with scoops of sheep's milk yogurt and a few slices of roasted aubergine. There's a hint of preserved lemon, and a light layer of raz-al-hanout oil - additions which elevate this seemingly simple dish. There's an edge of gaminess, a dollop of creaminess, and and a faint tartness and smokiness that make this carpaccio like no other. I did also get the chance to try the Tuna Tartare (excellent, fresh, and lightly spiced) as well as the Mille Feuille (chewy, under-seasoned, and strikingly unpleasant), so reactions to our dishes were mixed across the board.

I wasn't expecting much from the Porc aux Moutardes, but I was presented with two impressive cuts of pork ribs (bone-in), paired with a reduction of Calvados Apples and a mustard sauce. The dish was executed well, consisting of tender, well-seasoned meat smartly highlighted against the sweetness of the apples and the sinus-clearing punch of mustard (and generous amounts of mustard seed as well). My friend's Duck a l'Orange was delicious and fatty, although the portion was quite small and the skin could have been more crisp, and the Lamb Saddle was equally impressive. 

So why the three stars? In hindsight, I probably wouldn't return to Dirty French. The food, from what my friends and I tried, is across the board and inconsistent, and the near-deafening volume that grew towards the end of the evening made it nearly impossible to have a conversation. For the curious, I'd recommend visiting for brunch (where they offer a brunch-only Lamb Burger and French Dip sandwich) for a slightly more peaceful ambiance and a smaller dent on the wallet.

I manhandled Dirty French's possibly brunch-only lamb burger a while back. It felt more dirty than French, but who's arguing when you need to be speed stuffing those expletive delicious French fries? This restaurant deserves another visit from me, but first it deserves five stars for a memorably stellar first meal.

I've eaten here several times. Excellent food, excellent service. Great selection of wines. I tried everyone else's orders and all of the food was spectacular. Each time I have gone, the quality has been consistent and I recommend this place for anyone who is the mood for trendy French cuisine. Two thumbs up!

Very pretentious and rude staff. They try hard to seem "high class", but they are lower than the lowest level of human behavior inside-out. We didn't enjoy, because they were literally "intruding" in front of our face without any reason (e.g. moving the candle  an inch away and nothing more). Very pretentious "service" and smiles and no real character and definitely not exquisite food for the prices you get to pay. 

Never back there again!!
I absolutely loved this place! The food was tasty and delicious. Our tables got the chips and the chicken along with 3 desserts. Recommend the "outdoor" patio for a romantic date.

We have waited a while to get a Rez here and overall it was a good experience but not sure it fully lived up to all he hype. Cocktails were good with the bartender agreeably making us 2 really nice cocktails. Our first course of trumpets and tuna tartare were really delicious with some great spice and the flavors of Italian parsley, mint, and basil. Our salad of kale and mixed greens was also really fantastic. Our trout was beautifully prepared and served filleted and was both crispy and moist. We had a really not very dry riesling with out first course after cocktails and then an '08 cab franc for $88 which I highly recommend. The one glaring miss was the lack of a cheese and we heard that the warm temperature in the restaurant didn't permit cheese but it seems if dirty French wants to be part of the echelon of gramercy tavern and a revamped Balthazar or Modern day Odeon they need to raise their game with a cheese course and more expansive selection of entrees.  The sommelier was great. Overall I think it's great if you haven't been to France and want a NY French experience.
1/2 hour wait from our reservation time, no apologies. But if you miss your reservation by 15 minutes you lose it. Waiting for a waitress...
Went last night and LOVED it! The food is delicious! Really! Drinks served with a heavy handed pour. Atmosphere is dope. In a killer neighborhood ... Will def go back.

Best dinner I've had in NYC and the service was impeccable. Dirty French is not a place you just go to eat because you're hungry; it's an experience and almost a performance. Everything we had was amazing, but if I went again I would get the flat bread that comes with dinner and about 4 orders of the grilled oysters and leave a happy man.

It is impossible to get decent dinner reservations here so the minute a friend of mine had reservations I made sure I was available.
The SHORT RIBS and MUSHROOM side dish is all you need.
I usually never order steak at a restaurant...we ordered a few entrees to share and decided to throw in the short ribs since we already had fish and chicken ordered.
I hardly touched the fish and the chicken was okayyyy but the short ribs were to die for.  Everyone at my table said the shorts ribs were their favorite!
The chicken is a bit intimidating....they bring out the dark meat first, basically whole chicken legs (claws and all!).  It IS the best part of the chicken but a little unappealing eating it this way.  Then they bring out the white meat which was a little dry.  
Fish, don't remember a thing about it.
Aside from the fantastic shorts ribs and mushrooms, I do have to give an honorable mention to the bread/cheese that they provide for the table.  It's basically a soft, warm, chewy pita-naan-like herb bread served with a pile of soft cheese similar to the Boursin cheese...I totally filled myself with the bread and cheese, I couldn't help myself!
I can't wait to go back!!!!

We came for brunch and were greeting by a very friendly hostess.  We had already eaten an early breakfast and planned to get the eggs Benedict to share.  After realizing that there was prosciutto on the eggs Benedict, we had requested for one of them to be without meat.  Our server was hesitant to ask the chef (not sure why?) but it worked out in the end.  The home fries were extremely extremely greasy (almost inedible after 2-3 bites).  The eggs Benedict dish was  delicious though.  Overall I give 3 starts for a pricey OK meal...4 stars for the service and ambiance.

The wine list is amazing. So many to choose from! We got 4 appetizers-2 were great and the other 2 not so much. You def have to try the lamb carpaccio! Service was great, the atmosphere was great. Definitely will be going back.

Just to put everyone at ease, the service is fine. The hostesses are terrible though. No manners, no personality, just resting bitch face and a terrible attitude. The food makes it all worth it though. The duck is everything you ever dreamed of, and the hanger steak will blow you away. The beignets for dessert are a must. Just don't wear pink, or someone will mistake you for a waiter.

This place has excellent Moroccan-style bread served at your table instead of the regular bread you get from restaurants.

This time our desserts at the table is excellent!  We enjoyed the tart made with bananas and pineapple with rum raisin (literally soaked raisins in rum) and a scoop of ice cream.  This dessert is like a very thin version of an Apple Tatin except it's pineapple with bananas.

They also gave us a thin long lemon bar with piped in meringue.  Very sweet but delicious. They used true lemon.

The mushroom dish with ramp sauce and the foie gras is not to be missed.

Our only pet peeve is that we were early and the restaurant just opened while our friend ordered a drink and we were prevented to sit at our table which we reserved.  Finally, a guy came in who was friendlier than the talk lady at the desk who let us sit down 10 minutes before our reservation.   Our friend contacted us that she would be slightly late and start before her, but they wanted us to be complete! 

I think they should sit us at our table since only 1 of us ordered a drink at the bar.  This way, we wouldn't be occupying the chiais at the bar. We certainly would not wait standing up either.  We also planned to have some appetizers at our table while waiting - not at the bar.  I think if no one is sitting at our table and it's early enough that the opening while no one is around; we should be able to wait sitting at our table instead of waiting at the bar.

When they turned back the ceiling fan on, we and the lady at the next table began to cover ourselves to keep warm. We requested to turn it low or off but this time they did not listen.  Last time, the manager turned off the blower where me and another guest requested to turn it off because we were getting chilly.

The staff should behave like their managers and listen to their client! The customer is always right!

came here for a birthday dinner and had a great time. there was a delay in sitting us but we didn't mind because everyone was very polite and there was lovely lounge to sit in as we waited. drinks at the bar were great. we had both tequila drinks and were not disappointed. 

service was great throughout. 

the food was good. my company thought it was amazing, but i wasn't that overwhelmed. the foie gras was a bit sweet in my opinion. we often order duck and this was very good but a bit too heavy on the fat, which i typically like. the kale salad was good, again not amazing. lamb carpaccio was eh IMO (tho everyone else seems to rly like it).

the sides, on the other hand, were great! the pomme frites and haricot asiatique were stellar. as was the bread. hate when great food places have bad bread. the bread might have been my favorite part of the meal here hahah 

the desserts looked SO good but we were SO full (portion sizes were descent) and could not eat anymore unfortunately.

would recommend this place for drinks, environment, service, and solid food. would also bring out of town friends here. heads up to make reservations well in advance. we ate here on a wednesday, made reservations 2 days in advance, and could only be seated at 10:15 pm. super busy

I first heard about Dirty French shortly after it opened in Fall 2014, and only heard great things.  I tried and tried to get a rez each time I came back to the city, but unless I wanted to eat at 5pm on Wednesday, there was no shot at getting in.  That is until, circa 8 months later, I got my rez after things cooled down a bit.  

The neon sign guarding the door gives the place an almost red light district feeling, and the interior felt as if it was suitable for a burlesque show, making the dirty portion of the name very befitting.  

I started off with a Pigalle, their spin of an old fashioned, to loosen up a bit, and while it wasn't the old fashioned I was looking for, it wasn't too bad.  The bread with bechamel is a hit, and is their house bread.  Forget your gluten-free diet and have some, have lots.  Foie gras is very hit or miss for me - Dirty French's was a spectacular hit.  The block of fioe was placed inside a crispy bric pastry, giving a very nice contrast of texture between the creamy fioe gras and the crunchy pastry.  The main course was the Duck Al'Orange.  You need this in your life.  The skin was perfectly crisp while the breast was a spot-on medium rare.  The accompanying sauce was a perfect compliment to the duck.  To finish the experience, I went with the Gâteau, a chocolate cake with mango chutney.  Great way to end.

Come prepared to drop a cool $80-100 on dinner.

I doubt they care about a little yelp review because this place needs no help. It's stellar. I actually had a bad experience but still have it 5 stars because they did everything they could to turn my mood. It was the 2nd time I had been and raved about it to my friends.  I had a 930 reservation and after 30 min you tend to get annoyed. ..at 45 min you're pissed ...after an hour I was walking out. They asked to please stay and not wanting to ruin the night for out of town guests I calmed myself and stayed.  They pulled out all the stops and our food was incredible. I highly highly recommended the sea bass its like butter you never want it to end.  They took it upon themselves to bring us great mock tails ( we don't drink) and brought us damn near the entire dessert menu.  The manager and waiter were very gracious that we enjoyed it all.  Now this is definitely a place where you would expect them not to care if one party left. ..I mean they had people pouring in looking for a table.  They treated us very well and we have since been back and the manager recognized us and the level of service never waivered. I really appreciate a business that cats about service because good food served poorly kills the dining experience. The food here is worth every penny and the way you're treated makes it feel like a bargain.

I didn't think I would love the food here, but frankly it exceeded my expectations. Although we had to wait 30 min after our reservation time (11:00pm) and I was getting annoyed by then. They were polite, apologized for the wait and served us champagne while we waited for our table. Our servers gave us amazing recommendations and we left very pleased. Prices are high but well worth-it! 

Still dreaming about the flatbread. Yum!

Trendy & delicious. I had the duck l'orange - the best I've ever had. Also their bread is to die for. Someone else at our table had the steak and it seemed to be the knockout winner (but everyone was happy with what they ordered). Service was good, but we were the first seating for dinner and it was obvious they were trying to hurry things along. Seems like this is something you just have to live with in NYC. Luckily the hotel has an awesome indoor garden/courtyard lounge where you can order drinks & keep the evening going. I will be back.

As a guest of the Ludlow hotel we managed to get a reservation on the day of asking which was unexpected. We booked it as a celebration for my 50th birthday whilst visiting New York. 

Service was really good with our waiter for the evening being very warm and attentive throughout our dinner. The wine waiter was also very helpful in deciphering the French wine as both my wife and I are big Australian meaty red fans.

Anyway onto the food. We both had the ribs with puréed potatoes and mushrooms and I have to say it was one of the best meals we have ever had. The whole meal had so much flavour that there was virtually no conversation during the main. The desert was equally as good which capped off a wonderful experience. 

The meal cost around $300 which ain't cheap but I would say it was worth every penny.

My NYC gentleman and I recently had a fantastic date night here while staying at the Ludlow.  Our server was excellent - friendly and knowledgeable, attentive but not obtrusive.  The bread and labneh style spread was flavourful and different, also dangerously addicting enough to fill up on.  We had a nice white Beaujolais to go with our meal and it complemented the lighter flavours well.

Everything was shared so for appetizers we got the grilled oysters and the lamb carpaccio.  Quite the contrast in flavours but I liked the oysters better with the spinach and garlicky butter/oil.  For entrees we shared the scallops and the duck l'orange.  The scallops were cooked beautifully and were a nice lighter option.  However, the duck was one of the best renditions of this dish I have had yet.  The fat was rendered beautifully causing the skin to be crispy but still have a bit of that unctuousness.  The meat was perfectly done and every bite was a pleasure.  For dessert, we decided on some sorbet but I was not that impressed with the selection.

Overall, this was an excellent dining experience giving us a feel of an in-city vacation.

Chic setup with a very French 'tude & vibe; cool & effortless. Hostess & servers were just friendly enough. No artificial sweeteners added here. 

Decor is chic-cozy and quite intimate-the tables are pretty close to each other. Our table for 2 was snuggled between a pillar and what appeared to be a couples table (#32). It could have been uncomfortable for my friend who was seated on the traffic side but she was too distracted by the yummy courses. 

The oiled Flatbread served with rosemarie'd goat cheese was the perfect opener, it accompanied our sparkling rose really nicely. Nothing like getting off on the right foot. 

We ordered the garlic oysters to start, the hanger steak and scallops with champignons and smoky green beans for our main and the (lavender) beignets with caramel sauce (on the side) and 3 scoops of ice cream which I didn't really bother that much with since I was smitten with the beignets and just about ready to explode at this point.

I will definitely be back, armed with a healthy appetite. This time with my hubby since the ambiance is perfect for an easy, romantic dinner.

My dinner at the Dirty French was inventive, eclectic and at times bizarre. Ultimately the overall experience was enjoyable and unique. 

The atmosphere was striving for the impossibly hip, over the top, almost baroque luxury meets what you might find as a disturbing and kitschy vibe that is somehow at times still an alluring combination when found in some Soho loft space. Porcelain, Bright fuchsia chickens, busts with smeared mascara makeup and lipstick (as if they've been crying?) brass chandeliers decorated the place....might be too much for some crowds. I found it interesting or curious at least. 

The service was attentive and answered all questions about the menu and wine pairings with ease. Excellent wine list. I am always able to fine my favorite, wines here - Clos de la Chapelle  was perfection with my lamb.

In delivery and concept the food had an interesting humor and playful creativity that was inventive and was articulated through well executed, classical french technique. 

To start I had the Mille Feuille in a sweet corn and curry sauce and trumpet royale mushrooms. Mille Feuille is traditionally made with puff pastry. However in this case, the mushroom was used as the puff pastry and served in the curry sauce. Interesting, savory, and rounded out by the refreshing pops of summer corn. Definitely the highlight of the appetizers at our table. 

For my entree I had the Boulangere which was lamb "saddle", potatoes and cumin. Lamb saddle is the under belly of the lamb, a fatty cut that also contains some tenderloin. As a result it was quite tender and was exceptionally roasted in a way that brought out the unctuous flavors of roasted lamb fat that was expertly soaked up by the potatoes. 

To finish I shared a variety of desserts, including the Beignets in hickory caramel sauce, the preserved lemon tarte, the Paris-Brest (blackberry and peanut profiterole that tasted like PB&J...very clever given the P-B in the name). All of the desserts were made to the level of a pastry chef. Not sure if one is on staff, but they were certainly fresh. The Beignets were airy and than Cafe du Monde, but the Paris-Brest won for its surprisingly dressed up appearance yet throwback childhood comfort flavor.

Lively, open, fun and unpretentious atmosphere with excellent brunch food and cocktails. 

Food: 4.75, Atmosphere: 5, Service: 5
Cost to worth it rating: 3 (brunch items ~$15-22)
Eve award: best crispy potatoes
Return worthiness: yes

Highlights:
- Cocktails: not just mimosas for brunch. Inventive ones like a uniquely spiced old fashioned, bourbon with ancho chili (pigalle), tropical passion fruit and rum (lilikoi) and refreshing ones by the pitcher to share. Delicious 
- Duck hash: wow. Duck confit for breakfast. On top of delicious cubes of potato. Topped with a runny egg. With hidden crispy skin pieces. Brilliant. Wayne's World we're not worthy status. 
- Potatoes: not your standard frites. Flat and long slices with the maximum surface area to crisp all around. Crispy loving hub was thrilled.
- French dip: on a skinny french baguette with shallots. Solid version of a sandwich the hub orders a lot. 
- Waitress: so enthusiastic about the food--it was contagious. She was new and I loved her and wished she could join us.
- Atmosphere: bright, open, and roosters everywhere. Fun and comfortable.

Lowlights:
- Professional reviews: I expected it to be pretentious or snobby based on what I read and was happy to find it to be the polar opposite.

One of the best all around brunches I've had. I recommend it to anyone who will listen and would love to come back.
Food, service, decor and drink selection was excellent. The string bean side dish kept me munchin even though I was beyond full! Great for dates or group settings.

Exceptional food.  Excellent but not over solicitous service.  Very cool decor + Ludlow Hotel Bar access.  Loved lamb carpaccio, baked oysters, corn curry appetizer, nan + goat cheese, grilled scallops, black bass, beignets, outstanding coffee & awesome lemon tart.  Great bar & tender too.

Very small portions. Overpriced. Mostly fried and fatty appetizers. The complimentary flatbread they serve is fried and you can see oil dripping from it. We ordered tuna tartare and the crepe it came with again was swimming in oil. The main dishes were small in size, but tasted good. I had sea bass entree, it was small, but delicious.

after a great deal of effort, was able to score a reservation.  the host and hostess at the front couldn't be nicer or more welcoming. the place was fun and had a great vibe. drinks were great and so was the food. our blond waitress wasn't that helpful or friendly - but everything else was great enough to make for a fun dinner outing!

I was very skeptical about this place because of the reviews and the fact that it had become one of these typical New York hyped hot spots. I was so very pleasantly surprised though. I can't wait to go back.

The bread and spread they bring out first is heaven. I dare you not to fill up on it. Also, we ordered a rum cocktail for two (lime and grapefruit juice) and it was so light and refreshing. We started with the tuna tartare and the escargot style grilled oysters from our server's list of favorites. The tuna was good but the crêpe it came with was so interesting and tasty - a savory and slightly oily addition to the light tuna. The oysters were great. I love escargot but to use that preparation on oysters - even better!

We had the duck for the entree which was crispy and oily on the top and tender in the center, as duck should be. The meringue dessert was slightly a disappointment and almost tasted freshly thawed - too cold for my taste.

Go have a drink in the hotel's "garden" before or after dinner - it is a delight! Another LES favorite!!!

In the LES there are some great brunch options. Dirty French had the worst service of any brunch spot I've been to.  First off, they were out of the pastry basket and 4 menu items. The waitress disappeared and left us sitting there. Then when we begged another server for the check, the check was wrong. We saw three tables returning incorrect food items. For over $200, I expect much, much better.

Great restaurant. Just go.

Cocktail menu is excellent, wine list is expansive. Apps were on point, led by the frequently mentioned lamb carpaccio, but also the foie gras and the bread. For mains we had the cote de boeuf which was prepared very well. Pommes frites were cleverly prepared slices of heaven. Attentive but not intrusive service was well balanced and helpful with recommending dishes and drinks.

Great starter cocktails. 
We had a truly awful experience with the sommelier- what was described as a buttery oaked Chardonnay came as an overly sweet,plum smelling fruity wine for 88$. No one in the party drank any and we apologetically addressed the issue. It was suggested we just order by the glass from there on out with avoidance of service from there on out. We were also charged a 21$ bottle open fee. 
The chicken was very good as was the lamb, though neither lived up to the hype or price. Although our server was lovely she seemed unable to amend any aforementioned issues. 
For this 'caliber' of a restaurant the experience was dismal and I would truly recommend considering other options-

IN SHORT: Dirty French is to French cuisine as Marc Chagall was to the French tradition of art. In boldly and brashly referencing material far beyond the confines of the classic canon, the restaurant creates a serious meal that somehow feels much more charming, and much more fun.

THE STORY: I probably relate food to art far too much, but more often than not, the analogy fits. Conceptually, Dirty French is one of of the most ingenious restaurants to open in New York, for many of the same reasons that we praise post-modernist painters and thinkers. The rules of French cooking here are challenged with a confident bravado, the discipline of the classic cuisine pushed to include influences from Tunisia, Morocco, India, Vietnam, and even Louisiana. Dirty French imagines what French food would look like if the relationship between France and its post-colonial territories were more reciprocal, and the result is as instructive as it is inventive. These types of cultural statements and fusions are doubtlessly the most exciting aspects of contemporary art, and indeed, of this restaurant as well.

The Mille-Feuille bridges geographies in an enlightening display of technical dexterity, with thin, silky slivers of royal trumpet mushrooms layered, pressed together, and roasted, flaring the edges with a thread of crispiness. The buttery, almost noodle-like texture is then complemented with a fresh, green Thai curry that adds an additional energy to the dish. And it's only the introduction to a meal that is so clearly French, but without all the trappings of tradition and formality.

Paradigms of French cooking are elevated with style, particularly in the Lamb Carpaccio, which takes soft, paper-thin slices of lamb and infuses the meat with flavors of spicy, aromoatic oil, eggplant, yogurt, lemon, and various fresh herbs. And it's the most deeply flavorful treatment lamb has ever seen.

The main courses also look toward this diverse evolution of French food, where Duck à l'Orange is treated with ras el hanout, a Morocan spice blend with strong notes of cinnamon, cumin, clove, and peppercorn.
