Preserved mandarin oranges frame the irony, juicy piece of duck, whose extraordinarily crispy and salty skin crackles with every solid bite. The flavor of lime cornichon against the hangar steak in the Au Poivre also adds a refreshing vitality to a classic cut, proof that the seemingly unnatural, garrish, and outlandish combinations at Dirty French are actually enlightening and enchanting lenses through which we can look at French cuisine.

Unfortunately, the service at times can come off as anything but enlightened. While our waiter was only one of two in this city that have ever been able to understand my bivalve allergy without needing me to make a clam shape with my hands and list everything that comes in such a shell, the front of house is jarringly vapid and inexperienced. One hostess just seemed confused when she accidentally tried to seat the wrong party at the wrong table, awkwardly then bringing them back to the bar to wait even longer for their seats. It's unfortunate that a restaurant this wickedly smart cannot seem to employ anyone with nearly as much thought and focus as those found behind the kitchen doors.

But once one gets past the few incompetencies in service, it's clear that Dirty French is a stylish French bistro that has roared into New York with guns blazing, flashing glamor and arrogance with none of the pomp and circumstance that the old cuisine seems to require. It is a restaurant that embraces a radical way of thinking about French food, and the dining scene in the city is unequivocally better for it.

I came here for my friend's birthday on Thursday around 7pm for drinks and small plates. We sat in the back patio area (covered room). It's very cute! Very chic vibe inside. 

I would come back here for drinks and apps. It's great for friends or for a "drinks" date.

RESTAURANT OVERVIEW:
-Very spacious. There was lots of rooms you can sit in. We sat in the back garden patio area. It's very cute back there - I'd recommend sitting there if it is warm, or sitting inside for a more intimate vibe with dim lighting.
-Very chic/trendy

FOOD:
-Pommes Frites (fries): shaped in a potato chip form. Crunchy on the outside, nice and soft on the inside. Seasoned well and comes with a dip. These were yummy!
-Tartare (tuna tartare): This came with a sheet of what looked like a thin fried egg, but I don't think that's what it was...underneath was the tuna. We took pieces of the thin egg-ish sheet and used it as a cracker for the tuna. This was good!
-Pain Maison (flatbread with cheese): This was also a good dish. Warm, soft bread with melted cheese on top. In the center, was a dab of what tasted like ricotta cheese.
-Jambon Américain (prosciutto with sauce on thick pieces of bread): This was my favorite. It was very good!!

DRINKS:
-Pigalle: This was good. It came with a cinnamon stick in it. I only ordered one and then switched to Old Fashioneds. I liked the Old Fashioned better.
-Old Fashioned: This was great! It should be, because the Old Fashioneds are $17! You are definitely paying for the trendy spot and atmosphere. The drink itself is very well made though. They use standard ingredients - Angostura bitters and whatever whiskey you prefer.

SERVICE:
-Good. We had a very large group (maybe 15 or 20?), and they were good about taking our drink orders for the couple hours we were there.

This place is awesome! Breakfast, lunch, or dinner they kill it. There cocktails are ON POINT. Our server Pamela is the best we've had in NYC. Their whole staff is amazing from the management to the host! Going to be coming back very very soon.

Been waiting to try Dirty French for awhile, and it absolutely lived up to its hype. 

Service was top notch from David. He was super informative and attentive. Some of the best service I've had in awhile. 

For food:

Lamb carpaccio was out of this world. The most tender carpaccio I've ever had. Do not miss it! 

My husband and I had the chicken for dinner. Let me start by saying we NEVER order chicken when dining out but decided to take a chance based on reviews and our waiters advice. It is to die for. Amazing flavors, two different servings that are unique and each bold and juicy. I am already dreaming of it! 

Side dishes- haricots were amazing, simple but delish side. 

Drinks were great as well. I had the Pigalle which is a bourbon drink with chile and cinnamon clove.  Overall great experience in a super trendy environment.

Great food and service. Highlights of the meal for me were the flat bread, jambon American and the country pork ribs. I don't eat oysters but my parents thought these were great. The chicken and crepes is among the most popular dishes. While I enjoyed it very much I think maybe over hyped. The fact it comes in two preparations is cool. I shared with my wife but it can probably feed more than 2 people as we had leftovers. The complimentary flat bread was very buttery and delucious. The frommage blanc served with it paired nicely and made it all very decadent  I definitely look forward to coming back again.

Lunch deal of $20 is so worth it.  Do yourself a favor and take advantage of this high quality and more than satisfying be lunch.  You'll be blown away by the taste, the temperature, the textures, the ambiance, the friendly and efficient waitstaff and the wonderful manager Olivia!

E and I came here for date night on Friday and it was perfect. The ambiance is cozy, intimate with candles, dim lighting and mirrors. It's tres sexy, but nothing to worry about - still classy enough to take the fam if you want! Kind of reminded me of a seductive Balthazar. 

We got two entrees - Meuille feuille with trumpet mushrooms and it came on a bed of corn. It was delicious - buttery, rich and earthy - and the corn's sweetness was a perfect foil for the complex flavor of the mushrooms. We also got the PEI mussels. The sauce was tangy from lemon zest, and the mussels were interspersed with peeky toe crab (although I wished there was more crab). We shared the chicken for two - perfectly cooked, super moist chicken. It comes in 2 courses. The first course is the chicken breast with skin on (yum!), which is very tender and comes in a heavy cream mustard sauce. The second course is the hoisin dark meat chicken legs and thighs. The meat is so sweet and tangy - so good! The crepes are thin and perfect for wrapping the chicken in, and the little rooster accompaniment holds red chilis, basil, cilantro, and other assorted herbs. The chicken is pricey at $36 per person but some of the best chicken we've ever had! It's also a lot of chicken so we took the rest home. Also, no fears on service - our waiter was spot-on, and very attentive. Our table was constantly bused by the waiters in hot pink, and we were very happy with the service. Perhaps management has improved the service based on the earlier reviews? 

In any case, we had a lovely date night and Dirty French was a great find!

My two lady friends and I chose DF to celebrate our mutual friend's birthday last night and were extremely pleased.  From the moment we entered the restaurant, we were warmly greeted and embraced by the lovely hostess and relaxed in the restaurant's ambiance which was created by a decor of candles, perfect lighting and antique mirrors.  Our server was the funny, engaging and friendly Frances who only heightened our experience with her warmth and professionalism.  Usually, i completely ignore any bread that is served to the table and most times, refuse it....however, DF's bread was enticing and delicious, I couldn't resist.  Our table enjoyed the foie gras terrine (even those who had never tried it before) and the mussels as our appetizers.  The main courses included the trout and the chicken/crepes for two.  We also shared a dish of trumpet mushrooms that were delicious.

After such a wonderful experience, we all agreed that we will have to pay DF another visit....and soon.

Figured would take my fiancé here for his birthday in hopes of reliving delicious food experience of Torisi from years ago when it first opened.  Unfortunately, just like Carbone on his last birthday, it is more about the scene than truly good cooking.
Our waiter was super nice - complete contrast from walking up to check in and receiving the nastiest looks and attitude from the hosts.  Telling them my date might be a few minutes late, you would think I was committing a crime.  Actually, it was the most unfriendly welcome service I've ever experienced and usually service doesn't get to me.  Couldn't have walked out then though, they charge a ridiculous $50 per person if you cancel a reservation after 12pm same day.

Like everyone says, the bread with goat cheese spread is very good.
Amuse bouche- usually this is the most delicious part of a meal.  This was the worst. Some sort of fried chickpea, which was burned to a crisp. 
Tuna tartare - too spicy but overall a-okay. Didn't care for the crispy fried crepe served with.
Mille Feuille - did not at all live up to the hype in some of these reviews.  Lacked a good mushroom flavor.  Again, an average a-okay dish.
Duck L'Orange - the worst I have ever had but I have not had many. My fiancé thought it was good.  Inside of the duck tasted too fatty and much too rare, the skin was not at all crispy.  The duck itself was one of the worst things I've ever tasted - raw and rubbery. 
The orange sauce had hints of spices which was quite good and definitely different than your usual orange sauce.  The portion was tiny and ridiculously priced at $39.
Pureed potatoes side - yes, even with the crazy sky high price of the entree, you have to pay 10 bucks for a side.  Good thing this one was delicious.   Thinnest pureed potatoes I have ever seen (picture farina) but absolutely delicious, with what I am guessing is one stick of butter to get them that way.
Chocolate dessert with coconut - quite good, with several different flavor combinations.  (Were told beignets are the thing to order). 

Loved the decor/ambiance.  Can't help to say though that it is really about truly good food for me when dining out.  I would do anything to go back to that modest, regular looking dining room of Torisi for their tasting menu - the nights Torisi was there himself cooking - that was fairly priced with absolutely delicious food.  But once again proves point that what is happening in NYC these days is - unwarranted high prices for food that is average, at best and it is now becoming all about the trendy scene.

Had the most amazing meal there last weekend!! Cannot tell you what an experience this restaurant is from start to finish. Came early from a show and the front door staff couldn't have been more accommodating seating us earlier than reservation. We had a delightful lovely server named Brandy and a fantastic knowledgable sommelier that picked out a gorgeous bottle of wine for my family. The food is beyond every course better than the next!! The Country Ribs are a must try!! This may be my elderly fathers last trip to the city and I cannot tell you what a special experience this staff and chefs provide!!! An unforgettable night my thanks to Dirty French this is what dining is all about!!

Sub-par food, passé decor and even worse service. 

Not being famished my friend and I decided to split a dozen oysters, we both ordered a salad and some side vegetables and a bottle of wine. After our order was taken by a water who would be better suited for working at a sing-a-long restaurant in the theater district the host came up to us and said that we could only sit if we ordered a full dinner and asked us to move to the back lounge. His delivery was about as appealing as the Panama hat perched on his head which makes complete sense since it was evening and inside a hotel restaurant. To avoid any further unwanted attention we obliged and were moved to the back and seated at a bistro table that couldn't even hold the food we ordered. It seemed as though when we divorced our prior table we didn't manage to get custody over a waiter, not Cheyenne Jackson or any of the others. We finished our tiny non-table-worthy meal and figured another drink couldn't hurt but after waiting for another 30 minutes to get the attention of a staff member we opted for the check. Overall it comes across as a chain restaurant parading around as a chic french boutique eatery with poor management. If it were in Des Moines, Iowa I may give it another shot but in a city chock full of delicious food and great service I would skip it.

Best brunch in the L.E.S. 
Lunch is also a great option for this area. 

French toast sticks are amazing, the lamb burger is the best there is. Best French dip in the city.

5 stars for decor. 5 stars for the service. Waiter was super attentive. 3.5 for the food. For all the interesting facts that the waiter gave nothing really knocked my socks off excepts for the complimentary nan bread. That was goooood. Also the drinks were too strong to the point that they were not so enjoyable. All in all it was a good experience just wish the food was special. I found it to be good, not bad, but just good. 

We had:
Lamb
Tuna tartar
Mushrooms
Pomme frites
And the fish
This place is amazing!  The bread and the chicken - yes the chicken!!!  The service can be spotty - but the food makes up for everything

Dirty French was more like dirty bridge and tunnel, with a tacky bar crowd and even tackier service staff.  The hatted host was ineffective, and we were seated more than an hour after  our 10 pm reservation.  The service was slow and unhelpful.  The food was mediocre at best, with three recommendations that were  bland and boring.  I'm sorry that I took my wife here on what was supposed to be a great night.  Awful.

Bad from start to finish. Do not believe any positive buzz. Food was bad. Service was worse. Host had horrific breath and seated us 45 minutes after our 10:15 pm reservation. Repeated excuses regarding the delay. Surrounded by horrible bridge and tunnel crowd. No real New Yorkers to be found and for good reason. Heinous, appalling excuse for an It restaurant. Do not waste your time or energy. This place had nothing to offer. Even the bartender was bad. A one star review is too high for this poor excuse of an eatery whose fifteen minutes in the sun is definitely up.

What a treat! Terrific service and excellent food. Had the Duck L'Orange and Millefeuille, (actually mushrooms over sweetcorn curry!) really indulgent. Broad wine selection and fine cocktails. The desserts are sumptuous. A few menu items were sold-out, likely due to the late Sunday reservation. Certainly worth the price of admission.

Oh holy hell this place is amazing.  Enjoyed a wonderful dinner with 5 of my friends last night.  We ate almost everything on the menu; the jambon american, ahi tartare, foie terrine, millefeuille, etouffee, pistou, meunière, Duck à l'Orange, Au Poivre, chicken and crepes, and finally the cote de boeuf.

At the top of my list of enjoyment was the foie terrine, Duck à l'Orange and cote de boeuf.  That is not to say that any and all of the other offerings were not delicious in their own right, because they are, but my favorites just blew it out of the water.

The staff was amazing, they neither hovered too much nor too little, attentive to the very end (and yes, we closed down the joint) and not overbearing in the least.  I am an absolute sucker for this kind of service.  I will most definitely be returning.  WELL DONE DIRTY FRENCH!

(Also, I could probably survive entirely on the delicious flatbread alone)

We didn't end up having dinner at Dirty French.  This one star is for their reservations systems.  

If you make a reservation at DF and cancel the day of, they will charge $50/per person.  I'm totally fine with this requirement because it prevents the restaurant from dealing with last minute cancellations and should help them plan their seatings better.... right?

We show up for our 8 pm reservation at 8:07 pm.  The host tells us that there are a couple of tables wrapping up, so I gave him my number to text me when the table was ready.  Both of us where hungry, so I also told him we might eat elsewhere if it's too long of a wait.  

I got a text at 9:11 pm that they had a table ready.  For a 9 pm reservation, that would have been great.  For an 8 pm reservation, I find that ridiculously late.  By 9:11 pm, we were already seated at Wildar and having an AMAZING meal.  And btw, we waited on DF until 8:45 pm before sitting down at Wildair.

DF - Manage your seating times better!!!  

I highly recommend you skip through the hassle of going to Dirty French and walk a couple of blocks south to WIldair.  We had a delicious meal of Olive Oil & Bread, Scallop Crudo, Beef Tartare, and Spicy Tuna.... and the total came out to be less than $50.  Service at Wildair was super friendly and warm, and the atmosphere was relaxed.  They had their windows open, so we could enjoy the fall air.  Just go there instead.

Great overall experience! Our bartender made a perfect vieux carre while giving us great ideas of other nearby cocktail spots to check out and our server steered us perfectly to the amazing lamb carpaccio, sea bass and hanger steak. The flat bread with some magical butter to start was a wonderful alternative to the basic baguette you would offer in most French restaurants. The sommelier guided us to a great Syrah and the 80s music was popping.
Certainly will be back.

I have to start by saying ... We knew someone... So on that note... The service was phenomenal (biased but still..) The food: I'd say 70% of it was f*ing amazing but the 30% that wasn't was pretty bad, not just a little bad. It's super hi energy, loud, bustling, great for a girls night (or boys night there's a cote de boeuf) but it's expensive and not everything is worth the price. An experience I'd say, try it maybe once for an occasion (ie birthday)


Flatbread Bread 5: served with formage blanc and heavenly definitely one of the best things there.

Grilled oysters 2: it was okay, I'm not a huge fan of parsley and it was covered, like caked around the oyster so thick the oyster was lost.

Lamb carpaccio 4: I loved it! It wasn't gamey it had a delicious sauce and I usually don't like eggplant but even the eggplant was good!

Tuna tartare 2: meh I've had better it had nothing going for it. It wasn't bad but it wasn't good, just completely forgettable and a waste of space in my belly.

Asparagus: I actually try it but my friends loved it so maybe it's good.

Millefeuille 4: yum!!! I love mushrooms if you live mushrooms too you'll love it. Even if you don't love mushrooms you might like it as long as the reason you don't like mushrooms is the texture... The texture is definitely mushroomy texture.

Endive Cajun shrimp salad 3: pretty good salad I could have this as an entree for lunch or something...the shrimp was definitely cajuny but not overkill, complemented salad very well.

Country ribs 1: TOO smoky, I felt like I was licking a smoker. Bleh!!! 

Chicken and crepe 5: omg please order this! It comes with crepes and some veggies and 2 sauces and oh my god it's soooo good!! The white meat comes out first then the dark on the bone and both are amazing 

Lamb 0: yuck! Super gamey and it was super rare.

Duck 3: meh

Trout 4: it was good very good but can't quite remember why... Was pretty buzzed at this point.

Beignets 3: meh good but nothing special 

Sorbet 5: can't f that up 

Gateau (Chocolate with coconut sorbet) 3: i not a huge chocolate person but the coconut sorbet was amazing

Lemon tart 4: LOOOOVVEEEE lemony desserts!

One of my favorite restaurants in nyc. If youre two, you should get the chicken and crepe thing dont remember the exact name but it is for two people. It is AMAZING. youre not gonna be regretful believe me. And their bread is soooooo good.

Ok so a group of 5 of us went last night with extremely high expectations.  I had read tons of articles and reviews and couldn't wait to try Dirty French. And here we are today thinking about the dinner-what we all agreed upon was that this place rocks!!! Big 5 stars. There wasn't a single thing that we tried( and we tried many different dishes) that we didn't absolutely love.  Keep in mind that we aren't the easiest to satisfy as 2 require gluten free and 1 is a pescatarian.  Our only complaint was the the wine service was a tad slow and the pre dinner drink service in the lobby area was even slower. But at the end of the day-dinner there is a must.  Enjoy their oysters, mushroom,salads, ribs, tuna, fabulous sides and awesome desserts and smile widely.  Well done Dirty French.

This came very close to being a two star review and then became a four star one in an instant.  Read the story - it has a happy ending. 

We made a same-day Sunday reservation at Dirty French for 12:15.  Due to a combination of faulty map applications and delayed subways, I got to the restaurant around 12:35.  They had held our table and we sat immediately.

We were starving and pretty excited to order.  After a few minutes, we noticed that the tables around us were having their orders taken, but not us.  Strange, but it was busy, so we waited.  After 15-20 minutes of this (before you chastise me for not speaking up, remember that I was 15-20 minutes late for my reservation), someone finally came to give us water.  He didn't appear to be a waiter, but when we said we were ready for food, he took our order.  We ordered three items.

A bread selection was delivered to our table.  We received a donut, two Madeleines, and monkey bread.  I love that these were not only complimentary, but delicious.  The donut was incredible and the other pastries were nothing to laugh at.  Scarfed this down.  Food was off to an excellent start.  

After some more waiting, we were not checked in on and the table next to us was all but wrapping up.  Our food eventually came out, and it was brought by a busser.  I would have not said anything about not being assigned a server, except no condiments or drinks ever came out.  We asked for ketchup.  We waited some more.  Nothing.  

Here's where our luck changed.  One of the managers proactively approached our table.  He could tell we were annoyed and, without being prompted, he explained that our table had slipped through the cracks and hadn't been assigned a server.  He then proceeded to bring me my drink, bring out the ketchup, and comp our entire meal. Yes, you heard me right there.  While I was personally pretty shocked that it wasn't simply a round of drinks, I was glad that he recognized how our experience had been and was intent on rectifying it.  That guy gets five stars himself.  Not to get off topic, but I've always had similar experiences at Major Food Group restaurants - I was at Parm during a black out and had similar treatment.  The people at these restaurants are fantastic.

Onto the food!  Once we got our full meal, we were blown away by the food.  I got the eggs Benedict which was incredible.  The cook on the eggs and the hollandaise sauce were on point.  We also got the duck hash which was AWESOME.  I don't even like hashes generally speaking.  I ordered the lilikoi drink which was great since it wasn't too sweet.

At the end of the meal, as promised, everything was comped - and they brought out spoons.  Complimentary dessert.  See the picture - self explanatory.  I was stuffed but I managed to make some room to consume it.  

In the end, our not-so-hot experience was turned into a much better one.  The food was great anyway but the service was even better.  They went above and beyond to ensure a positive experience.  Do I expect something comped every time something goes wrong?  Not at all.  But I appreciated their willingness to admit their mistakes up front - before we had to have the awkward experience of asking for a manager.  I will definitely be back.  Dirty French has gained a fan.

Another DISASTER in the CARBONE WORLD. The Duck L'Orange was like two undercooked fatty slivers that were taken from an overweight Jeffrey Dallmer victim. Everything was oversalted. Terrible preparation hiding under the pretense of cutting edge cuisine. The biggest mistake we made, besides eating there, was not going to Katz's (around the corner) and eating real food. One positive...the room is quite nice, if they could only serve food that was at the same level

This is a great place to eat before you go out in the LES, but the food was generally just OK with the exception of the main courses and dessert, which were pretty good. 

Food: 
Flatbread: delicious
Duck rillette with foie gras: would not order this again; the foie was not very flavorful and the duck did not taste very good
Mushroom millefeuille with curry sauce and butternut squash: very good
Brussel sprouts: on the very salty side
Duck l'orange: the duck was delicious and tender; the sides were not (why bother?)
Trout: this was soft and delicious with butter all over 
Lemon torte with meringue: pretty good

Waited an hour for our reservation... ok, it was Halloween Sat but??.... Waiter asked for my order, then informed me I had the wrong menu! How'd that happen?? (trick or treat?) ... Scored a 'free' bowl of lettuce for my trouble (nice salad dressing) and a kind of pizza bread, but was pressured to order as everyone at the table was salivating (and forced to drink second round of $$martinis).... food is delicious as it SHOULD be as the tab was enough to feed the subcontinent (you know 50cents could feed a child somewhere outside of the Bowery...) ...

This place is pretty cool. I have never been to the lower east side. We came for brunch on Sunday and we really went to town. My favorite was the ham plate and I thoroughly enjoyed everything.YOU MUST ORDER THIS!  Our server was fabulous and super friendly. I had two bloody mary cocktails and I was in heaven. 

I strongly suggest coming here if you are given the opportunity. The decor is also pretty cool as well.

I don't understand why all the buzz about this restaurant. The place is huge and so loud, it feels more like a lobby of a clubby hotel rather than a restaurant. 

We ordered a lot of appetizers, duck, lamb and some side dishes. Most of them were tasty but I could barely enjoy anything because it was so greasy. Don't get me wrong I love my fat, big flavor and French cuisine. This restaurant complete overdoes it though!!! My food was literally half submerged in fat.
I had the most amazing time at Dirty French, the food was great, and the service was impeccable! Everyone is so friendly! I can't wait to go back!

I knew this place had a great atmosphere so it would be perfect place to take friends who were in from out of town but I didn't count on how good the food will be.  Seriously, there are plenty of places that serve decent food and are fun so you go and you pay. 
Dirty French doesn't settle when it could, instead it exceeds expectation. 

A trifecta has to be met for 5 stars, and the night we went it definitely was. 

1) Service -- Lovely. Bruno the sommelier was awesome as was our waitress, we asked for three portions of the bread they serve (which I dubbed "crack" bread bc it was so good) and they obliged w/o batting an eye. 

2) Food -- see "crack" bread above. The fish I had was perfectly cooked and I like the concept of melding all of these French inspired cuisines. 

3) Ambiance -- so much fun. The reason I initially picked Dirty French and one of the several I will return. 

The one draw back is they get booked up so early, it's insane. If you want to eat at 8:30 on a Turs/ Fr/ Sat book well in advance. My planning skills aren't as developed so I'm left with the 10:30pm reservation and the place is still packed.

Deux Stars for Dirty French

Dirty French is a trendy restaurant nestled inside the Ludlow Hotel. I had made 6:30 reservations for this restaurant on a Friday evening. Upon entering the restaurant, my friend and I had informed the hostess that the 3rd person in our party would be 10-15 minutes late. The hostess assured us that this was not a problem, and that she would seat us as soon as possible- we were seated around 6:50.  Upon being seated, my friend and I ordered a bottle of wine, and perused the menu. On two separate occasions (within a 10 minute time frame), the waitress came over to our table to ask when the third member of our party would be arriving. She then came back a third time to tell us that if we did not order soon they would have to rush us out. Luckily the third member in our party came soon after, and we all ordered our meals immediately. 

As far as food goes, the Steak Au Poivre, the Pommes Purée and the Haricots Asiatique were phenomenal. Each of us cleaned our plates and could not get over how well prepared everything was. That being said, I can confidently say that I will not be returning to Dirty French solely because our waitress was so rude. Upon finishing our meals, the waitress immediately brought us the check. She then proceeded to come back to the table 2 times (within a 5-7 minute time frame)  to see if we were ready to pay (at this point in time we took the hint, and paid the bill). She then returned to our table a THIRD time and rudely said that while she wasn't exactly kicking us out, if we wanted to continue talking, we would need to relocate to the restaurant's lounge. UM- no thanks. 

At this point in time I looked at my watch, it was 8:06- we had been seated at our table for a little over an hour and this woman was rudely pushing us out. Maybe it's me, but I just can't return to a restaurant where such little value is placed on the customer. The food and atmosphere at Dirty French was great, but the service... not so much, and in my opinion without good service there's no way you can have a great restaurant.

Dirty French was the perfect location for a leisurely lunch with a friend. We started with some bubbles and the ahi tuna served on a delicious crepe with some greens - absolutely delicious! The bread served with our meal was also divine. 

For our next course we shared the chevre salad with crunchy sunchokes and pears. It was a perfect fall salad! I don't always love fruit in my salad but the combination of flavors was spot on. I've been looking for something similar in Philly ever since! 

Finally, we shared the roasted chicken and amazingly hot, crisp, perfectly-salted pommes frites. The frites were thick-cut and served with an incredible aioli. 

Service was great and very accommodating with the fact that we were not in a rush and wanted to space out our meal. I'm very excited to have another go-to restaurant while in New York!
Went on subday night with my husband, setting was incredible: great crowd, great music, the tartare was great, the duck amazing. Didn't think much of the millefille, lamb carpaccio or the beignets.

Fantastic service, food, drinks and experience. The ambiance is very nice, bartenders very knowledgeable and attentive. Had the tuna tartare that was unique, and delicious. The beef short rib in an incredible sauce, perfectly cooked. The roasted squash will change anyones mind that hasn't liked squash before. The wine by the glass list is simple and to the point, with bartenders happy to walk you through deciding the right one to accompany you meal and your night. I will definitely be back.

I love everything about this place! Food, atmosphere, drinks. The duck was delicious and I love their take on fries (sliced long wise and served with sour cream). This bread with cheese that they serve with the meal is AMAZING. I've actually been back just because I want that bread and cheese :-)

A space that feels new and old simultaneously is a joy. Add a touch of quirky service personality and a delightful menu and you have a winner! Breakfast options are included in your Hotel stay at The Ludlow and you can upgrade (at a cost) to other items. Brunch was amazing and a big thank you to the uber charming Pamela for her service and care! Lunch is a leisurely affair - if you are in a rush - maybe not your first choice. I love this spot and will return!

Went here for brunch on a Sunday -- the lamb burger was tasty, as were the pastries they brought for the table.  My friends weren't as impressed with their egg dishes.  Unfortunately, the service was really bizarre.  There seemed to be about as many waitstaff as patrons, but it took us 20-30 minutes to get coffee refills, water, etc., even after a couple of reminders.  After our plates were finally cleared, a new waitress came to tell us about dessert, pausing every few seconds to space out and look around the restaurant, and finally telling us she had no idea why she had come to our table.  Two minutes after she left, another waiter unceremoniously dropped our check on the table.  He was startled when we burst out laughing, but we weren't going to bother with dessert at that point.  All in all, the food was largely good, but I don't think I'll be rushing back any time soon. I hope that the dinner service is better!

Service is atrocious. Made us wait over an hour for a reservation we made over a month ago. We were driven to the bar to wait for our table where the bar staff were just as complacent and undue. We are finally seated, and waited on by a glorious waiter, who was more than attentive. It seems her management feels that they only need two waiters to handle the entire restaurant.  The worst thing was the host promised to "take care of us" and send a bunch of extras over and we never received a single thing.  Not acceptable to not follow through. 
Food is phenomenal, waitstaff phenomenal-management blows.

***Contrary to popular belief: YOU DO NOT NEED A RESERVATION!***

We were wondering where to have dinner after leaving Meow Parlour when my friend said "Have you been to Dirty French?" I went on a whole spiel about overhearing ladies in my yoga class complaining about how difficult it was to score a reservation even a month in advance and was pretty sure we would be turned away. Instead, he was like "Well, it was raved by the NYT, so lets give it a shot since we're practically here." Well guess what, I love being wrong for the better lol. We approached the host reservation-less and they were super accomodating. We were seated in the enclosed garden which was lovely! 

Our server was absolutely the sweetest!  We spotted Frank Lampard at the bar and my friend was starstruck. +1 for celebrity sightings. 

Service is extraordinarily polite and lovely. Bread is unique and tasty. Millefeuille a must-get, oysters fresh, and scallops on point. 

Bathrooms downstairs.
Had a decent meal and i liked the lounge. swanky place with good food and cocktails.  nice place to take a date.

What a lively place with the best collection of 80's music! Service was wonderful and the entire staff did so much to make sure we had a great experience- starting with a booth seat which I would highly recommend. The mushroom appetizer was delicious and unique with curry flavors. The duck l'orange was wonderful (wish they gave a bit more). We did share that our cod and tuna tartar were way too salty and we just couldn't eat them. As a result the highly apologetic manager took them off our bill and gave us a free dessert. I am chalking it up as a one-off salt lick issue and would still come back here again. Great place for a group or couples dinner.

KenScale: 8.0/10

It's been a while since I visited Dirty French. I wanted to check in and see how the restaurant and its decadent French cuisine have evolved over time. The super-chef duo of Mario Carbone and Rich Torrisi certainly don't mess around. As with my previous experience, there were some really big flavors; on the other hand, there were still some mixes that made it hard to justify the hefty price tag at this constantly buzzing restaurant.

The highlight of my meal last time was the mushroom millefeuille with green curry. This time, the dish instead came with yellow squash curry, and I still liked it as much as last time. One of my dining companions who is a lifelong vegetarian certainly approved of this dish. Another dining companion was really looking forward to grilled oysters with garlic and parsley and absolutely loved it, as did I. It was one of the most luscious oyster dishes I've had in a while. I also loved salmon maison (think lox but in more extravagant form) that was more or less perfectly cured. I didn't have the famed chicken and crepes last time and had the appetite to try it this time. First came the white meat that came with mustard sauce; it was alright, but the meat could've been more tender and the mustard sauce felt a bit overpowering at times. On the other hand, the dark meat portion that you can wrap in crepes was more successful; it somewhat reminded me to Peking duck dish with French twist. I enjoyed the rich flavor of the dish and you can spice it up a bit more with pepper. Desserts were somewhat mixed. Preserved lemon tarte with almond was nicely executed, but not particularly mind-blowing, while chocolate fondant with coconut sorbet was a bit too sweet for my paste. 

The restaurant is still overflowing with people and getting a reservation is still very hard to pull off unless you're willing to dine at really early or late dinner hours. It still has that trendy vibe but if could also overwhelm you with all the craziness and noise surrounding the dining room. If you're looking for an extravagant dinner in a chic setting, Dirty French is still the place to try; just make sure to book early or show up early and try your luck at the walk-in tables.

Food: pastries on the house. Can't go wrong. Brunch: duck hash was so so. Duck was dry and the potatoes where so deep fried it as borderline hard to chew on.

Place: decent spot. Not too tightly spaced spot.

Took 35 minutes past our reservation to seat us but did not offer water while we were waiting, so that was a disappointment.

Even after we were seated the service was very slow. We finally got to order our food 15 minutes after sitting down. The waiter offered a glass of champagne on the house to make up for the wait. He was sweet but It seemed like they were understaffed the entire time, so I think they'd do better on the service front if they had more people working during the peak hours.

Also, the dip sold out by the time we were ordering, so they should step up the planning game too. 

The great food made up for the service. The lamb burger was amazing and came with a side of steak fries, which was top notch too, I didn't try anything else so can't speak for other dishes but all of my friends thoroughly enjoyed their food. 

The entire experience was pleasant because of the cute decor and good food but I would be annoyed if the service was this slow again during my next visit.

We came here for a birthday with a party of five.  We were seated right away in a booth in the corner.  The service was excellent.  They kept our waters full and someone was always coming by to check on us.  I was surprised about the menu.  I get that this is progressive traditional French cuisine, not Americanized.  But the only chicken option was for two people, there was no salmon, no onion soup, etc.  I split the mussels appetizer with my sister and that was very good.  It could have been a meal.  I ordered the trout as my main course and that was great.  Generous size and very flavorful.  My sister got the bass and it was a much smaller piece and it was floating in a bowl with a green broth.  It looked so unappetizing. I would have sent it back.  

We also got a side of pomme frites and mashed potatoes.  The pomme frites were nothing special, even not good.  The mashed potatoes were the best mashed potatoes on this earth.  They were amazing.  I tried not to tell the others about it so I could have more to myself.

We also got a bottle of pino gree which none of us really liked.  For dessert we shared the beignets which were okay.  I probably would not come back.  For the price you can find more satisfying food elsewhere.
Another amazing experience at Dirty French! The Trout Meunière was fabulous! Thanks Jaimie and Diego!!

I can't figure out what all the hype was about. When making reservation on open table, we choose the 5:30 over the 10:30 pm option. When I arrived the place was empty. It did fill up fast, but was still not full at 7pm when we left. I ordered the vegetarian special: artichoke and sunchoke in a phyllo dough with black truffles appetizer- sounds great right? Was really mushy and tasteless and $43. I expected it to be expensive bc it had truffles but I didn't even taste the truffles at all. It was very bland. I then had the beet and roquefort salad- two of my favorite things. It had so much orange zest on it, it was inedible and we sent it back. My friend ordered the duck which was the most unappetizing presentation I have ever seen (someone else posed a picture on yelp of this) so it must just be me, but looked like two raw slabs of meat with a layer of fat. After we finished our $17 glasses of wine, we decided to have a drink down the street elsewhere. I would not recommend and would definitely not go back. Over priced and tasteless.

ahhhh dirty french. you are so so dirtyy, just the way I like it. 
what can I say? This place was wonderful. From the moment we walked until my last bite of ice cream.. the service was impeccable. Luckily, my friend was able to get last minute reservations for a Sunday evening dinner to celebrate my birthday. Our host, Jeff, made my night. He was sweet, attentive, and thoughtful. Jeff noticed I was looking through the pictures on Yelp trying to figure out what to order so he recommended a couple of dishes to us. with his insightful knowledge we ended up ordering the millefeuille, lamb carpaccio, meunière, and duck l'orange with a side of pommes frites. 

Let's start w the appetizers. 
Both of us really enjoyed the lamb carpaccio.. I am not a big fan of lamb but this dish bought lamb into a new light. It was seasoned with olives, black pepper, olive oil and some green peppers. Eating the lamb w the warm toast was delicious. The thinly sliced meat quickly melted in my mouth and made me want more! we had to ask for more bread since the dish was so savory we took smaller portions of lamb so we could enjoy it longer. The millefeuille was a bit too salty for me. It came with squash sauce that complimented each other. It does looks pretty interesting how the mushrooms were thinly sliced and well put together. 

As an avid potato lover I was excited to try their pommes frites. Thanks yelpers for the rec! we both enjoyed this side dish. it's thinly sliced potatoes accompanied with a lightly spiced sour cream herb spread. Some pieces were a little too crispy but the spread made up for it. 
The duck was my favorite dish of the night. I am so glad I listened to Jeff's recommendations. I loved everything about it from the crusted skin to the juicy meat. It paired well w the leeks and this side sauce... 
The meunière was interesting. The sound of buttery fish lured me to try it but it was a bit too heavy for us. We had a hard time finishing this dish towards the end. it was dressed with a lot of sesame seeds on top. 
Overall food was 4/5. Sooo why did I give this establishment 5 stars? Well because of Jeff. He had noticed my friend handing me a gift and asked if we were celebrating something. At the end of our meal we were stuffed and didn't have any room for dessert. Jeff insisted that I pick out an ice cream flavor so I could at least end the night by blowing out a candle. I opted to get the banana bread. When he bought it out there was a candle on the side for me to make my wish and blow it out. Thank you Jeff for being such a wonderful host / waiter. I couldn't have asked for a better meal.

Great atmosphere and food all around. 

Got the tuna tartare and lamb carpaccio to start- both were great though the carpaccio in particular was excellent. 

Had the trout and duck for entrees. I'd avoid the trout the next time. It wasn't bad just nothing special in comparison to the duck.
For sides you can't go wrong but the verte and Brussels sprouts were spot on.

Sorry to be negative as we love the Torrisi guys other joints but this was the worst meal of 2015. The appropriate moniker would be "greasy French". Everything ordered, from leeks in an oily batter, to overly oily trout, to, you know, oily potatoes was so petroleum laden that no one in our party could finish. Service and staff were lovely but the chef really needs to dry out the food.   It's a costly restaurant and they should do much better. Have had so many great meals at other Torrisi restaurants it really pains to write this but it feels like an obligation to the yelp community

Great five, fun atmosphere and great hotel bar experience. The waitstaff at the hostess desk were fun and welcoming.  The table and bar service were disappointing and attentive and distracted often. Menu list fun different and everything that you would hoped for in a trendy French restaurant. Unfortunately the food was very disappointing. It was heavily over sausage and I love the presentation nice and not nearly as wonderful as it could have been. 

Sad to say I would recommend it for a drink but I would not recommend it for food.

Went on a busy Friday night to celebrate my college graduation. The hospitality my friends and I were shown was second to none. It's really amazing when you experience a restaurant where the food is sublime and the service feels like a hug from a best friend. Way to go, Major Good Group!

Dirty French is, smash your plate on the floor because it's so f@&king good, good. The grilled oysters were out of this bloody world. Because we were seated late, they brought out an extra appetizer on the house, tuna tartare (blew my mind). We had the ribs and duck for our main course and I cannot describe the yumminess. Yes I can, it's slap yo mama, good. The service was really good. They were very sweet and apologetic about the delay and made sure we were well taken care of once we were seated. No attitude, no hype, no fake glossy BS. Just good ass food, great ambiance, and fun 80's throwback music. We will definitely come back when we're in NYC again.

Food, yes. Cocktails, yes. Ambiance, fantastic. But I just had the most mortifying experience when they accused me of stealing...

To give context; 

They give you beautiful knives with your meal. Gorgeous, fancy knives. I noticed them. I did try to ascertain who made them by wiping the blade to see the engaving. Maybe that was a big mistake. 

At the end of our meal, our sweet waiter came over and said "I don't want to make any assumptions..." I cut him off, assuming he was about to let us know he was getting ready to leave. I've been waitress for 15 years. I wanted to assure him we were finished and that bringing the check would be fine. But, as it turns out, he was trying to tell us he'd have to charge us for the "green knife" that was sitting right on the table (under my napkin) and had been assumed stolen. 

I would never steal a steak knife. I just wouldn't. I've worked in New York restaurants forever and I would never put a fellow service person in that position. Also, like, morals. But that's beside the point...

The point is, obviously this happens all the time, and obviously their thief-dar is set to hair trigger. And mayyyyyybe if they're so worried about their fancy knives they should use less fancy knives. I dunno. I don't blame the waiter. He was professional and great and was put in a bad spot. But... I'll just never go back. It was such a demoralizing experience. 

I'm not a huge believer in Yelp reviews that completely obfuscate the point of everything (the food!), but the vibe was so ruined for me I had to say something. I hope maybe they read this re-evaluate their apparent mistrust in their customers.

THE SERVICE HERE IS AMAZING!!!!  

I picked this place for my birthday brunch after seeing it featured on "Masters of None". This place lived up to hollywood hype and everything was so delicious! 

I loved the service here, we had the best waitress and she even gave us a tasty little drink to celebrate my birthday!  Oh, and because it was brunch she brought out a little sweets tray early to make sure we got one since it was the last one!  

I loved the look of this place!  Its a LES gem and everything you want to see in a real NYC restaurant.

A very five-star worthy restaurant experience. I thought this place was all hype - and I usually find French cuisine overrated - but nope, this place made me believe.

Service here is absolutely amazing. When we walked in for dinner without reservations, the main dining room was full and reservations had it booked until 11PM. However, the host MADE SURE we got a table. Looking back, I wish I would've tipped him for his effort in this as my party and I would never have gotten a chance to eat here if it were not for him. Owner, if you are reading this, he wore a fedora and had a slight accent - give that man a raise! Great start to the night.

Ambiance is dimly lit, a little bit noisy but still able to have a conversation. Music is late eighties pop-rock. Some Prince was involved. Toward the back is a better lit area, reminding me of a ski lodge - Christmas lights galore. It was a bit more homey. The drinking area also has couches - a little reminiscent of Raines without the privacy.

Waiter (who was from Montenegro) made excellent recommendations, especially for my vegetarian friend. Let's start with the food:

Complementary House Flatbread came with a strong but not sharp fromage. Bread had the right amount of salt and the cheese had a strong pleasant flavor - slightly sweet.

Get the Ludlow Gimlet. The best cocktail I've had in a restaurant. It's like drinking a cold cinnamon apricot.

Hors d'Oeuvre: each plate was very plentiful - almost enough for an entree.
- Millefeuille. Trumpet mushroom had a distinct favor but the squash curry is what made it. Smooth and kind of sweet but nothing was overpowering. Even squash and mushroom haters would find this dish delicious.
- Carpaccio - Plentiful, comes with bread. Did not eat this but friend enjoyed it.

- Chevre Salad: They made the Artichoke and Pear really stand out.

- Chicken and Crepes were very rich. That's all I can say - I'm not a fan of chicken skin but the sauce made it work.

Accompaniments:
- String beans, Pomme Frites (comes with a smoky cheese), and brussel sprouts were great - nothing that would blow your mind though. It's not meant to be a main course anyway.

The real star was the dessert though. The Beignets dish: one of the best desserts I've ever had. Not necessarily the beignet but the caramel-chicory dipping sauce was one of a kind. Not too viscous and fits the lightly powdered beignet perfectly.

Without a doubt, this restaurant is worth every penny.

Had a bit of a wait for brunch, even after making a reservation, but boy was it worth it. I can't even remember what else we ate because the duck hash was one of the dankest dishes I've ever had in my life. My mouth is watering just thinking about it. They should change the name of the dish to Dank Duck. If you order anything at this place, it must be the duck hash; you won't regret it.

Came for dinner, as soon as you walk in the place just has a "cool trendy" vibe. The host was very fashionable, you couldn't miss him which definitely sets the scene.  

On to the food, to summarize, De-li-cous! Oysters fresh and buttery, Lamb Carpaccio came and went at the snap of the fingers, omg the bread! Those who don't eat bread were devouring, that good! (never thought I would include bread in a review but it deserves a mention) Ahu tuna Tar Tare, yumm...Grilled Oysters delicious as well (I preferred the raw though) Mashed potatoes were especially creamy and buttery, definitely one of the best. the entree I got was the Duck al Orange and its not a preparation I have tried before. Simply amazing. 

TLDR - Trendy, Sexy people and even sexier food that will leave you tastebuds very happy (but maybe not your wallet)

Friends of ours had recommended this restaurant located in the Ludlow Hotel, just below Houston. A Monday nite @ 5:30. We were the first ones there and boy did the room fill up to capacity! The decor has an arty, rustic modern feel with retro designer fiurnishings. The cuisine was French with a Moroccan flair. And it was over-the-top. We couldn't help ourselves,We ordered two appetizers, salad and a main course for 2+2 desserts. Every single item we ordered was absolutely delicious. Our server, Vanessa, couldn't have been more professional and personable. She made the evening even more delightful. Don't think twice, this restaurant is where you want to be.

Precisely what I wanted/expected out of a New York restaurant; great food, hip, but relaxed ambiance, interesting decor and layout, good wait staff, stiff drinks, and above all outstanding food.  My confession: I planned on eating at Katz's Delicatessen, but the line was down the block so I bailed, and mercifully Dirty French is located to catch the disappointed Katz's refugee.   I'm glad I didn't get into Katz's.  The waiter immediately brought a hot focaccia with herbed fromage blanc, which took me over the center field wall. Out freaking standing.  Ordered The Dip - dry aged beef sandwich on french bread laced with what I'm convinced is an addictive chemical in the boursin-like spread.  The hot au jus coupled with the french bread on a cold day made me exceptionally satisfied.  We ordered the Imperial Planters Punch (listed on the menu 'for two') and this concoction did not let us down.  Served in a large pitcher along with fine bone china tea cups.  You must try this cocktail. Next important confession: the night before we ate at the three Michelin star restaurant Jean Georges, but Dirty French satisfied me far more than the expensive JG. I expected to be blown out of the water by Jean Georges, but wasn't - it was good, but as my wife explained the cuisine is bordering on the 'unreachable'.  The Dirty French bistro style fare is far more satisfying, familiar, and quite 'reachable'.  The Dip dry aged beef sandwich marked a high point in my culinary assessment of Big Apple eateries, and created a desire to re-visit this outstanding bistro.  You know right away that no matter what you order here you will not be let down.  The only thing I didn't really go crazy for were the pomme frites.  I would have preferred shoestring fries to the large russet cut offering, but I did not refrain from stuffing three or four down my gullet, due to the fromage dip that accompanied them.  The waiter was young, attentive, laid back, friendly and quite cheerful. 
Note to management: the dining area was wonderfully warm on a cold day, making the experience so welcoming.  I will return on my next trip to New York.

Grim Eater Approved.

Oh my god.  Food is pretty good.  Music is beyond horrible.  I am a child of the 70's, so I basically grew up in the 80's.  The music they play here is horrible.  Beyond horrible.  Straight out of the early 80's.  Totally intolerable.  It's like the dance hall culture club meets butter sauce and meat. It totally ruins the vibe.  I wouldn't come back here if you paid me.  As I write this review they are blasting invisible touch by Phil Collins.  Come on people.  This is 2016.

You must eat the DUCK! Vous devez manger Canard à l'Orange! "Duck a L'Orange" is a phenomenal French classic. I've had dozens of duck dishes in my life, but how about 2 big pieces of roasted duck that take up to a month to make? The skin is thin and crispy. The duck is so soft that its melt in your mouth. I thought the duck is tiny (because it's French, duh), but no my stomach was filled up contentedly. Imagine a whole duck, it must be ridiculously large before dry-aging. Check out this article to see how it takes 30 days to make duck at Dirty French: http://ny.eater.com/2014/10/30/7078243/dirty-french-rich-torrisi-duck-lorange-photos#4329920. 

I found Dirty French from Master of None, and now I see why Aziz Ansari is so crazy about this place. From appetizers to entrees, everything is meticulous and precise. The ambiance is not at all formal. Some customers even proudly sang along and danced to the music at a table. I guess they didn't expect to hear their favorite hit songs from the 80s besides a nice dinner.

There are seemingly endless Brunch options in the city, but Dirty French is a particularly good one with extremely high quality dishes.

Star 1: How were the service and atmosphere?

You know, I honestly can't place the decor here at Dirty French, but there's abundant seating and a great crowd of fast and knowledgable servers who, in the case of my party of four, lead us all to fantastic dishes. Make a reservation - obviously. Star Granted. 

Star 2: How were the portions relative to the cost?

A friend and I split two dishes (the Duck Hash and the French Dip sandwich), and if I recall correctly they were $21 and $18 respectively. While the portions weren't massive, the dishes were filling in their own right, and as you'll see they were of very high quality. Also of note here is that each table gets a tray of four exceptional pastries, so it's essentially a free dessert. Star Granted. 

Stars 3 and 4: How was the food?

Very good. The Duck Hash was reasonably portioned between the eggs, the potato and the duck, and it all came together brilliantly when mixed. 

The French Dip sandwich was of the same caliber, with a nice crunchy on the outside soft on the inside consistency that served it's purpose of absorbing the au jus and coming together with what was some excellent roast beef cooked medium/rare. 

Finally, the pastries served prior to the meal were out of this world, and I'd gladly come just for the pastries. Dual Stars Granted. 

Star 5: Would you eat here every day if you could?

Dirty French is a great Brunch option, but there are so many other good options nearby that I can't quite go full five stars here. No Star Granted.

We had drinks at the bar. As always we choose our place to go depending on setting and decor. This place is beautiful! Some really interesting decor settings. Cozy and modern with a warm feeling. French restaurant as the name suggests... 
All American whiskey and bourbon in the bar and the bartender knows her stuff.
It's pricey but really nice.
Will be back for dinner later this week.

As seen on Master of None. Although, I'll bet Aziz didn't have this much trouble getting a reservation at a normal dining hour. Jeez.

After entering, I was pretty happy to see a very casual, laid-back vibe, despite Dirty French being touted as a very trendy French restaurant. The place is fairly large, located within the Ludlow Hotel. I was able to snag a good reservation time, but only because I booked weeks in advance, so be on the lookout for that. Unfortunately, we were both feeling fairly under the weather, so we decided to forgo the cocktails. However, as a result, we dove right into the menu. 

The highlights:
- Roquefort salad: Delicious with the very pungent cheese, and the candied cashews are bomb
- Millefeuille: Mushrooms in curry with a bit of creaminess, likely my favorite dish
- Lamb Carpaccio: super thinly sliced and delicious
- Ahi Tuna Tartare: tender, and served with a crepe crostini.
- Cote de Boeuf for 2: On the rarer side, but delicious and fatty/flavorful

Also, the complimentary flatbread is pretty unreal and comes with some really good crème fraîche. Unstoppable. So good that we even asked for more, despite us ordering like crazy. The fatassery is real. 

Service was very friendly and attentive, and was very good about the recommendations.  On the other hand, prices are on the exorbitantly expensive side for some of the entrees. The quality is definitely great, but it is very pricey. Again, we did go for the most expensive stuff on the menu, so you can take my advice with a grain of salt.

I'll be back to try the cocktails, and to get some more of that free bread, or try the lamb burger for lunch/brunch, or the chicken and crepes. I would recommend Dirty French for a special occasion or for casual drinks, if you manage to snag a couple seats by the bar.

I went to Dirty French for my birthday dinner. We were sat at our table quickly. The waitress gave us recommendations on appetizer and entrees. 

Bourguignon(Lightly grilled oyster) i loved the topping and the bread that came with it

Meunière(brook trout, sesame, dried apricot) skin was fried crispy

Duck à l'Orange(ras el hanout, preserved oranges)

Haricots Asiatique(string beans i think) a little bit too salty
And for dessert we ordered Beignets with chicory caramel sauce. Small doughnut kind of pastry with dipping sauce.
Overall it was a good experience.

Dessert came with a small candle on a jelly for my birthday.

French bistro with an edgy feel.  80's pop soundtrack in the air. Went for brunch on a Sunday.  Split grilled oysters, Cajun shrimp, steak au poivre, pommes matin.  All of it so good.  So rich.  So delicious.  But no one asked how I wanted my steak.  And, we had no drinks for some 30 minutes after our order.   No pastries or bread.  Tap water assumed.  We would have said sparkling, but no one asked.  I will remember a big lag between courses but really good food.  Service, for me, is a reason not to come back.

One of the best restaurants in NYC.

In the spirit of true French service, the host was pretentious and couldn't fit a party of 2 in on a Weds night without a reservation.  Only seats available were FCFS at the bar, which I almost enjoyed because my final victory in scoring 2 seats at the bar left me with such a feeling of accomplishment!  If you're not into stalking and pouncing for your dinner table, make a reservation :)

The Cocktails are a little on the pricey side ($16) but expertly made and strong!  I had the Chai something and it was similar to a Manhattan with a chicory flavor.

My friend and I had the:
Baked Oyster appetizer - 5 stars, delicious!!
Chèvre Salad - I didn't try this but my friend seemed to enjoy
Duck a l'Orange - very good, nice crispy skin on top.
Pommes purée - this is basically butter with some potato sprinkled in it :). In other words, rich, smooth and delicious!!  Exactly the way mashed potatoes should be.
Haricots asiatique - these were good, not mind blowing 

And then...for dessert....

The beignets!!!!!

Delicious, light, fluffy beignets that my friend (who went to college at Tulane) said were better than Cafe du Monde's in New Orleans.  The flavor was subtle orange and floral bergamot, and came with a delicious caramel dipping sauce.  This is the perfect end to a perfect meal.

Highly recommend!
Great vibe, nice crowd, good food. Can't wait to come back and check out more dishes...

We went with pretty high expectations. We had family from out of the country and we're excited to take them to experience some good food in New York. Friends had told us it was great. 
The good things- we had a great bottle of wine. 
Other than that it was a disaster. We ordered  the kale salad, lamb carpacci, grilled oysters . The kale salad was great but other than that it was all too salty. 
For the mains we got the chicken for two (better for about 4 people or two giants!), the pork chops and the sea bass and again everything was uncomfortably salty. We brought it to the attention of our server- she tried a couple of things and agreed with us that everything was overly salty.
She spoke to the manager-
Told us that the manager would come and speak to us and no body came! Not just that but they charged us for everything though most things were inedible.
Terrible terrible experience. 
And this is three days after we had a very underwhelming experience at Santina.
I am not inclined to recommend the restaurants by the major food group again- pain to get a reservation and then the food is really sub par.

Best food  I've ever had in my whole life. Please try the oysters and the mushroom carpaccio. 
Nothing less then perfection!!!

Went in for breakfast at 10 am on a Saturday. Great experience top to bottom:
1. Not crowded at all
2. Got a great table
3. Amazing food. Benedict and bagel and lox both were decadent, fun takes on classics.
4. Kenyon was a wonderful waiter. Friendly, made great suggestions, never pushy. We'd come back just for him! 
5. Super cool design and good music. Just a great place to be. 
6. Fair, reasonable prices. 

Would recommend for a date, special celebration or meal with friends. There are some large, cozy booths for larger groups.
Although the food is delicious here, the service can be sub-par during their busy days. Perfect for date night!

Delicious food, for the most part. Too bad about the noise level. See below. The lamb carpaccio appetizer was outstanding. The second part of the very interesting chicken entree would have been enhanced considerably if they had sliced up the chunks of dark meat to make it easier to eat with the accompanying crepes. Otherwise, great flavors, as long as you don't mind sous-vide texture. We started our meal at 5:30 in a mostly-empty restaurant. It was delightful. A lush warm atmosphere, excellent service. Unfortunately, as the place filled up, the management turned up the 80's rock music louder and louder. This caused patrons to shout ever louder to be heard. At a 5-second break between songs, you could immediately hear everyone automatically adjust their voices lower. When I tried to mention to the maitre D' that the unpleasant noise levels would prevent any of my friends being willing to dine there, he was unsympathetic. He said that there were plenty of 50+ year old customers who had the best time of their lives because of the loud upbeat 80's music. That struck me as a most depressing thought. Either he sorely misjudges us "geezers", or it is a pretty miserable lonely bunch! He did mention that there is a quieter seating area, so if you intend to try to converse with anyone at your table, be sure to request a table in the back room. Unfortunately they didn't deem it necessary to decorate that room to the same standard, so it is rather plain. Food should still be good, but definitely not the same warm environment or luxe experience.

Don't believe the hype. Ridiculously overpriced and plain out bad. We started with the etouffée and then shared the chicken and crepes. The etouffée was reasonable but drenched in butter and with soggy crab.

Now on to the main dish... The white meat tasted like the chicken you find inside a chicken nugget - overprocessed, tasteless and rubbery. They say tender but it just tastes fake, exactly like airplane chicken. Actually my airplane chicken was more edible than that. I don't know how they can serve something like this for $39 pp. The brown meat was reasonable but I can get chicken wings for one third of that price.

On the plus side, the drinks are delicious (one star for that) and the complementary bread was probably the best thing we ate all night.

The service is also spotless. Read the not recommended reviews on here and you'll get a better sense of the stars this place should actually have!!
Food is good. Service is terrible. Waited over an hour for food and the waiters just stopped coming to the table. On top of it all we were celebrating our engagement. So disappointed.

What a way to cap out 2015 with a dinner at Dirty French!  I heard about its opening about a year ago but thought nothing of it until I was discussing dinner plans with my friend who wanted to try it.  I reread Pete Wells' review in the NYTimes and decided to try the Duck L'Orange.

We had reservations for 7:30pm and arrived a bit early so waited for my friend in front of the Ludlow Hotel where I people watched.

Despite the reservations, we still had to wait at the bar but no longer than 5 minutes to get the table ready. My friend and I usually purchase a bottle of wine to go with our meal and since it was Dirty French, all the wines were from France and very, very expensive.

My friend J and  I read up on other reviews so she wanted to try the millefeuille as appetizers and we both agreed we would share the duck l'orange and the boulangère with a side of pomme frites.  Since the bottle of wine was out of our price range, we decided to order cocktails.  I usually like J's choice and she sometimes likes mine so we ended up switching from time to time.   She ordered a chai matsuda and I had a muddy water since I am a fan of whiskey.

Our waitress and sommelier were very attentive and were available to answer any of our questions regarding the dishes we wanted to order.  Despite that fact, it was a very busy night, surrounded with very trendy and beautiful people, the waitstaff was always there to refill  our waters and we never had to wave anyone done.

Our waitress started us out with this amazing flat bread with light herbs that doesn't overpower the taste and which you can spread with butter.  Both J and I immediately fell in love with it and our waitress was nice enough to offer another plate as we waited for our dishes.

Since Dirty French was relatively new and trendy, my expectations were small plates but when our main dishes arrived, I was surprised how large the duck and the lamb servings were.  My duck l'orange had three enormous chunks of breasts and J's dish had 4-5 pieces of large cut lamb.  As usual, we shared the dishes and both agreed the Duck L' Orange was spectacular.  I didn't know much about the preparation that went into the dish until I mentioned it to a coworker who sent me a link from Eater stating how its dry aged for 30 days and seared at 1,000 degrees. WOW, that is one impressive dish that you can easily seduce someone who has a penchant for all things duck!

The whole meal was impressive and I was suprised J wanted to try the dessert here as she usually is the one who indulges me.  Our waitress again went over the dessert menu with us and left us to consult with each other.  J choose the tarte which was preserved lemon, almond and toasted meringue.  it was a refreshing way to end the meal.

I'd definitely come back for the Duck L'orange but equally interested in their brunch menu.

I love this place. Its my go to. I love the cocktails. The food. The atmosphere could be cooler, but overall its amazing. Here is the breakdown. 
If you like lamb, duck, or other gamey meats this is the place that knows how to take that awful flavor out and bring some amazing flavors in. 
*Atmosphere: Ok.. nothing special, just another restaurant. Age group 30-40. 
*Food: amazing, the lamb is delicious. One of the few dishes in NYC that fills me up and I can't even finish my plate. Its my favorite dish in the Lower East Side. The portions are great and I salivate even while I write this. The duck is sweet and amazing, I hate duck and I love it here. The foie gras is too salty, ask them to not make it salty. The lamb carpaccio is delicious but they could add more. The fish is not their strong point. The deserts are not that great. 
**Drinks.. if you love apotheke, if you like real drinks that are not too sweet, too sour and just perfect...THIS IS THE PLACE.

This is really great place to take a fancy-ish date without breaking the wallet. 

As we walked in, we were promptly escorted to an antique table with dimmering candle light by waiter dressed in the classic "Garcon" uniform. As we sat, we are enveloped by light, vanilla scent. I can hear a faint french jazz playing the background to add to the mood ... or was it my imagination? 

The waiter was very knowledgeable about the menu and french wine, and has just a whiff of pretentiousness to let you know he is french.

A manager (or a random french guy) person stopped by our table to chat with us for a little bit as we were nearing the end of the meal, and gave us some recommendation for dessert. In the stereotypical french manner, he shamelessly, flirtatiously complimented my date, and as he left he did the french laughter "a-hoh-hoh-hoh", as if he were delighted by our exchange. 

The food itself was excellent. Millefeuille which I order after reading yelp reviews exceeds my expectations. My lamb was a little overdone, as i suspect the waiter heard "medium-well" instead of "medium-rare" as I specified. the steamed bass has a nice fishy taste to it that I enjoyed even though I normally dont eat fish. 

The dessert,we ordered the beignet, as recommended by Flirty McFrenchy, which 100% was on-point. We could not stop eating the soft fluffy pastry dipped in sweet caramel even though we were full. But its ok because we needed the extra layer fat to protect us against the cold NY winter. 

Overall, it was a fun French experience for this non-French person.
we had late lunch , little pricey for lunch,  but it is good, only wish the dessert - Lemon tart less sweet, but other than that, I think food and service is good.

So I was trying to decide between 4 and 5 stars and decided on 5 because I think it is up there amongst my favorite French Bistros in  the city... soooo it's as good as it gets.  I had heard a lot of mixed reviews early on when it opened and for some reason that turned me off from going.  Last night i was invited out with some friends and had an overall fantastic meal! I started with the Kale Salad, I really was not going to get it as I am annoyed by how many Kale salads there are but the waiter convinced me it was the right call.  And he was right, it had pear, crispy sunchokes (perfect amount of crunch) and a dressing that I believe had a bit of curry in it.  Ummm curry salad dressing... Are you kidding?  Dope! It was so good and worked so well, being just light enough to match welll with  my healthy portion of perfectly cooked lamb.  I also was able to try the Leaks, which were fantastic, braised and then wrapped in phylo (i think) dough.  Nice balance.   The Short rib was tender and flavorful.  Seared and served MR so it was not mushy.  Our table of 6 were all very happy (some other stars of the menu were the grilled oyster, the duck and the haricot verts) and could not believe we had not been before... We will be coming back.  The staff was very professional, very attentive and knowledgeable.   I would say across the board of a possible of ten to knock our socks off, they knocked to the tune of a solid 9! Haha! 

Oooh ooh I almost forgot dessert... Beignets, they had mother @#%@#%@ Beignets! Don't even talk to me about how much i love these... Delish.

Poor experience Saturday night. Party of 6 reserved at 10PM. We ended up getting seated at 10.45 PM with absolutely no excuse or compassion whatsoever, merely told that this is how it is because "we're so popular". Waited another 40 minutes for our main course that was disappointing for everyone. I personally had the duck, which was decent  but not worth either the wait or the price

hard to fault the torrisi folks.. it's decadent, over the top and not particularly authentic or focused on a region in france. but the concept works and this is one of the hot places in town nowadays. the bar area outside is great for just hanging out over a drink and some apps.

Summary:
I rarely, if ever, go to the same place twice.  Why would I need to in this amazing city?  But man, Dirty French deserves a second, third, and fourth look.  What a great spot!  It serves many different purposes, meeting friends, hot date spot, work colleagues, small parties, the works.  A great spot in the Lower East, for sure.

Food:
So tasty!  I've come here twice now, so will go about describing the dishes I've tried.  The Duck al orange was absolutely phenomenal.  Best duck I've had.  Usually it's gross and fatty, not here!  My only gripe was having had to share it with my sister's friends, ugh.  I also had to begrudgingly share the etouffe, which consisted of mussels, rice cakes and crab, oh so yummy.  The piece de resistance, the chicken and crepes: Bangin.  I had this dish twice.  Their best dish on the menu.  It could easily feed three people though it's listed as for 2.  Dark and white meat chicken, cooked to perfection.  Fixins and crepes.  Amazing.

Drinks:
I remember having the Pigalle.  It reminded me of the spicy tequila drink at Park Avenue Winter.  Maybe the bartenders know each other?  Who knows, who cares.  It was delicious.

Service:
They are very accommodating and courteous.  Definitely not douche as most of these types of places can tend to be.  I wish they could handle the reservations a little better.  I arrived with my girlfriend for a 10:30 Valentine's dinner and still had to wait until about 10:50 to sit.  I guess that's why they have the 15 minute buffer disclaimer?  Not sure.

Atmosphere:
Very cool, chic.  Reminds me of the meatpacking, but since it's not douchey, then it's entirely different.

Recommendation:
Chicken and crepes.

Came back after a not-so-stellar first time experience and I am so glad I did! The food is truly fantastic, I love the french cuisine with a twist, the spices, chili and curry notes really make for a great tasting experience. It always bums me out having a great dinner and then ordering dessert and it being a let down - this isn't the case at Dirty French, if you are ever in doubt on what to order, just go with the lemon tart - it's so good and a dessert I will happily over each and every time I come back. As for the service - everyone really made an effort to ensure we had a great dining experience and we genuinely did. They really went above and beyond - Dirty French is a keeper.

The food is very good, and the choices and ingredients interesting. The service, while good-natured, is terrible. Was taken for lunch on a Monday afternoon; there were maybe five tables with customers. We waited a laughable amount of time for our beverages. Our side dishes arrived as we were finishing our entrees (despite our reminding the server about them as our entrees arrived). Again, the food is very good, but management really needs to encourage the service to match the price points and the type of restaurant this purports to be.

celebrated a friejds bday here in november 2015. gread night. have drinks forst at thr ludlow. between the four of us we sampled a lot of the menu and everything was great. we waited a while even with a reservation but we were having a great time at the ludlow while we waited

Beautiful space on Lower East Side.  Delicious French food with African, South East Asian and Creol influences.  Very good service and attentive service.  I wish music was a little lower and deserts were a little better.

LES changes so much every time I visit. And for better or worse next to NYC classic such as Katz's Deli, there's now Dirty French in the Ludlow Hotel. Trashy hot pink neon lights with the word "dirty" welcomes you into a rather classy looking dining room that's blasting 80's hits that make it seem like a club / karaoke bar. The sound level is very high almost approaching annoying depending on how much conversation you want to have. 

One pet peeve of mine is having a menu online but with no listed prices. Why so lazy or pompous in this day and age where we all need and want to know everything before we visit a place? Just add the prices. 

Here's the price list:
- wines by the glass focus on northern France which is lovely and nearly all are around $19-$21 / glass. Lowest price one was $14
- cocktails all $16
- appetizers most are $20
- fish entrees $29 - $39: rotisserie items like short ribs, lamb saddle and duck close to $40 and comes with no sides. 
- side dishes are all $12 for fries, mashed potatoes, green beans, mushrooms etc
