The complimentary flatbread  that begins the meal is warm and slightly crispy and very addictive and is served with soft sheep's milk cheese. They only give you one piece to share - just give us two. 

Most of the dishes are French with northern African flavours. Lamb Carpaccio ($20) is absolutely delicious though the meat is sliced so thinly you could see through it. There's a lot of flavours like eggplant, sheep's yogurt and spiced oil  

The duck a l'orange ($39) with ras al hanout and preserved orange was what I was looking forward to. Happy that it was a larger portion than expected but disappointed as the promised crispy skin was rubbery. otherwise the duck breast was good but the knives could be sharper as my husband could barely cut through his short rib and I struggled with the duck. 

The short rib ($38) comes on the bone with turnip, spices and coriander under a lovely rich sauce. Dish was good but not as fall off the bone tender as expected. 

No side dishes so you kinda have to order at least one to share. I think $12 for any of the sides is quite expensive. The pomme puree was silky and buttery but too pricey. 

Service was ok. Bus staff seemed to pour water and clear plates almost too quickly yet the request for the second bread service took forever. Our server was friendly but almost seemed too scripted and fake. At these price points service needs to match. 

Overall, the flavours were interesting but hits and misses would have me pass this place for another as NYC is abundant in restaurants.

Oh yeah a reservation here requires a credit card and a threat of $50 per person penalty (that is donated) if you miss your meal or cancel less than the predetermined time which was two days initially on open table but after you book it says same day by noon. So that was confusing.
Lovely ambience Cheery service excellent wine list and the food is delicious Highly recommend this restaurant for a fine dining experience
Went here last night with a friend for dinner.  The food and atmosphere were amazing.  Service was fantastic!  Would definitely go here again and try the breakfast and lunch.

Round 2 at Dirty French.
Wow. After my previous review and a bit of back and forth with the restaurant, I decided to dine there again last week. I wasn't quite sure what to expect but was surely hoping for a better experience. 
And WOW! I sure got it. 
Our seating was prompt. Our waitress was uber nice, friendly, calm, patient and knowledgable. In fact everyone from the concierge, to the servers, to the clearers, and of course the wait staff were fantastic and happy to be there. They all made for a wonderful dinning experience. 
The food was fresh, delicious and served in a timely manner. There was no rushing us thru our meal. 
I'm a convert now and will frequent this restaurant again and again. 
Bon appétit.

I loved the service and food in the restaurant. The lobby bar was awesome save the lousy dismissive selective service from the bar crew. The tatted up manager enjoyed showing off her double handed shaker skills versus customer interaction. After years in the service industry I was unimpressed.

From the intricacy of the decor to the complexity of the fare, my wife and I savored our experience at Dirty French. 

As for appetizers, the lamb carpaccio electrified our palates in a way that is difficult to describe. The subtle flavors, rye toast, and melt in your mouth delicacy of the thinly sliced meat was a perfect combination. The tuna tartar was far above average but did not compare to the carpaccio. 

My wife ordered the short ribs, and I ordered the Duck a L'Orange. The short ribs were rich, fall off the bone, and generously portioned. Although the duck portion bordered on the smaller side, the bite-through skin came crisped in that rare, Goldilocks area of not burnt but not rubbery. 

For dessert, we enjoyed delicious beignets and coffee. 

Our waiter demonstrated an adept ability to recommend wines that complemented our entrees and was attentive throughout. 

Easy five stars.

This was my first time at a French restaurant and it was glorious. The lamb carpaccio appetizer was probably the best item we had. My husband's Duck a L'Orange was perfectly cooked and mild, not gamey at all. My short ribs were plentiful and falling off the bone. We topped off the meal with coffee and caramel-drizzled beignets, which I'd never had so I can't compare. 
The ambiance is cool, eclectic. You don't have to dress to the nines to fit in; I was comfortable in a blazer and skinny pants.

Although I only had the continental breakfast here that was part of my hotel package, it was still pretty darn tasty. The service itself is worth 10 stars as everyone was so friendly. The continental breakfast included coffee, juice or tea and your choice of either fruit, danishes or yogurt with granola. We actually go to try all three (seeing as it was two of us) and we both ordered the yogurt the first day, which was quite filling. It had lime and coconut with tons of fruit and granola. Delicious. The next day I ordered the danishes and my BF ordered the fruit. The chocolate croissant was heavenly as it was oozing with chocolate and quite warm. The BF had the cheese danish in which he said was also delicious and warm. The fruit was a mixture of berries and strawberries and we fought over the last little bit. The coffee was nice and strong just like the BF likes. I wish we would have been able to get a reservation for dinner but sadly they were booked solid both nights we were here. It just means we will have to come back again soon.

Dirty French is a trendy restaurant that is incredibly loud. Blasting music from the 1980s (at least that night), the restaurant specializes in French dishes with southern middle-eastern flavours. 

I tried their Lamb Carpaccio as a starter and it was excellent. As my main course, I ordered the short rib, which was presented on the bone. Dish was good but not as tender as I would have liked. A tad fatty as well. Sauces and flavours were above average. One needs to order sides (yes the bill adds up quickly) and I went with their pomme puree. The dish was silky and full of richly induced butter. 

Service was OK, but not that engaging. 

Enjoy NYC!
Came for my birthday and it was great! The place is very chic and the vibe was chillin. The venue is as if an old traditional French restaurant and The Box had a beautiful baby. Loved it.

Cool vibes. Good foods. 
Went here for brunch with my family when we were visiting the city. The area that it is in was very cool and we enjoyed walking around. It is attached to the Ludlow Hotel, and the lobby of that as well as the restaurant are very well done and have a unique feel. 

The food was very good. I think everyone was very satisfied. I had the hanger steak and eggs, there were some bagels and lox ordered and they all were well devoured. Pro tip: get a bagel on the side of the steak and eggs and diy a breakfast sandwich. YUM.

The prices were on par with others like it, but by no means should you be expecting to get a bargain, this is not the kind of place to hit up for bottomless mimosas.

Dirty French was an interesting experience from the funky décor to the eclectic mix of servers.  We waited 45 minutes for our table even with a reservation and there was only 1 bartender working at the bar so it took almost the same amount of time to get a drink.  Once seated, the server was very knowledgeable and recommended a few dishes.  The appetizers were great but the chicken crepe dish was mediocre and the sauce was overly salted.  This occasion was a birthday celebration and I had requested something to be brought out in advance.  We ordered the ice cream dessert and to my surprise I was charged for the dessert which was almost indelibly bitter.  Everything at this restaurant is overpriced.  Not sure I would ever come back.

If you want a fun dinner, with a good scene and a killer playlist... This is your place.

The food is so good. Get the oysters, it's like an escargot style and dip the bread in the sauce. I could come here just for this. But the short rib is easily one of my favorite entrees here. It's French food- seriously how wrong can you go?

But this place is special because it's not stuffy, and there's always good people watching. 

Great cocktails here and wine. 

Come here and bring some good company and you will have a blast.

We stayed at the hotel and came here for breakfast.  Only about 20% full.  Service very slow.  We needed to keep asking for coffee.   Food took over 30 minutes.  They said sorry because of a transition to brunch menu (?).

5 star food-Quality of food is very good. 
1 Star Service

Not a great experience.  Sorry avoid for breakfast.

My favorite spot in NYC. Food and service were amazing, all served to the back drop of 80s music, perfect. 

Jaime and the team made us feel very welcome and nothing was too much trouble. We will be back soon.
Perfect late night ambiance! Loved hanging out here. The beignets and coffee were good, albeit a little pricey.  Loved the atmosphere, would definitely come back for dinner.

Went to this unassuming spot late on a Saturday night for some cocktails and conversation. A bit busy for table service so sat around the bar area to enjoy our drinks.

Pricey for sure - at $16 a cocktail. However, the ambiance is very nice and the bartender puts careful preparation into each drink. To start, I got the Muddy Water cocktail - a strong blend of rye, whiskey, and bitters. Definitely a sipping drink but sweetish enough to not overpower the tastebuds. Also got to try the L'usine - a coffee based drink with rum; somehow even stronger than the cocktail I had previously. Different with a big bitter kick from the coffee liquor.

Service here takes its time as the drinks are involved. I would say this is more of a date place or an after hours nitecap. Not sure if I'll be back.

I had a fly in my salmon, and one of the chefs came outside at one point covered in what looked like raw meat blood. Even if it looks nice, there is something seriously wrong with this place. On top of that, my coffee was cold and my friend said that when he went there, his fruit juice was warm. It's like they're playing a practical joke.

Great atmosphere, food and service doesn't get any better.....

At the bar ask for francis she's amazing 
Oh wait let's not forget about javiz...
Five star

Been here twice, both times the meals were awesome.  I don't dole out a lot of 5 star reviews, but there's really not a lot more you can ask for from a restaurant.  Vibe is great - loud and fun.  Menu items were exquisite and creative.  I'll be back.
Great food and service. The duck was great and even their pre meal bread was delicious. Definitely a new favorite for my girlfriend and I.

All I have to say is make your reservations now!!! Dirty French is a winner and one of the best meals I've had recently in New York. It is located in a beautiful venue with a great outdoor lounge. This is also a great place for a nice date night. The chef was amazing that night and we got so much food but all worth it! Staff was super attentive and friendly as well.

Lamb Carpaccio: MY FAVORITE! we had 2 dishes and we finished it all! You won't regret it.
Ahi Tuna tartare: This had great flavors
Asparagus & Shrimp: Another top favorite of the night! Very tasty and great use of flavors
Duck: Good but preferred the apps 

For dessert we somehow had all 4 desserts... 
Beignets: Favorite dessert! The beignet was so light and fresh it was heaven eating it!
Tarte: These are always good
Tatin pinapple and rum ice cream: Worked really well with the rum ice cream 
Chocolate Fondant: really rich but if you love chocolate this is for you.

I am disappointed that for the second year in a row of bringing clients from Chicago to The Dirty French, the restaurant has not yet figured out how to keep a reservation.  I had reservations at 10:15p this past Saturday, arrived on time and still waited over an hour to be seated!  Shortly after we arrived the host informed us it shouldn't be long as the table we were going to be seated at had already paid and they were just waiting for them to get up.  Last year was a very similar situation where we waited approximately 45 minutes and then only had time to rush through appetizers before we had to run off to our event.  

As somebody who dines out nearly every lunch and dinner with clients, at many different "hot spots", I understand things happen, but an hour is completely unacceptable- I've never waited so long before with a reservation.  The table had paid!!  As a diner, I've  been asked before to relocate to the bar to continue our evening, and informed another table was waiting.  

It is very unprofessional, and embarrassing to me in front of my clients, to keep guests with reservations waiting so long, especially since you have such a strict cancellation policy which clearly states if you are more than 15 minutes late you may be subject to an abbreviated dining experience.  

From my confirmation email as sent out by the restaurant:

 We allow for a 15 minute grace period for confirmed reservations so that we are able to honor the next reservations made on those tables. If the reservation has not fully arrived within that period we may not be able to accommodate these guests or may require an abbreviated dining experience to properly honor those later guests' reservation.

If for any reason you need to cancel, we ask for notification by 12pm tomorrow.. Cancellations after 12pm will be charged $50/person. 100 percent of the money from these fees will be donated to The Robin Hood Foundation, an organization that aims to fight poverty in NYC.

I challenge The Dirty French to work both ways on their arrival/cancellation policy- donate $50 for each of our 7 guests in our party for keeping us waiting over an hour past our reservation!  

However, our server, Chae, was awesome, and the food was great, which is the only reason I gave the second star.

One of the best restaurants in city. If you're looking for great food, a trendy vibe & great music this is your spot!

The food is exceptional. You'll drool over the complimentary bread with house garlic butter. You MUST order the lamb carpaccio for an app, even if you don't like lamb. It's a combination of sweet and mediterranean flavors that I guarantee will make your mouth water. The duck entree is the best duck I've ever had, even in Paris. The short rib comes in at a close second and is cooked to perfection. 

Great cocktails and an extensive wine list. Come with good company and you'll have a great night. For out of towners, this is located right in LES which is a great area for cocktails after dinner.

One negative thing..they are VERY strict with their 2 hour/table limit. Twice they've physically moved us to the lounge for going over our time just by 10 mins. This is the only thing I think they can work on. Everything else is so great that they still get 5 stars.

Went here last night very disappointed! The food is mediocre at best. Not sure what the hype is about. Over priced, not that great, will not be returning. My duck was bland, the cold oysters were not so cold, the best thing we ate was the bread they serve. Service is good, drinks aren't bad bur food eh

Rarely do I ever write a review .  I could not forgive myself if I didn't warn others to avoid this trendy hipster restaurant.  It's all smoke and mirrors . The claim to be untraditional French food  ia quite accurate  and for the most part inedible .  While the staff is extremely cordial and professional the food was a huge disaster.   The worst upscale wannabe restaurant I ever went to .  I cringe every time I think of the six meals we  were served.

The service gets two stars and the food gets four stars, so I settle on three stars.

We had a horrible experience here regarding the service. We were promptly seated at our reservation time. Our waiter came over right away to take our drink order. So far so good!!! Then we didn't see him for over 25+ minutes. WTF! We flagged him down when we finally saw him again. He told us to give him a few minutes because he needed to tend to a few "demanding tables"! I was in shock. We were out for the night trying to enjoy ourselves as well. He didn't send someone else over to tend to us. We literally sat there trying to decide if we should walk out. When he came back I asked to speak with a manager, which I never did bc no one came by. The host finally came over and asked was everything ok and were we ready to order. I told him that we had been sitting there forever at this point and he promptly took our order. The sommelier came by and offered me a glass of wine until we got our appetizers.

Food - it's unfortunate that the service was so off, because the food was amazing! Lamb Carpaccio was amazing and my favorite dish of the night. Grilled Oysters are also phenomenal! We had the Stuff Crab appetizer, which was my least favorite. For entrées, we had the Duck a l'Orange, Pommes Fries and Morels. All three were huge hits. 

I might give Dirty French one more try, bc the food is really good. However, there are too many great spots in the city to be this frustrated by poor service.

This falls just shy of a 5 star review-- With that said, I was super impressed by this meal-- The food really blew me away. I went last night with four girlfriends for a birthday dinner and we were all very pleased. The only things that shave this from 5 stars to 4 is a) Although our waitress was very energetic, engaging, funny-- the table was neglected at several points during the meal. Even though she acknowledged that she was busy and running everywhere-- you should be able to man all assigned tables or the restaurant needs to hire more wait staff. b) The cocktails range from $16-$18 and are tinnnnnyy.

First of all-- The house bread. Wow. It is flaky, buttery, salty, warm and comes with a garlic butter? Maybe it's cheese? I don't know what it is, but it is out of this world. I could have left the meal happy just after the bread- not kidding. To start, we also got the grilled oysters, the millefeuille, crab croquettes, and the lamb carpaccio. Every starter was better than the next. I would recommend getting all of them because they were all so delicious. 

For our entrees we got the Chicken and Crepes along with the duck. The Chicken and Crepes was interesting-- make sure you like the taste of mustard if you get this. The white/light meat was cooked perfectly and the dark meat (drum sticks) were delicious. Then there's the duck. The duck was one of the best pieces of duck I have ever had. The duck meat was cooked perfectly and the skin was so thin and crispy.

For dessert, we got the beignets and the tarte. Both were delicious. We truly did not taste one bad thing all night. The food was near exceptional. Overall, this is one of the best meals I have had recently and would highly recommend dining here if you are looking for a decadent French meal with a good scene.

Dirty French serves unbalanced, over seasoned French fare in a thumping, club-like atmosphere. Maybe the '80s are back, but that doesn't justify blasting A Flock of Seagulls during dinner service. Sitting awkwardly in the darkened interior, I could barely see the $80 chicken & crepes entrée in front of me. 

I could certainly taste it, however. I started the meal with a serving of foie gras, heavily crusted in charred black peppercorns. The flavor was so intense, I gasped as I scraped pepper off the lobe. Likewise, the chicken & crepes was overpowered by tarragon and salt, ruining an otherwise tender breast.

I can't speak for their cocktail program, but I tried a vermouth and cacao concoction called "L'Usine" that was fairly revolting. Service was okay, but I felt queasy surrounded by tipsy, porcine men in open-collared shirts. This is definitely not the LES I remember, even five years ago when the tear-downs began.

The one positive element of the experience was the beautiful interior design of the Ludlow. The restaurant flows easily into a separate bar, outdoor terrace and understated lobby. I may not vibe with their clientele, but they nailed understated contemporary elegance.

Don't waste your time. This place is a rip off. 

We ordered an $140.00 of Cabernet when the server DECANTED THE BOTTLE AROUND THE CORNER WHERE WE COULDNT SEE IT! She returned to give us a bottle that resembled a cheap light Pinot Noir (if you know wine, that is a HUGE difference). We politely told her that we were unsatisfied with the wine and she GAVE US ATTTTUUUUUUDEEEEE! WOW she was out of line! It was so awkward and inappropriate. She refused to give us a different bottle even when we said we didn't like it. 

They play LOUD 80s rock music which is totally tacky and wrong for the space. I was not pleased at all what so ever.

The food is over priced. Over spiced. And the service is less than average. Save your money and go elsewhere. HONESTLY! Its a total disappointment. 

Im giving it 2 stars because I liked the dessert. The rest of it can be thrown out with their less than standard service and cheap wine manipulating tricks.

A nice lively restaurant in Les with good food and drinks. They leave the floor to ceiling windows open on days with nice weather which is a big plus for me. 
The food is good but tends to be very salty. The LAMB CARPACCIO is everything!! I ordered two of the whiskey drinks. First one was good and the second one I didn't like because it was too sweet and the server was very nice to switch it out for me. Service is slow but good considering how busy they were. I will be back if in the area.

Oh my, for the first time in a long time I did indeed feel "the generation gap" or as its called nowadays "the genterfaction of the milenials" at Dirty French this super sleek, very good french restaurant in New Yorks lower eastside.

As loud as a place could be without pushing the decibel barrior, as soon as I walked in I knew my dinner would be conversation free. There was no way I could shout this loud or remotely hear anybody including the person sitting ten inches from my right ear.

With that, I loved the food and thought the service was spectacular. 

The menu was classic french cuisine with some cool twists and turns you probably wouldn't find eating on the Rive Gauche in Paris, thus the name "Dirty French". 

I opted for a white shrimp appetizer and a very unique spare rib main. Both were really really good. My three other table mates (whom I was desperately trying to lip read) ordered appetizers and mains they devoured. 

The desserts were wonderful (Ah, the French) and the wines were superb with the help of their Uber cool sommelier. 

So food, service, drink all five star quality. Even the ambiance was nice! It's just difficult eating at what I'd  compare to a Led Zeppelin concert at 8,000 decibels......Oops, I just showed my age.

I opened for a lighter simpler breakfast. Went with scrambled eggs with a side salad. The eggs were a bit runny, as requested, and delicious. The salad was fine. I also had a side of the mushrooms which were quite good. I'd definitely go here again to try other dishes.

After a mediocre experience at Dirty French in January, the Manager, Nick, invited me back to give it another chance, and I'm so glad I did. Took a couple of friends there last night for dinner and was treated exceptionally well by the entire staff, and this time, the food was absolutely delicious! Nick gave us champagne, a few appetizers, sides, and dessert, which was super generous, and everything was perfectly executed and tasty. The grilled oysters were superb, as were the mussels, scallops, and donuts! I'm really glad I gave it another chance and thankful that Nick was so generous and welcoming to my group. Also, definitely try the gimlet, it's super refreshing and well-balanced.

I'm not sure where to begin... Service yes.
Food WOW‼‼
Then the service... Above, Pamela...and beyond,... Jenny!  Not sure where great began and delicious happened. 

THANK YOU DIRTY FRENCH!!

Great spot in terms of food, ambiance and service. Tried the trout, grilled oysters, tuna, lamb and flatbread. Also digged the chocolate cake with coconut. Very cool vibe at the restaurant - it's kind of like going to a hipster bistro. Overall I'm a fan!!!

Went on a Tuesday night with my sister, place was packed but we were lucky enough to grab a seat at the bar and eat. We ordered several of the apps and just split everything. The flat bread that is complementary is out of this world!! We ordered the striped bass, tuna tartare, Crab croquet, mussels and the beet salad. Everything was excellent except the crab croquet...it wasn't bad just not something I would order again...it had that deep fried taste...drinks were good as well....would definitely come back again but would highly recommend making a reservation if you want to sit at a table! Oh, they also have a really cute lounge area in the back that you can go to just have cocktails....overall this place was awesome!

Where do I start with this amazing restaurant? Well the most memorable part of the night is the flapper at the surf to you before your meal. I know that sounds crazy but believe me it is really delicious. The drinks are strong unique and amazing. Came here with a bunch of girls and we all love the restaurant very much. The atmosphere is sexy and sultry but exciting as well. 

We tried almost everything on the menu and everything was absolutely amazing. Some say the food is too salty and yes it can be a little heavy on the salt but that didn't matter to us too much. I personally have the duck entrée which was beyond amazing. Whoever heard of dry aged duck? The orange sauce that came with the duck was flavorful pungent and bright. 

Honestly everything we ordered was delicious and it's hard to pinpoint which one was my favorite but it's worth trying anything that gets you going. Love this place!

I cannot express how much we enjoyed our night here! My sister was in town with some friends and made reservations here. We got there a little bit early and sat at the bar for a quick drink. The bar tender was so friendly and quick to help us decide the best drinks for each of us. While we were waiting, a server brought out mushroom croquettes for us to munch on. They were delicious and such a great start to the night. 

We sat down and our waitress ( Frances) was awesome! She brought us this complimentary appetizer with three types of soft cheeses, olive oil, and herbs served with this garlic flat bread. Amazing! We ordered seconds and had to warn ourselves not to get stuffed because of all the food we had coming. 

We ordered two salads, beet and kale I believe. The green beans, millf...( mushroom..by far my favorite dish) however I am sure I butchered the name, and the chicken dish. I thought the food was delicious, though just a tad on the saltier side. Honestly, this would have bothered me but the drinks we had balanced it out. It was more than enough food for the four of us ! We ended the night with beignets. I had just gone to Nola and had these and I have to say... These were so much better! They were light and fluffy and came with a dipping sauce that was delicious! Try them!

Sometime between dinner and dessert, we noticed two people making a flambé drink table side next to us. Being of course nosy, we asked what it was. Turned out to be some banana drink which we were not interested in. The waiter however came back to our table once making their drink were done and brought us complimentary shots that were delicious! I cannot tell you how great our night was! 

I cannot believe I got so far in my review and have not mentioned my drink for the night! Try the gimlet...it was so fresh and flavorful! I had several through the night and after our meal we wrapped up drinks in the garden out back. All of the wait staff chatted with us and was great at suggesting places to mingle and get drinks at afterwards. 

Great night and worth the hype! Check it out!

Dirty French is such a great name for this restaurant bc it is French cuisine with "dirty" twists that make all of the dishes so interesting and new but with a hint of the classic. 
This was a 5 star experience from the start. 

First the service... We weren't happy about the location of our table and they so sweetly moved us to an amazing table once it became available. Then I ordered a cocktail that just wasn't for me, so without hesitating they switched it for the gimlet. BTW the Gimlet was an amazing fresh, strong and delicious summer cocktail on the rocks. 
It's not the fact that they responded to our requests that surprised me but how sweetly they did it without making us feel uncomfortable. No one wants to be THAT person. At least I don't, but at the same time I don't want to settle for something I really don't like. And honestly I could really tell that they want everyone in the restaurant to have a great experience.

Throughout the meal the maitre de would stop by with a question or a funny anecdote. Just lovely.

The rest of this review should be about the food but honestly everything was so delicious that I don't want to waste your time. Just go and order a little of everything. 
Make sure not to miss the tuna tartar, carpaccio, foie gras, short rib, and the side of carrots with chickpeas. And don't be surprised to taste a lot of twists highlighted by middle eastern and Mediterranean spices. Ah it was all so different and delicious I would recommend for anyone to go and enjoy an expensive yet worthy meal. 

Also!!! The soundtrack was great!!!! All movie soundtrack hits and throwbacks from the 80s.  Think dirty dancing, flash dance, st Elmo's fire, Toto Africa, etc. So fun!

Was at the patio in the bar area recently. Had an awful time, which is a shame as the food is really very good. The service however, is atrocious! I mean astonishingly bad. Here goes...

Barely any tables at 5:30pm and the nice server (Asian girl) who obviously hasn't been trained at all, had not even a remote hint of urgency in her service. It was almost laughable. One friend said "maybe if these guys didn't open a new restaurant every 6 months, their places might be good". We almost fell over laughing....but didn't because we weren't drunk enough because of the shite service. 

So we left, more sober than we liked, but confident in the conclusion that most bars and restaurants in hotels continue to suck.

Dirty French has to be one of my favourite dinner restaurants in the Lower East Side. It has an amazing vibe and ambience, exceptional service, and outstanding food and drinks. 

First, you can't go wrong with any of their cocktails. They are flavourful and strong. Second, they offer an amazing complimentary flatbread that tastes mad good. It was buttery sprinkled with spices and herbs. Third, the food is so rich and well prepared. My friends and I ordered the duck à l'orange, meurette (cod), bourguignon (grilled oysters), and Roquefort (roasted beets salad). The beets salad was good and added a freshness to an otherwise heavy and rich meal. The grilled oysters were amazing. So buttery and well-flavoured; they were reminiscent of escargot. We dipped the complimentary bread into the leftover oyster juices and it was perfection. The cod was light and offered contrasting flavours to the other dishes. The duck, however, was by far my favourite. It was tender and juicy, infused with the citrusy flavours of orange. The additional sauce on the plate paired so well with the duck. Lastly, we had the beignets for dessert. They're great for sharing and came with a decades caramel dipping sauce. It was a great way to end a scrumptious dinner. All throughout the meal, our server was attentive to our needs and super friendly without being overbearing. The host, Jaime was so great, too. While we were waiting for our table he gave us complimentary hors d'oeuvres. He was adorable. 

I highly recommend Dirty French, not only for its exceptional food, but also for the environment, superb service, and drinks.

Came by here a few days ago- Petra was our server, what a sweetheart! This was literally the best meal of my life !!! Service was top- notch from the second I walked in! I've dined in Napa, Chicago, SF- nothing could be better !

Great experience!  The food was wonderful and the service was very good.  I was there with a group and our waiter did a great job answering questions and making for a good experience.  I started with the Grilled Oysters.  I was not disappointed!  They presented beautifully and tasted wonderful.  Their Duck à l'Orange was very tender and had great flavor.  A number of people in my group ordered the COD, BEREBERE, HAZELNUTS , BACON and all really enjoyed it.

You won't be disappointed unless you are looking for an over-the-top fine French food experience.

10 of us had an early brunch there on Sunday. Loved the place, the decor is grand rich and beautiful! Lots of mirrors, flowers and roosters. 
We got a pitcher of Bloody Mary that came with 4 oysters and 4 cutest shrimp-pickle skewers. The Bloody Mary was very acidic but I liked it but i was the only one who liked it. We also got a few pitchers of the Rum Punch, it was delicious and refreshing and it came with the most adorable glass tea cups. 
A lot of us got omelettes. They were tasty, loved the potato, crispy and well seasoned. 
The service was slow and choppy. Our waitress was not very attentive, our waters were empty and cocktail drinks were not refilled. Nobody brought us additional glasses for our pitchers of Rum Punch. All is well, we still liked the place!

My daughter and I came here during my recent visit to see her for the July 4th holiday. My daughter had been here for lunch and was anxious to try it for dinner. Service was a little spotty, which was strange considering it wasn't busy and we did have a reservation. Food was very good and nice decor.

The appetizers were excellent. We had the fois gras special appetizer which was delicious. We also had the special mushroom appetizer which was phenomenal. Overall the setting is Sleek, sexy, and trendy. Great surrounding environment. Main course was good but not excellent. I had the lamb saddle and the wife had the special frisee salad which was overdressed. The wine selection by the glass also was subpar for a restaurant of this caliber. The waiter and the wait staff was very attentive and excellent. Bartenders also were very nice and attentive. Service overall was five stars. I gave it three stars due to the lackluster entrees.

I agree -- the service isn't professional.  Telling your server you have theater tickets at 8:00 should elicit a certain response.  Not here.  Too self-important, too chatty.  Then to deliver entrees at 7:50 without an apology isn't ok.  Wine list was nice but very pricey.  Food was smothered in salt and butter.

I consider myself technologically savvy, but for the longest time I had the filming locations from Master of None pop up every time I opened Google maps on my phone. Dirty French always caught my eye as one of the must try eateries on the show.

We had a late Monday reservation - 9 pm - and it was still completely packed. 

I went with a larger group, and our waitress steered us toward splitting a vast range of starters and mains - family style.

I was a bit nervous about all of the splitting, but the team reassured me that they would let me know what options were gluten-free. I was thrilled to learn that I could eat everything we ordered, save for the bread and the fried chicken & crepes from the chicken and crepes.

Unannounced they brought out warm and delicious gluten free bread for me to eat with the fromage blanc that I had been eye-ing jealously.

Everything we ate was DELICIOUS but the standouts for me were the mussels, the trout and the green beans. 

In an entirely different standout category were the Pommes Puree (mashed potatoes) - oh my god, potentially the most amazing thing I have ever eaten. They look thin, almost soupy, so we were a bit suspicious, but good lord these were the creamiest, most buttery, amazingly delicious potatoes I have ever had. Our group polished them off and ordered another serving.

I would say this is a solid 4.5 stars as the food was that spectacular - it was just a bit loud, and a bit slow - great spot to splurge on amazing food in a great atmosphere though. Would definitely love to come back for a special night out.

I can't understand the negative comments. The food was fantastic and the server one of the most knowledgeable I have seen. Our booth was very comfortable. The only complaint was the loud (70s/80s era) music, but I'm older than their target demographic. We had grilled oysters, mushroom millefeuille, duck, steak, and beignets. All very good.

I've been here several times and will definitely be coming back!!! 

Make sure to make reservations or be ready to wait for around an hour for a table (regardless of the night), they are always busy

The food is delicious, service is great, and atmosphere is fun and hip!

Wonderful evening, wonderful meal. Pamela saw to our every request. Gimlets expertly made. Grilled oysters superb. Mushroom millefeuille splendid. Duck and steak spectacular. Great atmosphere. Even us old fogeys felt comfortable. The mysterious Maharishi added color. We will be back.

The best part of this meal was the potatoes which were perfectly crispy. Steak was ok. Duck was chewy and odd tasting- kind of made me nauseous to be honest. Fish was not good. Mussels were just OK. Overpriced and not even a decent or good tasting meal.  disappointing.

Apparently it's really difficult to get a table here at dinner. Lunch = empty. Came in this week and there were only three other tables seated which was perfect. Rundown:
 - Tuna Tartare App, (A+) I'd come back just for this
 - Striped bass App, (A-)
 - Lamb Burger, (A) Ridiculous
 - Scallops (B) Pass

New move: hitting up the hardest reservations in NYC for lunch.

Loved the room.....loved the atmosphere.....bartender was world-class......waitress was world class.....but the $350 bill for TWO is just not worth it. 

Wanted to love the place, but its a rip-off even by NYC standards!

We had the kale salad, orange duck, and foie gras. The foie gras was one of the best I have had. It was prepared with a lot of pepper, chard, and flavorful. The duck was my second favorite. It was sweet but not too sweet. It was hard to get a reservation for 7 on Friday night when I called at 11. Call in advance, it fills up.

I'm going to be honest, after reading the reviews online, I was dreading coming here last night for my sister-in-law's bachelorette dinner. The prospect of leaving Brooklyn for the Lower East Side on a Saturday night, to drop a ton of cash in a place infested with all the most condescending douchetastic humans the city has to offer...ugh. 

The reality: Dirty French is a beautiful restaurant, a glammed-up take on a Parisian bistro. We arrived 20 minutes early for our reservation because the heat was insufferable, prepared to have to wait at the bar. We were immediately shown to our table, a big banquette, given water, ordered drinks. Our server was wonderful from start to finish- attentive and helpful and genuine. She and the rest of the staff left us wanting for nothing  the whole night. 

The food is incredible as well- and abundant. I had an amazing tuna tartare and the Provencal scallops, and I tried my friend's duck dish and the heirloom tomato special. Everything was divine. 

Thank you for making her night so lovely! I will happily come back, and soon.

Apparently, dinner here can be $$$$, but I've come for brunch several times - with large groups and just 2-4 people and have really enjoyed it each time. Brunch entrees are reasonably priced ($18-19 for eggs, $20+ for more hearty lunch entrees).

It's a very cute take on an upscale French bistro. They start off brunch w complimentary pastries - this is only hard w a big group because you have to cut the few pastries up to share and they are good! 

For brunch, the potatoes are always crispy and well-seasoned. They are known for their Duck Hash and I've had the Benedict and Herb Omelette without complaint. Drinks were always good too. 

Service can be a little slow - but the food/ambiance more than makes up for it.

Love it! It's a super cool, easy atmosphere. Not a dive obviously, but it's the furthest thing from stuffy with food that would normally be in a much more stifling-type atmosphere. This place lives up to its reputation in every possible way. The server was incredibly sweet and she totally just understood how to give good service. She left us alone to enjoy our time, but was always right there when we needed something. The kind of service you only get from truly professional staff. The sommelier was great and recommended an awesome bottle of wine that met my boyfriend and I in the difficult middle ground of my style, big-dirty-earthy-red, and his style, super-balanced-light-floral- almost exclusively Pinot Noir. The duck a l'Orange is. To. Die. For. My most favorite dish so far in life. Honestly. Try it!

Excellent food but very, very poor service compared to other fine dining spots like Carbone. So if you are planning an important celebration or want to impress a date, go somewhere else especially if you have a group of 6 or more. The last two times I went we waited nearly 45 minutes to get seated and then waited 30 minutes before our orders were taken. The food is excellent though!

Dirty French was a near perfect experience. The restaurant is beautifully designed including an amazing lounge and very nice nice bar  House cocktail list is truly creative and the drinks were as special as they looked.  We were seated promptly and our waitress was proactive, friendly and very knowledgable about the menu.  She was always there when we needed her, but never over bearing.  Attitude of all the staff was friendly and helpful. Cajun shrimp with asparagus was a generous portion and flavorful (though not quite as spiced as I might have hoped for).  The trumpet mushroom Mille feuille was amazing.  Great texture and impressive presentation with amazing sauce.  I've never had a dish quite like it.  The Cod, which was perfectly cooked,  was served with a rich savory sauce that paired perfectly.   The Ribs were tender, well spiced and served in a huge portion.  Beignets for dessert were advertised as being worthy of cafe du monde, and it was true.  I read a review that was critical of the pricing, which I think is unfair.  Pricing is in line with other fine New York restaurants.  Sure, it's a bit of shock to find a place like this in the East Village, but a high end dinner with two drinks each ran about $275 which seems about right.

This is my happy place. It was such a pleasure dining here - everything from the food and lovely wine list and strong cocktails to the polished service to the dark, cozy and charming way that it looks to the amazing 80's playlist that dazzled my ears was pure joy. It was unfussy, unaffected, unsnobby. Just beautiful food with humor, levity and heart! Our server Pamela made every moment a treasure. She aimed to provide the perfect wine pairings with the food and steered us into the right choices on the menu for us. She wanted what was best for us and delivered. I haven't had a dining experience like this in years and I will definitely be back.

Love! I was walking by after being rained on and wasn't wearing decent attire at all. I peaked in and noticed everyone was dressed really nice but I gave it a shot anyway. I walked in and instantly the hostess was extremely nice and welcoming. This was a breath of fresh air since elsewhere I would have been looked at funny or been told I didn't meet the dress code. 

We sat down at the bar, got an appetizer, food, and drinks. The bartender served us and he was so nice and helpful. He helped us pick our food and recommended the east coast oysters - DELICIOUS! I'm not a fan of oysters but these were so fresh, we got some for our appetizer and then some after our meal just to top it off! The trout was delicious as well. 

Bottom line, this is a great restaurant with even greater staff, from the hostess to the bartender to the servers to the busboys. I was impressed and am definitely making this a new go to spot. Was pricey, but worth it! I always appreciate good vibes from employees. Loved it all.
The duck, fish, salad, bread, everything was good, but too salty. It was like we were in that salty lake in Utah. The service was great tho.

I've been to DF once for dinner and twice for brunch. The food is five stars but the service is three. Dinner is pricey but brunch was par for the course in NYC. Atmosphere is great inside the Ludlow Hotel. 

The tuna tartare is to die for - best I've ever had in my life. French dip is also amazing. 

If you go for brunch, make sure to ask for the complementary pastry basket otherwise they won't bring it which is kind of shady, in my opinion.

I was disappointed by our brunch at dirty french. Way overpriced for brunch ($16 brunch cocktails is absurd). The mains were pricey too. Service was spotty (had to ask for a juice a couple times). I thought the french dip was quite nice, but the pancakes were worse than you'd have gotten at the diner around the corner. I will give them credit for complimentary pastries.

I was hesitant to eat at Dirty French as the hotel where it is located displaced one of my favorite bars and altered the entire feel on historic Ludlow street. After tearing through our appetizers I was glad I overcame my grudge. The oysters, crab stick and foie gras were all amazing and unique in different ways. The foie was perfectly seared, crisp on the outside while the middle melted as soon as it came in contact with my tongue. The yogurt sauce surrounding the fried crab was refreshing and surprisingly flavorful. The grilled oysters were herbaceous and rich without being overly greasy. The bread, which is a cross between Naan and roti was a dish in itself. 

The entrees were also well seasoned with a mix of spices resembling North African curry. I had saddle of lamb which was more tender than the best leg of lamb, yet more flavorful than a lamb chop. 

I ate at a restaurant run by one of the top chefs in the world the previous night and can honestly say Dirty French was FAR superior in every way. I think the chef/owner of the restaurant it blew away would even, himself, agree.   

I have a new 'go to' restaurant for a decadent meal in NYC, Dirty French. I can't wait to return!

I frequently come here for brunch. Giving it 4 stars instead of 5 because it is way overpriced. And look, I am used to overpriced and I accept overpriced. But this is WAAAYY OVERPRICED.
Pros: I love what they did with the space and the food is good with lots of healthy options. 
I recommend for groups / girls brunch.

At the end of the meal, when the manager, Jaime, asked how it was - my truthful response was that it was the most enjoyable meal I had eaten in the last six months, an opinion that I am hanging on to this morning.

I did find the chairs uncomfortable, but we negotiated a table with two seats on the banquette. For a first round of beverages, I had the Pigalle, my wife had a glass of the Maury/Rivesaltes, and the feinschmecker had a dirty vodka martini. While Pigalle certainly invokes dirty and French, the cocktail was a pretty straightforward bourbon and bitters libation, the chili peppers being a little too subtle. It was a generous and well mixed pour. The dirty martini, made with Tito's, was not dirty enough for the feinschmecker, but to me it was on point. The glass of Rivesaltes was a small pour, and while that is sometimes typical with a "dessert" wine, I thought a more generous welcome was in order as an aperitif.

Generosity arrived in the form of warm moist, heavenly house made flatbread -- imagine a lahvosh fresh from the oven but soft and buttery. This is accompanied by a creamy dip - another Yelper has identified it as fromage blanc  I'll go with that. 

We chose three starters, the foie gras, the mussels, and the mille feuille of mushrooms. The foie gras was a good-sized portion, if fairly ordinary preparation, served warm on a salad. The mille feuille was not a pastry as expected, but a playing card sized deck of thin sliced, well seasoned mushrooms. A good dish for sharing, easy to portion and perhaps a little monotonous if eaten by a lone diner. The mussels were the killer app - plump and juicy, the Asian inspired broth super savory and the rice cakes a nice touch. We requested bread for mopping and some wonderful warm French bread arrived - the restaurant would be well served to distribute this without asking, it was great.

The feinschmecker was being celebrated, so she chose the chicken with crepes over the cote de boeuf. This entailed little sacrifice, as this whole poulet was an innovative and satisfying dish. First up the roast chicken, two good sized sliced breasts, two condiments - a tomato chutney and a white sauce (yogurt). Spread the chutney on the crepe, layer on the chicken, top with some veggies and Bob's your uncle. (I think six crepes would suit better than 5, as it makes the math easier, and avoids recourse to fisticuffs over the last crepe.) Later, the thighs and drumsticks, presented as excellent fried chicken appear. The white sauce is best for them.

Our other main was the lamb "boulangere" - a roast saddle. Pricey, but this is one expensive cut of lamb even if you eat it at home. Here, your sheep is perfectly cooked and nicely spiced, although the feinschmecker felt they went a little heavy on the cumin oil. For sides we had the pommes frites, which were thin paddles of whole potato, with yet another white sauce - cream cheese and sour cream? Wonderful, but a larger portion would better fit the price. Squash epices was the sole wrong note in this dinner. I was thinking a puree, but what arrived was sort of like a ratatouille, with some uneven heat and less fragrance than the name would suggest. For wines with the entree we chose the Trimbach Riesling and the Faiveley "Pinot Noir." I was slightly disappointed with the Faiveley which was not quite as good as this negociant's AOC wines. The pours were fine.

For dessert we had the chocolate fondant, which was more or less a coconut topped lava cake with a nice vanilla gelato on the side. The espresso came with it, not before, not after, exactly as I had requested.

In the complaint department: We also ordered the salad with sunchokes and chevre, which never made an appearance, which, given the size of the poulet was just as well. Suggestion to the staff - let the customer know before opening a second, and certainly  a third, bottle of sparkling water. Lest this critique give a negative impression, in the main service was excellent.

All in all, a great meal. I'll save up to come back for that boeuf.

Wow wow wow - chicken for 4 yes! Mussels with that amazing sauce - yes! Fabulous service? -yes!! Tuna Tartare - what is that mustard sauce!? - more! Secret present a few minutes after the Chicken came out -- yesssssssss honey! Thank you thank you thank you
The restaurant's quality has gone down dramatically used to be good but now sucks food and service wise

Loved the open space and decor here.  I ordered crepes with lemon.. which are pancakes.. with maple syrup.  Coffee is very good, and the vibe is brilliant, it's worth walking in the door and checking this place out.

This place is awesome. The decor is unique and fun, 80s music plays throughout, gorgeous chandeliers line the ceiling, the outfits are spot on, and the food is incredible. We had the lamb carpaccio which was the best thing on the menu for sure.  We also had the tartare I didn't like that but that's my personal taste. We had the cod entree which is not to be missed. The lamb entree was huge but too much salt for my taste.  We did have to ask for more of the amazing bread 6 times but we got it so it all worked out. The service was fantastic. Definitely a must try restaurant!
Really great experience here! Great ambiance, good food and super attentive staff! Will definitely come back!!!

New French is how I'd describe their menu with worldly flavors to excite your palate. Don't miss the mushroom Mille-feuille & the  whole chicken entree. If you have room for dessert the beignets are bad either;) one star deduction for the noise level. It was way too loud to hear anyone at the table and put a damper on the full experience. I'd still check it out and sit really close together.

Pretentiously overpriced. $300 for steak??? not even in one of the best steakhouses of NY you will ever pay that amount. And the dish wasn't special, just a regular steak. There are so many good restaurants in New York city that can be found with a little research, let's leave this one for the tourist who wouldn't know better.

My husband and I went to NY today and decided to have lunch here. We usually go to Balthazar or Mercer Kitchen but Dirty French was on the to-be- tried list. To be fair the madeleines, sticky bun, and doughnut were a nice touch instead of a bread basket. But after that the problems started.  I ordered an egg white omelet, and I don't like cheese and can't eat peppers.  I asked for an egg white omelet with avocado and tomato (both offered as sides on the menu).  I was perfectly willing to have the cost added to my eggs, but was told that I had to order them as sides as it was not offered as an omelet on the menu. So I ordered the omelet and a side of avocado which was drenched in oil.  I was expecting a lovely fluffy omelet but to my dismay it was a sad flat thing folded over. I also asked for a cafe au lait and was told that it wasn't available.  This is supposed to be a French bistro.  My husband ordered the French dip sandwich which was cold and soggy.  The service was amateurish and the cherry on top of the sundae was when a member of the wait staff walked by and said , "Ladies, how's everything?" 

It was no surprise to me that at 1PM the place was mostly empty.
Not good. Sure salty! Bad services. Waitress edit is half way through dinner. The bar is good. But I wouldn't go back

This is the best meal I've had in a long time. The ambiance is cozy, romantic and trendy. It's the sort of restaurant you want to tell people you went to, and lives up to the hype. 

Weirdly enough the highlights of the meal were the appetizers and the salads. Our favorite was a mushroom appetizer, which i believe was a special, and it was outstanding. I've never had anything like it and it was delicious. The lamb carpaccio was also excellent. 

The kale salad was a highlight, which normally would say something about everything else but this kale salad may be the best salad I've ever had. It was extraordinary, which I never thought I'd say about a salad. 

The entrees we ordered were the duck and the cod, and both were excellent. The cod was perfect, and I'm excited to try more seafood entrees here in the future. Looking forward to coming back!

Celebrated my birthday at Dirty French last night and I have to say, it was an amazing experience overall! We started being greeted by the host, wearing a huge smile and Frenchy hat, who right away seated us! A very friendly Omar approached us and I asked him questions about the menu. I told him we were hoping to land at Carbone for my birthday, but we were given an 8:15 reservations that was rather late for me & my husband! With Omar's very thorough and amiable answers to my questions, we started with the Tartate (Ahi Tuna, Bird's Chili & Crepe IndoChine) which we loved! I also had the Bourguignonne ( Grilled Oysters!) which was the best oysters I ever had! (Coming from me who has been eating oysters since I was a kid in the tropics with fresh oysters, you have to believe me). For our main course, we went for the specialty of the house and for what they are known for - the Pour Deux- Cote de Boeuf and Chicken and Crepes! And it was, to say the least, gastronomically appetizing and simply heavenly! The chicken just literally melts in your mouth! The sauce just complemented everything that the sensation of savoring the dish makes you reach for more. Amazing presentation as well! On the side we had the Haricots Asiatique that went well with the chicken. 

I have to mention, we love Paris and the ambiance just gave that Parisian vibe. The very friendly and yes, fast but efficient service with a smile completed the experience! Thanks for making my birthday awesome! Thank you to Omar!

Sorry this update is so delayed!! Shorty o wrote my last review the restaurant manager contacted me and kindly asked us to return at any time to give the restaurant another try with comped dishes. 
We went back with a few friends! Our experience was completely different than the last. The short rib was worth the hype, it was delicious. The rest of the dishes were lighter on salt which was great! We were truly taken care of this time around :)

Ahhhhh. Dirty French. I came here about a month ago and am still dreaming about my meal. This may be one of the best restaurants I have been to in NYC. Everything from the atmosphere to the service to the food was just perfect:

The atmosphere: Decorated almost like a country kitchen but darker, more upscale, chicer if you will. You know you're at a fancy establishment but it doesn't feel stuffy. The waiters are clad in sneakers and dark jeans. You don't feel underdressed in jeans, but you also don't feel overdressed in  dress pants and heels. 

Service: I had a 7:00 reservation for an anniversary dinner booked. We arrived right on time and it was by no means crowded/ The hostess asked us if we wanted to have a drink at the bar first so we obliged. The bartended was extremely friendly and helped me select a drink from my narrowed down list. After enjoying said drink we were shown to our table. The host carried our belongings for us. Our waitress came over to introduce herself right away. She was peppy, upbeat, a little quirky, but EXTREMELY knowledgable. I was thoroughly impressed when she rattled off the entire specials menu including how each dish was prepared, and why that preparation is different from every other establishment. The sommelier also came over to help us with the wine selection.

Food: oh my god. I can still taste it. We ordered an appetizer from the specials menu. It was a salad with bacon bits maybe? Some kind of ham? A delicious dressing? I can't remember specifics, which is disappointing because I've been trying to replicate it ever since. For the main course we split the short ribs which came with 3 ribs the size of dinosaur bones. They were delicious. But the real treasure of the night was the hazelnut and bacon crusted cod that cut like butter. I can't even explain in words how delicious this was. 

Dirty French is certainly pricey and I would only recommend for a special event. But it was worth every penny! My only complaint would be that it got very crowded and the seats/tables are very close together. It was hard for our waitress to get to our table at times.

PS- Shoutout if Master of None brought you here!

I came here on a Wednesday night and it was the perfect meal to get through the hump. We ordered three appetizers:  Millefeuille,  Crab Croquette, and the Tuna Tartar. The tuna was my favorite of the app because it tasted so fresh and had a delicious and biiig cracker style crepe. Also, the bread to start was perfection - we were all really hungry walking into the restaurant and the fromage blanc was better than butter.

For my main course I had the black bass, it was light and airy and delicious. I wish I had a spoon to slurp up the remaining sauce. My friends had the scallops, duck l'orange, and the short ribs...they were all equally pleased. For dessert we had the beignets which were melt in your mouth but the only negative was the caramel sauce was a little artificial tasting, i would have liked a creamier dulce de leche version to go with the beignet.  We also had some kind of peanut butter crack cake with banana ice cream that was creamy and tasty.  I would highly recommend for a night out with friends or dinner for work.
Great spot, good service, very happening and delicious food. Gets super busy. Expect to wait even with a reservation. It's worth it! Will definitely be back.

Great restaurant! Very trendy! Had to wait extra 30 minutes with a reservation but the manager was kind enough to take care of our drinks and dessert. Food was beyond delicious. Their kale salad is amazing. The donuts are to die for. Highly recommend when In NYC. We will defiantly be back!

I didn't like the food.  Had the short ribs which were very fatty.  I could only eat about half of it because they were so fatty and the sauce wasn't good.  The place itself is nice.  They have a lounge in the back were we sat while we waited for our table but no servers came around to take our order.  We had to get up and go to the crowded bar whenever we wanted a drink.  Not enough good things about it to outweigh the bad in my opinion.
Service is excellent. Great dining experience! Be sure to have drinks in the lounge before or after your meal.

Place is amazing! The bartenders are very polite, we were seated promptly, felt like 5 ppl waited on us, never a shortage of anything. As for food, we had the oysters for appetizers, trout and short ribs for dinner and can't rem the name of the desert but it was great. Def will be back next time I'm back for a visit!

This place is buzzing and the food totally does it justice. Go for the mushroom filo pastry and the bresaola... for starters! The cocktails are also fantastic, and great wine suggestions and custom-made shots too!! At some point I found myself moving to the fab music on my bar stool. Thank god I was staying in the hotel - I'm not sure I could have found my way home!!

I have enjoyed Dirty French for brunch once before, but this time I wanted to have a Saturday night dinner experience. Our reservation was for 8:30 PM and we were escorted to our table shortly after we arrived. Our table was next to the bar and I usually would have asked for a different table but the crowd at the bar was absolutely beautiful and the noise was somewhat absorbed and allowed us to have a conversation. We had a good idea about what to order from the menu but decided to ask sommelier about the wine. The wine selection was amazing and he recommended a bottle of red from Burgundy. We were very happy with his recommendation. The tuna tartar was amazing and etouffee was to die for. However, my favorite was Pommes Frites. It is definitely a chef's take on the traditional Pommes Frites. I loved it so much, I ordered one more portion at the end of our dinner and had it for dessert. Shhhhh....

Had high expectations. Had reservation, but no table when I arrived. Sat at the bar. Got a glass of red wine. The initial taste was delicious. Then got a glass from a bottle straight out of refrigerator. No taste whatsoever. Finally got table. Out of what I wanted to order. I left. Went to Lucien around the corner. Great service. Great food. Great wine. Half the price. Forget this pretentious restaurant

I absolutely enjoyed my first experience here that I HAD to come back. Recommended going here for one of my friend's birthday, and made reservations. I strongly suggest RSVP ahead of time, because they're usually booked, and the earliest they can sit you is 11pm without RSVP. 

Staff are always pleasant. Very nicely decorated, lightly dimmed, so this is the perfect spot to take your first date. Food is just phenomenal! You can't really go wrong with what you order. Their flat bread with goat cheese and olive oil is so delicious. First time I came her I had ordered their grilled oysters, HIGHLY recommend if you love oysters. 

For the main course, I had ordered their duck. UHHH, I'm drooling just the thought of it. Their pork is delicious as well. Basically everything in their menu is AMAZIIINGGG! Place is pretty pricey. Between a party of 5, our bill came out to $500+, considering we ordered 2 bottles of wine. But seriously worth it. We also had an amazing hostess. Shout out to Pam!! She was hilarious! 

If you live or visiting NY, must try. At least once in your life. You will not regret it.

I have been dying to come here, so I was so pumped to finally try it out. The decor is cute, simple and sparkly. Service was great! At first I thought we were being rushed, but our waitress was just being attentive. I usually get annoyed when I'm forced to put a full order in at once, but the courses were nicely spaced out.
The grilled oysters were just too good, only to be out done by the striped bass. The tuna was probably by least favorite thing we ordered, but not bad. For our entrees, I had the duck and omg I was dreaming about it for days. I tasted the short ribs which were also yummy, as well as the scallops.
Can't wait to go back!

we started with some cocktails at the bar in the hotel lounge, very well made drinks. also the set up in there is very cozy, after that we were sitting in one of the booths on the main dining room, to start we carpaccio, all of them were very delicious i mean the food is solid, for main course we had some very juicy steak, duck a la orange as well some black bass in some sort of green sauce, we all felt the steak was very over priced, just the steak itself was $320. not worth it, thankfully money was not an issue, but i felt a bit overcharged, 3 bottles of wine very nice wine service by the sommeliers by the way, some desserts and coffee bill came to $1,200 tax and tip for 4 people, the music is nice but too loud.
am i coming back? no, i don't think so, why? is definitely not an once a week spot,

I was actually quite impressed with this place. Although I would say that it's quite pricey. We went on a Sunday night and after being sat around 7pm, it's was completely empty inside, by 9pm, the place was packed - albeit with a 40+ crowd; don't expect this being your pre-party spot on a Sunday ;) overall, the mushroom appetizer was unique and for you vegetarians out there, I highly suggest it. Following, I had the kale and pear, which I would next time pass on... for almost $20, I expected to be wowed but this was ONLY kale, goat cheese and a few slabs of pear with an underwhelming dressing.  OVERALL nice spot, for possibly Thurs-Saturday but the food (as a vegetarian) was unimpressive for the price: total. 92.00 for two drinks, an appetizers, potato wedge and salad. + 15% tip.

The Bachelorette party were from out of town and staying at the Ludlow Hotel, so we decided to go close to home and wandered into the Dirty French. Table for 8, no problem, and while we waited a few minutes we sat at the bar and mentioned what happened at another restaurant to the sweet bartender. After being seated for dinner, the bartender came over with complimentary flatbread and spread, because she was so torn up about what happened to us at the overhyped lounge down the block. The menu is small but packs a punch - I ordered the short ribs and my sister ordered the spicy pork. Both were delicious, large portions and worth the price! The ambiance is fantastic as well - low lights, eccentric and stylish decor and no snobby waiters or patrons. I will definitely be back to try the dessert! Thank you to the staff for treating our Bachelorette with the kindness and love she deserved!

This place is awesome. Such a nice scene. Good music playing, great vibe, awesome drinks. AND THEN THERE'S THE FOOD. Everything was delicious. You must have reservations, and they're strict about that so make sure to call ahead of time. Highly recommend.

Nothing Dirty About this Place
Mouthwatering French // Solid

What didn't we eat here? This place was unreal. 
The pork by far was the best item on the table, the baked clams shouldn't be missed, and everything was great. 

Some of the seating seemed a bit squished in our booth, and when the drinks were delayed they kindly gave them to us on the house. 

All around a good experience, would go back.

The Scene: Trendy, Upscale, French
Destination Rating: 7
Date Rating: 8
Hob Nob Potential: 4

Strong Suggestion: bring some friends, you'll get to try more dishes.

Very trendy place for a good night out with friends or special date. The food is amazing but so expensive. Service is very attentive and the place can get really crowded, I had their mushroom Mille feuille and short ribs and loved it

This is just an amazing place.
Nothing else like it in New York...or anywhere really.
The place hits all the important points:
Great Food, Great People, Great Vibe.

The food is incredible. The duck is out of this world.

The people really make the place. Jamie at the door is the freaking man. Made me and my girl feel really special. The dude with the makeup is also hilarious. 

I'll be back, thanks guys for an awesome time.

Food is cooked well. However it is VERY salty and sour. I had smoked short rib and my wife had sea bass. The Kyle salad and bread are super salty too which ruined my appetite. I went in quite hungry, but could only finish 1/3 of my short rib after eating the VERY salty bread and salad. Certainly not worth for the $38/ dish and $17 for the salary.

I'm so disappointed the way the hostess was rude to us and the manager also 

We spend over $700 we had the bad service experience ever

Trendy but loud and very dark restaurant.  Tuna tartare 5/5, salads 5/5, but the short ribs were over salted and the lamb saddle was rare and impossible to cut. Kudos to the excellent servers who passed on our comments to management who offered to ensure a better experience next time. Not sure there will be a next time, but I learned the lesson to speak up and give my opinion when there's still time to fix things. I cant remember the last time I critiqued food at a restaurant.

Great service and great food!
We had the Lamb carpaccio, mushroom app, broiled oysters, and crab crepe. Teh only one I would pass on next time would be the crab.
Chicken for two was out of this world. Also the cote de boeuf was amaze.
And the sides..the sides were DELISH.
Dessert- no contest- the beignets.

Can't wait to go back.
One of the best brunches I've had in NYC!  The breakfast sandwich was unreal and those donuts they bring you as an appetizer, so good! Can't wait to go back.

Dirty French makes you Rarr. Super cute, rustic place! And they had the holiday decorations up already so I was very excited. Came here for brunch with friends and they were able to accommodate 15 of us easily. Good menu, good drinks, and excellent complimentary pastry. However, the duck hash I got was a little dry and had too many potatoes. And the duck was a bit heavy. The portion size's great though. Their espresso is also excellent. Great spot for weekend brunch in a happening neighborhood.
Food and atmosphere is great. Service is slow and uncoordinated-very very long wait for food. Seems to be understaffed.

How do you spell, "Yum!"?  Dirty French.   I'm not sure why this amazing French restaurant is called Dirty French because there is nothing impure about it.  It was extremely stylish and hip with incredible food and wine to back it up.  The cocktails are delicious (I tasted everyone else's drinks) and innovative.  Wine list is impressive but I cannot afford $4,000 bottles of wine.  They had more reasonable and good wines around $75.  Service was good though our main server was a little serious (but did an excellent job).  The wine stewart knows a lot about wine though he said, "This wine is very specific."  (What is specific?)  The apps were HUGE - so don't eat anything all day to prepare for an incredible meal.  The beats with chevre  was awesome.  A flat bread with cheese was to die for (and I tried to be low carb).  The clam crab app was so incredible delectable.  Chevre salad also great.  Duck à l'Orange was made to perfection and even my friend who is in Paris all the time said it is better than in Paris.  We were too full for dessert, so like I said, come with an empty empty stomach!

Overall it's a greate scene and vibe. Apps are good, lamb carpaccio is great. Lamb saddle, is too tough, they should serve with steak knives instead. Mushroom appetizer is so-so, it just nice mushrooms over thai panang sauce, imo.

I wanted to love this place. The lighting and decor are modern, but still comfortable, and very much looks like an upscale dining with a bit of funkiness in their signage and branding. 

The ambiance would be perfect for date - except the noise level is almost intolerable. We arrived at 7:30pm on a Wednesday night without reservations. There was an hour wait for the dining room, but they offered us the covered garden area as an alternative. I'm so happy we chose the garden, because it was like a different restaurant. 

The garden is a combination of tables and garden lounge furniture and is significantly quieter. It's an interior courtyard, bricked in and with a plastic grooved ceiling. They don't have speakers out there but you can still hear the loud 80's music blasting from the adjacent bar area. 

Our bill was $158 for two people and I'm guessing that is on the low end. The server treated us like we were peasants after he found out we weren't interested in ordering after dinner drinks and dessert. He was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu, although he bordered on salesman - pushing products on us, telling us we "MUST" try a dish. 

The flavor of the food was great, but super salty and overpriced. The chevre salad with kale, goat cheese and pears was the best thing we ordered, but even the dressing seemed to have an overwhelming amount of salt in it. Granted, I'm not a huge salt fan, so I'm a bit more sensitive to it than others, but it seemed excessive in the appetizer, entree and salad that were ordered.

Overpriced mediocre food, slow disorganized service. Lovely place but they don't back it up competent service. Couldn't get silverware, sugar or drink refills. Food was cold but no one even came back to the table to check in.

Like others, I read so much about this place and was on my list to check out for the longest time! I came here on a monday afternoon for lunch with my team and we got to try their appetizer, entree, and dessert. 

Decor -- beautiful and intimate! The lounge in the back makes me want to come back next time in the evening. Definitely a date or a girls dinner type of place. 
Food -- the flatbread and grilled oysters. They are literary the only thing that I can recommend that stood out for me as a good memory from this place. 

Looking forward to returning back during dinner time to try some seafood dishes from the menu.

A rather dull experience. Yes, the food was delicious and the wine pours were generous. However the atmosphere was lacking. The decor felt cheap and the severs were a faux french rude that only exists in their imaginations. 

It's a fine place to eat. Happy that we tried it, happy to not return.

the ambience of this place is super fun and lots of photo opps! the food was amazing!
we started off with the croquettes and bourguignon then had two servings of the chicken and crepes and bourride. this was way more than enough food for three and everything was amazing. for dessert we got the opera cake and glace et sorbets.

Felt terrorized with salt bomb!  
I've ordered two appetizers and two mains with sides. Everything was exceptionally salty that you could not even have the second bite. Shocking. 
If u r looking forward to having hypertension and a stroke, you know where to go!
However, wine pour is generous. 
Interesting decor
Weird service....

Food is tasty but too over super salty (came with friends and tried different dishes they orders -all are very salty). All dishes are very large serve, even the appetizers -also a little pricey. We got about $70 per person (main course, shared starters and desserts).

You can see quite a few waiters walking around but they are not attentive enough. We didn't know that we have to wait for the assigned waitress to start our order so we talked to another lady. She seemed very unhappy to talk to us and left arrogantly. The assigned waitress is a little better but still not really warm. A manager look-like gentleman was polite and nice asking us about the food, but the first lady already made us feel very bad.

Awoke this morning to realize Dirty French had cancelled our Christmas Day reservation. Made the reservation for my wife and two children through OpenTable about a month ago. Someone should have made the effort to speak with us.
Starter, flatbreads & deserts are amazingly delicious. Entree are a little bit oilly and salty. Overall it's great

We were intrigued by all the positive reviews, but ended up leaving disappointed. For $250 for two before tips you would think one should have an extraordinary experience. Unfortunately, it wasn't. Salt and enormous amount of either butter or fat in almost every dish. The smoked short ribs were 80% fat and 20% meat. It was really bad. I asked the waiter if this was normal and he said yes, that's how we choose the meat for this dish. Maybe it's true maybe not, but there has to be some kind of disclosure that you are paying $38 for the huge piece of fat. Yuk! We won't be coming back...

If you're looking for an amazing and romantic dinner this is the place to come to. Pam is the most wonderful server! On our first night in New York, staying at the Ludlow, we decided to give our hotel restaurant a try. We were far from disappointed! After being sat, Pam came to our table full of energy (and excited about our yoda backpack) and made the most perfect references based on our tastes. She did not leave out a single detail about each menu item, or the suggestions she made to us. Every thing that came to our table from the drinks to the bread and food, we were amazed at how great everything tasted! Whenever we're in New York again we plan on staying at the Ludlow and eating here. Thanks again to Pam for helping add to the magic on our first night in NYC!

For MEH drinks, and pretty standard 'American (New)' category the food isn't that imaginative plus non LES price makes this place super MEH. Plus the loud crowd and super cramp seating..perhaps that's the draw for all the trust fund babies who think hanging out in LES will add character to their ho-hum life. That or maybe I'm just too old **sad face**
Was decent. Nice atmosphere, very good service. The food was not as great as I expected. With so many place to go in New York, I doubt I'll go back.

I did New Year's dinner there. The food was great. The music was great. 

The service was off. In a crowded restaurant, the high-strung staff made the night really uncomfortable. They seemed frustrated, and jumpy ... constantly inserting themselves and insisting that the food was heavenly.

I can see how this could happen on New Year's, but it made me wish I'd gone somewhere else.

We went here in or last night in New York and the food is amazing... some of the best we have had in NYC... the downside to the restaurant is that you are basically sitting on the person right next to you ... it needs more space and light. The staff are obviously busy and don't take a heap of care and all over you but that's fine with us because I hate being annoyed but I could understand how some people might think they are being rude... I think it's more that they are busy. Would recommend it as a must for anyone going to NYC! Will be going again.
