I really enjoyed my experience and food here. It was fun to dine here, the atmosphere was pleasant and the food was great. I love restaurants with the dark atmosphere :) The drinks were also fun. I recommend it.

I liked everything I ordered, and I don't remember what it was now. But yeah.

Went here yesterday with a couple friends! OMG WHAT a DELICIOUS experience. From the exquisite  capaccio to the Duck á l'Orange. Everything was cooked to perfection. Also, the SALAD. Hands down the best salad I've had. Great hostesses that kept the fun going even on a Wednesday night. Keep in mind Dirty French might not be the right place for the older conservative type. Just keep that in mind before dining in. Thank you Kelsey for your excellent service!

Ricks Cafe, in the movie Casablanca, could have had this cuisine with it's mix of French and maybe Morrocan flavors and spices. While the food was good, and the visual appearance of the restaurant was pleasing, the constant loud blast of '80's music all night like Lionel Richie's "All night long" or Duran Duran's "Hungry Like a Wolf" didn't fit or help my dining experience. It was my hope for a more classical French cafe flair.  With a clientele of mostly loud millennials, it would explain my lack of enthusiasm for the place as it made it difficult to enjoy the meal.
So, while I wouldn't go back, I can't say the food was not good.  In fact, the DUCK l'ORANGE, a breast of duck (I prefer a whole half), was cooked pefectly with a great sauce.  The COD was done with the same skill.  The grilled OYSTERS, with a unique taste, had very large shells but the oysters themselves were very tiny.  All 6 of them could have fit nicely on one tablespoon and all that for $24.
The PINEAPPLE TARTAN was very sour and came with an overly sweet rum raisin ice cream that, for me, was not a match.  A plus was the wine list that was extensive.

Love this place. The beef carpaccio is so delicious. The patio and lounge in the back is so cute. Great place to have drinks in the lounge or dinner. The service is great and drinks are amazing as well. The "Dirty French" sign in the front is cute for photos. I've been twice with girlfriends and will def go back.

Upon arrival we sat at the bar for a drink while we waited for a table for our 9:30pm reservation. When our table was ready the hostess kindly sat us then another gentleman took our coats. The tables are close to each other but it was fine!  We ordered wine and for food we got the kale salad (amazing) and  the pomme frites (amazing), lamb (amazing), short ribs (way too fatty-would not order again...but I like lean meat in general). The house bread was out of this world!  Our waitress was a girl named Alex. She was so great...taking great care in explaining the menu. Great ambiance and service. Food was great. Bill was $95 for each of us plus tip. Delish!!!

I have to say -- Dirty French exceeded my expectations.

Major Food Group, the folks behind this and some of the most popular restaurants in New York, certainly know what they're doing. In an industry with a 90% failure rate, it's remarkable they're able to drop hit after hit. They're like the Michael Jackson of restaurant owners. And while I wouldn't say Dirty French is their "Thriller", it's probably more like their "Dangerous". A little more modern than the the old-timey counter style of Parm, and a leap into the future from their take on red sauce Italian at Carbone. 

First and foremost, you're going to drop some loot here. If you don't own all of the East Village like Jared Kushner, and don't have an expense account, I hope you're here for a special occasion and you've saved up for it. It's going to set you back hundreds of dollars. But if you're prepared for the hit to your wallet, there's a good chance you're going to enjoy yourself.

On my group outing, we tried a smattering of different options. One thing I'll say is that their portions are very fair for the amount of money you're spending on entrees. Our eyes were definitely bigger than our stomachs after ordering the chicken and crepes -- a Lebron James favorite [http://variety.com/2016/biz/news/lebron-james-jeff-zalaznick-restaurants-carbone-dirty-french-zz-clam-bar-1201870147/], the duck à l' orange, the pork chop, and several different sides. All were delicious, and there isn't one thing we wouldn't order again. 

Food aside, you're paying for the immersive experience. The sexy vibe, hip music... it all plays into the theme. Much like going to Sleep No More instead of just watching The Crown on Netflix, you're paying for an experience, and not simply consumption. If you can wrap your head around that, you'll have a great time.

We were party of 14. Their seamless service made us never feel that it was a big brunch party. The food was delicious and the place was classy. Also it is located in the middle of les which is plus! I would love to be back!

Was very confused as we had about 5 different people show up to our table, we almost didnt know who our waiter was. Steak came to the table and light was so dim couldnt tell that my steak was underdone and raw until I bit into it was supposed to be medium . Sent it back and came back raw again. I will not be coming back here. Too expensive, many other places in the city for better food and service.

I don't normally review because every place has a bad night. This place, however, I think people need a warning for.

My fiance and I went to Dirty French for Valentine's Day. I had repeatedly seen positive reviews since its openings, and figured it was worth a shot and a good bet for Valentine's Day. I was wrong.

I sent Major Food Group a long email, but here are the major points: (i) very little attention to taste and preparation, e.g. they didn't ask about temperature for the steak and it was chewy, the baked oysters were tasteless and came out five minutes after ordering (assembly-line?), the desert was hard to swallow, (ii) the service was "eh," e.g. the bartender poured my fiance's glass into his own to taste the champagne, the sommelier just sort of walked up without any introduction as to who he was, and we told the manager the salmon was a 6.5/10 and he didn't seem to realize that that was a failing grade, and (iii) the ambiance is lacking, e.g. flowers and music were put together with clearly little thought and there are bus boys hovering like vultures.

Granted, I went to Dirty French on Valentine's Day, when everywhere in the city is extortionary. The average bottle of champagne at Dirty French that night was $300, prices normally seen in the Meatpacking district clubs, but at least those come with a table. So, with the qualifier that I went on Valentine's Day, I would not return when there are so many other excellent options throughout the city.

From start to finish this was an amazing dinner! We went on a Sunday evening, but it was still packed and lively. High energy atmosphere, great menu, and outstanding food. The staff was super friendly.

Ooh la la! If you've got the big bucks and a fancy appetite, then Dirty French is where it's at.

They were booked solid online, but my husband emailed (2 wks in advance) for a 7:30pm Saturday reservation for 4 people with no problem . The only catch is you need to leave your credit card as a hold in case you're a no-show....at the hefty price tag of $50pp... YIKES.

We were seated right away in a cozy booth. The atmosphere is great inside, feels very naughty french bistro with rando head busts along one wall and dark seductive Moulin Rouge vibes. The restaurant is in the Ludlow hotel so it's jointed by their sexy bar lobby which seemed like a great place for drinks and flirty affairs. 

Our group decided to go ham on the appetizers and split 2 entrees, so here was the line up:

Complimentary bread - AHHmazing soft and hot fluffy nann-like bread served with a soft melty butter-oil concoction that was to die for. We all could've just ate this forever. I regret not asking for more.
Grilled Oysters - dynamite! it came with a piece of baguette to mop up all that delicious leftover herb butter... I was in heaven.
Lamb Carpaccio - this was the STAR of the night. Paper thin slices of lamb with sprinkles of herbs, spices, and even a few slices of eggplant... almost contemplated ordering a second helping; that's how good it was.
Millefeuille - this was an interesting dish as the mushroom was folded into layers on top of this rich and delicious curry sauce. It was fun and a party in your mouth.
Roquefort Salad - meh. It wasn't bad, but paled in comparison to the rest of the dishes.
Bourride (black bass) - my god!!! Perfectly cooked filet (albeit a tad on the smaller side) with clams and an amazing flavorful green sauce. One of the best pieces of fish we ever had. 
Hanger Steak - delicious! cooked to perfection, nothing but rave reviews all around
Haricots - listen, I don't know how you make string beans taste so effing phenomenal, but Dirty French does it so damn well. Served in a small cast iron skillet, they were perfectly crisp and satisfied all your veggie fetishes.
Tarte - refreshing and bright, perfect ending to an exquisite meal

Long story short, your traditional french bistro fare gets amped up and "dirty" with some eastern flavors. Maybe I'm bias because it was my birthday and everything tasted extra delicious, but it was genuinely one of the best meals I've had in a LONG time. I see some mixed and polarizing reviews here, but I think we just got lucky and hit the jackpot with our choices. It's definitely NOT cheap, but it's worth the splurge. A+++

I have been meaning to try the Dirty French for dinner for sometime, and I finally did!  Honestly I keep going back and forth between giving it a three or a four star rating: the reason is that with all of the hype I expected to really really love the food and although it was good, I wouldn't call it the best I've ever had. My girlfriend who I had dinner with was actually quite disappointed with what she ordered. On the other hand the atmospheric and service were excellent and I have to say I really loved the vibe.

I ordered the Chèvre salad (kale,'sunchokes and sandpears)  to start which was absolutely delightful! In fact it was so robust I felt quite satisfied after. So my advice is if you get this appetizer order a fish or other light entree. I highly recommend it. I had the black bass for my main course and it was good but not great. 

The restaurant gets quite loud by 8:30 p.m., so not all that great for intimate conversations. 

I would try the Dirty French again and try another main course.

Echoing Heather D. Sat in corner couch in garden, which was quite pleasant. Except for being completely ignored for 15 minutes. We were literally waiving our arms at various employees trying to get service...nothing. Finally just got up and left. The Italian place across the street was great!

This is my favorite place in NYC!!! Starting with the amazing host!!! He was attentive! Fun! And amazing! Our waitress Pam was so helpful! Fun! And suggested the best of the best! And the entertainment was incredible !!!! So fun! Never a dull moment! Truly the best service!!! The food beyond amazing! Full of flavor and cooked to perfection! The decoration beautiful and perfect for the city!!! Truly I want to go back! A perfect place with the right combination of fun! Glamour! Taste! Quality! And service! A must if you're in town!!

Food, ambiance, service was all great. Came here to celebrate a friends birthday. We had an excellent bottle of wine to start. They brought out a flat bread with sea salt and cheese to start that was divine as we were all starving at that moment. 

We ordered oysters and tuna tartare to share. Both were great. The baguette to dip into the butter from the oysters was my favorite part. 

For mains we got the lamb, duck and oysters. Each dish was great. Everything was cooked perfectly and tasted great.

We were so full after the meal and were going to head to a cocktail bar for drinks and dessert after. We had mentioned to the waitress we were celebrating a birthday so even though we didn't order dessert she brought us a blueberry Thai basil sorbet with a candle. The sorbet was unusual and a great end to the meal and the gesture was so so thoughtful. It made the perfect end to a great meal.
Had a Sunday breakfast here, not all that special. The wait staff was just there, not rude but not friendly and certainly not helpful.

Had brunch here over the weekend. We had ressies and got seated promptly. Our server was super friendly and constantly checking on us. Since we had a toddler with us, he brought a high chair without us even asking. We had the duck confit hash, bagel with lox and a board with madeleines and other sweets. The giant bloody Mary for the table was a great addition. Everything tasted great esp the duck hash and the lox. The lavender madeleines were great too! Would def come back for brunch!

Came here on a Saturday afternoon with a couple of my former coworkers to catch up. Reservations were made. I was early but my two brunch dates were late. I waited at the bar until they arrived. Restaurant is really cute, nice decor. Restaurant area is a good size not large. Then there is a lounge area in the back. There are doors that separate the lounge and the restaurant. 
By time they arrived it was about 20 minutes past our reservation time but we were still seated promptly. After reading the Yelp reviews I was afraid of what the cost of this brunch would be.  It thankfully the food was reasonably. The drinks were pricey though. Opted for the run punch pitcher. Which was pretty tasty but not strong. 
We ordered eggs and toast with breakfast potatoes, the duck hash and pancakes. Everyone enjoyed their dishes. The breakfast potatoes were really good and so was the pancake. The pancake pretty big and thick. We were all full at the end. Before you food comes out they bring out a pastry basket which were yummy. I would come here again for brunch.

Have come here many times for drinks and have had a great time...awesome music, good drinks, comfy seating. However, last time we were here they didn't even turn music on in the back room on account of "guests complaining it was noisy". It felt like being in a nursing home. What a waste of a great space. Dear tourists -  If you were looking for a quiet place to chill, you probably shouldn't have come to NYC.

The food is great but they couldn't push us out fast enough!! Between the Sommelier being rude to us and maitre de who actually would not let us sit down at our table till our other two guests came back from the restroom. We will not be returning. They are an extremely snooty restaurant and in NYC there are thousands of other restaurants that the food is better and the staff is actually nice to us.. we will not be returning!!  I guess the staff at Dirty French doesn't realize without patrons they have no job!!

Was expecting a little bit of a chaotic atmosphere similar to say Balthazar from what I was told but it turned out to be just your standard NYC busy brunch. Everything was perfect- and you must try the Planters Punch! Amazing! I had the pancake and it was delish. My gf had the duck hash and loved it. Totally reasonable, great service- our waitress was so sweet and not intrusive :)... Great atmosphere. Will def be back.

Food was very good. Ambiance was lovely. Bartender was super friendly when we got a drink before our table was ready.  I don't know if the waitress was trying to be rude or if it came off the wrong way but she seemed to have a bit of an attitude and wasn't the most attentive..... I think she may have realized towards the end of the stay because she did become a lot nicer and a bit more attentive.   I would definitely come back again, I just think that if you are one of four tables in the entire restaurant the servers should be giving you the best service possible, not hanging around the bar folding linens completely ignoring a table of 8 people spending more than 300 on brunch.

We had a fantastic dinner at the bar. Service was great, food was delicious the staff looked like they are having a good time serving their customers with an amazing attitude! Francis at the bar was super, Bruno the sommelier was very knowledgeable and friendly all staff members were amazing. Loved the decoration and the location. We had a great night! Thank you :)

The appetizers and main dishes were superb, but several problems:
-Lightning is too low that you can't see what you're eating, which is a real pity because some of the dishes were very nicely presented.
-Noise level is too high which made it difficult to share a conversation even among a party of four.
-Their version of "pommes frites" (fried slabs of vertically sliced potatoes) was a disappointment. -This was a definitely case of "don't mess with what works".
-And the Swiss chard was way too salty!
The waiters and sommelier were very helpful and nice so no complaints there at all.

Beautiful bar in hotel lobby leads into a nice space to dine. We had a lovely booth and a nice server, though she did spill a bit too much!  Everything in the beginning and at the end of our meal was terrific. Lovely but very pricey wine list. But we were offered a taste of any of the wines by the glass. Alas, the entrees in the middle were not. First, the flatbread is yummy. The desserts are great--we had the opera cake, the tarte tatin, and the lemon mousse. But the steak au poivre had not one peppercorn, and why place it on a pool of lime cornichons, whatever that is? The duck looked bizarre on the plate and tasted pretty much how it looked. The porkchop was redolent with spices that just seemed overkill. Why oh why take classic French cuisine and "innovate" just for the sake of "upscaling" it?  See the quote from the owner of Lucien on its website to see what I mean.  I almost forgot---the fries are wonderful even though they were totally non traditional.  Go and see for yourself.

Really good experience here.  Had dinner and drinks with friends, first met at the bar for a well crafted cocktail.  Then the hostess seated us, nicely telling us we can transfer our bar tab.  Servers were equally friendly and accommodating as was the sommelier.  We split several dishes: mallifeulle which was delicious and exquisitely layered and textured, the baked oysters which featured a delicious flavor, the lamb tartare which also had amazing spice flavor and the tuna tartare which was ok, didn't knock me out.  Flat bread with white cheese spread was very good, as was the buttered baguette I guess for the oysters.  

For mains we split the trout which was very good and cooked perfectly although needed some flavor, the black bass which was stronger flavor, the Berkshire pork which was excellent and the gem of the main dishes with amazing pork flavor you don't get often.

Opera cafe and the little donuts for dessert were both excellent also.

We then went next door in the lounge for a nightcap.  The fireplace along with ultra comfortable couches and a dark vibe made the end of the night a great one.

I don't get to NYC as often as I would like to but whenever I do, Dirty French is one of my favorite places to dine. As far as food goes, I love the lamb carpaccio and the duck. And for cocktails, my go to is the Belmondo (margaritas are my drink of choice). I never finish a meal without dessert - so go for the beignets. I let the servers guide me through the menu and they never disappoint.  Everything is made even better by the wonderful hospitality. Nick always takes care of us and ensures that we have the best dining experience possible. Can't wait to get back there! Try it out - you will have fun!

It became one of my must go restaurant when I'm in town. And being French myself, I was very curious, and intrigued  by what "Dirty French" could translate into for a French restaurant. Nick, the GM, was very friendly and professional, as the rest of the staff was. He explained to us that the chef was going for "classic" French cuisine, with adding influences from places in the world that had political or economical ties with France, also known as "French colonies". We had tuna tartare, sardines, only available as a special that night, duck a l'orange, steak fries, desserts. We really enjoyed everything, the mix of flavors worked very well. The decor is mostly French brasserie meet New Orleans French Quarter at Mardi Gras. Cocktails were good, a little pricey compared to LA. Wine list included a lot of little more obscure French wines, which stayed very  well in line with the whole concept. They also have a very cool lounge in the back with its own bar. 5*
This place is awesome I am just sitting at the bar enjoying this awesome place ! Javis our bartender is an absolute doll ! The flowers the lighting music amazing!!! Nyc at its best !!!

What a special meal at Dirty French. We were offered a seat in the garden which we highly recommend - the main dining room is LOUD, so if you are here for a more intimate gathering, opt for the less scene heavy spot in the back.

Loved the lamb carpaccio, though the lamb a bit of an afterthought in the dish - there was precious little of it and the sauce, peppers, etc. were the star. Incredible either way. The mushroom appetizer is gimmicky and not great. The flavors have nothing to do with anything else on the menu and while it is visually interesting, I would opt for something else.

We were with fish-free friends for the evening, so we ate meat, meat, meat for our mains, and we are so glad we did. The chicken breast was absolutely beautiful...the mustard sauce alone should be bottles and put on everything you can find. The pork was perfectly pink and juicy, with just the right amount of smokiness.  The duck was cooked to perfection, and it had this dry aged gaminess that couldn't have been improved upon. Another great sauce - to the Dirty French staff, PLEASE include spoons with the serving plates! We were pouring our plates inelegantly to get the good stuff.

Green beans! Get them. You are welcome.  They were so good they deserve their own paragraph. Skip the pommes frites. 

Service was unfortunately a low point - sommelier's recommendations were a little ridiculous (oh, the $500 bottle of x is awesome? I bet)...he must have realized this and eventually offered us something beyond the stratosphere (but still, on the pricey end even for your average high end night out). We ended up with a very lovely bottle to follow our excellent cocktails, but he should have read the temperature of the table better (we were clearly not an after work on an expense account table).  Beyond the first glass, we poured the rest of the wine at the table (no server came by until the end of the bottle).  Little things were also awkward - server started to leave without offering the 4th person at our table a drink, suggestions which were strongly offered ended up being our least favorite items at the expense of other things, slow bar service even at an empty moment, big delays with getting the check.

Dessert menu was also really underwhelming. Mostly ice cream - given that, we opted instead for a trip next door to il laboratorio di gelato, where the ice cream is a guaranteed hit.

In sum, 5 star food that the night of was a 4 star service experience. That said, the management has more than made up for any discrepancies in service with unbelievably kind and thoughtful correspondence since. Dirty French is a class act. 

Overall, we will be back to Dirty French and we will bring a group. This is a place to share and try, and if something isn't quite right, tell them.  I can attest that they are more than receptive, and more than willing to make sure you leave happy. 

Next time, we'll ask for spoons.

Not only disappointed but shocked at the service. I booked this restaurant two weeks in advance for my 25th birthday. The reservation was for 9:45 pm and we were not seated until after 10:45. The dessert my friend requested (along with candles) never came, instead the waiter brought us the bill before we even asked for it. This was a waste of time, money and an unfortunate way to celebrate a birthday. It goes without saying that I won't returning.

Great restaurant!  Awesome ambience, and the food was fantastic.  The scallops entree was amazing, and the appetizers were great too.  The desert - beignets - was incredible!  The server was super attentive throughout the meal.  I am giving 4 stars, not 5, because the host had a little attitude when we asked how much longer it would be until we were seated.  Although he suggested he had the power not to seat us at all, he still gave us a great table.  Despite the host's "power trip," the restaurant is still very recommended.  Awesome spot.

I think the atmosphere is exactly what you will experience when you are looking for a French class meal.
I am not a fan of French cuisine.  The complimentary bread and spread was great! I ordered the beef sandwich dip with soup.  The soup was a mushroom soup, that was incredible! The rest in the food was not all that great. We orders the green beans and fries. 
I most likely won't go back.
It is a cute little place but very slow service and food is not great. We waited about half an hour just to get the check and then our waiter disappeared for about

I went there for an anniversary dinner since I had really enjoyed the ambience and food when I went there with a friend several months back. Because of a mishap, we were 25 minutes late for our reservation. 

Instead of forcing us to reschedule or mill around until the next table was ready, Lonn Coward (one of the managers) served us free champagne (I mentioned on my reservation that it was our anniversary) and sat us in a lounge area until our actual table was ready. 

When we were officially seated, we got our delicious cocktails in a short period of time along with our main dish (the chicken and crepes), which was so tasty and tender, I barely wanted to finish eating it. Amazing food, service and ambiance. Kudos to the folks at Dirty French.

The food is absolutely delicious. The menu is pricy but after tasting it you don't mind paying it. We attended with a large group with a reservation that was made long in advance. Upon arrival, we were told there was a wedding party occupying the main dining room and that we'd have to sit in their lobby bar area, which is an enclosed area that replicates an outdoor space (without the open air.) With that also came a very limited menu (lobby bar menu) without main dishes that many of us seeked from prior research. The manager did grant/comp us some dishes that were off the main dinner menu that were not on their lobby bar menu which was fair but....mind you, this is after we placed our orders off the limited menu. We ended up being burdened with lots of food on the table- Too much food, in fact. However, I felt that was fair given the circumstances. BUT I (and I'm sure others) would have ordered those main dish dinner items that they provided after, which many of us asked for initially, instead of plates off their limited selection, lobby bar menu items....Instead of as an after thought we should have had the opportunity upfront to order those items.  They did comp many drinks for us which was nice and again fair. Service for the evening was solid. After all that...I still would go back

Overall fantastic food. Thoroughly enjoyed the mushroom millefeuille and the baked oysters. The complimentary flatbread was a tad underdone as it came to the table but actually kept cooking on the hot plate, so be patient if you like firmer breads. I had the seabass which was light and tender, but would much rather have gotten my friend's duck, which was so succulent and juicy. The place has cool decor and is good for people watching, including the no name celebrities that go in and out of the Ludlow Hotel.

Great spot! 
Went there for brunch with a group of friends last weekend, and I have nothing but good things to say about this place!
The service was on point, as were the oysters.
A complimentary pastry basket was provided at the start of the meal, and can you imagine a better way to start a brunch than with some lemon glazed donuts, madelines and a perfect pitcher of  bloody mary?
Every dish on our table looked delicious; there was the salmon bagel, lamb burger, tuna crepe and shrimp frisee salad. My only disappointment would be the small portion of shrimp in the salad; but the dressing and overall salad was delicious.
The ambiance was great, and it looked like a relatively kid friendly place. It wasn't as busy the afternoon that we were there, but I've heard reservations well in advance are recommended.

Came in for lunch on a Friday, and there was no wait place was empty. I'm guessing nobody else knew about their lunch hours either. The meal started with some off the hook complimentary flat bread and goat cheese spread. My lamb burger and fries were equally good. Salad was amazing. So was everything else. Yes,it's pricey, .... but  well worth it. We left very happy .

A dimly lit cozy restaurant around the corner from Katz deli serving French creole with sort of an Asian twist. Besides the large dining room there is a cozy lounge area in the back. 

The menu listed what seemed like your typical French bistro food; but, each dish has a special twist to it. 

The Étouffée is not the usual creole dish with crawfish. Instead, it is basically a plate of mussels with "rice cakes". I thought the rice cakes were scallops at first glance. 

The pomme frites were very crispy and delicious. 

The cod was moist and tender albeit it tasted like Greenland turbo. 

The duck a l'orange had a touch of some African herbs and was roasted to perfection first. 

Overall a decent meal.

Brunch, a sacred time when Saturday hangovers are nursed by good friends, some hair of the dog and a beautiful restaurant. Dirty, delivered, but also, the salt to hangover quotient was a bit high. We stepped in on a slow paced Sunday, service mimicked the pace as it took a bit of time between menus, ordering, checks and payment. What didn't stop moving was that coffee guy... I mean, "literally", there is a guy who just makes and serves coffee, nonstop. Paired with the complementary bread tray of madalines, sticky buns and muffins, the brunch started on a high note.

The food..... I'll just say..... , ham is salty, but the jambon was a new level of curation. Delicious on a small scale, and perfect for a bite with a crust of bread. The second bite sent my blood pressure through the roof. The remedy, a morning cocktail, I honestly can't pronounce it right, Pigalle???? How do you.. Oh.. Never mind.. The champion of the starters was the char grilled oysters. Slathered in butter and garlic and... Basil??? Maybe also crack... Not sure... They were gone!!!  There was some tuna tartar, that was nearly tasteless after the Jambon. 

For mains, a friend raved about their bagels, there's a story behind where they come from... Google it. I had the classic eggs benidect. The Jambon was back... It's salt covered any and all other flavors. There was just texture and salt and these amazing fat fried potatoes salt crystals. The first two bites were ethereal... After that...fat fingers would cap the remainder of the day. My friend had "the dip", a take on the French Dip, with the perfect hint of horse radish, it was the winner of the day. 

Beautiful ambience, bold flavors and dranks, the price was a bit high, (like my blood pressure), but all the potential of a great brunch was there. I think a well curated order of oysters, those potatoes and the dip would have given this nearly 5 stars. When you try to throw the kitchen sink at every plate... You end up with a lot of dirty dishes!!

Sorry guys, had really high expectations after our last visit, but it seems we arrived at an entirely different restaurant. 
Every single dish we ordered was a miss. Every single one. So it was not a just a glitch. Maybe they had an off night, I honestly do not know, but there are too many other restaurants in New York to give them another shot.

Trendy, dark, great cocktails. The bread, mussels, and the chicken crepes are great. The cocktails are a must have especially the Faragoza (reposado Tequila, vanilla yogurt, creme de peche, fresh lime, clove). This place is a great date spot, but it is pricey (although the portions are large).

This place has everything you need.  

Bar to grab a drink, seating to have a nice dinner, and an outdoor lounge/brunch area that would be perfect for a sunny summer NY day.  

Dirty French is probably always busy - I've tried to drop in for dinner a couple times already and there has been over a 1 hour wait for a party of two.  Well this week I got lucky, they had a cancellation which I took over with a coworker for an early dinner.  

Seating is a bit tight, but that's typical at any great dining spot in NYC.  The Flatbread with fromage blanc is next level, probably one of the best I've ever had.   Wine selection was great and my manhattan cocktail was on point.

We skipped the appetizers because frankly nothing really stood out to us, and we ordered entrees.   I ordered the Meunière (brook trout) and my friend ordered the Dry aged hanger steak au poivre with a side of fries.  Both were delicious.  The Trout filet was a great cut of fish, very fresh, and had a very unique seasoning which put it over the top.  The portion was actually very acceptable.  The Steak, although portion was a bit small, was delicious. Cooked perfectly at medium temp and the pepper sauce was just on point. Definitely will have you asking for more!

My best assessment of Dirty French is, if you see something on the menu that you love at other establishments, I'd try it at Dirty French to see how it stacks up.  I think you'll be pleasantly surprised. 

Bon Appétit!

Had Sunday brunch here today.  Not a great experience at all.  It began with $14 mimosas, which were almost undrinkable.  Not sure what the bartender put in them but whatever it was, it was bad.  The food was just ok.  The service, however, was horrible.  The restaurant was out of their signature "free donuts " which are served to all tables.  When we asked about the donuts we were told they did not have any more.  No "sorry", nothing.  The waiter forgot to brinks drinks for 2 kids at our table.  The food for 6 was landed on the table one plate at a time...over a10 minute period.  We had to ask 3 different people simply to get a single refill of coffee, despite there being 7or 8 employees milling around.  Do yourself a favor and go somewhere else.  Anywhere else!

This turned out to be one of the best meals I've had in a long time. For one, we got an earlier reservation, which actually turned out to be incredible -- we got a waitress who was fantastic and able to describe a lot of the dishes with enthusiasm because it was quieter. 

The atmosphere was cozy but lively, like a living room party you have to pay for. 

The cocktails were delicious -- I had a ginger tequila drink that tasted fresh, not too acidic, and sweet but not overly so. And the food! Everything seemed to melt in your mouth, which is actually one of those sayings that sounds unpleasant but is associated with deliciousness. We got the tuna tartare, which was fresh and herbaceous and not really spicy but had a spicy tuna roll flavor profile. We also split the steak and the duck with pomme purée and Swiss chard. The chard was cooked like spinach. The steak was buttery, covered in an inch of a sauce that I'm probably paying for now, cholesterol-wise. And the pomme was like thick, viscous sauce. 

But that duck. Man, that duck. That place could have had alien invaders barge in with lasers and I would have sat there quietly and happy, just eating that duck. Get the duckin duck.

Really eclectic place. So much to look at. DF has created a unique ambiance. We had an early reservation on a Saturday night. As we finished, it seemed like everything was just getting going-- the lights turned down and the music turned up. Our meal was delicious. Our server didn't really put us at ease. A bit pretentious and self impressed-- kind of annoyed me. Buckle up for the prices! Overall we had a great evening at Dirty French!

My rating remains the same but I wanted to mention that the Manager did reach out to me to apologize for the poor service we received. I appreciated his dedication to customer service and would be more willing to give this place a second try because of his outreach.
Wow - a great spot!  DF never disappoints!

Had a pleasant evening here with friends.  Overall, while the menu is well conceived, a lack of finesse in execution leaves many of the dishes a tad clunky and with too much salt and fat.  To get right to the point, I feel Dirty French is far too overpriced for what is delivered.  At $35-40 per entree, there are many alternatives that deliver much more.  A bit more attention to detail would go a long way here.

Atmosphere
- Relaxed and casual, mostly groups of friends or people on dates.
- Front is lined with windows which were opened on a pleasant summer evening.
- French brasserie feel with some kitschy accents.

Food
Began with Dirty French's complimentary flatbread which was served with a tasty boursin laced spread.  I found it a tad addicting for all the wrong reasons, as it was a bit greasy given the bread was aggressively brushed with oil, topped with cheese, plus the spread.  The Millefeuille ($22) made of thinly sliced mushrooms was tasty and unique, while the overdressed Verte Salad (Little Gem, Buttermilk, Radish - $16) was fine but banal.  For mains, the Duck a L'Orange ($39) had good potential, but was simply not executed properly with un-crisp skin and a ring of fat crying desperately to be rendered.  The Le Creole ($34), a gigantic well-marbled pork chop with gently spicy cajun style rub was quite moist and flavorful.  Frankly, it's enough meat for two to share, and decadently rich with the marbling (took half home).  Unfortunately, the rub was salty.  We sampled the Pommes Frites ($12) on the side, which were more cajun than traditional French in concept, having been dressed with a spice blend and served with an aioli.  Again, we found the salt quite aggressive.  Overall, would say the food here was fine, but nothing more really.

Beverage
Enjoyed both the Chateau de Breze Chenin Blanc, Loire Valley, France ($15) and Joseph Faiveley Bourgonge Pinot Noir ($19) off the wines by the glass list.  Found the selection interesting and prices reasonable.

Service
- Polite, accommodating and very attentive.
- Our waitress was very happy to help with recommendations and assist with recommendations from the wines by the glass menu.

This place is the 180 degree opposite of your typical hotel restaurant. Really good French cuisine, cool/hip atmosphere, hard to get a reservation, and this place is actually a DESTINATION for those out on the town. Place is HOPPING from about 630p until way past 11p. The only drawback is, it is loud and like a party scene. If you want to try the food when it's not a party, go at lunchtime.

The food and cocktails here were amazing. I liked every thing we had. We were part of a big party and had the private room upstairs in the back. This room was super cool as the stairwell is hidden between a fake sliding wall. Cool ambiance. 

The drinks were very well made. They have all kinds of cocktails or you can order your traditional drinks. Either way they were delicious. Perfectly made and mixed. The bartender was delightful as well offering up recommendations and being very accommodating. 

The Food!! Unreal. Must have. Since we were a large group, we order a bunch of plates and tried everything. We tried: chicken & crepes, fried chicken, beef, tuna tartare, grilled oysters, and several kind of bread along with sides like carrots, fries, green beens. Since I loved it all I'll recommend my top 3:

Fried chicken... might be the best fried chicken I have ever had. It has a like spice to it and the flavor and crunch is perfect! Must order!!

Grilled oysters... I'm not usually an oyster fan but these were delicious. They were tender and well seasoned and cover in a delicious garlic Parsley "sauce". Again must order

Chicken and crepes: sounds unique and different and it is. The chicken on its own is amazing but you build a little bite with the crepe and a little sauce and pepper. Very good. Another must order

I highly recommend this place and will definitely be back

I've been coming to Dirty French since they first opened their doors. Literally since the beginning. 

The bartenders that were there the first year disappeared eventually, they didn't stay around long for some reason. They were all really, really nice guys & gals. I especially miss Sean who was one of THE COOLEST guys, just really, really down to earth and customer service focused! And if I ever catch wind of where he is bartending at right now I would be there in a heartbeat.

Then came DFs 2nd year open. A bunch of new faces, it was all good though. I'd still stop by and every once in a while.

Third year. Again, more new faces. They don't keep people long I guess. Discouraging, difficulty in connecting when not even ONE person is familiar (except for I guess a floor manager? not sure who the guy in the fedora is). In contrast I went over to Employees Only a couple of weeks ago with friends in town and it's still the SAME cool-as-hell guys! Here at Dirty French not so much.

Recently: I haven't been to the front in a while, but the hipster bartenders working in the back have no personality at all!!!!  I mean, AT ALL!! Nothing. Nada. Zilch. Like, I feel like they were just dropped into Manhattan from Middleofnowhere, Idaho by an alien spaceship conducting some kind of "Will they make it?" experiment. I mean, I've put off reviewing DF for so long because my experience as a customer had been getting more and more and more dismal as the years go by. But at this point I've thrown my hands up at it all.

If I am going to spend $17 or whatever it costs on a cocktail at the very least I'd like to drink that cocktail without being mean-grilled by the miserable bartender who just made it and is acting like I'm taking up valuable space, cramping the style of the important. As part of what I am paying for with that $17 drink is the experience. And this is from a collection of experiences over the past handful of months, not just one off night. 

Like I said, I waited quite some time to let this all loose because I really started out liking Dirty French, but honestly I'm just not a fan anymore. Since they don't keep their staff long, maybe once the two hipsters with no soul move on to serving artisanal cocktails with homemade bitters at some nose-in-the-air breathetarian/vegan members only bar, perhaps I'll cautiously try coming back around. 'Cause I'm a New Yorker and we like our people to have a soul. 

Until then nope. Au revoir.

The reviews here are quite polarizing and I will echo a common sentiment. Very good food at a very high price. 

Ambiance is dark, trendy and romantic. Service is good. 

Started with the gimlet which was solid and refreshing. A bit on the sweet side. 

The complimentary flat bread is similar to a lighter naan and comes with a fabulous Boursin-esque cheese. Very tasty. 

Tried the grilled oysters which were phenomenal. I would get these again in a heartbeat. Incredibly flavorful with tons of parsley. This was the highlight of the meal. 

For our mains we tried the hangar steak and duck a l'orange. Steak was succulent, cooked perfectly with a super buttery pan sauce. The duck was a little sweet for my taste and skin was not so crispy but meat was cooked well. 

Got a side of the hericot vert which were nicely charred but oversalted. Probs wouldn't get again. 

For dessert, we tried the beignets which were super light and fluffy and came with a luxurious chickory sauce. Good but misses the mark if comparing to cafe du monde!

Sky high bill but very good food. Would def get the oysters again.

hands down, one of the best meals i've had in years. our server, Chae, was flawless, and gave us excellent advice. everything was perfect from start to finish. the duck was amazing, as was the mushroom appetizer. delicious, fresh oysters. the opera for desert was devine. delicious cocktails and an excellent wine pairing recommendation from Chae.
Good wine list good place to sit and catch up with friends a nice quietish out doors area.
Great decor and great food. Literally everything is good here. The drinks were good but on the pricey side. Highly recommend it!

The experience started so well at the bar with the best strawberry lemonade.  I eat out a lot in different cities and let me say Pamela "spamala anderson" was THE BEST server I have had in years.   The knowledge of the menu and entertainment value was amazing.   Ask for Pamela when you visit.

This is one of my favorite places to eat in NYC!

First off, the name is fun! And, to my understanding, indicates the inspiration for the food which is french colonialism. So this is not your average french food, which makes this place even more of an exciting, varietal experience. 

Some highlights include the lamb carpaccio and beignets.

We started with the lamb carpaccio which was superb! Like one of my favorite dishes I have ever had. It was perfectly seasoned!

We finished our dinner with 3 desserts, the opera cake, the key lime pie bar and beignets. Now the beignets are the best I've ever had. Melt in your mouth good, with a light espresso dipping sauce. 

The service was also superb, with a very attentive wait staff. 

I highly recommend!

I only had drinks here - but damn! It is nice and chic and spacey and you're in the heart of the LES - great to being friends for pitcher of deliciousness ! 

Going back for sure :)

We still love it and the food is still superb. Maybe cause it was a Monday and maybe cause there were some very needy tables...but when the service is off, it is way off.  Sort of ruined a great meal and a great time. I rate this place among the best in NYC...still not to be missed.

While a little strange in terms of design, this place has some pretty great food.

This is a place in the LES on Ludlow.  It's got great open doors to the outside, making it a bit loud, but really ambient.  The decor is a bit on the extreme and fun side, treading right on the line between class and camp (the outfits definitely fall into the latter category).

The food is pretty darn great.  The chicken and crepes are amazing - while it isn't exactly unexpected or mind-blowing in terms of flavor profile, it's a solidly delicious meal with a lot going for it.  The mustard does a lot in making the dish more than just bread and chicken.  The fried chicken is, as one might expect, superb and spicy. 

Definitely a cute place to check out if you're ever in the area!

I was here with a few friends as part of a bachelorette. My friend was able to get us the reservation using Amex Platinum Concierge service. The ambience and service were truly beyond!! The food itself, I don't eat shell fish so didn't really get to try much...but love love loved the Sea Bass. Also they have a great, well priced wine list. I was pleasantly surprised that after 2 bottles of wine, several appetizers and main dishes we ended up spending less than $500 for a party of 6.

Spacious place divided into 3 sections: dining area, lounge in the middle with plenty of couches and a nice fire place, and a pretty garden. 

We weren't even late but we were seated an hour and half after our reservation time. Terrible!!!!

Food was good but pricey. 

Ambiance was lovely. Loved the vibes -  very cool and cozy!

Come here for special occasions or enjoy a nice drink at the lounge.

Cute place with a dining area and lounge area!

Will order again: trout, duck, grilled oysters, chicken crêpe & fried chicken, lamb saddle, beignets

May try again if someone really wanted to share: lamb carpaccio (too salty), hanger steak (average)

Had a fabulous time last night for our anniversary. So much fun! All the gracious hospitality of Danny Meyers' establishments, plus effervescence. Every person we interacted with seemed truly happy we were there and cared what we thought. Yes it is pricey, hence the anniversary choice. The food was sort of like classic French run through the French colonies. Ex.: a little heat in the duck a l'orange and not too sweet. Green beans in a soy based sauce. Merguez and harissa in something else, I forget what. But you could avoid these strong flavors if you wanted (we didn't want to.)  The mushroom millefeuille was one of the best things I ever ate. The lemon tart with meringue was, well, tart, with creamy meringue. Tried two wines, both really delicious. Will remember this meal for a long time!

Top breakfast! 
If you want to taste a bite of French just go to the dirty for an elegant and tasty breakfast

would give it six if i could. mille fueille, lamb carpaccio and vert salad for apps. the flatbread they brought out was somehow crispy and chewy at the same time in the best way possible. the duck a l'orange was melt in your mouth. expensive for sure, but worth it.

Awful, awful service. Brunch day before Labor Day and we were completely ignored once we got our food, which was actually good. People on both sides of us were asked how they were doing and if they needed anything ... tried to get their attention and they didn't even look at us. Had to flag someone down rather aggressively to get water glasses filled and the bill. Told them we felt ignored. No apology, nothing. Really appalling for an upscale Manhattan restaurant. I have no more words.

One of the coolest place in Lower east side. It gave some quaintly vibe to downtown. Beautiful people around, good decor. The food is amazing. Perfect for dining and hang out 
Must try- Duck. One of the best duck ever. 
And the dessert gave it the happiest ending

I dined at Dirty French recently on a Saturday night with a friend. Overall we enjoyed our experience. The service was good, as was the food. 

We got a drink after dinner in the restaurant's lounge area. We were honestly not very impressed. 

It took forever for someone to come over and take our drink order, and she was very brusk. For the very high prices, I would expect the bottle of wine to be presented, then poured in front of us. Instead, the threw each glass of wine down in front of us, and disappeared for the next hour. 

Overall a great experience. The service in the lounge area, however, was not amazing.

Dirty French is my favorite restaurant in NY. First of all, the flatbread is so good that I'd go just to eat that alone. The boursin-esque cheese they serve it with makes for a delicious and deadly combination (your arteries will not thank you later but your tastebuds will). The trout entree is seriously next level, one of the best dishes I've ever had (it's soaked in butter, natch). The tartare and lemon tarte also receive honorable mentions. I think the key with Dirty French is ordering the right items off the menu, because you can either have an amazing food experience or an "eh" food experience.

That being said, IMHO the "eh" items are:
lamb carpaccio (sometimes its too salty)
opera cake (get the lemon tarte or beignets instead)
scallops (nothing special but good if you're on a diet or want a light entree, i guess)

"Big Jorge" is an amazing waiter and was not only very accommodating  of our food requests but also brought us complimentary champagne and desserts on multiple occasions (we pretty much eat here on a weekly basis, its that good). Contrary to other reviews, I don't find the prices high given a) we're in New York and b) the quality of the food and service. This is a really unique (and delicious) menu that you can't find elsewhere. Dirty French is always a good time and we love rocking out to the 80s music.

If I could give a zero, I would. Probably the absolute WORST DINING EXPERIENCE EVER! Do not go - do not waste your time. Can't really review the food because nothing we ordered ever came out. Drinks took about 30-45 minutes. Bad bad bad...

Let me tell you even though some girls at our table didn't quite enjoyed what they have ordered I loved everything! I tried every dish on the table at least a bite and all was perfection. 

I ordered duck for main and it was so so tender. Sauce added a nice hearty sweet touch. 

Our server was great, we were also been checked on by other employees and i feel like it adds extra special feel when celebrating a birthday. 

Deserts are a must try!

One of the best meals my wife and I have ever had. I though the duck at EMP was great, Dirty French's duck L'orange was the best duck entree I have ever had. It was so good on Friday night I came back on Sunday night to have it again. The Bourguignon (grilled oysters...incredible. Can not rave enough about this place.

This was my second time at Dirty French and it's still amazing. Our waitress offered some recommendations and she was spot on. The spicy pork was tender and delicious!
It had a spicy but sweet taste, I mentioned to our waitress about the sweet taste and she said there's brown sugar in it which made it that much better. The atmosphere is great with 3 different large rooms. The only negative thing I have to add is the 80's top 40 pop music, terrible for a french restaurant. I still give 5 stars but PLEASE get better music.

One of my favorite restaurants in the Lower East Side. Gorgeous dining area and the service is awesome.  I highly recommend the chicken and crepes for two.  It is delicious and a fun eating experience, as the chicken dishes come out in multiple courses.

Service was excellent. But the food was disappointing. WAY TOO MUCH SALT! This is hypertension central. Make sure you ask them to go easy on the salt when you order. We couldn't even finish the dishes.

Looks like we found a new go to spot for drinks.

This restaurant is amazing.  Cool, luxe and buzzing.  

The first time I had dinner with a girlfriend.  The food was amazing and staff was better than we could have asked for.

Returned the next night for drinks with a bigger group and hung out in the back lounge area.  They welcomed us and were accommodating to our large group.  

Get the fries - that creme fraiche does not disappoint.

Ugh yum this place is so good I can't wait to go back! Who wants to take me?!

The flatbread with the cheese spread is crack. My dying wish is to shrink down to action figure size and use the bread as a warm buttery blanket. 

The lamb carpaccio is amazing and the tuna tartare was excellent although the crepe was a little greasy. The whole atmosphere is trendy and perfect for drinks and dinner before a night out. I had two cocktails and felt loose as a goose.

Went here with my parents yesterday for brunch after randomly walking by.   The decor is beautiful!  Luis was our waiter and he was honestly so great!  He helped us with our drink selection- we got the champagne special and gave his honest opinion on our choices of what we ordered.  Everything was delicious and we cannot wait to go back for dinner!  Thanks Luis for making brunch so great!

Absolutely love this place! They have a fun unique decor, very exciting menu and great cocktails. Food is phenomenal, they always know what spices to use and everything has such a great flavor. Definitely order the carpaccio, millefeuille and tuna tartare, it`s delicious!
Can`t wait to go back there for dinner!

I always stay at the Ludlow when visiting NYC and have been to this restaurant located at the hotel a couple of times.  The first time I tried it I got a seafood entree and I was honestly not impressed.  However, I recently got some breakfast from their room service menu and I liked it very much.  The reason for the 3 star rating is that as far as a good French dinner is concerned, there are just much better places in the city to get it.  However, Dirty French certainly is not bad and it is convenient if you are staying at the Ludlow.

Dirty French was on my to try list for a while, but it was alright. Nothing was amazing to me that absolutely had to come back for again. We began our meal with their FLATBREAD w/ FROMAGE BLANC before we shared the CHICKEN & CREPES. The dish was good, but was it worth how expensive it was? Not really. I have a feeling that I perhaps did not order the right dish. Should a friend invite me to dine there again, I'll give it another go. Until then, I won't be returning. ENJOY!

I've wanted to come here for a while since we live nearby. I was expecting a lot and was very disappointed. Best items were the complimentary flat bread and cheese, grilled oysters, and shrimp salad. The chicken two ways wasn't great. The fried chicken was decent (very spicy) but hoped for a tastier piece of chicken. Lamb carpaccio was gross and saw someone at the table spit it out. The sea bass came in a soupy broth that wasn't great. The fish was fresh but the broth/soup was nasty. I will come back for breakfast because the Eggs benedict is the best but won't come for dinner. The place was pitch black ..

Came to Dirty French on a Tuesday night with reservations at 9:00 PM for 5 people, we were not seated until 10:15 PM, so there goes the service. As for the food, their flatbread and grilled oysters for appetizers were pretty delicious. For main dishes, I would stick with their fish selections. Their steak, lamb, and duck entrees were okay, surely not worth it for the price. You can definitely get better ones from other restaurants.
Hip, low key spot in the LES. Excellent menu. Sit down tables, and lounge area with couches and bar at the back with a great conjoining outdoor patio heated in the colder months.

Great find! We stopped by after dinner to have drinks and check it out. Cool bar scene and lounge. Amazing drinks. Be prepared for a lively bar scene and "sit where you may" (or where you can squeeze in) lounge. Fun atmosphere in the back lounge. Food must be good because the place was packed! We will definitely be back.
Ordered a Tito's and Soda, which was $2 more than their signature cocktails. What?! And $18 Tito's? Insane. Overpriced and awful service.

This is now one of my favorite spots. I love the vibrant scene which is entertaining but not intrusive. The music was really good. But oh the food is the standout. The flat bread that they start you out with is divine especially when slathered with the buttery, herby cheese spread that comes with it. I definitely recommend pre-ordering the suckling pig if going with a group. The lamb carpaccio is so delicious even for those who don't like lamb (it's not as gamey tasting as lamb usually is). And the chicken and crepes comes with both a skin on chicken breast in a creamy dijon sauce and a few pieces of fried chicken. I couldn't have liked a meal more. Plus the service lives up to the food ; knowledgable and friendly without being too much so from both the wait staff and the sommelier.

I had a legitimate reservation and showed the confirmation email. They claimed they no longer use the service, but never properly shut off the booking engine. Host/manager in the questionable hat needs to be fired - he said Jesus Christ under his breathe and started to curse me out, then talked down to me. Never experienced such attitude in a restaurant where I have diner so many times, including for work events. Employee turnover and more attentive management is needed so the staff is at par with the good food. Have never been so embarrassed in a formal restaurant setting due to an inept and uncultured management team - please consider a staff turnover.

My favorite place to get together with friends for special occasions . Very cozy atmosphere. They have lounge area with sofas and a fire place . Amazing food  very creative  and chef driven . Very nice staff and the drinks are on point. Very romantic sexy Ambience if you want to impress someone this is a great place for date night.  It's classy and upscale but not stuffy.  The oysters are delicious come with soft fresh baked bread to sop herb infused oil.  Sooo good .  I had the lamb for my main course  and key lime desert . Yummm...

Always a memorable experience. I've been here 3 times in past year and and has been consistent. An intimate experience with good energy in the room, delicious flavorful food, well sized portions, impeccable service and a first-class Maitre'd. I always leave satisfied, this restaurant never disappoints.
Started out with the tuna tartare and it was . The burger was quite tasty as well. When we went there for lunch it was fairly quiet and not very busy. Would definitely recommend.

I came in at a Sunday night and fortunately seats were plentiful at 6 pm. The internal furnishing is delightful and waiters were very nice.

The starter bread was good although not surprising. The salty flavor from scallion stimulated appetize before following dishes.

Carpacci is beautiful. Different tastes of lamb, bell pepper, sheep yogurt and eggplant is harmonious. The toasted bread is satisfying but I expect  better ones  next time.

Duck L'Orange. This my favorite in this meal was composed of duck breast, resevered orange, garlic sprouts and sauce. 
You can find a flavor of duck in the sweet sauce cooked with various spices, indicating it was cooked carefully with duck bone (or other parts of the duck). This sauce connected the rest parts, uniting them as a whole dish instead of a merely combination.
The reserved orange was made from oranged peel and orange flesh. A routine accompany of duck breast or other fatty dishes. However, regarding the sauce was sweet enough itself, this fruit part slightly lacked a brisk feel. I guess it was because using more brisk flesh would add more sweety taste, which is unnecessary. Unexpectedly, this lacked brisk, fresh taste was completed by my glass of wine (2016).

All in all, I had an enjoying night here. The price was somehow expensive, I have to admit; however I don't regret paying for a delighted experience.

This should be zero stars. Do not go here. My group was overcharged for drinks, but we just paid it to avoid a dispute. I saved my receipt though. Then, the next day, I checked my credit card statement, and I was charged double the amount that was on the receipt I signed. My friend said the same thing happened to her. Her receipt and credit card statement didn't match either. So, you better either avoid altogether or save your receipts and check your statement if you go here.

Came here for dinner, atmosphere was really nice. We had wine to start in the hotel lounge which was nice. Our reserved table was ready for us on time. 

Once seated for dinner, we had ordered more wine and starters. We shared the flat bread, lamb carpaccio and the baked oysters. All of this was really good and delicious. Especially the oysters. 

For dinner we had the black bass and lamb. Both were ok, I would say the bass was the better of the two. Very light, moist and tasty. The lamb was not great. The meat itself was light on flavor and the entire Slav of meat was coated in a thick mushy layer of cumin. Not sure if this texture was the intent but didn't really do it for me. I would definitely. It order the lamb again and try either the duck or pork. 

All in all, pretty good meal. The price was what you would expect and ran the two of us with wine around $300.

I've been to Dirty French three times now and the food and experience has always been amazing.  In my opinion, Dirty French and Carbone is Major Food Group's best restaurants.  

The ambiance is definitely cool plus the location on Ludlow allows you to enjoy the night life after dinner.  Wine selection is on point and flat bread starter was damn good.  Cote de Boeuf and the Duck were my favorite entrees.  I would also recommend the lamb carpaccio, and pomme frites on the side!
How cute is this place?!?! Came here while waiting for my table next door, it was amazing.  So cute and great drinks. Definitely an insta worthy spot. Grab a cocktail and enjoy!!

Expensive Mediocre food.  

We waited 45 minutes to be seated for our 10pm reservation.  Otherwise the service was average.

We were a party of 6 and everyone just thought the food was just okay.  The lamb in particular was uninspired.  Some of the appetizers, such as baked clam were good. 

At least the music was nice.

The food here is just ok but over priced. I ordered duck, skirt stake and grilled oyster. The oyster is pretty good and side dish mushroom is very good. I were not impressed by the main dish though. The service is pretty good.

Had a great time at this place after finally listening to my boss and coming here for dinner.

Table of 4 - seated straight away. Drinks came quickly and Sommelier was very helpful in choosing the wine.

Waiter helped a lot with the ordering and we had some fantastic oysters, maybe the best I've had in NYC so far, with the Lamb carpaccio and Tuna Tartare. This of course comes after the famous flat bread with fromage which is A+. 

Carpaccio was great, tuna tartare also really good. We had those 3 across 4 of us, and it was more than enough to tie us over to the main. 

My wife and I split the Chicken and crepes, my friends had had the duck w/ orange and the scallops.  We all had a little bit of everything and the Duck was really good, the chicken though was awesome. It comes with a Dijon reduction which strong, almost overpowering but then also a spicy chicken drumsticks and wings with a great yoghurt sauce. I found it hard to stop.

Wine was well enough priced and given that we had probably 4/5 drinks each plus dinner, 125 per head with tax and tip was fair.

Price - 4.5/5
Food - 5/5
Ambiance 5/5 - we didnt go but there is an awesome bar area we would definitely try out sometime.
Service 5/5.

Fantastic place, highly reccomend.

We met about 30 minutes before our reservation for a cocktail. We were sat on time, but a bit tight for a group of 6 in their booth. 

We all thought the appetizer were terrific, but the entrees about average. We had the kale salad, a mixed green salad and tuna tar tar. While the salads were very big, the tuna was not large and presentation could have been more polished, but it was tasty.

For dinner there were 3 fish and 2 steak Au poivre. Ithe meals were fine, just not anything to remember. 

The service was very good. My only complaint besides the entrees need more work, is the wines were pricey. Bottles start at 90 to 100. In this day and age, a quality bottle for a bit less should be doable. 

Cool hotel in a great location, but needs some work

I was astounded by the rudeness of the staff, particularly the bar tender. We waited about half an hour to get a menu, and again, the same amount of time to finally receive the drinks we ordered. (Not to mention his unprofessional and condescending remarks to questions my friend asked about the menu).. And then, once we were ready to close our tab.. you guessed it! another half an hour to get the check. It was a quiet Wednesday night, and there did not seem to be any explanation why the bar tender blatantly ignored the patrons that were patiently waiting for service. I would not recommend.

Sexy!  This was the last unplanned stop on my bachelorette party.  We went to a show nearby that was not very enjoyable and left early looking for a bar nearby.  We saw a sign that said "hotel" and my friend remembered coming here, so we decided to go inside.  It was crowded and everyone was looking too-cool-for-school.  Then my crew shows up with me in-tow wearing a fake tiara veil and a large pink button that says "Bride to Be".  We loved it, but stuck out a bit compared to the too-cool folks in this bar.  

But we asked for a table and they very happily found us a section with sofas and chairs.  The drinks were good, but I was done drinking by the time we arrived.  We really loved hanging out here, and everyone really much just did their own thing.  I don't think this is somewhere to meet new people since most people were in groups.

But a cool place to come with friends.

Stayed at the Ludlow hotel for New Years. The restaurant's atmosphere was very nice. We were told we could sit at the bar for the a la carte menu, and they insisted we could order from that menu sitting down at a table. We got pushed into ordering the three course meal which we were told was $60 per person- fine. When the check comes it was $135 per person for the most mediocre food we've ever had. Not to mention the waiter was judging us by asking how much we "loved" the food and seemed surprised that we never finished any of the courses. Everything was either over peppered or flavorless. Again, this is a review for the New Years 3 course meal, so maybe the regular menu has some good choices.

Went here with a couple of friends to grab a bite for brunch on a Sunday afternoon. The place was decently crowded, but we had no problem getting seated right away.

To start the meal off, they brought out three baked goods--each of which were pretty tasty--a madeleine, a lemon glazed donut, and a pecan bun. I think the pecan bun was my favorite of the three.

For my meal, I went with the burger. The burger was cooked perfectly and served on a great bun. It had nice flavor with the cumin being very pronounced with the onions and the cheese breaking through as well. The only pitfall to this burger was that it was impossible to eat with my hands since it basically fell apart, but I enjoyed it with a fork and knife nevertheless. 

It was also served with potato crisps that I really enjoyed, though I swapped out the creme fraiche for a chipotle mayo.

Overall, this place served up some great food and is a decent place to check out for brunch. Service was friendly and food came out quickly.
Stopped for a quick cocktail and enjoyed our visit. Super professional mixologist. And there's a whole other scene as you walk further back. Highly recommended a stop. .

Came here for my friends birthday. Cute and cozy setting, if you come in the hotel entrance there's the dark lobby and some seats behind it where you can sit and have drinks. We started with the layered eggplant and the fresh bread which was a delightful pairing. The bread with the spread was amazing, I could've probably eaten 5 plates for myself. For the main, I ordered the duck which was a bigger portion than I thought and my friend ordered a fish which was a large portion as well. Both were okay. The staff was friendly and attentive. Nice place overall.

The earlier you make your reservations- the better! Dirty French is a one of the best meals I've had recently in New York. It is located in a breathtaking venue with a great outdoor lounge. Amazing place for date night. The chef was amazing that night and we got an insane amount food but it was well worth it! Staff was super attentive and friendly, will return soon. 




:(01/27/2018)

Service was good. We had a great wine guy who helped us choose an excellent bottle in our price range when we sat down. Our waitress was attentive, answered our menu questions, and helped us order.

We went there set on getting the Cote de Boeuf per the recommendation of a client that said it was the "best steak in NY". A bold claim and came no where near that expectation. It was medium rare and certain pieces were melt in your mouth delicious, but there was also a lot of fatty pieces and very over salted on certain bites. For that price and the hype, really a big let down.  Sides do come with the Cote de Boeuf. Bib lettuce salad was overdressed with too much salt and vinegar. Broccoli with horseradish was DRENCHED in the horse radish and overpowered every bite, then that taste lingered on my plate.  The potato puree was straight potato soup and not very appetizing or pleasant to look at. It came with leeks as well, I'm not a fan of those and can't say if they were good or not. There was a bearnaise which was okay, but on the salty side.

Overall everything was fine. For the price, I want to say "get over yourself" to the restaurant.  If it wasn't for the incredible wine, servers, and the bread, this would be a 1.  I can't speak to the rest of the menu, but the price and quality of the steak was very disappointing.

Place is really great.. had dinner for 2 at the bar, both bartenders were excellent, from their hospitality to their service.. we had the trout and spicy pork. Both were fantastic dishes. Headed to the back lounge for drinks after.. all around great experience. Must try!

We visited Dirty French today, as a group of 5 for brunch. It was surprisingly empty on arrival - and even emptier when we left. Having now eaten there, it is no surprise as to why. Here goes:

Service: the service is horrible. It's not that the staff are unpleasant - although I will say today's Sunday team was definitely not warm, nor particularly friendly - but it's really all over the place. No bread until after the appetizers arrived, we never had the correct silverware on the table at any point throughout the meal, and at times there was just no one on the restaurant floor.

Food: SO BAD - AND FOR THE PRICE. We've all lived in NYC for more than 7 years, and this menu and food experience falls firmly into the 'super disappointing and surprising' category. How does this place get such hubris around it? The salads are lame, the burger is an embarrassment, the beef dip is deli-standard and so on. Not one of us thought the food was good. In fact, at the end of the meal we were trying to remember who on earth had recommended the place, and why?? We were at a complete loss.

Overall, there are hundreds of really great brunch spots in the city and Brooklyn. This is not one of them... unless you want moody (or absent) service, food that will leave you wondering what the menu is all about - and then a bill that really kicks you where it hurts. If you're going to charge $20+ for a burger, it needs to be a really really good one.

Love to find a new spot to eat, but this is definitely not to be repeated. If today's experience is anything to go by, none of us have any idea how it's attracted so much buzz - and bookings. 

Save yourself the time and effort and eat elsewhere.

NOTE: The manager took the time to read this review, contact me soon after, and offer to make-good, which is appreciated. Reassuring to know someone on the team has good style!

Brunch, brunch, and more brunch.  But every meal is great here..... I just prefer brunch.  First the gratis pastries they bring out while you read the menu in detail. The tuna tartar I order every time.  The duck hash is also terrific. The lamb (isn't the Breslin's) but is also good.
Order the oysters with parley and butter, also get the lamb carpaccio and the mussels.  You will be very happy.

Dinner Saturday night to the tunes of Phil Collins? No thanks. We complained repeatedly about the lame 1986 doctors office muzac and were told it couldn't be changed. Food mediocre, decor nondescript. NOT 4 stars but then again I'm a New Yorker, no wide eyed tourist. But even if i were a tourist I'd want a better place than this to celebrate my few nights in town.

One of my favorite NY brunch spots - live jazz, yummy French pastries & charming European aesthetics - where you feel like you stepped into a different world beyond the concrete jungle of the city. I still think about the delicious complimentary pastries which were perfect in texture and sweetness. Topped with a fried egg, my flavorful duck hash is worth coming back for. Add in some jolly jazz with an accordion and saxophone player, this was a great brunch experience. Dirty French is also connected to this beautiful hotel which has a stunning lobby and outside space to sit in. It was worth coming through just to see the design of the hotel. Completed with excellent service (albeit they gave us the wrong bill initially but they resolved this immediately) I would highly recommend you give it this place a try.

Love everything about this place. Cool sexy vibe, friendly staff. Cocktails are out of this world amazing. The bread they give is heaven. Love the tuna tartare. The chicken for two is so so good. Had the pork chop another time which was ok. Beignets are fantastic. One of my favorite places

I ordered the duck and it tasted as if someone just drenched it in salt/ seasoning. They even made it sound like it happens all the time soooo maybe fix that problem ... The worst French food ever, actually it is a disgrace to even call this French food. Atmosphere is cute that's the only good part.

Our server was really nice. The chicken for two was really good. The bread at the beginning is delicious. The cocktails are yummy. Good vibe overall. Just don't like having to wait over twenty mins for a table even after making a reservation.

Went for dinner and overall was unimpressed by the restaurant.  If you want French food go elsewhere.  If you want very tasty food, go elsewhere.  If you want a scene, this is your place.  The ambience was great for a Friday night dinner with friends but the rest left  a lot to be desired.  Giving 2/5 stars as I would return for a cocktail (not food).

*Food*
- Unimpressive (esp. given the price point)
- Heavily seasoned / salty
- Appetizers: Carpaccio, Flat Bread were tasty
- Entree: Duck (so-so), Scallops (a bit fishy)

*Drink*
- Decent cocktail list
- Wine is of course pricey
- If you get a bottle, note they will decant and store (red or white) somewhere other than your table

*Service*
- Very pleasant staff
- Do not expect a 'fine dining' experience

*Ambience*
- Noise level was buzzing but okay for conversation
- A bit too dark (every table had a flashlight out to see the menus)

Took my wife here for her birthday and Dirty French instantly became our new favorite place!  Carpaccio was amazing as was the endive salad. My wife ordered the trout and I had the hangar steak and both were absolutely delicious!
Good brunch place and good service, live music and love the lemon donut that comes with the starter dish and one of the best place to be for Saturday brunch.

Came to Dirty French on a Tuesday night with a reservation for four at 730. The space is gorgeous and well designed. The bar is also beautiful. This is a Torrisi restaurant (team who owns Carbone). The staff is diverse and dressed stylishly. The service isn't exactly warm and wasn't really personal but it was solid and efficient enough. We were also late but they didn't stress which was nice. Additionally while I loved the 80s and hip hop soundtrack the music was loud so you couldn't hear across the table - maybe I'm going deaf and old but it was loud. Here is what we had
- wine by the glass (Syrah grenache) - this was excellent and the cheapest glass at $16
- flatbread with cheese spread - as good as advertised and it comes freely
- lamb carpaccio - excellent
- grilled oysters - excellent
- millefeulle - mushrooms. Great presentation but I didn't love it
- hangar steak - very good
- bass - i didn't eat it but I was told it was good
- chicken and crepes - loved it! Cooked perfectly both fried and in a cast iron pan
- beignets - light and delicious 

Our bill was 500 with tip. Expensive. And they charged us for something we didn't get but I missed it until later.

I will definitely come back for this super flavorful food despite the issues mentioned - really good restaurant.

Literally loved the brook trout and the free bread that came out before our meal!! Came here tonight with a few friends and we were all blown away by our meals.
