It's a fun swanky setting to get cocktails or a bite. I would say it's a bit overpriced but the service is good and they were quite accommodating to my peanut/tree nut allergies. Will definitely be returning to impress any friends visiting the city!

Lovely place, the atmosphere is so cozy. We had friends staying in the hotel and met them here before dinner. A great place for couples or groups. 
However the service is terrible. Every bartender and waitress had a very bad  attitude. If I am going to pay $18 for a vodka and club soda I hope to have top notch service or at least  a polite bartender.
Very disappointing.

Had a lovely Saturday breakfast (at 10:15am so not really brunch) here this weekend. This restaurant is part of the Ludlow hotel. The decor is very clean, sleek, jazzy and instagram worthy. I really like how cozy and relaxing it felt. For food I ordered the Ludlow hotel breakfast sandwich I think that's what it's called. It's an upside down croissant with ham, cheese, tomatoes and egg ($14) It was very tasty! I also had a cappuccino ($5) with my sandwich. 

Overall this is a pretty pricey place for brunch, but you are definitely paying for the atmosphere. There is also live jazz starting at 12pm which we just missed as we were heading out. Very neat establishment and I definitely would come back to try other items on the brunch menu. I saw people with cute donut platers as I was leaving so I def will get that next time.

Very much enjoyed my experience at Dirty French. Vibe is great and food is impeccable. Made a reservation for a group of 5. Had a drink at the bar and let the bartender free style it. He made my friend and me an insanely yummy and spicy tequila cocktail. A couple of us split the duck, the trout, and the beet salad. Everything I put in my mouth was heaven. The duck with specifically the standout. Also, the complimentary bread was so good. Highly recommend. And great service.

Went to brunch on Sunday
Mediocre in every regards.

Service: 3/5
Not terrible but nothing impressive
at least, very friendly, which was good.

Food: 3.5/5
Tuna tartar and duck hash was good.
oyster was good though tiny
Steak was rare when order was medium rare
meat was good but now great. 

Interior: 2/5
Cheaper, more cheesy version of Balthazar, pretend to have some sort of 'edge' unsuccessfully.

I never miss out on a restaurant by MFG and been wanting to try this place for brunch for a while. I enjoyed eating here and the portions are extremely generous by NYC standards. They also provided a "bread" basket to start which included donuts and muffins-was delicious. I had the French dip-was great. The food is just lacking in freshness. Otherwise was great.

We had dinner last night at the Dirty French a recommendation from a friend, as we are visiting from Toronto and wanted something with good food and a good vibe. During the dinner service at some point, I was pickpocketed and someone took my credit card and $300 from my wallet.  I must say they had a bit of class to at least throw my handbag back under my chair before making off with my cash. I tried to call the restaurant after I got back to my hotel, but they don't have anywhere to call rather an annoying voicemail letting you know to "email" them to change or cancel reservations. I would think a Restaurant of this caliber would at least have somewhere for patrons to call if something happens, I was so upset that I couldn't even get a "Human" on the phone to let them know what happened. So in short Patrons beware when heading to this Restaurant and DONOT let her hand as out of your sight, I Had mine hanging on the back of my chair, with my back on it, and I still got jacked!! Not a great experience for my first night a weekend in NYC.

we had a group dinner and the foods was great and we kept ordering the same bottle of red wine we enjoyed very much. since we share some foods the bill was $120 per person. not bad for great wine and foods. 

Our waitress was hilarious. She knew all things that she was talking about. She definitely has a passion for the foods and is as funny as Margaret Cho! We will be back for her. 

The sea bass was very good, mushroom millefeuilles was interesting with texture. hard to tell it was mushroom. We had two dessert but begniets was too delicious, so we had to order more. It was so light like cloud and perfectly warm.

The steak was garbage - full of sinew, undercooked even for someone who enjoys rare, and exorbitantly priced. The staff was insulting when the food wasn't praised. The service was unorganized and  inattentive. The cocktails were fine.

Perfect place for a Saturday brunch to catch up with friends and family. There is live jazz from 12-3 which adds to the experience - we were there for around 2.5 hours and never felt rushed by the polite and friendly staff. I had the omelette which was excellent and my friend had the duck hash which was also wonderful. The starters, sides, and sorbet are also great and nicely portioned. This place is my new go to for a fun brunch without the booze (although I'll be trying their cocktails next time!).

Hands down one of the best meals we've both had in a long time!!! I was hesitant at first as I am with most hotel/restaurants. But the food was amazing! We had the grilled oysters, artichoke salad and the steak as well as this amazing punch cocktail!!! Highly recommend ;-)
The food is very tasty, however the room is extremely loud, the portions are VERY small, and it's way overpriced. After I left I went to eat pizza because I was still hungry.

I hate restaurants with attitudes, and this group is awful. I can't stand all of the protocol and the stupid rules. Never again.. I don't know how New Yorkers go to this place. No more for me. Great cheff with bad bosses ! Making a reservation at this place or cancelation is a job. And we just wanted to go to dinner. 

Went back cause the manager wrote me back,  and had a good meal, service was good and everyone was friendly. However the reservation and cancellation system is absolutely ridiculous.

Very cool atmosphere, good service and excellent food. I had the duck and my husband had a spicy pork, both were amazing. We also had two sides which were also fantastic. It is very pricey, but totally worth it!

I have a mix of emotions for this place. The food was delicious (had the chicken crepes as a main and I highly recommend), but the waiter was a whole other story. 

The main thing that set us off was he failed to mention that with the steak for 2 people (my 2 guests ordered that) would include an array of sides. Since the only thing the menu states is the steak, we thought sides were separate so we ordered an additional 4-5 sides. As the food gets brought out, only then does the waiter mention that the steak comes with mashed potatoes and a couple other sides.... Like are you for real? We wouldn't have ordered all the extra sides if it already came with it! 

It just seemed like a cheap way to bamboozle people into spending more money and wasn't appreciated.

Very strong food, at decently strong prices.  If you don't sweat the dollars, many of the dishes are quite interesting.  In particular the lamb carpaccio and the tuna tartare starters are both worth a shot.

Had a wonderful Saturday brunch experience here a few weeks back. The decor is definitely worth mentioning - so different for Manhattan and kind of quirky with little red hens and ceramic statue heads on the wall as decor. Also a bit rustic with the wooden ceilings. Its very clean and well lit by the chandeliers, and would be very relaxing if it wasn't for the extremely loud live jazz music - they just need to take the volume down a smidge. My uncle joked the entire time we were there about ways to make them stop.

The food and service were however, phenomenal. The waiter was very attentive. They provide a "bread" basket to start which includes donuts and muffins- all delicious. I went with the classic eggs benedict, which was one of the best I've had in NY. Everyone at the table couldn't stop talking about how good the home fries were that came with most dishes- just the right amount of crunch and so flavorful. Although the price is high, the quality is too :) 

After brunch we went over to one of the couches and got drinks from the bar, such a nice family atmosphere and much quieter than the main brunch area. We noticed little tables out back on a patio set up for brunch as well, it was too cold that day but I would love to come back and try them out!

Mixed feelings for Dirty French

Pros 
Great atmosphere 
Wonderful staff
Delicious food

Cons
$19 Moscow Mule (not in a mule mug)
Super expensive ($17 apps for small portions)
I would not accommodate A friend with a restricted diet   She literally ended up with a bowl of dry romaine leaves with a Side of lemon for $12
Fussy reservation system 

A nice place for an occasion but beware the cons

Sad. We were excited to try this place. From the moment the hostess said 'FU' about my son who just turned '21' to the bartender being ridiculously rude when we ordered drinks. We didn't stay for the drinks let alone wait for a table. Uncalled for rudeness. We were completely shocked at the only 2 staff members we came in contact with. Pitiful they ruined what was a special night planned. #lbgtq #gaypride #notcooltranshost #sad-bartender  #nypride

My first 5 stars in awhile! I first came here 2 years ago when it was impossible to get a res. Came back tonight and hands down the best yummiest fun dinner I've had in NYC in the last 6 months. The bread they serve is UN-effing-real. Then--the chicken crepe for two--bye, dead. It's the most interesting dish. It's perfect. Come here, now and order the chicken. You're welcome.
Come here once or twice a year ... Diandra makes this space for me in the bar/back room! Excellent service and incredible interaction.  Lovely decor also. Food ain't shabby either ;)

Had a great dinner here last night!   Started with a drink at the bar before snagging a table without a reservation. The bartender makes a mean negroni and there is a nice by the glass list.

Food here is pricey but extremely well prepared and flavorful.  We started out with the special fois grais (no clue how to spell that).  We also got the beet salad.  Decent portions on both and they were both delicious.

For mains we got the creole pork chop and the steak au puove (yea, French isn't my strong suit in spelling).  Perfectly cooked. Steak was normal side, the pork was on the larger side! 

Excellent and very pricy wine list.  Definitely some stuff that was way out of my league.  But the knowledgeable and friendly sommelier was able to guide us in the right direction!

Overall food and service here is top notch, but it's not cheap so definitely a special occasion place.

I went to this restaurant as my cousin was there a week before and he gave it such great reviews.  We had 7:15pm reservations last night.  We were seated right away and the waitress immediately came over to ask if we wanted some water.  We looked over the menu and although the restaurant ran out of the lamb, my friend ordered two Au Poivres, one for his appetizer and one for his dinner. My friend and I shared the Millefeuille for the appetizer.  It simply was amazing.  For our dinner,  I had seafood dish with sausage and my friend had the Duck A L Orange.  Everything was simply amazing.  All three of us had dessert and it was delightful.

Amazing always amazing! We took our lawyer and we really impressed her.... she gave us free legal advice all night long !! I like going early to get easier seating . The Maitre D' Jaime is so cool, he really sets the tone of the restaurant to make you feel like you are " in the know" I cant wait for our next visits!! Oh and if you lucky you will meet "Royce" ( its as new York as New York gets !!!)

This place was amazing. From the moment we got in, everyone was so nice and sweet. Great service, very attentive staff, and the food was just exceptional! Highly recommend if you've never had French food

This place is certainly more style than substance. As many have noted - Great ambiance and decor.  Very pleasant and attentive staff.  Great bartender who poured nice drinks.   The food however, just WAY TOO SALTY!  I'll nickname this place "Salty French" -  The naan like bread your are brought was a good starter, but after a few bites, it was just too salty to continue with.  I ordered the charcuterie plate which was huge, and at $25 a good item to split.  My wife ordered the lobster app, which didn't seem very fresh - in fact it was rather mealy and fishy, which she promptly sent back.  (our waiter was very courteous and apologetic about this by the way).   We ordered a bottle of wine after discussing our likes with the sommelier - who first tried to steer me to a $250 bottle.  We settled on a "fabulous choice" (his words) for $80.  And I was very good, so hats off to him on the choice.  Unfortunately, both our mains were way over salted - i chose the pork chop - which is crusted with some sort of rub and sauce, making it taste more like a BBQ rib - it was really tasty for the first few bites - then the salt just took over and that's all I could taste.   I thought it might just be the rub,m but the meat itself was really salty so maybe they brine these.   Either way, after a few pieces I could barely eat it, my mouth was burning.   My wife's steak au poivre  had the same result.  Nice sauce, but very very salty.  I really wanted to send my pork chop back but i stuck with it.   The "pomme frites" were good but not what I expected or wanted - their version is a 1/4" thick slice of a whole potato. Again not bad, just not fries.  Overall, it was a nice, chic spot for a date night - just don't come with high expectations for the food.  Not sure we'd return again for dinner given our experience, but it is def a cool spot to grab a cocktail.
Yum and yum!  Food & drinks are spectacular and appealing ambience.  Recommend checking out and will certainly be back.

Just stumbled upon Dirty French last Saturday afternoon. .... what great luck. Eggs Benedict and Duck Hash were incredible. Service was friendly and professional. Beautiful dining room. Worth the price. Can't wait to return!

Had a really delicious dinner here the other night. Standouts include the pork chop, beignets, and scallops. The hangar steak I could have done without. The cocktails are also super tasty and do not disappoint. Will be back again soon.

I was visiting NYC last week, and went to Dirty French on Saturday September 15th... We sat at our table and waited 2 1/2 hours and our food never showed up, and we got refunded for the drinks we got.  Our water was never refilled once in that time, and 5 of us shared two pieces of bread for 2 1/2 hours.  Every worker I saw including wait staff and management was openly drinking alcohol and walking around the restaurant, and no one ever told us why we were never getting our food.  Seriously egregious restaurant management skills and service.

The food is absolutely phenomenal. Every bite of seafood was over the top. DO NOT MISS THE OYSTERS. I could make a last meal out of the grilled oysters as long as they promised me 70 or more. And the beignets to finish--oh my god. Get there early to grab a drink and crash on the couch in the back bar. It's so good. Just go why are you even reading this anymore go eat oysters

On the pursuit of something new for French food, the Dirty French has promising signs to please those who have intimate, dark lit, and nourishing food/drinks in mind. As a first timer, I was impressed for most things, and made my brunch a success! The Dirty French is located in close proximity to the Ludlow Hotel, and as with most prestigious hotels in NYC, they need a reputable restaurant to depend on/viceversa, so it also caters to patrons there too. This restaurant is located in the northern part of the Lower East Side off of east Houston St, and the closest subway stops are: 2nd Ave (F) being 5 minutes away walking, Delancey St (F/M/Z) also 5 minutes away walking, or Essex St (M/Z), also 5 minutes by foot, and plenty of parking garages and street parking in sight. I've only been there for brunch session today, so I'll base my review off that. Dirty French, on the outside, looks notably similar to other buildings seen on LES (a striking feature is its pink neon doors near the entrance), and inside, you're greeted with an old style, French dining room decorated with accessories that makes you feel welcomed. 

The menu (in terms of brunch), offers usual French classics, such as bourguignon (French beef stew), parfaits, omelette, tartine, and American classics such as eggs, oysters, pancakes, grilled salmon, and bacon to name a few items. Drinks are the usual classic cocktails and wines, priced by glass or bottle. There's a note on the drink menu saying that the restaurant only accepts cards only, in other words, cashless. Might be a convenience to some, or a detriment to others, but know before you go (lest you want to panic)!

My personal experience at Dirty French was mostly positive! As a last minute plan, I've went here for brunch, and fortunately my reservations were honored (plus the crowds were silent). Greeted by the friendly maitree d' to my seat, and my waiter was also friendly while offering the usual starting dialogue of "Sparkling/Still (Tap)/Bottled" water before I've commenced. My starting drink was a lemon tea, and I've patiently waited for my food to arrive. A short time later, I was greeted with a complimentary pastry basket, comprising of: fresh baked madeleines, lemon glazed donut, and I believe a muffin/pastry with chocolate and nuts, most likely customary for other brunch sessions, and it wasn't that bad! The donut was a bit "juicy" brimming with lemon extract, and the madeleines were baked to perfection. A bit more time passed and I was greeted with my main dish: pancakes, and an order of Pommes-frites. 

Munched on my Pommes-frites first, and on one hand, the ~12$ price tag was a bit baffling for a small (?) amount of fries, but on the other hand, the quality was exceptionally well done. Baked to a golden brown crisp, thicker vs fast food fries (but not as thick as wedges/steak fries), and a perfect balance of salt/oil for this side dish. Also paired with a "special" house dip, I'm not sure if it was ranch or another condiment. The pancake itself was only by itself (as in one, not 3 or other quantities), but it was large enough to encompass the whole plate. It was topped with in-house soft butter, and lemon preserves, and a small tray of maple syrup. Exceptionally soft/chewy (no "crisps"/brown spots), and easy to gullet down, I've thanked my waiter for those pancakes. Afterwards, it did "feel" I was a bit too full, maybe the high density of the dishes helps, but it's by no means an offset. Contemplated on ordering a dessert (as I would with some places), but I didn't necessarily need to, so I've waited for my bill (which was a long wait of ~20 minutes). The waiter arrived and gleefully sent my check, which to the surprise of myself, had a "Credit Card only" sign! Normally I'm accustomed to cash, and I've frantically searched for my card to mitigate this, but it's hard to go around this (w/on negotiating with management to access the cash from the bar), and I've left with a healthy gratuity to my waiter. 

To close this, Dirty French happens to be one of those ideal LES restaurants that not only are a good fit with a successful hotel, but can make due with the usual Sunday fare or brunch crowds without haste. The food was exceptionally prepared, but "filled" quickly, and I was somewhat disappointed with the pricing of the French Fries. Nonetheless, I might return, maybe for a dinner service in the the future to sample more things! I'm glad to have paid a visit when I did. 

Until next time.

PS/Edit: Try NOT to cancel or "no-show" unless if things don't work your way (if you have dinner arrangements, call before 12PM the day of your reservation). A jaw dropping 50$ (per guest) would be priced on your no-show, which would be donated to the Robin Rood foundation to end NYC hunger. On the one hand, it's a good cause and I'd understand, but it does warrant people to seriously consider coming here and sticking by to plans.

Disappointing.

We came here for brunch and were thoroughly unimpressed. The service was good and we loved the 80's soundtrack playing in the background but we came for the food.

We had:

- Charcuterie -  practically​ inedible. The pate was horrible. The meats were greasy. 

- Pancakes - basic

- Omelet​ - average

- Granola parfait - my daughter wouldn't eat it after the first bite.

For the price, I expected more.

I'd give five stars for brunch but four stars for dinner. The quality of food and ambiance is the same for both but brunch prices are much more reasonable. Anything on the menu with duck is going to be great. The best item on the menu is the fried oysters (brunch). Also brunch starts with an assortment of pastries. Authentic and tasty French cuisine.

Update: the owner reached out to me and offered a free meal. Will update with how yummy the food is. Appreciate the owner caring about the opinion of his customers. 

Place is too pricey. We had walked by this place and thought it looked cool. So we saw they opened on Sunday at 7 AM, we came at 730 and the doors were locked. We came in through the HOTEL it's attached to, and the concierge notified the servers/hosts that they had guests. We were the only people in there, so we figured it would be fast service. It was perfect because we had a plane to catch later. Wrong. 
Each of us ordered a different dish, except for my mother and I, we both got the $18 special. 35 minutes later, when our food arrived, the server handed us our food and left immediately. After looking at our plates, my mother and I got something completely opposite of what we ordered. 4/5 of us had the completely same dish. I tried looking around for staff, but they all avoided eye contact or steered clear of us. I figured it wasn't worth the bother because they would have to cook up two completely new dishes and we'd miss the flight. Since there were 3 or 4 different people helping us, we figured we were better off not causing a fuss about it. Although both is us eat $14 dollar dishes and got charged $18, we only missed out on $8. It's the principal. 
The ambiance is cool and the place is really nice. The food was not bad, actually pretty decent, just not $20 a plate r. It's just the service and run of the place was shitty. Maybe we'll try again for lunch or dinner.

Unprofessional and horrible service is what Dirty French is about. I'm beyond baffled that this place has such a high rating, maybe it's due to being inside a nice hotel, either way the service was terrible!!!

Friday evening myself and a few coworkers sat in the lounge area to grab some food and drinks. I ordered a burger (medium well) and asked them to removed the tomatoes and mustard when I placed my order. My coworker ordered her burger medium. When the food runner delivered the food he asked who had the burger cooked to rare and who had the medium well burger. Neither of us ordered a burger cooked rare and we told him that, he then said it's cooked rare to medium. Again neither of us ordered a burger cooked to that temperature. He followed up by saying that it's all the same regardless of the temperature which is false. 

When my burger came out, he made sure to say it was the medium well burger, which luckily it was. I take a bite and there's mustard on the burger along with a side of mustard which I asked to them to remove in the beginning. I flagged down the waitress and she takes it back to the kitchen. She then places another order for a burger. The second burger comes out and it only has pickles on it, which isn't what I ordered yet again. 

I then take the plate of food up to the bar where all of the waitress are standing and punching in food orders. I begin to explain what I ordered to a man wearing a hat who I assumed to be the manager because he was giving directions to the others. He quickly says "no hablo ingles" and runs away, when 2 seconds before he was speaking fluent English to the other waitress and they all giggled and a different waiter listens to me. 

I then get a third burger to come out, this time the chef personally delivers it to me and explains everything on the burger. Again it's wrong and at that point I just take the plate and eat the fries and call it a night. I'm not sure what the problem was or why they're was such a lack of communication the entire night with my order. Needless to say everyone working in this restaurant needs a lot of training and customer service experience due to the lack of ownership and order taking skills. You'd think those would be the basic requirements to work here. I was wrong.

Met colleagues here for a business lunch.  The salads were excellent, and the service was also excellent.  We were temped by the wines but seemed unsure, so the server brought us all a taste - very generous!  Complimentary flatbread brought to the table was delicious.  Prices are a bit steep, but quality and beautiful atmosphere made it worth it.  Tip:  if you get there early, wait for your friends in the back garden, it's gorgeous.  In fact, come early and have a cup of coffee or tea in this space before your meal.  Best kept secret on Ludlow Street.

This is the breakfast only review. We stayed at that hotel attached to this restaurant. In town for work so breakfast at the hotel was a must. The eggs Benedict was delicious. Instead of Canadian ham found on most eggs Benedict this was a thinly shaved country ham that was delicious. My coworker got the pancakes which she raved about. The staff was fantastic very attentive and open to all request. They also have feeding in the hotel covered patio.Breakfast was around $16 so not bad. I would recommend

Sexy | Good Service | Chicken-dinner 

Fun! Had a great time!

Lamb Carpaccio | Chicken Dinner | Cocktails (hint: there is a cool back area outside and cozy fireplace for post-drinks!)

Really a great addition to the lower east side. The night started with drinks in the lounge in the back. I had a bourbon based drink pagalle, and my friends had a drink in a tea cup which was poured from a beautiful class carafe. The service was great here and the decor was stunning too from the fireplace to the lighting.  The food in our private dining room was great and the bartender had a bourbon and gin cocktail that we all liked. The appetizers were stands outs especially the lamb, shrimp, cheeses, and the egg rolls.

Overall the food was delicious, chicken was tender, lots of butter in most things so come to enjoy and not be healthy. My favorite was a quiche dish, and  the baked oysters.

Saturday brunch is always tough unless you reserved a while ago, Dirty French is located in prime LES among all those long line brunch place, at the ground floor of LES hotel. 

Surprisingly jazz band performed even during brunch time, the meal started with jazz and a free plate of bakery! Taste like heaven ! Ordered a pit of strawberry cocktail and duck leg hash, burger and egg Benedict, food are normal, not amazingly impressive but the atmosphere and drinks are good, the free plate of pastry definitely adds points to this. Bring your friends to impress them with an afternoon jazz brunch!

We came here for a bachelorette dinner. The service was stellar and everything that we ate and drank was delicious. Thank you for sending out special gluten-free items for me! My favorite items were the tuna tartar appetizer and the steak. Everyone else at the table loved the chicken dish that came out two different ways. I can't wait for my next visit!

Well it is snowing and sleeting out- awful weather - and the lobby and bar of the Ludlow Hotel is filled. So, wet and cold we (4 of us) make our way to the bar at Dirty French for a bar stool and a drink. (The dirty French is just beyond glass and metal doors off the lobby.)BUT. alas, the snooty manager ushers us out ( He's annoyed.) because the restaurant is closed and opens in 10 minutes! BTW The staff is flurrying around and the bartender is behind the bar twiddling his thumbs. So, cold, wet and being guests at the Ludlow Hotel, we get kicked out because we don't want tbreak the rules do we?  Whatever you do, don't break the rules at this restaurant! No exceptions------- even if you are freezing!!!!!

UPDATE: So, Jeff from Dirty French sought me out this morning after the above incident.Wow! He apologized for last night but much more importantly, he was a REAL gentleman. He did the right thing. My family and I ended up having our second GREAT breakfast at Dirty French thereafter. Jeff "broke the rules" so that we could have breakfast after the hours that breakfast is routinely served. Thanks Jeff and thanks Dirty French for making things right and filling our tummies with a fabulous breakfast!!!

BTW This  is our second stay at Ludlow Hotel and why we will keep coming back- in many ways they manage to be intimate and accommodating in a  NYC hotel.I am so appreciative!

OMG their house bread was FANTASTIC! The grilled oysters were mind-blowing. 

The entrees and the lemon cake were meh though. We wanted to order duck breasts but they were sold out. We ended up ordering the skirt steak and the sea bass as suggested. Quite mediocre. 

Waiters were nice but the wait time for the table (even if we had a reservation) or the entrees were long, like 40+min. Might have been just an exceptionally busy night. They also gave us a round of drinks for compensation. 

Overall, we'd still want to go back for the oysters and house bread! Maybe try out the duck breast next time.

Wow, this is the worst experience I've had at a restaurant, maybe ever. This was my fifth time having dinner there and it was a special occasion--my boyfriend and I were celebrating our anniversary. Drinks and appetizers were great, but then everything went downhill from there. The front of house/manager guy, a large man, kept putting his butt in our face to talk to his table of friends next to us. Eventually, he just plopped down and sat right on top of my expensive purse, coat and personal belongings to take a selfie with them!! My boyfriend and I had to ask him to move, and he got up off my purse and still sat there gingerly taking selfies. Given it was a special occasion, we ordered the Cote de boeuf. Not only did it arrive undercooked, ALL of the sides, the steak and everything that came out was COMPLETELY COLD. The béarnaise was starting to coagulate it was so tepid. Zucchini that was supposed to be grilled was cold, hard and inedible. Have you ever had cold pomme purée? It's not very nice. Béarnaise also tasted more like hollandaise. Even more shocking to myself, not a single person came to check on us during our meal and ask how it was. When we asked for the check (and the majority of our meal was left on our table), still, no one asked how it was. Considering the front of house guy was so unprofessional as to sit down on my personal belongings to take a selfie with his friends, we decided not to engage with him on the quality of the food. For two, the bill came to over $300 (the undercooked steak was $180). To top it all off, the bus boy aggressively came and wiped off crumbs while my elbows were on the table. I was looking at my phone so I didn't see him in advance and he didn't say anything, but he basically punched both my arms with a filthy crumb pusher thing. I am extremely disappointed and I will never be going back. Dinner there was like a joke and this restaurant is clearly going downhill.

Excellent food and wine selection. Our waiter recommended the grilled oysters as an appetizer, and we were so glad he did. Dirty French is known for their Chicken Maison for two and it was delicious and definitely more than enough food for two. Perfect spot for dinner with friends or for date night.

The service was excellent.  Extra mention of Jeffrey and managing customers in an exceptional manner. They have a cocktail that is like a margarita that has great flavor balances. The side of mushrooms were delicious as well as the starter flatbreads. The kale salad was excellent and perfect for sharing. The decor and ambiance is the plus, you forget its part of a hotel.

Big props to the management of Dirty French for immediately responding with attentiveness and humility when my experience wasn't what I had expected (or experienced in past visits).  Mistakes happen - and that kind of customer service goes a long way.  Thank you!

Exceptional service and food!! Brunch was amazing. Live music MADE MY DAY!! Fresh complimentary pastries as soon as you sit down?! Like whhaaaaaat!! I wasn't sitting for more than 45 seconds before the server came over to bring me a coffee. Then they brought us over the the lobby of the Ludlow to finish our drinks. Absolute must try!!! Never go anywhere else when you have visitors in NYC

Good brunch.

Went there for Sunday brunch with three others.

Menu was not large, but tood was very good.  I had the duck hash -- it was really good, and really filling.  The LES -- ludlow egg sandwich -- certainly looked good, and my companion enjoyed it.  The bagel and salmon was also good.

A few items of note:
* The food was reasonably priced
* The service was not just good, it was noticeably nice -- not common in a NYC restaurant.  They could give lessons on pleasantness to other NYC restaurants
* The brunch included, gratis, and excellent selection of little pastries.  The madeleine they served was particularly delicious -- best I'ver ever had.
* Live music playing, but not overly loud.  I was able to converse with my companions -- all of us nearly 40 yrs out of HS -- without a problem, other than a couple of moments when over-enthusiasm seized one or another member of the trio.

Really deserves 4.5 stars.

Ludlow St is a little out of the way.  That said, I would happily go there for brunch again.

Visited Dirty French on a Friday night.  Overall, the experience was OK.  The setting and ambiance are nice.  With regards to the food we had the grilled oysters, the chicken for 2 and a side of the pureed potatoes.  The oysters very good.  A few had some "crunchy" bits of shell in them but overall the taste was good.  The chicken for 2 is done 2 ways.  Breasts come in a mustard sauce and then the thighs and legs come in an asian style/type marinade.  Both were good but I thought the 2 flavor profiles were an odd pairing.  The other downside was the chicken was warm; not hot.  The potato puree was good but was heavy on the butter and salt.  So overall the food was good.  Not great and not bad.  Regarding the service, it started out very attentive in the beginning but as the night went on it just dropped off.  Water stopped coming, no one checked on us and we were never even offered a dessert or after dinner drink.  That was a bit disappointing.

Last night ordered trout. It was 5 star! Obviously fresh, beautifully cooked and presented. That's usually a dish to avoid, too hard to get genuinely fresh! We ordered every dessert, not one less than good, a few were great. Nice wines by the glass--not fabulous, but drinkable. The food and place deserve 5 stars, but dining room noise level was deafening. But then we checked out their lounges and rooftop, oh so mellow and comfy! Everyone was incredibly friendly to us. Going back SOON.

Came here for brunch and everything was impeccable. The atmosphere/decor was sophisticated but still eclectic. They had a super cute 3 person band playing music that was the right volume - entertaining but not louder than our conversations. The lemon glazed donuts they gave us to start were just the right amount of sweet.  My friend and I shared the breakfast sandwich and the burger. Both were great but the burger is a must have. Cocktail list is great and to top it off, our server, Mahdi was extremely knowledgeable and attentive and incredibly personable. He even helped us decide what to eat when most waiters usually just say "it depends what you want". Will definitely be back!

Very solid brunch. Ambience is five star especially during holidays. Love that they have a live band I didn't find it distracting. A lot of group seating but also went here with one friend - best to ask for booth. Mahdi rocking it with his energy and service too

So I'm giving this 3 stars ONLY because the food and drinks were great, with no complaints. 2 Stars for service. My issue was with the service. We had something on our serving plate and we asked for a new one. We got our appetizer before a new plate was brought, We waited a few minutes and still no server in sight - and we ordered the broiled oysters, which were a little messy to just eat without a plate. So we actually had to get up and go ask for a plate. Then we waited around quite a bit after our drinks were empty, waiting for the server to come back to let her know we wanted another round. When we were done eating, she didn't have anything in her hands when she came to the table and we told her we were done eating. She said 'that she was busy' and someone else would be by to clear the table - yep...had to wait quite a while for that to happen and for our waitress to come back with a dessert menu. 

When we sat at the bar before getting our table (we had reservations and they were behind about 20 minutes) the bartender didn't wipe the bar (we literally slid in to two seats as two people had just paid their check and left), so there was water residue from the previous drinks all over the bar. And there were no bar napkins around for us to wipe it ourselves. The bartender took our drink orders and still didn't clean the bar. No one wants to sit at a dirty bar, afraid to put their arms down for fear of getting wet stuff all over their clothes. 

This staff is not very attentive at all -it's almost like they were being inconvenienced by our presence there!  Thankfully the food was delicious! Everything we ordered we really enjoyed - but for a bill that we are paying over $200 for - you think the experience would've been better.. and we are not needy or high maintenance customers in the slightest! Quite disappointing.

Space is very tight as well - we had a small table for two and ALL the tables are extremely close to each other. I could hear all the conversations around me. AND kinda noisy in here - but that's still wouldn't be a deal breaker for us to eat here again.

Turns out one of my favorite hotel bars in New York has a *secret* upstairs room. But what's special about the private space at Dirty French at the Ludlow Hotel is that it still has that same ambiance as the downstairs dining room and lobby bar. (So many media events are held in windowless, mindless conference rooms that feel like oversized panic rooms from which you can never escape.) Also you can only access it from a door that looks like it's just another panel in the wall, and who doesn't love that?

We had a fabulous waitress named Pamela. We had two people in our party with two different food allergies and she was SO knowledgeable about the ingredients and preparation of all the menu items, that she could tell us what was safe and what wasn't for each to eat. The carpaccio was perfection and the duck was amazing. The sides didn't come out in time to eat with the meat, so she took them off of our bill. The sommelier was helpful and the ambiance was cool. Wish we had time to go back and hang in the bar.

OMG! Brought my wife and daughter for dinner here. The food was out of this world. Truly amazing and delicious. In addition the service was beyond perfect! This restaurant is a must go! We were all very impressed. Fantastic night!
We really enjoyed our stay hier.Breakfast is tasty and diverse.Thanks to Mahdi for such a nice service and friendly smile every morning!

Good service, good atmosphere, average entrées and fairly expensive bill. 

Dinner: Scallops for myself and Le Créole for my fiance. 
Dessert: Tarte

Overall, Dirty French is good but is nothing outstanding or spectacular. Our waiter was pleasant and attentive and the mood and atmosphere had hints of Parisian charm. 
The entrées had a French flair to them, but were not jaw-dropping. There was quite a bit of saltiness to the food and the dessert was not French styled but more American-French styled, à mon avis.
This place is inviting with a great wine selection, but it was overall just an average night of dinner.
May I just say, Fried Oysters are a must. Savory. Everything else was delectable indeed but this was my fav! (Did I mention the wine)

Yelp added this place to the suggestion that I might like and decided to try it since it has good rate and looks good, I got the pancakes and it was nice, nothing really special for me personally, I would say it's normal place above average and may have different taste for lunch or dinner.

Absolutely hit all the marks in all the positive reviews that have been written!

The atmosphere is wonderful, the food was delicious and the service was perfect!

The restaurant is so spacious, they've created uniquely distinct areas to enjoy in an open space where each area can be seen from other areas that you may be seated in, but no area intrudes or imposes on the other, and because all areas are aesthetically beautiful, you feel compelled to want to relocate to the next. 

I'm sure you'll not get to enjoy every area in one visit because you'll be so satisfied with your first 2 (probably dining & fireplace lounge seating), it would be unlikely that you continue to move to the garden room or seating at the bar. But, no problem. Just plan to go back - a lot!

The food was mouthwatering delicious. We were informed when we ordered that it may take a bit for the food to arrive, and I have to tell you, everything was going so well, we weren't even concerned about the timeframe. We just continued to enjoy the drinks, atmosphere and service - but NEWSFLASH! - the food arrived so much sooner than estimated. Just another example of the quality of service that we were experiencing. 

The entire staff was so pleasant, attentive, accommodating, and professional during our entire visit that, if it weren't for the fact that you're looking the individual in the eye while you're speaking with them and they've introduced themselves, it would feel like one large blurry experience of perfect service. This is not to take away from the individual efforts, but to show that they are all on the same page. I loved it!

Well, I have to stop now, but I could go on. 

I suggest you go see for yourself. 

I know I'm going back!

Enjoy!

Excellent ambiance- the back has a lounge area with a fireplace! Not too crowded (it was a weekday) and tasty cocktails. 

I highly recommend the Grand Prix cocktail. It's strong, and tastes legit, like something you would get in the 1920s. 

The restaurant was great, too! But, given that each main course is almost $45, the quality of the food did not match the price. I also found the food to not be very adventurous- traditional French meals like duck à l'orange. 

The service was exceptional: light hearted and fun but very professional and knowledgeable.

Best restaurant experience in awhile!  Service was super nice from the moment we walked in.  Food is creative and simply delicious.  Tuna tartare wrapped in a crispy crepe was special and the duck a l'orange was the best duck I've ever had.  Highly recommend!!

Eat. Here.  You cannot go wrong.  A lovely evening and ask for Kevin.  Start with a Grand Prix and work your way through the lobster and salads and FLATBREAD (ask for two orders) and whatever your main will be will make you happy though we suggest pork and duck.  Beignets for dessert and lemon tart.  Great evening!

This place is packed on a Friday night. I dislike any place that is elbow to elbow sitting arrangement. We had the bourbon cocktails and it was very good in hindsight.  tuna tartare was good, i can't say the chicken for two. just a bit flat, and you have nothing to eat with. So we ordered a mashed potato and the texture was more like condensed milk. my friend's pick and i do not care for this place.

We had a great experience here from the moment we walked in, greeted by the lovely Allison. What a beautiful restaurant, the ambiance is a combination of warm and quirky, and totally unpretentious. Make sure to arrive early to give yourself a chance to check out the lounge in the back before you sit for dinner. The mural out back from King Tut's Wah Wah Hut brought me back to my L.E.S. party days in the '80's-- Re: the food, we were not disappointed. The curry mussels we ordered to accompany our flatbread was amazing, and our server Jorge was most gracious and extremely knowledgeable and helpful. We will definitely be back!

My fiancé and I came here for Valentine's Day dinner. For spending a lot of money we expected a spectacular experience but I would rate it as just average.
It was the service that we weren't impressed with. They greeted us nicely and we were seated right away. However, we didn't get the menus for a very long time. When the server finally came to ask what we would like, we stared at him confused and finally he brought the menus over. And  we were just twiddling our thumbs for long periods before our dinner arrived. People who came after us had gotten their food before us. 
Food- we had the prefix Valentine's Day menu. Most of it was really good. Started with flat bread followed by grilled oysters and tuna tartar which were all yum! For our main course we had the strip and the sea bass. Strip was delicious, however, the bass smelled and tasted like the sea which made me nauseous and couldn't eat it. I called the server to take it. Which is where I was surprised as I am used to someone asking what's wrong or if they can replace it. The server took it without a word. Service is where they lose the stars.
Ambience- The place has a romantic, fun feel to it. From the entrance, to the ceiling and the lounge in the back it's all very intricate. Dark, romantic atmosphere. Love that part. 
Maybe I will give it another try but not for a special occasion or a busy holiday. 
For a special occasion and the price I expected better.

Awesome dinner. Great bar / wine list with lots of hard to find spirits and wines. Pretty high end, but there are some more reasonable options sprinkled in. 

Food was fantastic across the board. Charcuterie platter was actually not just stuff you could but at Eataly, duck was amazing, apps were delicious (and generous portions). Tatin and beignets rounded it out for dessert.

While I have been here for dinner - which was delicious - this review is for brunch.

The menu is somewhat limited but standard brunch fare.  The bread was DELICIOUS!  I had the duck hash which was filling and yummy! Others had the dip which I heard was excellent and the Tartine with egg which had mixed reviews.

Overall I wouldn't come back for brunch - it was good but not exceptional.

Great French downtown. I love the ambiance at dirty French, it's dark and sexy. The restaurant itself is a bit loud but that's almost inevitable in Manhattan. Overall good food and a great scene for the LES

I took one star off because of service. We came here for a special celebration and I had high expectations from this place specially after I learned that they were from the same group as Carbone. 

We were seated right away although there was some confusion on our reservation but that wasn't their doing at all so it was nice of them to honor it and still seat us. 

Our server didn't really bother about asking or striking any conversation with us. Again, this expectation is only because it is a high end restaurant and the service and food should be par excellence. 

We ordered the drinks and appetizers. Drinks were on point. I had the Petite Locco and it was delicious. 

They serve a flatbread and you could choose your topping for some additional bucks so we chose the Tomato Mustard. However, we were served Mussels Au Curry and it was just plonked on our table by some other server. We had to ask our server about Tomato Mustard to which he said  that they were out of Tomato Mustard so he made the executive decision of serving Mussels au curry (which he said were on the house but it magically did appear on our bill later on). Also which restaurant runs out of tomatoes and mustard? They were also out of the Lobster appetizer that we really wanted to try but I can understand running out of lobsters (although it was a Sat night so you gotta stock up). 

Anyhoo, for our mains we ordered Black Bass and Lamb. We have visited many high end steakhouses in NYC and everywhere the protocol of the server has been to ask how we would like the lamb to be done. Our server didn't bother asking so we thought maybe the chef wants it served only a certain way which is commonly acceptable by diners so we waited. The lamb was delicious in flavor but it was medium rare (a little more rare) and that's not our preference. Again, a $$$ restaurant ought to ask you these details when you're dining with them and you have a certain expectation from your meal.

Service overall was very disappointing and nothing was done to redeem themselves. I would go back for the food but I wouldnt recommend any friends to go there if they are looking at celebrating something special because I know you have to be on your toes now with ordering and that's a little daunting when the idea is to enjoy!!!!!

Pure happiness. From the service to the drinks and last but not least the food....pure bliss. I was smiling more and more with every bite. Thinking about planning my 40th birthday celebration here. The ambiance is cozy, not too loud, just right. Loved the staff, loved my meal, loved everything! Will recommend to everyone and will be visiting many more times including my birthday this year!! Je t'aime Dirty French

I had some time to kill and stopped into the nice enclosed patio. Ordered an overpriced cocktail that should have been tastier and decided against my better judgement to get 6 oysters ($22) and the beet salad. The salad was good. Better than good but not winning awards. The oysters? Please don't serve raw oysters with chopped up onion, parsley, really anything. I get that you have to hide the fact that they are tiny, but here's a thought- just shuck them and serve them. Nobody needs a tablespoon of red onion in every bite. 
And turn down the Glade spray please

Yeah, sex is cool, but have you had dinner at Dirty French? 
Came back to try the food after my friend and I were blown away by the cocktails and dessert last week, and all I can say is that Yelp needs to add more stars just for places as good as this.
We were shown to our table right away and started off with cocktails, I had the Belmondo with the modification of jalapeno tequila at the recommendation of our waitress (who deserves 5 stars all on her own), which was amazing, and my friend had the Laragoza, that was so irresistible that I had to switch over to it. I was a bit skeptical about a cocktail with yogurt in it, but it is as delicious as it is beautiful. 
For a starter I ordered the kale salad (despite the fact that I usually don't like kale) for the sole reason of how amazing it looked and smelled at the adjacent table and it may have just made me a convert. They somehow managed to remove that starchy, chewy texture that I find unpleasant and perfectly complemented the leaves with a deliciously refreshing dressing. I may or may not have also stolen a good portion of my friend's verte salad because of how good that dressing was too (sorry!). 
The main course... sweet baby Jesus. I ordered the Millefeuille, which at this point I'm pretty sure means "this is was heaven tastes like" in French (possibly not, but all the French I know I learned from Moulin Rouge so sue me). The dish consisted of a million paper thin slices of mushroom that were surrounded by a creamy, slightly sweet red curry with chickpeas that was so good I'm pretty sure my eyes rolled into the back of my head after the first bite. That sauce was astounding all on its own but also brought out the flavors and texture of the mushroom and I couldn't get enough of it. The chef is an absolute genius and culinary artist with hands of gold that deserves honorific statues erected just for this curry. The mashed potatoes were the perfect complement to our mains (our waitress rightfully described them as a hug in a bowl) and we ordered a second portion as soon as we tasted them because they were too good to share. 
Dessert was a lemon meringue tart that was a wonderful combination of sweetness and tartness and everything else that you want in a dessert like that. 
Throughout the dinner we also got to try their barrel aged Manhattan, which was the first one I've ever tried anywhere that I liked (and the bartender was kind enough to bring them over!). I want to come back here one time just to sit at the bar and drink Manhattans while channeling my inner Don Draper. We were also lucky enough to share a drink with none other than the handsome host from last time that was once again rocking absolutely perfect lipstick.
After my friend mentioned that she was on the hunt for a birthday party venue, the manager graciously showed us the event space, which was done in a gorgeous old world style and entirely remnicient of the Campbell Apartment, and the backyard patio area that seems like the perfect combination of intimacy and ambiance.

There are a lot of good restaurants in New York, what sets Dirty French above them is the level of service that they provide. The careful attention to detail, curation of atmosphere and the feeling that they will do whatever is in their power to make your experience the best possible one is not something that is easily achieved, and Dirty French has absolutely blown it out of the park. 
What are you doing still reading this? Go make reservations!

UPDATE on last week's review:

So last night, my friend and I came back to Dirty French to try a dinner this time. WOW. I truly have no words to describe how blown away we were, as if we had any doubt. We were met with the coolest host who showed us to a great table. Our waitress, Pam, was incredible. She knew the menu inside and out, gave recommendations, advised on dishes we might like, and was an overall pleasure that added to what would be an amazing night. We ordered two salads and a flatbread as appetizers and two other dishes for our entrees. Our cocktail of the night was the Saragoza and boy was it amazing! I've never tried a cocktail made with yogurt before and now I don't know how I'll live without it. The staff here is great, truly passionate about the restaurant, the menu, and making sure we had a great night. The food was superb. The slightly hefty price tags are well deserved and entirely worth every penny!

Food orders:
Verte salad - delicious!
Chevre salad - wonderful, especially for kale which isn't a favorite of ours.
Millefeuille - this dish is a labor of love. The mushrooms were perfectly, thinly sliced and stacked together within a sauce that I can only describe as an angel's magic sparkles.
Boulangere - I have never in my life had lamb so tender and the sauce it was accompanied by was pure perfection. The mashed potatoes it came with were, as our waitress so affectionately called them, a hug in a bowl. That they most certainly were and we ordered another portion for my friend because they were just that good.
Broadbent ham flatbread - perfectly salted and thin prosciutto with a soft and seasoned flatbread and delicious butter-like spread.
Lemon dessert - I forgot the name but this delicious little dessert was the perfect combination of tangy and sweet!

We also had two shot-sized drinks, one of which was their version of a Manhattan and the other had the lovely name of "pink pussy." Let me just tell you, I don't even like Manhattans and this cocktail was so delicious that I can now come back to the bar and order a Manhattan like a real adult! The other shot tasted like a melted starburst candy sprinkled with love. An absolutely amazing evening of delicious food, delicious drinks, wonderful ambiance, and a perfect NYC environment.

Dirty French does everything exactly as a great NYC restaurant should. Bravo!

Such a great brunch spot! Before I get into the food, I just have to say the inside was so cute and trendy, it had a nice vintage french vibe. There was live jazz playing and the windows let in a nice amount of natural light, all of which added to a great ambience. As for the food, I tried the avocado toast, duck confit potato hash and eggs benedict along with their bacon. I have to say, while all of it was delicious, their take on avocado toast had me hooked. Rather than an avocado mush, the avocado was finely diced. The "toast" was a delicious choice of french bed, soften with a mustard oil and a tomato jam. I promise, this will be the best avocado toast you'll ever try. Another thing I loved, they bring to each table a little plate of various fresh pastries. I am not sure if the pastries vary daily, but we had a maple sticky bun, glazed donut, and lemon poppy seed madeleines. It was a sweet and delicious snack to nibble on while we waited for our food, which did take quite some time to finally arrive at our table. I will definitely be recommending this restaurant!

I think my review is consistent with others' comments regarding service. Bartender was not only rude in demeanor but terrible at giving service in a timely way. Reordering a drink while sitting at the bar after a long day shouldn't feel like an Olympic sport, especially at these prices.

Solid innovative French with good cocktail list! Must get the trumpet millefeuille, sausage, duck a l'orange, as well as the chicken pour deux. Everything was nicely executed with max flavor and classy presentation. The sauces are to die for, as it should be at a French restaurant. Go with a bunch of friends and share a bunch of the dishes and you won't be disappointed!

Brilliant! We were staying at The Ludlow Hotel. My husband and I sat at the bar, Dan the bartender SO knowledgeable!  He made genius recommendations. We had the oysters, steak and pommes frites, flat bread with herbs and butter (complimentary) AND beignets with sugary rum sauce for dessert. Dan recommended a perfect cab blend for the meal. I dined here the next night, as I stayed in. Kevin my waiter was so attentive, like Dan. He made perfect recommendations. Started with the endive salad had the trout and haricots vertes. I was  fighting a cold he recommended the lemon ginger sorbet which was tasty and soothing. This is a beautifully run restaurant with an elegant cozy bistro atmosphere. Recommend 100%!

I came here for Sunday brunch recently with a friend and we loved it! I'll admit that going for a traditional French restaurant wouldn't typically be my first choice for brunch. At first glance, the ambiance of Dirty French was super cute as it is located at the bottom of the Ludlow Hotel. There was also a live band playing jazz music that definitely livened up the experience. To top it all off, the food was SO GOOD. Here's the rundown of what we ordered: 

- Bourguignon: Our server sold us on this appetizer. This dish is basically grilled oysters in this amazingly buttered garlic sauce & parsley. Comes served with a hefty slice of baguette that was perfectly crisp on the outside and soft on the inside. I'm not a huge bread person, but I was very impressed by this! Dipping the little baguette pieces into the leftover sauce was heavenly.

- Duck Hash: My favorite dish! The duck was so flavorful and pleasantly crispy. It sat in a bed of nice, equally crispy potatoes that were seasoned perfectly. The fried eggs on top were also cooked just right, and the runny yolk really complemented the rest of the dish.

- Dip: Slices of dry aged beef in between the same amazing slices of baguette. It came served with large amount of crispy pomme frites and of course, a delicious au jus sauce for dipping your sandwich. The serving was huuuuge so my friend and I shared. Very filling choice if you're on the hungrier side. 

All in all, we were really impressed by brunch at Dirty French. The quality of the food was amazing and worth the price tag. Check it out!

This restaurant was highly recommended. People said the food was wonderful. My friend and I ate there last week. We were not impressed at all with the menu choices or the execution of the food. We should have gotten the burgers.
For $240 : one appetizer, 2 entrees ( the trout) , 3 glasses of wine, one dessert plus tip, I felt cheated because we did not like the food.
The restaurant is pretty, however and the atmosphere is good.  The highlight of the evening was walking down Ludlow street and seeing all the cute shops and restaurants. Would I go back or recommend it? I would not.
My service here was amazing there is a very nice big smiled lady working in the kitchen who made my time here out of this world. It was above and beyond  her name I believe is Kashia

4.5 rounded up to 5 for a very tasty meal at Dirty French. The complimentary bread is a flatbread focaccia kind, oily, warm, and salty. It comes with soft cheese on the side. The bread is addicting and super good, we ended up asking for it 3 times over the course of the meal. For appetizer we ordered the sausage, which was really good, with sides of potatoes and mustard. The price for the sausage is a bit too high, $18 for only 1 sausage. Finally for entrees we ordered the steak frites, and the burger. Both came out fairly quickly and were very tasty. Overall great service and food quality, even though pricy.

4 stars if the price doesn't offend you...3 stars if it does. Delicious though a bit overpriced. The chicken for 2 was delicious but not worth $76. The duck was also solid. The real standouts are: flatbread, chèvre, roquefort, and verte. Chèvre was amazing! Bright, light, full of Moroccan flavor and lots of texture.

This is fast becoming my favorite restaurant in New York.   Everything is first class - from the fantastic host, who gave us a choice of tables, very attentive service, great cocktails, loved the baked oysters in garlic butter, all the way to dessert. You guys are amazing!  I will definitely come back again

Our waitress was exceptional, knowledgeable, thoughtful and very courteous. 

Food was on par, didn't care for the leak drenched in vinegar tho. Steak was cooked perfectly, duck L'orange had perfect crisp skin, lamb carpaccio had nice flavors-it's spicy which it did not indicate on menu, grilled oysters wasn't as meaty as I expected for being grilled but freshness and flavor was there. 

Extended wine list with on hand sommelier. Refused the rose wine I first hand picked because it tasted like gas station shutter home wine lol BUT they were happy to replace it. 

Dessert surprised me, it was better then I expected and I'm usually not impressed by sweets.

Oh wow - What a find! We were planning to go next door to Sweet Chick and the wait was too long. So we tried Dirty French and were so happy we did!! 

Brunch was so tasty. We had the duck hash, pancake and lox bagel. You'd never believe, the star of the table were those soft scrambled eggs. So good. But the entire meal was so damn satisfying! And that cute little cover band, how nice! Go, you won't regret it.

Foods were excellent! 
We checked reviews before we go and saw positive comments about grilled Oyster. I'm not a big fan of Oyster but Loved it! 
I wish there were more wine selections.

If your idea of a great restaurant is a loud room full of tourists and people in town on business. With terrible music playing too loudly. And a dinner menu filled with "fancy" items that cost upwards of $40 a plate. Then this is the place for you.  It's not a good date place. It's not good if you want to talk. It's not good if you love good music. It's not good if you don't have money to burn. You get the idea. It's a great expense-account/group meal place. 
All of that said, the staff are lovely. The lighting is very good. The cocktails are fabulous.  (Maybe I'm just an old curmudgeon.) It's a beautiful room. And the hotel it's attached to is super cool. And to be fair, I'm sure the expensive food is very good. It has to be right ?

I heard good things about Dirty French but it is sadly over-rated. Table of 3 ordered lamb (too salty), bass (bland), pork (over cooked).  For these prices it's not wrong to expect more. It's busy, but I can't figure out why.

This is one of the best restaurants I've been to in the city. Actually, this is one of the best restaurants I've ever been to. Like, top 3. A "tell your friends about it" type of place. The ambiance is cozy, upscale, and makes you never want to leave. I love the neon "Dirty French" sign outside. Perfect stop for a photo. Anywho, on to the drinks and food. Amazing. Point blank, period. I've had the luxury of dining here twice, and have always started with the specialty cocktail with Mezcal (Laboulaye). It's refreshing, tangy, delicious, and poured with a heavier hand as it should be. The wine list is superb, as well. After that, I moved on to the Charcuterie Hors d'Oeuvre and Chèvre salad. Devoured. Then, for my main, I had the Brook trout. It was also very good. I will try for steak next time, though, because I know just how good it's going to be. Each time I've come in, I've had the same server. He is a delight. I wish I could remember his name. I will definitely be back next time I'm in the city.

I took my mom here for a belated Mother's Day brunch. We went around 12:00 pm - it's better to arrive on a Saturday at 1:00 pm because that's when the live music begins, and it sets a nice mood! The music was lounge-y and great for the sunny summer vibe. 

The only thing I wasn't quite impressed with was the level of service - at first. The manager seated us and took our drink order and I eventually had to flag down a server to update us on where the heck our drinks were and let us order food. He was fantastic. Maybe if the manager could get it together - would have been perfect. 

I ate the pancake, which looks small - but is extremely rich and satisfying. My mom had the egg sandwich, which she said was the best she's ever had - high praise from her. The wines were yummy, and they give you a complementary plate of delicious French pastries at the beginning of the meal. 

I'd go back. Lovely scenery. Good food.

Not my favorite brunch place by any stretch of the means. My main gripe with this place was the terrible service. We never had a waiter come over and ask for our order. We had to get the hostess to grab a waiter for us. They came about 10 minutes later. We ordered coffee and the coffee never came either.
The coffee came when our food came out, so we were stuck waiting for 30 minutes in the morning without coffee! Not how you want to start a morning. The food was mediocre at best for the cost of it. The best part was they forgot part
Of our order as well. I ordered the oatmeal as well as an omelette. The omelette was good except that it was super greasy. The oatmeal was alright as well, the fruit on top of it was not fresh at all. I can not recommend this place, but the best thing about nyc is there are lots of places to try.

Hopefully this was just a bad day for the restaurant.

Got it delivered as room service, so greasy and it smelled funky !!!  What was that smell ?
Really bad, so disappointing cause the hotel is awesome !!!
Stay at the Ludlow just don't order room service.

What a beautiful place!
Aesthetically phenomenal, but not hard on the wallet. The waitstaff was attentive and polite. The food was phenomenal and full of flavor (my friends with me all agree). My only thing is the usual, ambiance. With a space like this it would have been nice to hear jazz, classical, French music, something mellow; they were playing mostly modern music. I loved the addition of the band (even though they also played modern music).

Would go again and bring friends!

I went there for the Fourth of July and stumbled on a breathtaking view of the fireworks across the Manhattan skyscrape . Had tea in king tuts tea garden and the service was 5/5.

My friends and I had a lot to say about the various food combinations and let me just start by giving a shout out to the chefs boldness , creativity and vision. That said, I would be a mess if I did not point out that there seem to be a consistent problem with the ratios of almost every single dish except for the dessert which was on point in every way - tried all them and loved al the creative pairings
I had an amazing anniversary dinner here. Thanks to the attentive staff who made us feel like VIPs!

Amazing! Came here for dinner on a Saturday evening, and the food was incredible. Their flatbread is amazing, and then we shared the millefeuille (which is a must), the lamb carpaccio, the goat cheese/kale salad (also a must), and the tuna tartar (which wasn't my favorite). So flavorful and delicious, all the main dishes we had were amazingly cooked and the flavors and sauces were out of this world. We had the steak frites, the chicken for two, the duck and the trout, and I would get all of them again. Didn't have room for dessert, but I would definitely come back here again.
This is a must go to. Everything was excellent, staff was super attentive,food was phenomenal. We had the trout and oysters.

Another great restaurant. The duck in red cherry sauce (Duck aux cerises) was one of the best. The duck was cooked right and the sauce went really well.

Another is the flat bread which they serve before the food arrive. And the bread was sooo good. Cannot have enough of it. 

Another thing the we love was the "corn" side dish. So buttery and well season. 

Millefeuille is also a must.

Great ambience, and service.

food is always delicious, subtly changing menu so you can try something new, I travel to NY several times a year and always come to Dirty French for dinner...this time had the beets, baked oysters, and trout which I love, and had the opera cake for desert....our server was Pam and she was amazing as usual, very passionate about the food and just a really fun and caring server.
Love Dirty French.

Was able to make a last minute rez last night albeit on the earlier side (pre 8 p.m.) The restaurant is not inexpensive but worth every penny.  The decor was inviting and cozy and we even had a choice of tables! 

I will get to the food in a minute but the service and attentiveness by our server and ALL the Managers that were there made the evening. It felt like home. 

We started with the fried oysters in garlic butter & parsley. One of our oyster shell lost its oyster! It happens. I asked for 1 more oyster and Jeff (Manager) brought us another whole order! Nice touch. The Little Gem salad was so good I tried to get the recipe. One of the other Managers did his best to get me the ingredients so.now I can at least try to duplicate. We finished up with Steak Frites which was in a very tasty sauce and cooked to perfection.  The lemon meringuey dessert was to die for but it was a bit small so do not share it! All in all a great meal.

Cohosted a bridal shower in the party room upstairs a few weeks ago. I absolutely adore the atmosphere, it's simple and not over done. The staff including the bartenders were super super helpful. They made drinks, they help to set up, they even helped us make some of the party favors when we were running low on time. Everyone was very professional. Food here was also really good I just wish I had more time to eat and enjoy instead of running around. Also the party room was pretty roomy. Fit a long table enough for 20 girls, and everyone had room to comfortably walk around and mingle. The large private bathroom is also major plus+++.

My friends and I had an incredible experience with exceptional service. Was a wonderful 30th birthday for my friend Lindsey! The restaurant ambience was magnetic and the carpaccio and duck were phenomenal!

I've eaten here 4 or 5 times for dinner over theses and it's always been exceptionally good. Today I learned they serve breakfast too! Great food, coffee and service. Eggs Benedict with prosciutto was a great way to start the day!

I made the reservations online on the website. I was able to make the reservation for the time I wanted and it was very simple. When I got there, I told them my reservation time. I did not have to wait for the seat. They brought me to the seat and I was very happy with my seat. It was spacious and the food was delicious. The waitstaff was also friendly. I would come back again on a different time to try other things and I would recommend this place for dinner.

Went on a Friday night, 9:00 reservation. Loved the atmosphere, but the food was average and nondescript. Glad to say I've been once since it was on my bucket list for a long time, but perhaps expectations were too high. Nothing special at all when it came to our dinners. 

However, the lobby bar at the Ludlow was great and I'd definitely go back. Interesting cocktail menu, appealing and comfy decor, big fireplace to settle next to on a cool early autumn evening. We had drinks there before dinner at DF. In retrospect, I wish we'd stayed by the fireplace and had more drinks and appetizers (though the Ludlow food is from the Dirty French kitchen, so the chances of it also being plain would've been high, I guess). On to exploring other new (to me) digs in the city!

Came here with my boyfriend for our anniversary dinner, probably had a 4.5 star experience. Loved the ambiance, lots of chandeliers and flowers. The back wall was lined with white skulls/sculptures of sorts. While it was a more upscale restaurant, it was also more casual than I would have imagined. 

Wasn't a huge fan of the cocktail menu, I don't like dark liquor and there were only two drinks with clear liquor. I asked our waitress if it would be possible to substitute the alcohol in one of the drinks and she came back and said the bartender wouldn't be able to do that without any explanation, which seemed strange to me. No "it wouldn't taste good with the substitution". The complimentary house bread was phenomenal. Kind of tasted like a scallion pancake/buttery naan. We were huge fans. For appetizer we started with the tuna tartare, it has lots of fresh herbs like mint and maybe lemongrass, served in a crepe which also kind of tasted like a scallion pancake. The crepe itself was crispy and flavorful, but a little on the oily side. The tuna was fresh and the sauce was great. My boyfriend had the steak frites which I loved. Steak was juicy and tender, fries were thick and delicious and the peppercorn sauce had a great kick. We thought it was a little weird that there wasn't a great sear on either side of the steak. I had the duck which was a super generous serving (probably the biggest I've had). The skin was crispy with a nice layer of fat underneath, and the actual meat cooked to perfection. I did find the sauce a little too sweet but my boyfriend was obsessed with the duck and said it was the best he's ever had. The little chive plants on top helped cut the fat/sweetness a little. 

I thought it was really interesting that a lot of the dishes seemed to have an Asian flair to it. Overall it was quite a delicious meal. However, while the restaurant seemed very over staffed (tons of servers, hosts, etc) our service was not super fast. With the price of the duck, I would have liked to see some side with it rather than a al carte as well. But we still had a great night and if you're looking to eat somewhere a little on the fancier side, dirty French isn't a bad choice.

Decided to check this place out for brunch after hearing many good things. I was pleasantly surprised that we were able to get a last minute reservation on Opentable on a beautiful Sunday. 

Here goes: 

Service was a 10/10. Hostess and waitress was friendly from the get go. Everyone also gets a free pastry platter to share and I really enjoyed it. It tasted like heaven, especially if it's the first thing you're eating after an evening out.

Food: check my attached photos. If I had to rate it overall, it'd be a 7.5/10. My avocado toast and croissant was just aiight. Pancake was good!

Ambience: nice looking place with spacious seating, attached to a hotel with more seating in the back. Just so happened that there was a live band playing when we were there. It was so loud, I nearly ripped my ears out. We had nowhere to move, and I was too hungry to leave. I like that they have the windows open to the street when the weather is warmer. Gives a nice Sunday breeze vibe to it. I'm all about the vibez.
 
Verdict: Pretty solid brunch spot good for last minute reservations. Just call ahead to see if there's live music or else your hangover headache might begin at brunch.

The food is great. However, that was the only positive part of the experience.

We were a party of four with a reservation. Two of us arrived about 5-10 minutes before the other two who were stuck in traffic but very close. I explained this to the hostess when we arrived and asked if my girlfriend and I could be seated and have drinks at the table while we waited. She said no and also that if the other couple didn't arrive within 10 minutes they would give away our table. Keep in mind, we were actually a few minutes early at this point.

Once we did get to the table, the waiter was rude almost to the point of being hostile from the moment he spoke to us. He was rude in particular to the two women in our party when they asked some questions about the items on the menu. Additionally it was impossible to get anyone to take our drink orders throughout the entire evening. 

While the food is good, I wouldn't recommend anyone pay the price to have dinner here because of how they treat their patrons.

Dirty French serves delicious French food and some of the best cocktails in a very trendy environment! 

The Etouffee for two is definitely recommended- the fish is cooked perfectly and the sauce is so flavorful. The duck is also executed very well. It was my friend's birthday and they sent over honey apple ice cream with a candle which was very nice! As for the cocktails, they're some of the best I've had at a restaurant. The Laboulaye with bell pepper is so fantastic. 

The attached Lobby bar next door is very inviting and cozy and serves the same cocktails!

Highly recommend Dirty French for a chic date night or special occasion!

Wonderful French food with a twist!
The service is attentive without being intrusive.The Endive salad was light and very good the pate with apricot mustard was a bit heavy but a good winter treat a few cornichon would have been nice. The bread was amazing. The Spivey pork chops with Calvados were moist and spicy. The duck with plums was a classic preparation perfectly done with a nice hint of Moroccan spice; it was outstanding. It was very sweet that they treated us to champagne to celebrate our Anniversary.

I went here for a private event and it was really lovely. The private room was Spacious, the bartenders were really nice, and the cocktails were great. We had appetizers and a great view of the Halloween activities out front. The tuna tartare was very good.The staff at the front door were really helpful in showing us the way to the private event. The space was really well lit And I really enjoyed the ambience. It did have a very Instagram ready vibe.
