We had an awesome brunch experience at Dirty French! We got seated in their patio area and it was so beautiful with a lot of light and it was very comfortable because it was covered. 

They also have live jazz music on Sundays so it had a great vibe. 

I got the duck hash for brunch... highly recommend it! It was tasty and eggs were perfectly cooked. 

We also shared the Pims drink which is not only refreshing but also pretty! 

I would definitely go back to Dirty French for brunch.

Easily one of the best hotel bars I've been to! Pretty unique, a little quiet but that's where the charm is. Great for having quality time with friends and loved ones. I think the bigger the parties, the more fun there is!

Really loved our evening here. We came with a private event, so were seated in a room upstairs away from the restaurant. Our host Alex? was personable and pleasant. The vegetarian dishes included a delicious flatbread with chèvre, kale salad, entrée of a delicate, almost crepe like sliced mushroom with a Thai curry coconut sauce and crisped butternut squash with just the right amount of spice. Dessert was a peanut butter chocolate slice topped with ice cream. Sides were pommes purées, haricots and mushrooms. 

For the wine, a 2012 red from Burgundy and a really delicate white I can't remember. Overall, a memorable and lovely evening. Even as we left our dimly lit oasis and ventured past the discreet door, back into the restaurant, I wanted to stay while. It's cozy, sleek, and more than inviting. I'll definitely return to try to restaurant and I hope that mushroom entrée is on the menu.

-great vibe and ambiance 
-well designed and up to date 
-service is on point; very attentive 
-phenomenal and extensive wine list
-great for a date night
-one of the more luxurious restaurants in the Lower East Side 
-their menu truly reflects French cuisine options 
-my favorite was the tuna tartare in a crepe: on the spicier side and the flat bread they gave with herbed butter and small meze 
-ordered the raclette cheeseburger: the burger meat itself was very good. I was hoping they would carve the raclette cheese onto the burger and/or the burger would be dripping in the delicious raclette cheese since it's rare to find that on menus.

This little hidden gem in the Lower East Side is a MUST! Wonderful atmosphere while keeping classic French cuisines but yet served in a modern eloquent rustic environment. Popped in with a reservation, glad I had one too as the restaurant quickly filled up, the service was exceptional and fast with the servers making sure my needs were met. Started the night with a Lilikoi and a Zaragoza from their drink menu, which I highly recommend, followed by a Shrimp cocktail before I was presented the main entree a 'Meunière' which was a trout seasoned in sesame and brown butter that practically melted away in my mouth with every bite.

We had an excellent time here. We had a great round table seat, superb wine, an amazing service. They were so good with my celiac, making sure to tell me things that were safe. The carpaccio was amazing and so were the potatoes! Next time I'm in New York, I'd love to take more people here!
The service was awful. Past awful, the wait for the  food was staggering! Plates weren't cleared, etc etc. Do not recommend!

My wife and I are big fans of the Major Food Group restaurants and Dirty French lives up to the high bar set by its brethren.  Let's start with the service and hospitality which were fantastic.  Everyone at the host station was extremely welcoming and our server, Pamela, was an absolute delight. She had great enthusiasm and a wonderful knowledge of all the dishes and a great sense of humor to boot. She was also great with regard to my peanut/tree allergies and all the assistants who assisted her were extremely attentive. 

Now, on to the food.  The warm flat bread with herbed cheese was a wonderful start to our meal. We tried the sausage dish as an appetizer which was perfectly balanced between sweet and sour and the mustard that accompanied it was perfect. 
For mains we had the scallops and crawfish in a saffron broth which was buttery and savory. The scallops were cooked perfectly and the sauce was divine. The steak with pomme frites had a savory green peppercorn sauce which was extremely well seasoned and the steak was cooked perfectly. The pomme frittes were an excellent compliment to the steak. We also had a side of the mushrooms which were extremely flavorful and quite unique. 

Finally for desert we had the beignets with a caramel chicory sauce with vanilla ice cream which was absolutely sensational. The ice cream was rich and creamy and was a perfect pairing to the fried doughy goodness and the caramel and chicory. 

Truly a great meal in a very lovely setting. This was our first time here but certainly not our last. Merci.

We had been wanting to try this place for a while and finally made it over last weekend to celebrate our anniversary. I'm Happy to say it was a very solid choice. We were greeted by the very fabulous Royce who gave us a lovely table and made some very good recommendations. We had the lamb carpaccio, the grilled oysters and the duck. All were excellent choices. The bread they give you is also delicious. We had the lemon tart for dessert which was also good and would have been great if it hadn't been still frozen. Royce came over again during our meal with a celebratory shot, and our server brought us some passion fruit sorbet with a candle in it for us. The restaurant was lovely and all in all a wonderful way to celebrate our anniversary. We'll definitely be back!

Great vibrant vibe for Saturday dinner. Celebrative but not too loud. Kind of a third-date intimate. Friend and I came for a light dinner after having some cocktails.

Good length of wine list and sommelier to assist in tasting before ordering. Who recommended a nice pino noir - pointy light red.

Ordered MilleFeuille and Grilled Oysters. Grilled Oysters and baquette went very well with our wine. On the other hand Millefeuille was amazing on its own. Perfect crusted outer layer and soft then softer inner. Dish was especially jaw dropping with the sweet corn and yellow curry. 

The bread and herb spread served with the dishes was absolutely addicting! An impressive differentiator.

Cannot say enough about the amazing Dirty French! 

My family and I dined here for Thanksgiving 2019 and I must say the food and service were out of this world.

Very friendly waitstaff from the host at check-in to the table service.

The prefix menu was great and had some traditional dishes with a twist; I was really blown away by the vegetarian options and my family said that the turkey was perfectly cooked.

One thing that really stands out in my mind is when my husband asked for additional potatoes and gravy, the server went above and beyond to say "whatever we wanted extra was his pleasure to bring to the table!" What an amazing guest experience.

I am definitely looking forward to trying the regular menus at Dirty French; if it is anything like the Thanksgiving menu, I am ready to be blown away.

Thanks for a great holiday meal Dirty French team! My husband and I cannot wait to come back.

Late lunch for the holidays courtesy of my boss. Nice ambience, especially for drinks with friends.  The food was good, but nothing to rave about.  I had the Roquefort with shrimp, it was grilled on one side but burnt more than anything.  I was way too hungry to send it back.  We all shared a side of haricots asiatique looked and tasted burnt as well.  Half of it ended up on the table because the tongs were super stiff and useless.
The waiter could have used a paper and pen cause he didn't remember our full order and messed up on one of our entree.  He even repeated the order back to us...
Nothing really special from this experience... NEXT!

I've been looking forward to sampling the menu at Dirty French and was not disappointed yesterday. 

I started with the flat bread accompanied by fromage blanc. The flavors of the two together were fabulous and hard to resist. Luckily I saved part for later. 

Next up, signature salad. Sadly for me it included finely sliced onion which makes it less enjoyable as I do not enjoy raw onion. Small matter as I ate around them. Delicious dressing nonetheless and the radish variety in the salad kept it interesting!

I ordered the steak au poivre medium well with a little trepidation. It's hard to get this right but the steak arrived perfectly cooked and seasoned. The peppercorn sauce was a delicious companion to the very tender steak with plenty left to take home. Pommes frites were included, crispy and seasoned nicely. I also has the haircots which were charred with a smokey flavor that had me saying WOW with the first bite. 

I didn't have time for dessert but plan to return soon with others in tow. I shared limited portions of my leftovers with my family who was unable to attend to rave reviews for unheated food. I can't wait to return!!
Very good food with excellent quality ingredients. The bread is a great harbinger of what comes next. We had the duck and the lamb and both were excellent. The ambiance is ok, could get a revamp

They took a perfect dish, the tuna tartare crepe and completely ruined it by creating a south east Asian greasy fried, overly spiced mess. So sad. It was a great dish, so unique, so clean and delicious.

Service is great, croque monsieur very good.

We loved this place! A friend recommended it and we owe them big time. The atmosphere was hip and fun, also very dark. The cocktails were superb and the food is incredible. Everything we ordered was delicious, but the standouts were the Millefeuille appetizer and the Boulangere main. Probably the best lamb I've eaten in my entire life!
The staff was super friendly and helpful with any questions we had. I can't wait to go back and try more awesomeness!

I've been here twice now and the service and food never fail to impress. We started with an order of the Pate with pan Louis and apricot mustard and it was delicious. We also had the garlic pork sausage and onions and potatoes, which was another five choice. The sausage was tender, juicy and full of flavor. Our entrees were the duck mirabelle and the lamb loin. The duck was juicy and the skin was so crispy. The lamb almost melted in your mouth. Dessert was the beignets with a chicory sauce which were so light and airy they were gone ad soon as the service plate was on n the table. Service is also excellent. I would highly recommend it and I will definitely be back again.
Amazing service AMAZING FOOD atmosphere comfortable and Sleek. Absolutely in love with this place. My palate is just happy as ever

- personable staff; the bartender is an absolute delight 
- recommend: spicy pork chops (had an unexpected southern/bbq flavor which was a pleasant surprise) 
- side of mushrooms was inedibly salty (unless mixed with the bland potato puree)
- duck and scallop entrees were both over salted 
- pork sausage appetizer was good but something on the plate had a strong vinegar element to it which I found off-putting but my companion enjoyed

Okay, you have to get the duck. I don't care if a little fat scares you, the duck was to die for and we are extra thankful Alex recommended It. The ambiance is fantastic but Alex, our waiter, made the experience! Super charismatic and attentive to our table and every other one he served (which is rare in New York). 10/10 would come back!

Dirty French is amongst my favorite restaurants in the LES. The food is consistently delish and the staff exceptionally hospitable and professional and do a lovely job waving the MFG banner. The grand plateau is always fantastic and the seafood is exceptionally fresh. In regards to all things booze related both the cocktail program and the wine list provide an ideal pairing to the delightful offerings coming from the kitchen. The Somme is extremely knowledgeable and passionate and does a great job with finding ideal pairings. Personal favorites: Tuna Tartare, Brook Trout, and Chicken and crepes. The Tatin is easily my favorite desert in the neighborhood. Highly recommended!

We went there after the exhibition opening at Richard Taittinger Gallery that's a few minutes walk. We had a superb dinner at the bar!   Glad to try our luck as we couldn't book a table.  Fun ambiance and a lot of energy.

This is the first time I've ever felt racially profiled in New York City. I would love to be able to review at least the coffee at this place, but unfortunately the staff actively neglected my presence after 30 minutes of sitting and trying to flag down some service. Even a direct wave and "excuse me" didn't get their attention.

I came here around 5pm on a Sunday with my husband. The place was not busy at all with empty tables everywhere. We decided to sit in the Greenhouse area outdoor in the back. He sat in his own area because I needed a table to do some work. Around us, people were served wine, looking at menus, having coffee, and enjoying their space. There were 4 servers working and none of them greeted us, acknowledged us, or even gave either of us a menu. I observed all of them cleaning tables and making sure everyone else was taken care of, all the while wondering why I could t get any service. Then I realized why -- everyone was white except for us. Want to know how I came to that conclusion? We were sitting at different tables and neither of us were waited on. Then a group of non-POCs came in to sit... guess how immediate they received service from TWO different servers?!?

I complained to the management and his excuse was that he was new. So what's everyone else's excuse? He offered me a free cup of coffee, but you know what... a free latte does not excuse your blatant racism.

I don't recommend this place to any person of color. This is appalling and unacceptable. Shame on you Dirty French!

Took 1 1/2 hours to get diinner. Very busy and service  was poor. Perhaps a bad
nite. But won't return.

Simply amazing brunch, great drinks and fantastic service. It is pretty hard to go wrong because everything on the menu that we ordered was amazing and we wanted to order more! The French toast stood out as some of the best French toast I have ever had. The Pate was also amazing, I will be back soon!

This is a painful review for me to write as I've had great experiences and meals at Dirty French, but this morning's breakfast was truly dreadful on multiple levels. The 2 servers were completely uninterested and disengaged (couldn't even bother to say "good morning" or "sit wherever you'd like") and I've rarely felt so unwelcome at a paid establishment. Furthermore, I ordered the tartine with a poached egg, a dish i've had before with great success, yet today the avocados weren't ripe giving them an inedible hard texture. When I mentioned this politely to the female server she reacted defensively and skeptically saying "this is a very popular dish and it's the first time anyone has complained about hard avocados". No offer to get me something else and no offer to remove a 1/4-eaten dish from the bill. After this she quickly brought me the bill -- not even asking if i wanted a second cold brew or anything else -- but proceeded to disappear for 15 minutes making me late for a work call. I had to wave down the host to grab my $27 check! Given its location I will likely be back, but only at night when the service and scene are dramatically better than what I experienced this morning. By the way, if Management is reading this feel free to contact me for more details as this review is actually better than what I went through.
I love the creativity of the food here! This from the carbone team and as usual food is great, only problem is service can be really slow, but it's that type of place , worth trying for sure

Came here as a party of two on a Saturday for brunch. I'd never been interested in visiting this place, as it looked like a mere hotel restaurant, lacking character, but my friend suggested it so I humored her. 
It was nearly summer, and I wanted to eat healthy, so I decided to have the eggs, and opted to have them poached. My friend got the duck hash.
The eggs were served with a piece of toasted sourdough, and were simply poached. There was nothing to recommend about this dish. 
My friend said her duck hash was good. They also brought out a tray of complimentary sweet pastries. I didn't try any, but my friend tried one and said that they were overly sweet. 
Ambience and service were nice. I think the food on the menu here is better for people if they aren't vegan/vegetarian, or concerned with healthy eating. There are very little options in the way of either of these.
I came to Dirty French on a Saturday night. The place was packed, the atmosphere was loud and fun. The food was EXCELLENT. The drinks were even better. I HIGHLY recommend coming to this place.

Came here for a late dinner date on a Friday night. It was an enjoyable experience.

The bread with soft cheese was salty, delicious and tastied of herbs.

The grilled oysters taste nice and meaty. They are really swimming in the sauce. 

The duck is a swirling storm of savory meat, perfectly crispy skin, fruity sauce and North African spices.

The beignets were warm, crispy and fluffy. The powdered sugar and caramel sauce brought plenty of sweetness to this dessert. 

The service was friendly, and very thorough without being intrusive. The decor is posh but in an artistic manner.

I confess to being disappointed by "Dirty French"; the decor is close to that of a French brasserie though the recipes are meant to "provoke" traditional French cuisine - hence the name "Dirty". Yet, IME, the challenge falls flat and reflects a jejune approach to food.

I'm not even sure where to begin. I was super excited to eat here and ended up being thoroughly disappointed. 

I don't think I really understood this place at all. The ambience and food do not match. The look of the inside is awesome. Definitely a cool vibe and the staff here are nice and attentive, so definitely can't say anything bad about that EXCEPT, at the end, our bill had a service fee??? I've never seen that before. It was weird and definitely not stated to us anywhere. Also, the tables were very small and hard to put everything on and the chairs were not comfortable. There were 3 of us and no way, 4 people could fit. I also want to state that our waiter tried to tell us that it would take a long time for our food to be prepared and we should ordered more appetizers. Not sure what that was all about. The food didn't take that long. 

Anyway, on to the food. We ordered the grilled oysters to start. Those were big and great, definitely tasty. You also get complimentary bread and some kind of creamy spread to go with it. It was good. For the mains, we ordered the steak and frittes, and the burger with a salad. The steak was ok, but basically doused in too much mustard sauce. The fries were pretty good. The salad was less than to be desired. No option of dressing. The burger? AWFUL. It literally tasted like a gamier version of a McDonalds burger, I literally couldn't believe it how awful it was. 

On top of this experience, the prices were legit outrageous for no reason? I understand it's New York City and you're going to pay but the quality of the food wasn't worth it. The experience was not worth it at all. 

Please save your time and money and go elsewhere to a real French restaurant.

Boy are they back! We had an AWESOME meal on Friday night. The cocktails were really fun! (we tried several!) Dinner was quite special. We tried the calamari, Mussels, Pork.... All excellent - but the dessert was amazing - Benets.. amazing...And of course .. the bread is back too.

Party of six last night, celebrating a birthday. Two of our number were hotel guests, so we drank a couple bottles of champagne on the roof before heading down to the restaurant. 

The menu is two pages long; scan a QR code for the full wine list. I was torn between starting with the calamari or the tuna tartare, ultimately selecting the latter when another guest expressed interest. Good food deserves to be shared. 

I ordered a pilsner and was thrilled to be notified that I'd be receiving Threes's Vliet, a crisp, wheaty favorite. We sipped drinks, swapped small plates (deviled egg gets a thumbs up), and gossiped mercilessly. 

Finally the mains arrived. I had ordered the New York strip (served au poivre), medium-rare, with pommes frites (french fries, if you didn't know). They took the liberty of pre-slicing my meat, which felt like a minor transgression. The steak was delicious, cooked perfectly, and the green peppercorn sauce paired wonderfully with the meat. For the most expensive thing on the menu, it was very good. 

Overall, a pleasant (and indulgent) dinner experience. If you want to eat somewhere fancy, but not too fancy, this is a perfect spot, in the always-popping Lower East Side.

Dirty French was a lot of fun. 
The oysters and house made flatbread are on my mind still. I'm thinking about it every hour at this point. Skipped out on the Chicken and Crepes special so I think that means I'll need to go back at some point. 
Drinks were dope. 
Service was excellent. 
Again, Oysters for the win. Grilled or the East Coast ones with the mind melting briny stuff.
Fun times for sure.

I've been wanting to try dirty French for a while now, what an amazing experience! Super friendly staff and the food was absolutely delicious!  Definitely have to get the grilled oysters, they were so big and juicy with butter, parsley & garlic, was the best thing I've ever eaten!  Also had the mussels entree and hanger steak with frites, for dessert get the beignets!  My boyfriend and I had to be wheeled out of there, the portions were a lot, also we love the dirty peach cocktail! We had about 5 of those, and the rooster design was perfect every time!
Went for a drink and had the best bartender Matthew- ambiance is super vibey & trendy, def recommend!

Vibes: 5/5- it was a really cool place, the windows were all open so it felt very open

Service: 5/5 our waitress was informative, kind and attentive to us throughout without being at the table too much 

Food: 
-From bar snacks- scallop cru- 5/5 it was very good, a little spicy which I liked and a great way to start the meal. They sliced a scallop thinly and then made it into a single bite size ceviche 

-appetizers: oysters bourguignon- if you like the taste of oysters this is NOT for you. They used way to much butter and parsley which entirely masked the flavor of the oysters. I would pass on this 

-entree: trout meunière- cooked to perfection, it was flavorful, yet light at the same time. Would recommend for a nice dish that is a little more light (since a lot of their food is heavy) 

-side dishes: POMMES LOUIS- yes yes yes!!! This was amazing and so good- if you don't like garlic then you won't like the food- but WOW! It was cooked in duck fat and perfectly crispy yet fluffy- would totally get again 


A fun place to eat at and would recommend if you are in NYC for a nice dinner

I was so impressed with our dinner at Dirty French! We ordered so much food and my picky fiancé (who can only generally tolerate canned tuna as seafood) even enjoyed the fish I ordered. He ordered a strip steak and it was so tasty - everything here that we tried was a hit and I don't think you can go wrong with anything off of their menu. Even the drinks were on point - dangerous though since you can't taste the booze i

Now this is a place, I want to come back to for more than just drinks. I came here to kill time for sweet chick , but the energy , the drinks , definitely were on point . They have a bar , lounge and lots of places within the space .

Had an amazing experience at Dirty French when visiting NYC with my partner. We had reservations for Saturday night that we were able to get the morning of. All of the staff was very friendly and informative. Our server gave great recommendations and really knew her stuff. They also had a sommelier on staff that was also super informative of wine options. 

For food we started with the bone marrow and shrimp bouquet. Both were super delicious and had lots of flavor. First time trying bone marrow and I've been wanting to try it so it didn't disappoint. For our main dishes we got the duck and the steak. The duck was the special of the night and recommended by our server. If was delicious, cooked perfectly and had the perfect crunch on the outside. The orange sauce was also super rich and flavorful. My patented got the steak which was also cooked perfectly. The sauce over it was also so good and the cracked pepper topping really added a little twist to it that we enjoyed. 

For dessert we had crème brûlée. Bomb! You can never go wrong with that for dessert. 

Overall service and ambiance was 10/10. I'd totally return next time I'm in NYC.

We were staying at the Ludlow Hotel all week and already had reservations for our week in the city, but were enticed by the menu and decor and decided to take a risk on our last night - best culinary decision of this visit to New York. Pam was an absolutely incredible server and the evening's cocktails and courses were phenomenal. Don't miss out on the deviled eggs and the mushroom millefeuille - if it is available, the duck à l'orange is cooked to perfection (if that isn't your cup of tea, the burger is equally wonderful). Make time in your schedule for this experience - amazing staff, fantastic food and an absolutely lovely evening. (And good God those deviled eggs.)

Wow. This place was amazing. We live in the NYC suburbs and decided a few days ago to do a one night getaway in the city. Between having a young kid, not working in Manhattan anymore, and now the pandemic, my knowledge of the NYC dining scene is basically gone. 
Between Reddit, Yelp, and the Resy app, I managed to find Dirty French. Reviews looked good and they had a table and who can go wrong with French food? 
They have ample outdoor seating (we're not eating indoors anymore) although I did get a good look at the interior when I went to the bathroom and it is very inviting. 
For cocktails I had the Dirty Peach, hubby had the Belmondo (he actually had two). They were both very good. For appetizers I had the mushroom millefeuille. Oh. My. Goodness. This dish was so good. Think of a traditional millefeuille made of pastry, but make it out of mushrooms instead and place it on a delicious delicata squash curry sauce. It was good and although the portion looks modest, it was very filling. Hubby had the tuna tartare and said it was excellent. 
While we were waiting for our apps, they brought out a complimentary flatbread with a creamy French cheese that was fantastic. It was like if a pita and puff pastry had a baby. So good. 
For my entree I had the trout meunière with frites. The fish was cooked perfectly and the sauce was very good. I was a little wary of the frites before they arrived because the pics on Yelp didn't look that good but they were excellent. Yes, I judge restaurants by their French fries. 
Hubby had the hangar steak and had the haricots asiatique as a side. The beans were amazing. They had this amazing umami flavor which we found out from our server is from a type of black garlic sauce used in Asian cuisine. The husband liked it so much that I am going to try and recreate it at home. 
We ordered creme brûlée for me and beignets and ice cream for him. After a while we noticed that it was taking a while. All of a sudden a manager came over and told us that dessert was being comped because it was taking too long to come out. Apparently the beignet dough didn't proof right and so they had to get another batch of dough. As an avid baker I am sensitive to that plight so I understood but it was nice that they noticed and comped the dessert. 
Throughout our two hour meal the service was fantastic. From the host (guy with better eye makeup than I've ever done in my life), to our server (young Hispanic woman with long pink hair), and the young man who refilled our waters and ran the plates (young Colombian kid who told us we had the same music taste as his dad). Speaking of the music, an excellent 80s playlist that made this middle aged mom feel so good. 
We don't get down to the city as often as I'd like anymore and there are so many restaurants that finding a good place on such short notice felt like looking for a needle in a haystack. I made an excellent choice.

We were staying at the Ludlow Hotel for the weekend and decided to give Dirty French a try. I've heard good things and the reviews were promising. The ambience is great, it's certainly a beautiful restaurant to sit in. The service was friendly, though slow (which I excuse in COVID times). The menu is basic French bistro with some fun takes on things. It's the execution which was off. We got two of the deviled eggs which may have been the better part of the meal. We also got the mushroom millefeuille which was very fun but too salty. My partner got the burger which tasted good but was overcooked. The fries that came with it though were awesome and perfectly executed. It was my entree which was a thorough disappointment. I ordered the mussels étouffée. I have lived in New Orleans and was excited to have this dish done with mussels! It came out in a broth not a stew thickened with roux which is its signature preparation. The mussels were still in the shell, the étouffée I've had the crawfish is always out of the shell. There was absolutely no hint of creole seasoning and strongly tasted of fennel/anise (which I adore but not really part of étouffée). It came with "crispy rice" which were four balls of rice they barely crisped in awful tasting oil which they served in the mussel broth underneath a cloche so by the time it got to me they were not crispy. Halfway through our meal a server brought us bread for the broth. The broth was far too salty to soak up anything with. I think the part of this that bothers me with this is when people who are not part of the culture try and reinvent a dish and do it poorly and charge an enormous amount of money for it. My suggestion: go to NOLA, eat as much étouffée as you can, learn how to make it, shell the mussels and serve over proper steamed rice and maybe sprinkle crisped rice (in butter maybe) over it. Otherwise omit the rice entirely and serve it with frites and call it moules frites which is essentially what it was. I left hungry and frustrated.

A truly disappointing experience! I brought my wife here for her birthday on a recommendation. It's a very hip space, lively. We were immediately seated, and the waiter was promptly at our table to answer our questions and take our drink order. The bottle of wine came and all was great. And it was all down hill from there because we didn't see another member of the staff for the next hour. No one asked about our appetizer. We finished the bottle before anyone thought to check in. Eventually the manager rushed by to say the food was on the way. After our food finally came....nothing. No one asked how our entrees were, no one asked if we wanted another glass of wine. Did we want desert? Who knows, because no one asked! Even the neighboring table asked us what was going on because we were clearly being ignored! We didn't see another member of the staff until they presented us with the $200+ bill. And to be clear, I paid and tipped before I expressed my displeasure. I wasn't looking for any free bees. After I settled the tab, I talked to the manager...nothing. No attempt to make it right. Just a weak "Oh, well, sorry, just a little busy tonight." Really? In Man-fucking-hattan? A little busy? We were treated like an expendable nuisance.

Wasn't sure what to expect at Dirty French... thought it might be just another trendy restaurant with ok food. I must say that I was pleasantly surprised! This was one of the best French restaurants with top notch service that I've experienced in NYC. 

Unique menu, well-balanced flavors and nice portions. Started with the baked oysters, which reminded me of a take on escargot... the butter & herb sauce was perfect for dipping bread. Next, we enjoyed the lamb carpaccio, calamari and millefueille. The calamari was honestly a standout dish! The lamb carpaccio was one of the more special menu items... I've only ever had fish and beef carpaccios. Also, the carpaccio was served with eggplants which complemented the flavors so well. For entree, we split the strip steak, which was perfectly cooked and dressed in a delicious peppercorn sauce. 

Truly an outstanding meal and would highly recommend! Very welcoming staff and lovely, dark ambiance.

Although the restaurant was empty, the food did not suffer. We had perhaps the best carpaccio I've tasted. The lamb carpaccio was spicy and with middle eastern influence. We followed this with the mushroom Millefeuille which did not disappoint. Truly a remarkable dish. 

For main entree we split a steak with pomme frites. Perfectly cooked an s sliced for sharing!

This was as satisfying a dining experience as I have had in quite some time.  The BTG wine list was outstanding, with bottle-aged selections from outstanding producers (e.g., Chave, Trimbach). The menu was excellent and the food was outstanding.  Deft use of spices and fresh herbs.  But the service raised things to the next level--specifically our server Pamela, who made great recommendations and guided us to wonderful menu choices and the right wines to pair with them ... and turned a fine dinner into a fun and memorable evening.

Ordered 2 burgers and deviled eggs. Burgers were ok, they were cooked medium rare which we asked for. The fries were almost better than the burgers. And that's saying a lot for me bc I almost never eat the fries. They were perfectly crisp! I just didn't know the burgers came with a mountain of pickles on them, which I would have asked for without if I knew. And the deviled eggs had an odd after taste. Maybe it was the capers? But something about them, I just didn't like. I'm sure if we would have dined in, instead of room service, we would have enjoyed it better. We wanted the bone marrow and shrimp beignets, which weren't offered on the room service menu. Either way, happy to not have to leave our room.
Excellent meal with top notch service from the entire staff!!!! 10/10 would come again ASAP

Dirty French is one of the top places I most frequently recommend my friends, and my recent visit solidified that spot again. It was my first time since their reopening post initial pandemic shutdown. 

I'd gone enough times in the past to sample most of the menu, or at least most of the appetizers and the more enticing-looking mains. While everything has always been tasty, my one true love at Dirty French is none other than their duck a l'orange. During previous visits, they had different fruit-based sauces (I remember a cherry and maybe an apricot?) but it seems they've settled back on the classic orange. It's no longer on the printed dinner menu, but as the manager Jeffrey helpfully mentioned in my Q&A above, you can reserve the duck ahead of time in your reservation notes. Given that information, my husband and I reserved TWO (because even though we usually go the divide and conquer route at literally any other restaurant, Dirty French is where I REFUSE to share my main with him).

I just can't mimic the perfectly crunchy-crispy skin nor the tender meat at home--juicy yet not at all fatty, so perfectly medium-rare that you wonder if it's almost *too* rare because the texture is like a melt-in-your-mouth beef filet. The sauce is sweet and sticky, like an upscale McDonald's Sweet N' Sour sauce (if you know my love for McD, then you'd understand this is a LOFTY compliment). Seriously my favorite duck in NYC, and yes, this includes pre-vegan Eleven Madison.

Service continues to be friendly and efficient. Looking forward to my next visit!

Dirty French is always a treat. The team is always super nice, and have the best drink recommendations. I dream about the flatbread and creamy cheese dip that they bring out when you sit down - it's phenomenal. Other highlights are the oysters, flank steak frites (those duck fat fries!), as well as their signature burger. The steak is served au poivre & sliced and their peppercorn sauce is rich and delicious. The burger is also a delight - especially loved the touch of thinly sliced pickles and onions. Can't wait to go back and try their brunch!

We're staying at the Ludlow. I had the Eggs, the bread that came with it tasted a bit burned as though they used oil. The bacon though in the plate had a fun chicharrón taste to it. The eggs just tasted like how eggs should. Not my favorite spot in lower east but it just seems like that's what the breakfast options are near here if you aren't willing to wait forever at a spot.

Super cute restaurant. The staff were super friendly. I made reservations for my gf birthday about a month in advance. I had a pear margarita that was really good. The grilled oysters were amazing! For the main we had steak and fries and the snapper. The snapper was super salty. Overall I would definitely come back. I thought there was a dress code but there was not.

Solid meal at Dirty French. The flat bread and cheese is reason enough to come here... you will not be disappointed! The strip steak au poire was cooked to perfection, and I didn't want the Pomme purée to end! The tuna tartare with Asian Crepe was a unique flavor but delicious. Definitely will return

One of my fave restaurants in NYC. Warm and friendly service, everyone is so fun here! The food!!! Everything is good, especially the duck (which wasn't on the menu but was verbalized to us). Truly unforgettable.
Best time ever!! Food was so good. Service even better! Shout out to Royce, Jean-Pearre, and especially PAM! Had the best time! Give those angels all raises!

I was lucky enough to go to Dirty French with a few of my gfs, the service was amazing and so was the food. What can I say?! Everything was immaculate, from the lamb carpaccio to the duck and also the tuna tartare (one of the best tuna tartare's I've ever had!)... they have an extensive wine menu which is great, if you're at a French restaurant then get a French wine. Everything paired so well, can't wait to go back!

DID YOU GO OUT OF BUSINESS???
OR DID YOU JUST DO ME DIRTY, Dirty French????

YOU TOOK MY MONEY, but did NOT send the gift certificate I purchased and you don't respond to emails. 
And your phones lines are dead. 

So I'm leaving his review with hope someone finally responds. 

I purchased a HUGE $$$$ gift certificate from your website... but it did not send...  
There is NO WAY to reach a human. I have emailed multiple times and the phone numbers so not work.  -- they say to email. I've emailed soo sooo sooo many times.

If a customer can't buy a gift certificate then DISABLE IT FROM YOUR WEBSITE. Otherwize it's like stealing, right?
The credit card company says to contact you directly. Maybe you can contact me back?

"Guess who's back? Back again!" -- Eminem, "Without Me"

So I said that I'd be picking up the pace with these reviews, and I failed. But now post-omicron/delta, I am back for good. It may take some time to get a rhythm going again. Klay Thompson doesn't go on hot streaks with 3-5 minutes a time.

Dirty French is a questionably named -- yet ambiguously so -- French restaurant that's attached to a swanky hotel. The decor is a mishmash of influences: Nic Cage's "National Treasure" franchise (a random sphinx is placed near the ceiling), midnight bistro decor, and upscale bar. 

We had the mussels, chicken, pommes puree, and the tuna tartare, plus bargain-rate deviled eggs. All were amazing except the tartare, which was oppressively overspiced and clouds out the taste of the fish. I also highly recommend getting the desert. Go for the beignets. We ordered them and a more standard chocolate cake, and I anthropormorphized (sp) the cake and felt sorry for how poorly it stacked up against the exciting beignets.

We did the fixed menu for Valentine's and had a wonderful time.  The server was Pamela and she was fantastic.  The support staff were also attentive and personable.  I started with a Muddy Waters cocktail which was a nice twist on the Sazarac - very well done.  We started with the chèvre salad, grilled oysters and tartare - all very good, the tartare our least favorite but I enjoyed the heat from the spices, my husbands favorite was the sauce from the oysters and the chèvre salad.  He had the hangar steak au poivre which was cooked to absolute perfection - medium rare and I had the salmon which was good but not as good as the steak.  The pomme frites and haricots vert were a nice accompaniment.  I had the Chablis with dinner which was nice and crisp.  My husband had the Pilsner which he enjoyed.  The meal was finished with lemon and chocolate desserts.  Both were delicious.  This is now my new fav French restaurant in NYC!
I was worried because I have celiac and a dairy allergy, but it was amazing. Our waiter was knowledgeable and I ate a fantastic meal and dessert. The salmon was amazing!!

Amazing! The type of restaurant that's still worth for your money in NY! Too many places in town that have been leaving me disappointed post COVID but Dirty French continues to keep up. Maybe the best burger in town? With raclette cheese inside. The chicken and crepes was amazing as well but for me the star was the duck. One of the best ducks I had since I came back from France, perfectly cooked! The only thing could use some improvement are the cocktails, specially the martini but besides this everything was great !

Had a great dinner here with a friend. I tried:

+ Lilikoi cocktail 
+ Ludlow gimlet
+ Lamb carpaccio
+ Bone marrow aigre doux
+ mushroom millefuille
+ Little gem salad 
+ Oysters bourguignon 
+ Mussels etouffee
+ Pommes frites  
+ Lemon tart 
+ Chocolate gauteux

My favorite cocktail was the lilikoi one, though the gimlet was also great. Little gem salad and lemon tart were my favorite dishes, though everything was super tasty. The only letdown was the mussels, which were nothing special. 

Service was also amazing - they brought us the mushroom millefuille on the house!

4.5 stars.
Amazing spot, great for large parties. Service phenomenal. Everything on the menu is of caliber

It had been years since I had come to Dirty French so when some friends suggested it for dinner I was happy to try it again.  Some things we ordered were good, but others were a letdown.

I had remembered that the duck l' orange (which is now a special) was fantastic, with crispy skin, and delicious flavors- but this time unfortunately, it was over cooked (not even close to medium rare) with the fat not rendered properly so overall not a good dish that I'd recommend.  

We also ordered:
- deviled eggs (which were fine they tasted like deviled eggs should and were gluten free)
- tuna tartare (this was really good and gluten free)
- baked oysters - I didn't try as I prefer raw but they were gluten free and my husband enjoyed them 
- foie gras that was wrapped in a pastry bread buff - very unique I hadn't had this before and it was pretty good
-muscles with the crab and crispy rice were good and surprisingly inexpensive.  
- The potato side dishes are all good.  

The service was great and the drinks were tasty, but it was generally not up to par to what I remember

First time eating at Dirty French and had an incredible experience. Phenomenal service from our amazing server Jean Pierre; delicious wine and cocktails and fantastic dessert. Highly recommend the lamb carpaccio, tuna tartar and sweetbreads to start followed by the chicken & crepes, Burger and Mussels for our entrees. Overall, awesome experience and great staff.

Food and service were amazing! Their drinks are truly delicious and works of art! The restaurant is also so beautifully decorated. We loved the vibe! 
Only down side was our party of 6 did feel pressured to order a certain amount of food. The waiter was pretty persistent that we order 3 appetizers and two veggies in addition to our main entree and drinks. 
The food was worth it but over $600 later we did end up over ordering and having so much food to take home. Would go back but order less!

Exceptional service by Pamela, she is an absolute gem and a rarity in today's society. The ambiance is cozy, decadent and funky all at the same time. Outstanding dishes, from appetizers to dessert. The best duck breast I ever had, just perfect. Will absolutely be returning.

We stayed at the Ludlow for about a week and weren't expecting to use the Dirty French bar or restaurant as much as we did, but it was a really solid place for breakfast, dinner or drinks. Everything we had was well executed -- steak au poivre, the baby gem salad (which I'm going to try to replicate at home), lemon pancakes, etc. You don't feel like you're settling if you want to hole up inside and hang out in the actual restaurant or lounge.
After going I don't know how many times. Depending on your luck you're treated like shit by one of the hosts. Some are really great. One is not. Jesus Christ can anybody be more rude

This meal was out of this world!!! Every dish was bursting with flavor, service was amazing, we had a group for a birthday- they couldn't have been more accommodating. Good tunes too. Can't wait to return!!!

I have been to Dirty French twice.  The food is very good and the service impeccable.  Don't miss out on the desserts.  I took our waiter's recommendation and he did not steer us wrong.  It is quickly becoming my favorite restaurant in NYC.

I attended my daughter-in-law's bridal shower at Dirty French and they did an amazing job. The staff is fabulous, the decor is so cool, the food was delicious.
The room upstairs was perfect for a party of 40. Downstairs the restaurant was packed. That's just a testament to how fabulous they are.

The starter bread is where it's at. Was not disappointed by any element of the meal, but the window was a little drafty. Servers could have been more attentive, but overall enjoyed the experience--will come back to try more menu items! Ambience is great.

The food is out of this world and the staff "TOP NOTCH"!  The only complaint I have is that the food and drinks are soooo good, I couldn't resist ordering more.  Must try items are the deviled eggs, tuna tartare, Steak Au Poivre, Pommes Louis and the  L'Échappée Belle drink!  I would also like to compliment our amazing server by the name of P, she was fantastic and Chef John whom we met, such a sweetheart!  We will be returning soon!

This place is fantastic!! Impeccable service that goes truly above and beyond! 

The food was delicious! We unfortunately didn't have any room for dessert with how many appetizers and entrees we ordered.

The oysters and mushrooms to start were definitely the way to go!

I got the salmon and it was A tad spicy but good!! To drink I had rosé picked out by the sommelier 

Definitely a place to recommend for any occasion!

Came here for a work event and I was amazed by the quality of their food. The steak was rare cooked, not bloody, and the meat was so tender. I would say the steak was my favorite out the preset menu. 
The restaurant atmosphere is romantic so this is a good place for date night. :)
Jeffrey the bartender was great! Very helpful/knowledgeable and made us feel special. Came in for a Bellini which had fresh juice (nice touch)

AMAZING. Worth the hype. Definitely one of the top restaurants in the city and worth a visit. 

We came for our one-year wedding anniversary and they gave us two delicious glasses of champagne on the house to start, which was super thoughtful and started the night off right.

Every other food item we ordered was mind blowing delicious and unique in its own way, which earned this place extra brownie points.
- Duck l'orange: Thanks to other Yelp reviews, we knew to reserve this ahead of time in the notes of our reservation. My husband loved it and said it was some of the best duck he has ever had. I normally don't like duck l'orange bc I usually find the sauce too sweet but have to admit this was cooked perfectly and I was very impressed by the crispy skin. 
- Roasted duck fat potatoes: There was one left so we snagged it and so glad we did. These were delicious! A must order. 
- Mushroom millefeuille: one of the best dishes I have ever had in my entire life. MUST ORDER. 
- Lamb carpaccio: very creative and delicious. Also highly recommend. 
- free flatbread to start: Free but one of the best things I had all night 
- Mussels etouffe: still good but maybe my least favorite dish of the night (mussels were very tiny).
- Beignets: pretty decent

This was quite literally the worst meal of my entire life. I ordered a medium-well steak and it was literally raw. At first I thought I was just being picky but then my husband ordered the salmon and it was raw too. How the hell do you serve someone a raw salmon. We're not eating sushi here. We sent it back and the waitress was confused with that the issue was and She said quote "what you wanted your salmon well done?"... no, but at least cooked all the way. As if she asked when we ordered. They took our plates back and it still came back uncooked. Disgusting. She was so unapologetic and they didn't even comp a drink or anything. I'm not normally the type to make reviews but wow I was in shock that we even paid for this shit. Terrible meal, terrible service. 10/10 would not recommend.

food was pretty overpriced for what you get, and servers were pretty pushy with trying to upsell you. there's so much more good food in the area, would not go here unless you couldn't find room anywhere else - the one benefit is maybe they have a lot of seating
Outstanding place. The portions are good and you won't be disappointed. Very comforting and a great place for date nights.
Had my bachelor party dinner here. It was absolutely amazing! Great food, awesome service, and an amazing time!

Came here for a late night drink, not too late, around 11. Bartenders were busy closing, annoyed that we wanted a glass of wine but said sure, here you go, you can drink it in the patio. After about 15 minutes, we were told they were closing and must leave. Could not sit inside by reception either. No exceptions. 
Had we known they were shutting down we wouldn't have spent $50 for 2 glasses of wine. Which we could not even finish. Rude and unfriendly all around.
This place is a gem. Friendly service, delicious food, awesome cocktails, it's the whole package. So good. You don't want to miss it.

Excellent location, and right next to Katz's deli. Nice decorations, moderate to high priced menu with tasty food. My favorite was the french fries, surprisingly. Good place to hang out and relax, get a drink and eat some food with friends. It doesn't hurt that the hotel next to it is so nice.

I went to Dirty French and literally tried everything on the menu! I will just say 5 Stars Across the Board! Megan was such a great host for my very first visit here! I definitely recommend getting the Duck and the Fois Gras! Sooo good! The duck is tender and melts in your mouth. The Fois Gras is savory with the perfect touch of sweetness because of a jam sauce they spread onto the plate. 

I had a drink that had a cinnamon spice to it, it was one of those drinks that came with a lot in the glass, and a very fancy tiki glass with a fire presentation when served. Which was a plus. I ended the meal with the crème brûlée. OMG ! Get it! It's so tasty you will not be disappointed!

To top off whole food be absolutely amazing, Victoria gave us A1 service, she's very knowledgeable about the menu and I enjoyed her explaining the dishes I've never tried before. I mean the whole staff was great and made the experience remarkable. Nelson made us feel very welcomed. I am definitely coming back here when I'm in NYC!

Had a great time at the Dirty French! My colleague made a reservation a few hours before on a Monday night.  When we arrived, it was relatively busy.  Loved the atmosphere of the space.

What we ordered in ranked order:

1.  Shrimp Beignet -- underrated! Worth trying 
2.  Kale & Sunchoke Salad -- super tasty
3.  East Coast Oyster -- can't go wrong here 
4.  Roasted Salmon -- was okay, not my favorite
5.  Mushroom Millefeuille -- was an interesting take on mushrooms, but I would pass
6.  Devils Eggs -- nothing special

The Somalia was super and the servers were all very friendly.  Would defiantly recommend checking out.  Hopefully I'll be back to try more of the menu.

Had a great dinner here this past weekend. I've wanted to go for quite some time, and it absolutely lived up to my expectations.

We started with the shrimp beignets and the gem salad. The beignets were really good, my only complaint would be the lemon was a bit overpowering. Would still order again if we went back. The gem salad was also good, but would maybe opt for a different app or salad next time.

I struggled deciding between the duck and the chicken and crepes. We decided on the chicken and were so glad we did. It's a difficult dish to describe, other than saying it's delicious. The sauce was fantastic. The chicken was easily the most perfectly cooked chicken I've ever had. I loved the dark meat which they provide separately as well. It all goes together perfectly when you wrap it up with the peppers and other fixings they provide. 

Drinks were awesome, and great service. I will absolutely be back, and maybe try the duck next time.

Nice environment, great staff, had the starter bread with spread, I can eat that day and night.  The little gem salad that also became a favorite. Hanger steak au poivre with fries, the steak was well done when I asked for medium well. The fries where ok.  I would go back.

Oui Oui and Oui! 

Aside from the host initially trying to seat us into a section where we felt we were sitting in the next table's lap (we were able to get another table) everything from beginning to end was really just amazing.  I dined there in August with my fiance and it is still in my top 10.  Our server (I don't remember her name) was so friendly and great at recommending some superb entrees and dessert at the end. 

Do not come here and leave without getting the duck and dirty rice!
This is a gentrifier spot but at least it's a good one loved,  the team here they made great drinks

The food, the service and the ambiance were all 5-star. Hadn't even heard of the place (probably bc I love uptown) but came on a date and it was amazing. We had a lovely dinner (Tuna Tartare; Steamed Black Bass; Steak Frites) and a bottle of wine and then retired to the lounge in the back right in front of the fire! What an amazing evening for two! Thanks to the amazing hosts abs hostesses. I will be back.

Brunch: Good food. Nice live music but VERY loud. And so close to us we had to switch tables to escape the volume. The duck hash was very flavorful. It was salty, but I like salty. The salmon and lox was just that. Nothing to write home about. Overall good experience and service.

The food and atmosphere is amazing! We had the lobster ravioli, duck, broccoli, fries and Cajun fish. Definitely will recommend. They do not allow flash photography in seating area. They play 80s music through out dinner.

This is a cute bar located inside the Ludlow hotel. The bartender was nice. I got the L'Échappée Belle($18). It came flaming and it was delicious! I highly recommend you pop down for a drink if you are staying at the Ludlow!

It was my first time here. We came to celebrate my birthday. 
From the door I loved the place. The ambiance is somewhat 1920 meets Dr. Scott lab/office from Rocky Horror Pictures Show without him and his wheelchair ‼
They have a sommelier which is amazing. I wish they were more of them as the studies are intense, impressive and fascinating. So if you have one, you might as well utilise them. They really know wine! The Somm here was no different and helped us figure the bottle we shared. We enjoyed it to the last drop while enjoying our meal.
The server came and introduced himself and later brought a plate with hot, freshly made fluffy flat bread accompanied with lightly seasoned crème fraîche. We couldn't get enough of it. A delight treat! 
And than came the appetisers we selected. WOW. There is no other word to describe the level of entertainment provided to my palate. We ordered the Mushroom Millefeuille is a very special and complexed dish to make and it was amazingly tender and tasty. The Lamb Carpaccio was to-die-for! So delicate, paper thin, melting in your mouth yet, so flavourful it's a party in your mouth. The Duck Rillette en Brik was another another delightful appetiser: tasty duck meet wrapped in a perfectly flaky filo dough, sitting on a bed of foie gras. YUM! Than came our entrée. A perfectly made medium-rare burger with hand-cut steak fries (showing respect to the fries by not using any pre-cut option). The salmon was fresh, flaky and just perfectly made so it's not dry but not raw. Kale salad with goat cheese and pears was very refreshing and satisfying! On the side we had the string bean which were a shout-out to all string beans and if you don't like them (bc many ppl don't) you should try this one, you'll change your mind. 
As we moved to cocktails, the server, who was very professional, attentive and knew just the right moments to check in with us, was delivering at every corner including the timing to present me with my Crème Brûlée and a candle for my bday. 
The cocktails were excellent, we had vodka martini, Gyn martini both w a twist and a Negroni Sbagliato made to order. 
So if it wasn't clear by now, I highly recommend. We are definitely coming back.

Great time at Dirty French! Came here recently with a date and loved the idea of french food in a fun vibe environment.

The servers were welcoming and kind, with prompt service. Their drinks were yummy and the menu was great, and we ordered a handful of dishes to share. The steak was excellent and I don't remember the other sides since I had a couple frenchie martinis! There was music playing too during Christmas week, and they had cute Wham! type 80s music playing.

Def recommend for couples, groups or want to take people out for a good time. Not cheap by any means as well, but that's New York!
Great bar, great music , great service. The food was mediocre and overpriced. Like the bar better than the dining room

Really disappointed by this place. I'm a big fan of other Major Food Group restaurants and this one just didn't impress. Firstly, the decor in this place was lacking. Every other MFG restaurant I've been to has gone over the top with decor, it almost feels like your being transported into a perfectly designed world/setting. The theme is clear and you feel like you're apart of the story they're telling. Dirty French on the other hand very much just felt like a standard hotel restaurant, which I guess in reality it is. 

The food was also extremely underwhelming. I started off with the Little Gem salad, which was a large serving (definitely enough for 2-4). The dressing almost tasted like a fancy ranch which I enjoyed. The crispy shallots were also a nice touch. This was probably the best thing I consumed, besides the free bread that comes at the start of the meal. 

For my main course I had the Chicken Persillade and Pommes Louis. The chicken arrived lukewarm, and the sauce had a strange consistency. The flavor was overwhelmingly garlicky, and there wasn't much else to the dish. The chicken had an okay texture but was a little stiff. 

The Pommes Louis was also unremarkable. The potatoes had a pleasant fatty flavor, but they were inconsistently cooked, some pieces being overly crispy, some soggy. The potatoes also come with garlic sprinkled on top, which didn't seem to incorporate well. It seems like the menu relies heavily into garlic to save the day. 

The one thing I will give this restaurant credit for it the service. Everyone was super friendly, attentive, and kind. 

Overall I think there are much better places to have not only French food, but a meal priced this highly in New York. I would not recommend going out of your way for this one.

Made a reservation to celebrate my birthday as we were going out in the area. As we were a bigger group, we got to try a bit of everything. The cocktails are very good! I had the L'Échappé Belle (tequila, strawberry, tangerine) and it was delicious (also came on fire, which was pretty fun). My friends were also very happy with their drinks. For starters we tried the complimentary bread which is FANTASTIC, lamb carpaccio (so good), tartare (fresh and had an interesting mix of spices) and the mushroom milefeuille (a bit disappointed as I was very excited to try this. The curry sauce is great but I don't feel like everything was coming together and the mushrooms lacked seasoning). For main course I had the hanger steak au poivre - right temperature, great sauce. Our table ordered a bunch of sides: the mashed potatoes were so silky and delicious, dirty rice was the unexpected favorite and even the green beans were great. There is no birthday without dessert, so we tried the beignets and the chocolate cake, both very good choices. We finished our amazing dinner with espresso martinis. 
Aside from the great food and ambiance, the service was top notch and we never felt rushed to order and leave, which I really appreciated - we had so much fun!
It had been a while since I've been here. Incredible food, attentive staff...and don't get me started on the bread with cheese...hard to stop eating it! Will continue to come here!

Tried this place last night for a friend's bday dinner. We missed our reservation time because of traffic and they still accommodated us. The staff was very nice and attentive and made stellar recommendations. I ordered the grilled oysters, and scallop cru for apps and they were phenomenal. Ordered the chicken with spinach and fritters as my sides. Was a hit bummed they didn't have the roasted potatoes in duck fat but got over that very quickly. My only negative is that the beignets were a B in a meal of A+s

what a difference nearly a decade has made. i remember having to plead with a reservationist (on a phone!) and "winning" a late night slot for our dinner, where they couldn't even seat us on time, and bounced us around different tables, until they were able to accommodate our reservation. no one would put up with that now, and no one does. after moving to brooklyn, i've been everywhere from aska to le crocodile, from st. anselm to gage and tollner, so expectations aren't as low as they were. but...

we were truly bowled over by the exploded french flea market decor on our first trip here, as well as all the food. but ... time has passed now. we have resy now. dirty french isn't exactly the hottest spot in town anymore. our meal, last night, was special in its own way, but it noticeably lacked the blinding transcendence of our first meal here, many years ago.

I love this strip of ludlow street, and I still find the decor of DF to be unique and quite pretty. the lobby lounge outside is beautiful too, their bathrooms resemble the labyrinthine underground tunnels of an old keith mcnally joint, and they use red flower hand wash/cream products. nice touch.

everyone was friendly. and the food? very good. the gem salad was delicious, and interesting. it is, in a sense, drowned in that punk-ranch dressing, but it's good. the oysters bourguignon were delicious. i was curious to try the pommes louis, after hearing an intriguing description from our server, but no go...at 7:45, they were already sold out. huh.

the chicken crepes for two is really good, and remains the restaurant's shining star, kind of like getting the whole duck at williamsburg's francie, it's probably why you should come. the chicken is delicious, and they do give you the whole chicken. the white meat is sliced, the dark meat comes on the bone in a different bowl, and you get a dish of tasty accompaniments.

i think they need twice the crepes for this dish to truly transcend time and space, like they intend, but it is really yummy, and decadent, but the bread (really, nan) that they give you with the boursin butter at the beginning of the meal almost makes up for the lack of crepes (I think you get only three, wuh woh).

what's going on with the service?? i must have read through the menu half a dozen times, opening and closing the damn thing, before a waiter ever approached our table to take drink orders. the sommelier seemed noticeably indifferent to us, and to our bottle of wine. in the middle of our meal, a random glass of vodka was placed in front of my face.

"this isn't mine," i told the man. i got a response along the lines of (and not really paraphrasing here) "i don't know, just drink it."

uh. ok.

when the waiter approached at the end of our meal and asked if we wanted to order dessert wine, we quietly asked, "whatever happened to our bottle of wine??" (it was supposed to be "on ice" lol).

the waiter scurried off and re-appeared with our bottle, more than a quarter full. this is the end of our meal now, yiiiikkkkkessssss. "sorry," he said, and i realized this was maybe the third or fourth apology we'd received for something. the somm obviously never bothered to inform the server we had a bottle of wine, a communication lapse more akin to a roadside diner than a major food group restaurant.

anyway. nice to be back, but i've grown too, it seems, and i'm not as easily impresed as i once was.

Service was terrible.  Absolutely terrible. Which is a shame because the hotel and the staff of the hotel were amazing.  This review is not a reflection of the Ludlow Hotel and their staff.  

I was celebrating my anniversary and wanted to purchase a bottle of champagne. I walked up and spoke with the bartender (Asian Woman, didn't have a name tag) I asked politely if she could recommend a champagne or sparkling wine, I described in detail of what I was looking for. The two choices she provided were not good and I asked if she could recommend perhaps another one, at that point she threw her hands up and said loudly "I don't know what you want" I was surprised at this outburst and said I am sorry about any misunderstanding but I provided you a description and it's ok if you can't recommend anything, I'll just try the Rose.  She doesn't respond and walks away at this point I just stood up and left. Luckily someone at the hotel staff saw what was happening and apologized and sent a complimentary bottle of champagne to our room which we appreciate.  I understand that people have bad days but that's no excuse for you to take out your frustration on innocent people. I hope the management can provide coaching and help her with her soft skills.

Delicious food and lovely ambiance! My boyfriend booked this spot for our 3 year anniversary and it was perfect. The bread and cheese that was served was SO good, we asked for more. i ordered the mussels etoiffe. We were also given complementary champagne to celebrate. The cocktails were also really good/not too sweet.

I will give a hundred start to this place just for their pancakes. They also make a mean espresso martini. 

Beautiful old school decor and lovely place for brunch. It was so easy to get a table! 

The Benedict was nothing to rave about but pretty standard. Note/warning: one side of bacon is huge and is good for 3-4 people actually 

They don't bug you to leave when you are done (may be because they were empty that day but still) 

Overall, great joint especially if you get a 2-4 h wait time from the surrounding more popular joints. 

Will I go back? Heck, yes, and have pancakes and espresso martinis.

My boyfriend and I went here for his birthday. The staff was very friendly and were fantastic throughout the experience.

We ordered oysters as an appetizer , and for our main entrees Ny strip and mushroom millefeuille. The steak was cooked to perfection and seasoned very well. The mushroom millefeuille was OUTSTANDING. For desert we ordered lemon cake, which was also very good.

It reminded me very much of a traditional french restaurant in Paris. We live close by and will be back!

Part of Major Food Group, I went to this popular bistro with one of my usual groups to have their famous duck a l'orange and share a bunch of other other things. The space was nice and the service was friendly with good suggestions. I ordered a cocktail and the waiter came back and said that the menu had unfortunately changed and told me the current selections also saying that I could try a drink first to see if I like it which was very nice. I got the One Way Street ($18) with cognac, pineau, and golden raisin to drink. This was a delicious with a cognac base and good fruity elements but not overly sweet and I would recommend it.

We were given the Flatbread With Fromage Blanc to begin with. Compared to most other modern restaurants where you have to pay for their nice bread, it was good to see that this place still serves theirs as part of the meal for free. This was a good starting bite albeit potentially a bit rich. The fresh warm flatbread paired nicely with the cheese.

From the hors d'ouevres section, the Mushroom Millefeuille ($29) with butternut squash and red curry was delicious. The mushrooms were thin sliced and had a pleasant plumpness with a slightly crispy texture with the slightly sweet and herbal red curry being a good accompaniment. I am unsure the mushroom used but I have virtually 0 complaints about the dish.

From the Plat Principal, their Duck A L'orange (I believe $49) was shared between two. The duck was crispy though I have had others which were more succulent with a better skin texture. The orange sauce however was outstanding. Not overly sweet and very well seasoned. My only complaint about said sauce would be perhaps that that there wasn't enough of it as a few of the pieces.

From the same section, the Steak Au Poivre ($39 base with various prices) or steak with green peppercorn sauce was probably the weakest of the dishes. We got it with hanger steak without the frites so at the lowest price point. The steak was a bit small for the price and it could have been a bit more tender (even with it being hanger steak) but the peppercorn sauce was very well prepared. It's hard to recommend however with the portion size and with the slightly chewy pieces even with the excellent sauce. 

This is a quality French bistro with some protein issues. While the quality of the sauces are on point for the prices, I would say the actual meat (outside of the mushroom dish) was a bit lower quality compared to some other places which are a bit cheaper. The duck was a big drier than other spots and the steak was both small and a bit chewy. If the protein was as well prepared as their excellent sauces, I'd probably give a 5 but overall I'm stick with a 4.

I'd recommend the dirty rice, pomme fries, pomme Louis, the oysters were amazing and the cod was ok. The salmon comes on the rare side and had little to no flavor. For dessert get the crème brûlée. The chocolate cake has a hint of mint and oddly came with melted ice cream on the plate. Not sure if it was a scoop at one point but they waited too long to serve it to us. The beignets are ok. I'm not a huge Carmel fan. They don't have any flavor without it but are good.

We had an early breakfast here on a Saturday. The vibe is interesting since it's part of a hotel and has a lounge just outside of the restaurant and the service was good. Their selection is somewhat limited but the overall food quality was good.

My friends and I chose to go to this restaurant for an Easter dinner and it did not disappoint. The ambiance in this restaurant is incredible and is definitely a great spot for a group of friends or for a date. This decor and ambiance in this restaurant makes you feel as though you are in Paris. I was honestly very surprised that the restaurant was not busier on a Sunday night.

To start off, the waiter was incredibly kind and gave us each a glass of sparkling champagne on the house. He was a little sassy but we definitely appreciated the kind gesture! We were also brought house bread and butter -- incredibly delicious! I wish I had asked for more bread because both the bread and butter were some of the best I had tasted in the city.

We ordered the Mushroom dish and Tuna Tartare to share and they both tasted amazing. The mushrooms were very flavorful and are definitely a must try. 

I personally ordered the salmon which was very good! I wish it had come with potatoes or a more heartier vegetable side dish, but, nonetheless, it was very tasty. My friends all ordered the mussels which they thought were tasty. The number of mussels that came in this dish was definitely generous -- they struggled to finish all of the mussels and I had to save the day. If you're looking for the crab in this dish it's hidden away in the gravy at the bottom of the pot. A bigger pot would've been better to fit all of the mussels and reach the bottom of the pot for the gravy.

Overall, this was a great restaurant that I would recommend checking out!

I love this place.  Every time I'm in New York, I make my way to the East Village and eat one of the best versions of pre-dinner  (free) bread and butter on the planet.  I dare you to challenge me.  That flat bread and chive butter is straight from the lord above. I am sure baby Jesus used his little holy, baby hands to patty this cake and serve it up with a puddle of hot butter blanketing the lower crevices of this flat bread.  It's so good. I could just eat that, but I don't. I don't have the willpower. 

The oyster are so fresh and so clean... clean. Like a splash of the crisp sea.  The bone marrow if flavorful, but a tiny portion as is customary with this dish.  I have never had a meal here that wasn't out if sight.  

The staff is a bit snobby, but once you let them know, listen Hunter, I belong here. They treat you with respect. But you gotta throw the snobby back at them like game recognizing game.  

Thus delicious spot is in the Ludlow hotel which has a comfy indoor patio area where you can chill and drank.

Came here for a work dinner and had the following

Lamb carpaccio - 3/5 had gyro type spices

Tuna tartar - 3/5 had a flavor I couldn't identify but wasn't a fan

Mushrooms - 5/5 was a table favorite and it was about the sauce

Oysters - 4/5 was basically an escargot flavor

Bone marrow - 2/5 they gave an end piece that had less than a dime size worth of marrow

Gem salad - 4/5 was refreshing

Chicken and crepes for 2 - 3/5 good roast chicken, not sure why you need crepes

Duck orange - 4/5 duck was good but in the sweet side which I guess is normal

Hanger Steak - 4/5 peppercorn sauce was good and steak was cooked to correct temp. Fries were good.

The service was good but after we finished and cleared plates they left us sitting for 10 minutes and I couldn't even get anyone's attention to ask them what desserts they have. I had to go up and ask the manager for desert menus. Apparently they don't have printed menus. 

Overall 3 stars with some good dishes and some bad dishes but bad service taints it all.

The atmosphere is nice... and that's where it ends. Every single thing we ordered was average to bad. The filet was chewy, the peppercorn sauce has so much salt it could send you to the ER, and the scallops taste like they've been sitting in the baking sun for 3 days. Possibly the worst most expensive restaurant I've been to in nyc. Barf.

Such a great place. The food and drinks were awesome but what stood out is the service. Our child was asleep when we left him with our babysitter and we were just trying to get out without waking him up. I left without my wedding ring by mistake and didn't want to chance making noise while going back to get it. My husband had his ring on. During dinner, when I had gotten up to go to the restroom, the waitress came by and asked my husband if he would like another drink and asked if she could refill his "lady friend's" drink as well. He said yes. 
When I returned he told me what had just transpired - apparently he was too taken aback to tell her I was his wife and then didn't want to look like he was lying since I didn't have my ring. I'm also super-impressed she had noticed enough to not embarrass my husband in case I wasn't his wife (not that I would have minded that!) Now I didn't want to look like his side-ho but also didn't want to make a big deal of it and thought I would say something if it came up (yes, I know, we were giving this waaaaay too much thought). 
The waitress returned with our drinks. I opened my mouth to say something, but there wasn't a smidge of judgment on her face. Nothing. Just friendly and kind and hospitable. So I just enjoyed the rest of my meal. Side-ho went home happy.
Best Gin gimlet I ever did have, bartender also made me a bartenders choice and it was even better!

Food was sooooo salty. The scallops were very fishy and the béchamel sauce was exhaustingly salty. The sauce for the hanger steak was also so salty and very meh which is unfortunate bc the meat was cooked great. Fries were great, kale salad is alright,  martinis strong. If you go- get the sauces on the side!!

Last time at Dirty French. "Omg Phillip and I had so much fun." Drinks were flowing the food was delicious and the waiter was cute. It felt like a Sunday brunch party. Everyone was having a good time.
A nice hotel lounge/bar, good vibes and nice lighting for a late night drink. The service was great and were given drinks and food quite promptly once seated.

This was one of the most upsetting dining experiences I've had in a long time. I've had French food before so it's not like I didn't know what the cuisine was about. 

The decor was interesting. Kind of drab but I guess if that's what they choose then it works. 

So we started off with drinks. I had the L Echappee Belle, it was rum, strawberry and tangerine served in a skull like glass with fire. The presentation was super cool and the drink I give a 5 out of 5. My friend had red wine and was impressed and my other friend ordered a lemon drop and was ok with it.

They serve the table a really delicious Flatbread with a butter spread. It was very tasty and fresh, so that was appreciated. 

For appetizers we had deviled eggs and the bone marrow aigre doux. I enjoyed the deviled eggs as there were well seasoned and tasty. I didn't partake in the bone marrow, not my thing. However, my friends enjoyed it with the toasted bread. 

For entrees we ordered the steamed black bass, it had absolutely NO taste whatsoever. That's right, NO taste. We had to add salt and pepper and even asked for some kind of hot sauce.  Still it was very bad.  We ordered the steak au poivre hanger steak, another bad option, I'm questioning if that was even steak to be honest, it was not even cooked the way we asked. The sauce was extremely salty and that "steak" was chewy and undesirable. My friend is a steak connoisseur, so I'm upset she had to be subjected to that. Lastly, I ordered the "special", this was the Duck a L'Orange. It was not bad, the sauce was good and the puree I accompanied it was good. It was actually the best thing on the table, but it was so smooth it was like baby food. Haha. For the money we paid we felt displeased.
