Here is the KICKER, my friend that had the seabass and myself that had the duck, we both had stomach aches and more the next day. 

The ginger ale was good.
Service was cool.
The atmosphere was good. The steak and sausage were delicious. I would skip the fish next time. Service was good. I would recommend people to come.

Food was great, decent price for the location and ambience. Service was great as well. 
I was here for brunch on a Saturday, I recommend this restaurant, quiet and great decor.

Dirty French is located inside the Ludlow Hotel. It was super convenient in the mornings when I'd grab an oatmeal ($11). One morning, I dined in for breakfast and the restaurant was quite empty. Only one of the servers/staff was picky with where we sat. She took a while to take my order and never checked up on me. I had to flag someone else down to close out. She made the morning an awful experience. However, the oatmeal is worth praising and checking out for breakfast.

We had an amazing experience here! I took my fiancée for her birthday- I had made a note mentioning it on the reservation ahead of time. When we walked in and gave my name both hostesses excitedly wished her happy birthday, and congratulated us on our engagement. We were seated in a corner booth- my favorite area. Our waiter Julio promptly came over with complementary champagne  and also congratulated us and wished her happy birthday. He walked us through the menu, answered all of our questions and was just so warm and welcoming. The food is SO GOOD! We started with oysters and shrimp beignets, the mushroom millefeulle, then had the chicken and crepes for two. We had cocktails and I asked for a red wine to go with the chicken- Julio picked out the perfect pairing. We were paid just enough attention to have our needs met consistently, but never felt rushed. We spent a couple hours enjoying a long romantic dinner, and at the end they brought us ice cream with a candle. It was the perfect celebration dinner and I would definitely go back.

Had a wonderful time here. There is a parking lot across the street which is helpful. 

Our waiter was great and gave good recommendations. The bartender made the drinks on point. 

Everything we had was delicious.

Pamela is amazing! Seriously so fun and such a great representation for Dirty French. There were 2 of us and we ordered the lamb carpaccio, salmon, half chicken, potatoes, and baby gem salad. They also brought out pita and tzatziki for the table. We ordered a little more than we could eat, when I'd probably cut out the potatoes (although delicious as well). The chicken was by far the best thing we ate, and one of the most flavorful and juicy chickens I've ever had. I highly recommend it. The lamb carpaccio was so different than I expected. It is also packed with flavor. The salad was a great compliment to all of these robust spices. I definitely recommend as it was a refreshing accompaniment. The salmon and potatoes were also good. I recommend dipping the potato in the chicken pot if you get both. We also enjoyed our drinks. Thanks so much Pamela- you made our dinner even more special.

I have mixed feelings about this place. While I enjoyed the atmosphere and the drinks, the food was only OK. I really had higher expectations for this place as it has been consistently referred to as a staple of the lower east side.

Server was very very polite, but the overall cadence of the meal was very slow. Took a while for our drinks to come out. Basically came a minute before the appetizers were dropped off at the table. Entrees came a while after that.

Meal came with complimentary warm flatbread which was very very good. 

We ordered the following:

Truffle Mac N Cheese: served on a plate instead of skillet or other baking dish. the sauce was really loose. Could barely taste the ham in it. Truffle flavor on top was nice and fresh though
Oysters Bourguignon - hard pass. Oysters were very rubbery. Kind of like an escargot sauce. There were 6 and we told the server to take the last three away
Pomme Luis - Ok
Chicken Persillade - pretty good, but at the end of the day it is just a roasted chicken. Nothing special
Burger Maison - great but SO salty. I'm usually not one to complain but I was chugging water the rest of the night. Real saucey. Fries on the side were excellently fried
Cote De Porc - probably the most interesting dish. Sweet sauce on the pork
Corn - special side for the evening... nothing special

Got a couple rounds of Belmondos for the table. Those were great

Impeccable service and food everything was absolutely amazing. The ambiance was very welcoming my food was plated so elegantly the chef specials and staff recommendations were all delicious. I will definitely revisit.

This place was absolutely lovely, although I'll say our service could have been a little better. A must-order is the mushroom Mille-feulle. Forgive me if the spelling is incorrect, however, the server mentioned that it takes close to 9 hours to prepare this dish and it is outstanding. Even my non-mushroom-loving friend agreed that this dish was superior. Since it was a birthday I was hoping to order dessert but unfortunately, no one informed us that the kitchen was closing soon so we hadn't placed an order for a birthday treat. I think most people can agree a birthday meal isn't complete with a bit of cake! That and also it was a teeny bit slow.

Nice ambience, large, noisy. The hanger steak was smothered in pepper, which I'm not a fan of. Underneath all that the steak was good and good quality. The spinach was salty and inedible. Won't be returning.
The manager said he would refund our money for dinner, but this has not happened. I wish i never ate the grilled oysters there. I was sick for 2 weeks.

We had their Christmas dinner and it was excellent. All of the dishes are also on their normal menu: tuna tartare, oysters bourgignon, kale salad, filet mignon, and the two desserts, chocolate cake and lemon tart. The cocktails were also delicious and creative.

I dream about the mushroom Meuille feuille here - it's that good! They rotate the sauces for it and I've tried the green curry which is amazing. The duck a l'orange is also *chefs kiss*. A smaller portion but perfect crispness to the skin and the sauce is wonderful.
Very good. Staff is great. I was so lost and felt out of place but they made me feel welcomed and had suggestions for me. Will be returning.

Amazing service amazing food.  At first I was a bit turned off when we came in.   We had 6:15 reservations we 15/20 min walk here (I am super pregnant) arrived at 6pm.  Restaurant wasn't even full it was empty... they had us wait in the lounge. We were seated at 6;15 and our server PAMELA turned everything around!! Pamela is a phenomenal server!! She just made our dinner experience  10x better!! She went above and beyond everything.

My friend and I came here for dinner the other night as she mentioned she had been before, and always enjoyed the food. We made a reservation for 8:30pm, but we were able to be seated earlier, which was great. We ordered the little gem salad, the truffle Mac and Cheese and the Duck (which my friend was very excited about). They came by with this amazing fluffy bread and dip before our food came out, and I was contemplating ordering another one because it was that good. The restaurant itself is very dimly lit and has a sexy vibe, so great for catching up with a friend or two or for a date night. Would definitely come back here again!

Everything at this place is incredible. The food, drinks, and atmosphere is incredible - but more than anything - THE PEOPLE. I highly suggest everyone come here and ask for Pamela (with the braids). Authentic, engaging, weird, and brilliant. Makes for an experience unlike something you will get anywhere else. Will become a regular spot. Pamela is one of a f*cking kind. Give that girl an Oscar we love her. Love this place but love Pamela more.. ASK FOR HER

Ambiance 4/5  Beautiful, but tables are small. 
Food 3/5   It was good, just not spectacular, and definitely not worth the price.
Drinks 3/5  Good, nothing special.

4 people $350.. yikes.. a bit crazy. It was a nice dinner but not worth the price

This remains one of my favorite restaurants in the city. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, food is delicious and beautifully presented, and the cocktails are not watered down.

My favorite drink is the Bellmondo.  So good.  It's hard to choose a favorite appetizer or entree from the menu, as everyone is so good.  The best thing to do, is to go with a group and share plates.  A few of my favorite starters are the lamb carpaccio and tuna tartare.  It seems odd to rave about a salad, but both the kale and the endive salads are exceptional.  There are several wonderful chicken dishes on the menu.  A fun one is the chicken with crepes.  The others are good too.  The steak was one of the best I've had, but my favorite was probably the dover, so beautifully seasoned with Moroccan spices.  One of the most unique vegetable dishes on the menu remains a personal favorite ~ the Miele feuille mushroom dish.  So good!  If you have room for dessert, there are some nice options ~ the creme brulee is a favorite, as is the sorbet. There is also a lovely cheese and guava jam plate.  You won't be disappointed, regardless of what you order. Bon appetit!

Rating is for the food. I ordered the pork dish which arrived undercooked and the meat was pink in the middle. Also ordered the tarte au citron which was cold and tasted like the way a fridgerator smells. Bread service was decent, deviled eggs, pommes
Louis and truffle mac and cheese were tasty.

Service was attentive until the dinner rush arrived and once crowded, we were left hanging and dinner dragged. The maitre d's, servers, bussers, and front of staff work hard for sure, so I give them lots of credit. They stand to have 1 or 2 more servers on the floor.

Would I come back? Probably not. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't amazing. Very middle of the road.

Ambiance is fine, classic bistro look inside of the Ludlow Hotel. The music playlist was too loud and random. Paul Simon and Aerosmith? Pick the right vibe.

Make sure to save your credit card receipt and check your credit card statement.    Had lunch here on March 25th, 2024.  There were 4 of us, and I and one other person asked the server to split the bill between our 2 credit cards.  I happened to check my online statement the next day and found that I had been charged for the total amount.  I did save my printed receipt which was correct.   First, the only phone number I was able to find was on the website and went directly to voicemail with no opportunity to talk to anyone or leave a message.  There was a way to send a message via their website which I did...  They did adjust the amount, but I asked what had happened and they did not answer.    Wondering whether this is something that happens on a regular basis...    Although I've had lunch there quite a few times, as I occasionally work in the neighborhood, and find the food decent at a reasonable price point, but will not be returning...
Amazing food, service and ambiance. Oliver is fantastic and knowledgeable! We loved it!
Came here for dinner the the service was great everyone was friendly and accommodating food was delicious. Drinks on point love the ambience and the 80s music playing in the background.

Dirty French is a New York bistro created by Mario Carbone, Rich Torrisi and Jeff Zalaznick located in The Ludlow hotel on the Lower East Side.

It's sophisticated and versatile; it is a great place to visit if you want to have a good time with great food. The service is superb and definitely can't go unnoticed. 

They use modern techniques and bold flavors in its food which is based on classic French bistro dishes. It's honest comfort food turned up a notch. 

From the welcoming bread gesture to the beautifully presented classic comfort food, this bistro is a treat.

Cheers

The service is 10/10. The waiter was so knowledgeable and nice. The food is okay. The free bread and spread was really good. The oysters were good and the little gem salad was good. I personally was really looking forward to the burger but it was extremely salty and not that great. The fries were also over salted as well. The chicken was also super salty. We did see a celeb when we were dining so that was cool.

One of the best French toast I have ever had! Two croissants dipped in pure heaven. Cappuccino was nice and strong. Service was very helpful. Taking a star off since it took us forever you get our food. Overall great brunch spot.

Solid 7.5 I loved all the appetizers I got and they were reasonably priced I got the bone marrow, east coast oysters, steamed sea bass (would skip next time) and the duck which i would definitely get again. And the fries were really yummy. Service was fine nothing to not but I loved the interior.
The food was pretty good, affordable (for NY) and the service was good. I would recommend this place and it is in a good location.

Sunday evening, the restaurant was empty. They must've knew what I didn't and they were right. It was empty for a reason, the flat bread came out soggy but was complimentary, the tartare was great, shrimp was great, wedge was soggy and was layered in crushed ice. Never had that before but okay.
Had filet and pomme frites for entrees. Asked for medium Rare, came out dry and medium. Waitress said it was the lighting. Swapped plates with my guests and it was a bit better not much. Waitress came, spoke to them, Floor manager came spoke to them. We will make it up. Finished dinner. Nobody made anything up. I paid the $300 for and learned the hard way. Now I am in the know and you guys are too. Overpriced mediocre food at best. 

It's now off my list and Pastis still remains on top. 
Good night to everyone except the staff at Dirty French.

I have such an amazing time when I visit this place. The wait staff is always so amazing. Today visit Ana waited on us in the enclosed patio area. It's a covered patio. So you'll have AC in the summer and heating in the winter. The food is standard with a French fair. We had the deviled eggs, wagu beef puff pastry, French dip sandwich and the burger and they were all delicious. The steak frites was great the last time I was there. Some menu items are a la cart. Cocktails are great and grossly underrated, we had the Belmondo and Paloma, they are delicious! Can't wait to visit again on my next trip to NYC.
This place is so beautiful  super chill, excellent food and delicious  drinks and flatbread with the butter  is to die for!
This quiet, cozy dining area in the Ludlum Hotel has a smaller menu, but the food was delicious. Fluffy, light scrambled eggs were accompanied by freshly made toasted sesame bread.
Great food, great service, great laughs... abdel suggestions were on point and the skillet croissant was to die for
Amazing lounge, great service! I didn't have the food but the drinks are delicious. The ambiance is top tier. I love this place.

Good food ..ambiance fits the name. Not the experience I had hoped for with the food selection being French cuisine. However, very tasty and the serve was very attentive. Very relaxed and comfortable as I dined with a friend/co worker as part of my pre 50th birthday festivities! The grilled oysters wasn't my thing ! I'd rather them raw and the filet mignon was really good except it was too salty! The peppercorn sauce would have been enough to complement the essence of the meat!

Yes, I do celebrate my Birthday for the month so Dirty French made it on my birthday dining list for the month of October. I will say the hostess was super nice, checked me in and I was escorted to my table. Placed my drink order while I reviewed the menu. Well, my appetizer was Deviled Eggs and they could have been warm but they did taste good. For my entrée I got the scallops, fries and spinach and it was on point!!!!!  To close out for dessert we had the beignets and ice cream. I will say the beignets could have been better the ice cream helped them taste better. 

The manager Emma was a doll she came over and gave us the details on the bread that they serve and I will say that was definitely the best bread that I have had. I can say I will be going back to Dirty French with my mate soon. 


If you are in the NYC area check out Dirty French. I will say take public transportation or a uber . If not you can park in the lot for $70 bucks  well I guess it's worth it.

Upon arrival, you are greeted with a warm welcome from the host.  Coat check is available and there are also golden hooks between tables to hang your own.  (For these approaching colder months in NY).  We arrived a few minutes late to a group dinner where there was a mix up with our reservation but all was sorted.  6 party group dinner, seating was a bit tight in a booth.  First round of drinks were on the house due to the reservation mix up.  (Wonderful grand gesture).  I ordered a dirty peach (bourbon, pimento and peach.) earthy and smooth with a hint of sweetness.  For appetizers we ordered grilled oysters (2) 6 in each order, with fresh garlic and parsley (delicious when dipped with crunchy french bread) which accompanied the oysters.  Also an order of tuna tartar.  For my main course, I ordered one of their signature dishes, which sometimes is unavailable due to popular demand.  Lucky for me it was indeed available: Duck Al' Orange. Tender and juicy, served in a subtle sweet orange glaze.  It was incredible! Paired with table shares of dirty rice, which has a smokey cajun flavor and grilled asparagus.  Other dishes were note worthy.  Chicken  Persillade, roasted (bone in) very tender and flavorful.  Scallops, grilled to perfection. Pork in a bed of sautéed peppers.  Kale salad with chicken.  We had another round of drinks, and everyone was too full for dessert.  Our server, Oliver was knowledgeable, friendly and checked in with our party regularly.  Lovely ambience, soft lighting, although there were some odd clown heads (long row of them) peering down on us that didn't much fit the decor. Recommend for a romantic date night, dinner with friends, a business meeting or even to grab a bite solo.  Sophisticated menu, and moderately priced.

Dropped-in to Dirty French for a very light lunch with a group the other day. The food was pretty good (apologies for the lack of photos). What we did really appreciate was DFNY accommodating our group of five without any hassle. The atmosphere (intentionally) has a French bistro vibe without being overwrought. I'm a fan - thanks for the hospitalité.

Food is delicious, can't speak to the drinks, but I had a sip of my mom's bloody Mary and it was good. Loved the pancakes! The staff is really sweet, especially Sadie and Cesar. They handled our big party with ease and no major issues. We were in a back room with tons of light. The space was beautiful and had some cozy seating beside the table we were at as well!

Service was excellent ! From the host to the waiter they were fun and friendly. The food was excellent and well prepared and presented. Ambiance was nice and dark with poor of pink. Lots of stories behind it all which our waiter knew all about. The farmers cheese and bread is to die for and the steak frites were insanely good.

I LOVED THIS PLACE! The ambiance is incredible, low lighting and the restaurant has a fancy-hip vibe. We had a reservation and were seated promptly. Our waiter was fast, got all of our drink orders in and got them back to us so we could start the night. Their menu is short, but the opportunity is endless. The deviled eggs were phenomenal- I can't tell you the last time I've had one let alone at a restaurant. The bone marrow?? Holy crap. That was done and dusted between the 5 of us really fast. So damn good. The tuna tartare was great, and had a nice lemon-lime flavor to it. I got the burger, felt like the best bang for your buck since it came with fries and it was so good. The fries were crispy too. I had an espresso martini and a Cosmo. Both were fabulous. The employee with the tattoos made sure every table was doing great. Wish I got his name (and his number!). Hope to be back soon!

I usually like to mark my birthday each year with dinner. Over the years I've picked a combo of my favorite spots and new places that I had been meaning to try for a while. This year, it was the latter as Dirty French was on my radar for quite some time. That being said, I booked a table and off we went. 

Dirty French is one of several restaurants owned by Major Food Group, the same company behind the hyped up Carbone and Torrisi. The restaurant is located inside the Ludlow Hotel, though it has its own entrance on the street so it doesn't give off hotel restaurant vibes. The dining area is all in one room - there's a combination of booths and tables with an impressive bar right when you enter and a lounge area in the back where you can enjoy a drink (I think this is shared space with the hotel). The decor is eclectic - kinda funky with knick knacks places throughout the dining room which makes it fun without being tacky. They were playing 80s music while we were there which added to the fun. 

As the name suggests, the menu consists of French cuisine - with a decent selection without being overwhelming. We were started with this flatbread that was served with a herbed fromage blanc. This was delicious - the flatbread was slightly grilled with mild seasoning and was soft and chewy; the fromage blanc provided a good balance. It was really everything you wanted out of a flatbread - bonus points for being complimentary. For my starter I had the saucisson which was served over lentils. The sausage itself was great - lots of flavor without being too salty. The lentils were flavored with mustard which really elevated them - a really good dish. 

For my main I decided on fish and went with the dover sole. This was delicious - the fish had great flavor and was prepared in a light but tasty sauce. We also got a few sides for the table - dirty rice, steamed spinach, and pommes Louis. All of these were great - the dirty rice had some heat to it which was welcome, and the pommes Louis were prepared home-fry style with herbs and garlic mmmm. We of course had dessert, and I went with the gateau au chocolat; I'm not a huge chocolate cake person but it just felt right being my born day. The cake was very good.- super chocolately and on the rich side (two people could have easily shared it, but I was up for the challenge). 

Service was great - everyone was friendly and food came out at a good pace. Overall, I had a great experience at Dirty French and it made for a memorable birthday. I'm not sure this is a 5-star experience, especially when compared to other MFG spots, however Dirty French holds their own and would definitely return for another meal.
Nothing short of perfect ! The food, vibe and staff were amazing. Great French Bistro in the heart of the city.

Amazing doesn't sum up this restaurant! It was more than amazing! We had the back room reserved all to ourselves, with our own servers. We had an open bar which meant thi minute your glass was empty someone was there filming it up again. The restaurant was gorgeous with a very elegant feel  to it. The service was what really did it for me though. They were extremely polite and helpful. If you left the table they refolded your napkin for you. The food was incredible!! We got a selection of small plates and a shellfish plateau. The Dover Sole Meuniere was my favorite!! The chicken and crepes was  my second. Also, you can never go wrong with seafood, so bring it on! I can't wait to come back!!

Loved the way the restaurant was set up, the free bread we got was a nice touch and not too bad. I would not get the calamari from here, it tasted like rubber or it was just not cooked well, the grilled Oysters were pretty good, and the burger was average. The buns on the burger were a bit burnt which I didn't like but the fries were very good! I love that they fry them in duck fat

The service was very eh, our waiter took our order and really only came back near the end when it was time for dessert/our check. The good thing was there were at least people walking around filling up the water constantly which I was very happy with and other people were able to help get sauces that i needed

Love the atmosphere they played great music all night. The decor fits the concept of the restaurant. The service was good. All the bus boys were attentive. 
The appetizers were great. Drinks were good. I do recommend getting the bone marrow. 

The main course is where I took away a star. The scallops that we ordered were really salty and slightly fishy. We did not bring it to their attention or make a fuss out of it because the portion was small, I took a bite then my boyfriend took a bite and that looked like we ate half the dish. 
The filet mignon was cooked properly, but the sauce was a little too buttery for my taste.
